the person who is UK resident and is closest, by reference to that series of contracts, to the client is a relevant party.
Subsection (5) applies if any of the following cases applies.
Case 1 is that—

a person (“the purported umbrella company”) participates in arrangements that would, if an individual were employed by the purported umbrella company, result in the umbrella company arrangements conditions being met in relation to services the individual provides to the client,
either—

it is reasonable to suppose that one or more participants in the arrangements, other than the purported umbrella company or the individual, would assume that the purported umbrella company is the employer of that individual, or

the purported umbrella company has taken any step that it is reasonable to suppose was intended to give the impression to any person (whether or not that impression is given) that the purported umbrella company is the employer of the individual,
the individual is not employed by the purported umbrella company, and
if the individual were employed by the purported umbrella company subsection (2) of section 61Y would apply.
Case 2 is that—

a person (“the purported umbrella company”) participates in arrangements that would, if an individual were employed by the purported umbrella company, result in the umbrella company arrangements conditions being met in relation to services the individual provides to the client,
the individual would, ignoring this section, be treated as employed by the purported umbrella company as a result of Chapter 7 of this Part,
if the individual were employed by the purported umbrella company subsection (2) of section 61Y would apply,
if it did apply accordingly, the contract referred to in subsection (4)(a) of that section would be between the umbrella company and the client, and

the provision of the services by the individual to the client was not as a result of services having been provided to the individual in connection with finding the client with a view to the individual personally providing services to the client—
by the purported umbrella company, or
where the provision of services to the client is as a result of a series of contracts, by one or more of the parties to those contracts.
Case 3 is that—

a company (“the purported umbrella company”) in which an individual has a material interest, within the meaning given by subsection (5)(a) of section 61Y, participates in arrangements that would, if the company were the umbrella company, result in the umbrella company arrangements conditions being met in relation to services the individual provides to the client,
either—

it is reasonable to suppose that one or more participants in the arrangements, other than the purported umbrella company or the individual, would assume that a substantial proportion of amounts provided to the purported umbrella company in respect of the services will be paid to the individual as earnings, or

the purported umbrella company has taken any step that it is reasonable to suppose was intended to give the impression to any person (whether or not that impression is given) that a substantial proportion of amounts provided to the purported umbrella company in respect of the services will be paid to the individual as earnings,
it is not the case that a substantial proportion of amounts provided to the purported umbrella company in respect of the services is paid to the individual as earnings, and
subsection (2) of section 61Y would apply if subsection (1)(b)(ii) of that section (requirement that the umbrella company is not a company in which the worker has a material interest) were omitted.
If this subsection applies—

the individual is to be treated for income tax purposes as holding an employment with the purported umbrella company, the duties of which consist of the services the individual provides to the client,
all relevant remuneration is to be treated for income tax purposes as earnings from that employment,

where there is any provision of relevant remuneration (by any person and to any person) that does not result (whether as a direct result of that provision, as a result of the onward provision of that remuneration or otherwise) in the payment of PAYE income of that remuneration, or any part of it, to the individual, the purported umbrella company is treated as making, and the individual is treated as receiving—
a payment of PAYE income in the relevant amount made at the time it was provided for the purposes of the PAYE provisions, and
a qualifying umbrella company payment made in the relevant amount at that time for the purposes of section 61Y(3),
Chapters 7 to 10 of this Part (deemed employment by intermediaries) do not apply in relation to the provision of those services,
section 863A (deemed employment of partners in limited liability partnerships) of ITTOIA 2005 does not apply so far as it otherwise would apply in relation to the provision of those services, and
accordingly, section 61Y(2) will apply in relation to the purported umbrella company.
For the purposes of subsection (5)—
in paragraph (c) the relevant amount means so much of the remuneration provided as does not result in the payment of PAYE income to the individual, and
that paragraph only applies in relation to the initial provision of an amount of relevant remuneration (and not to any subsequent onward provision of that same amount).

If subsection (5) would, ignoring this subsection, apply in relation to more than one purported umbrella company in relation to services the individual provides to the client, that subsection only applies in relation to the purported umbrella company that—
is a person to whom PAYE regulations apply and is closest to the individual, by reference to the contract or series of contracts resulting in the provision of those services, or
if none of the purported umbrella companies is a person to whom PAYE regulations apply, is closest to the individual by reference to that contract or those contracts.
Where subsection (5) applies and there is a person who is an umbrella company in relation to the services the individual provides to the client, that subsection has effect as if—
paragraph (a) were omitted,
in paragraph (b), the reference to that employment were to the employment of the individual by the umbrella company,
in paragraph (c), the reference to the purported umbrella company were to the umbrella company, and
paragraph (f) were omitted.
Subsection (10) applies where subsection (5) applies and there is more than one person who—
is an umbrella company in relation to services the individual provides to the client, or
is a purported umbrella company in relation to those services (including a purported umbrella company in relation to which subsection (5) does not apply as a result of subsection (7)).

Where this subsection applies, each of the persons falling within paragraphs (a) or (b) of subsection (9) is (to the extent this would not otherwise be the case) jointly and severally liable to pay any amount payable, in accordance with the PAYE provisions, in relation to the relevant remuneration.
For the purposes of this section “
” means—
all remuneration receivable by the individual (from any person) in consequence of providing the services, and

any other amount that it is just and reasonable to attribute to provision of the services by the individual (for example, any amounts that would form part of any deemed direct employment payment or deemed direct payment if any of Chapters 8, 9 or 10 of this Part applied).
Subsection (2) applies where an officer of Revenue and Customs considers that a person is, or may be, jointly and severally liable to pay an amount as a result of this Chapter.

The officer may at any time disclose to the person such information as the officer considers appropriate (whether or not such a disclosure would otherwise be permitted under section 18(2)(a) of CRCA 2005 or any other enactment) for the purposes of informing the person about that liability (“the joint liability”) including—
the identity of any person who is an umbrella company, a purported umbrella company or the worker in relation to the arrangements to which the joint liability relates, and
information about the nature and extent of the liability of an umbrella company or a purported umbrella company that (by virtue of this Chapter) results, or may result, in the joint liability.
Information disclosed in reliance on subsection (2) may not be further disclosed without the consent of the Commissioners for His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (which may be general or specific).
Where a person contravenes subsection (3) by disclosing information relating to a person whose identity—
is specified in the disclosure, or
can be deduced from it,
section 19 of CRCA 2005 (offence of wrongful disclosure) applies in relation to the disclosure as it applies in relation to a disclosure in contravention of section 20(9) of that Act.
In this section “
” means the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005.

Part.Title: Employment income: earnings and benefits etc. treated as earnings

P1group.Title: Earnings

P2para.Text: This section explains what is meant by “earnings” in the employment income Parts.
In those Parts “earnings”, in relation to an employment, means—

P3para.Text: any salary, wages or fee,
any gratuity or other profit or incidental benefit of any kind obtained by the employee if it is money or money’s worth, or
anything else that constitutes an emolument of the employment.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (2) “money’s worth” means something that is—

P3para.Text: of direct monetary value to the employee, or
capable of being converted into money or something of direct monetary value to the employee.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) does not affect the operation of statutory provisions that provide for amounts to be treated as earnings (and see section 721(7)).

P1group.Title: The benefits code

P2para.Text: In the employment income Parts “the benefits code” means—

Para.Text: this Chapter,
Chapter 3 (expenses payments),
Chapter 4 (vouchers and credit-tokens),
Chapter 5 (living accommodation),
Chapter 6 (cars, vans and related benefits),
Chapter 7 (loans), and
Chapter 10 (residual liability to charge)

Text.Addition: The benefits code has effect subject to section 554Z2(2).

P1group.Title: Relationship between earnings and benefits code

P2para.Text: This section applies if, apart from this section, the same benefit would give rise to two amounts (“A” and “B”)—

P3para.Text: A being an amount of earnings as defined in Chapter 1 of this Part, and
B being an amount to be treated as earnings under the benefits code.

P2para.Text: In such a case—

P3para.Text: A constitutes earnings as defined in Chapter 1 of this Part, and
the amount (if any) by which B exceeds A is to be treated as earnings under the benefits code.

P2para.Text: This section does not apply in connection with living accommodation to which Chapter 5 of this Part applies.
In that case section 109 applies to determine the relationship between that Chapter and Chapter 1 of this Part.

P1group.Title: Dispensations relating to benefits within provisions not applicable to lower-paid employment
Meaning of “employment” and related expressions

P2para.Text: In the benefits code—

P3para.Text: “employment” means a taxable employment under Part 2, and
“employed”, “employee” and “employer” have corresponding meanings.

P2para.Text: Where a Chapter of the benefits code applies in relation to an employee—

P3para.Text: references in that Chapter to “the employment” are to the employment of that employee, and
references in that Chapter to “the employer” are to the employer in respect of that employment.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the benefits code an employment is a “taxable employment under Part 2” in a tax year if the earnings from the employment for that year are (or would be if there were any) general earnings to which the charging provisions of Chapter 4 or 5 of Part 2 apply.
In subsection (3)—

P3para.Text: the reference to an employment includes employment as a director of a company, and
“earnings” means earnings as defined in Chapter 1 of this Part.

Text.Addition: In the benefits code “

Term.Addition: lower-paid employment as a minister of religion

Text.Addition: ” has the same meaning as in Part 4 (see section 290D).

P1group.Title: Meaning of “director” and “full-time working director”

P2para.Text: In the benefits code “director” means—

P3para.Text: in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by a board of directors or similar body, a member of that body,
in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by a single director or similar person, that director or person, and
in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by the members themselves, a member of the company,

P2para.Text: and includes any person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the directors of the company (as defined above) are accustomed to act.

For the purposes of subsection (1) a person is not to be regarded as a person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the directors of the company are accustomed to act merely because the directors act on advice given by that person in a professional capacity.
In the benefits code “full-time working director” means a director who is required to devote substantially the whole of his time to the service of the company in a managerial or technical capacity.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “material interest” in a company

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the benefits code a person has a material interest in a company if condition A or B is met.
Condition A is that the person (with or without one or more associates) or any associate of that person (with or without one or more other such associates) is—

P3para.Text: the beneficial owner of, or
able to control, directly or through the medium of other companies or by any other indirect means,

P2para.Text: more than 5% of the ordinary share capital of the company.

Condition B is that, in the case of a close company, the person (with or without one or more associates) or any associate of that person (with or without one or more other such associates), possesses or is entitled to acquire, such rights as would—

P3para.Text: in the event of the winding-up of the company, or
in any other circumstances,

P2para.Text: give an entitlement to receive more than 5% of the assets which would then be available for distribution among the participators.
In this section—

Para.Text: “associate” has the meaning given by section 448 of CTA 2010 except that, for this purpose, “relative” in section 448(1) has the meaning given by subsection (5) below, and
“participator” has the meaning given by section 454 of CTA 2010.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section a person (“A”) is a relative of another (“B”) if A is—

P3para.Text: B’s spouse or civil partner,
a parent, child or remoter relation in the direct line either of B or of B’s spouse or civil partner,
a brother or sister of B or of B’s spouse or civil partner, or
the spouse or civil partner of a person falling within paragraph (b) or (c).

P1group.Title: Extended meaning of “control”

P2para.Text: The definition of “control” in section 995 of ITA 2007 (which is applied for the purposes of this Act by section 719) is extended as follows.
For the purposes of the benefits code that definition applies (with the necessary modifications) in relation to an unincorporated association as it applies in relation to a body corporate.

Text.Addition: Subsections (2) to (7) have effect for the purposes of the benefits code.

A benefit provided for an employee is provided under “optional remuneration arrangements” so far as it is provided under arrangements of type A or B (regardless of whether those arrangements are made before or after the beginning of the person's employment).
“Type A arrangements” are arrangements under which, in return for the benefit, the employee gives up the right (or a future right) to receive an amount of earnings within Chapter 1 of Part 3.
“Type B arrangements” are arrangements (other than type A arrangements) under which the employee agrees to be provided with the benefit rather than an amount of earnings within Chapter 1 of Part 3.

A benefit provided for an employee is to be regarded as provided under optional remuneration arrangements (whether of type A or type B) so far as it is just and reasonable to attribute the provision of the benefit to the arrangements in question.

Where a benefit is provided for an employee under any arrangements, the mere fact that under the arrangements the employee makes good, or is required to make good, any part of the cost of provision is not to be taken to show that the benefit is (to any extent) provided otherwise than under optional remuneration arrangements.

Where a benefit is provided for an employee partly under optional remuneration arrangements and partly otherwise than under such arrangements, the benefits code is to apply with any modifications (including provision for just and reasonable apportionments) that may be required for ensuring that the benefit is treated—
in accordance with the relevant provision in the column 2 of the table so far as it is provided under optional remuneration arrangements, and
in accordance with the relevant provision in column 1 of the table so far as it is provided otherwise than under such arrangements.
For the purposes of the benefits code “the amount foregone”—
in relation to a benefit provided for an employee under type A arrangements means the amount of earnings mentioned in section 69A(3);
in relation to a benefit provided for an employee under type B arrangements means the amount of earnings mentioned in section 69A(4);
in relation to a benefit provided for an employee partly under type A arrangements and partly under type B arrangements, means the sum of the amounts foregone under the arrangements of each type.

Subsection (3) applies where, in order to determine the amount foregone with respect to a particular benefit mentioned in section 69A(3) or (4), it is necessary to apportion an amount of earnings to the benefit.
The apportionment is to be made on a just and reasonable basis.
In this section and section 69A references to a benefit provided for an employee include a benefit provided for a member of an employee's family or household.
In this section and section 69A—
” includes any benefit or facility, regardless of its form and the manner of providing it;
” means earnings within Chapter 1 of Part 3 (and includes a reference to amounts which would have been such earnings if the employee had received them).

P1group.Title: Sums in respect of expenses

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to a sum paid to an employee in a tax year if the sum—

P3para.Text: is paid to the employee in respect of expenses, and
is so paid by reason of the employment.

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to a sum paid away by an employee in a tax year if the sum—

P3para.Text: was put at the employee’s disposal in respect of expenses,
was so put by reason of the employment, and
is paid away by the employee in respect of expenses.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter it does not matter whether the employment is held at the time when the sum is paid or paid away so long as it is held at some point in the tax year in which the sum is paid or paid away.
References in this Chapter to an employee accordingly include a prospective or former employee.
This Chapter does not apply to the extent that the sum constitutes earnings from the employment by virtue of any other provision.

P1group.Title: Meaning of paid or put at disposal by reason of the employment

P2para.Text: If an employer pays a sum in respect of expenses to an employee it is to be treated as paid by reason of the employment unless—

P3para.Text: the employer is an individual, and
the payment is made in the normal course of the employer’s domestic, family or personal relationships.

P2para.Text: If an employer puts a sum at an employee’s disposal in respect of expenses it is to be treated as put at the employee’s disposal by reason of the employment unless—

P3para.Text: the employer is an individual, and
the sum is put at the employee’s disposal in the normal course of the employer’s domestic, family or personal relationships.

P1group.Title: Sums in respect of expenses treated as earnings

P2para.Text: If this Chapter applies to a sum, the sum is to be treated as earnings from the employment for the tax year in which it is paid or paid away.
Subsection (1) does not prevent the making of a deduction allowed under any of the provisions listed in subsection (3).
The provisions are—

Para.Text: section 336 (deductions for expenses: the general rule);
section 337 (travel in performance of duties);
section 338 (travel for necessary attendance);
section 340 (travel between group employments);

Text.Addition: section 340A (travel between linked employments);

Para.Text: section 341 (travel at start or finish of overseas employment);
section 342 (travel between employments where duties performed abroad);
section 343 (deduction for professional membership fees);
section 344 (deduction for annual subscriptions);
section 346 (deduction for employee liabilities);
section 351 (expenses of ministers of religion);
section 353 (deductions from earnings charged on remittance).

P1group.Title: Cash vouchers to which this Chapter applies

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to a cash voucher provided for an employee by reason of the employment which is received by the employee.
A cash voucher provided for an employee by the employer is to be regarded as provided by reason of the employment unless—

P3para.Text: the employer is an individual, and
the provision is made in the normal course of the employer’s domestic, family or personal relationships.

P2para.Text: A cash voucher provided for an employee and appropriated to the employee—

P3para.Text: by attaching it to a card held for the employee, or
in any other way,

P2para.Text: is to be treated for the purposes of this Chapter as having been received by the employee at the time when it is appropriated.

P1group.Title: Provision for, or receipt by, member of employee’s family

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter any reference to a cash voucher being provided for or received by an employee includes a reference to it being provided for or received by a member of the employee’s family.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “cash voucher”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “cash voucher” means a voucher, stamp or similar document capable of being exchanged for a sum of money which is—

P3para.Text: greater than,
equal to, or
not substantially less than,

P2para.Text: the expense incurred by the person at whose cost the voucher, stamp or similar document is provided.
For the purposes of subsection (1) it does not matter whether the document—

P3para.Text: is also capable of being exchanged for goods or services;
is capable of being exchanged singly or together with other vouchers, stamps, or documents;
is capable of being exchanged immediately or only after a time.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) is subject to section 76 (sickness benefits-related voucher).

P1group.Title: Sickness benefits-related voucher

P2para.Text: This section applies where—

P3para.Text: the expense incurred by the person at whose cost a voucher, stamp or similar document is provided (“the provision expense”) includes costs to that person of providing sickness benefits (“sickness benefits costs”),

the voucher, stamp or document would be a cash voucher (apart from this section) but for the fact that the sum of money for which it is capable of being exchanged (“the exchange sum”) is substantially less than the provision expense, and
the whole or part of the difference between the exchange sum and the provision expense represents the sickness benefits costs.

P2para.Text: The voucher, stamp or document is a cash voucher within the meaning of this Chapter if—
or

Para.Text: where—
E is the exchange sum,
PE is the provision expense, and
D is the amount of the difference between E and PE which represents the sickness benefits costs.

P2para.Text: In this section “sickness benefits” mean benefits in connection with sickness, personal injury or death.

P1group.Title: Apportionment of cost of provision of voucher

P1para.Text: If a person incurs expense in or in connection with the provision of vouchers, stamps or similar documents for two or more employees as members of a group or class, the expense incurred in respect of one of them is to be such part of that expense as is just and reasonable.

P1group.Title: Voucher made available to public generally

P1para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a cash voucher if—

P3para.Text: it is of a kind made available to the public generally, and
it is provided to the employee or a member of the employee’s family on no more favourable terms than to the public generally.

P1group.Title: Voucher issued under approved scheme

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a cash voucher received by an employee if—

P3para.Text: it is issued under a scheme, and
at the time when it is received the scheme is a scheme approved by an officer of Revenue and Customs for the purposes of this section.

P2para.Text: An officer of Revenue and Customs must not approve a scheme for the purposes of this section unless the officer is satisfied that it is practicable for income tax in respect of all payments made in exchange for vouchers issued under the scheme to be deducted in accordance with PAYE regulations.

P1group.Title: Vouchers where payment of sums exempt from tax

P1para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a cash voucher if it is—

P3para.Text: a document intended to enable a person to obtain payment of a sum which would not have constituted employment income if paid to the person directly, or
a savings certificate where the accumulated interest payable in respect of it is exempt from tax (or would be so exempt if certain conditions were met).

Title.Emphasis: Benefit of cash voucher treated as earnings

P1group.Title: Benefit of cash voucher treated as earnings

P2para.Text: The cash equivalent of the benefit of a cash voucher to which this Chapter applies is to be treated as earnings from the employment for the tax year in which the voucher is received by the employee.

Text.Addition: Where a cash voucher to which this Chapter applies is provided pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements—
subsection (1) does not apply, and
the relevant amount is to be treated as earnings from the employment for the tax year in which the voucher is received by the employee.
In this section “
” means—
the cash equivalent, or
if greater, the amount foregone with respect to the benefit of the voucher (see section 69B).

P2para.Text: The cash equivalent is the sum of money for which the voucher is capable of being exchanged.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of subsection (1B), assume that the cash equivalent is zero if the condition in subsection (4) is met.
The condition is that the benefit of the voucher would be exempt from income tax but for section 228A (exclusion of certain exemptions).

P1group.Title: Non-cash vouchers to which this Chapter applies

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to a non-cash voucher provided for an employee by reason of the employment which is received by the employee.
A non-cash voucher provided for an employee by the employer is to be regarded as provided by reason of the employment unless—

P3para.Text: the employer is an individual, and
the provision is made in the normal course of the employer’s domestic, family or personal relationships.

P2para.Text: A non-cash voucher provided for an employee and appropriated to the employee—

P3para.Text: by attaching it to a card held for the employee, or
in any other way,

P2para.Text: is to be treated for the purposes of this Chapter as having been received by the employee at the time when it is appropriated.

P1group.Title: Provision for, or receipt by, member of employee’s family

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter any reference to a non-cash voucher being provided for or received by an employee includes a reference to it being provided for or received by a member of the employee’s family.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “non-cash voucher”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “non-cash voucher” means—

P3para.Text: a voucher, stamp or similar document or token which is capable of being exchanged for money, goods or services,

Text.Addition: a childcare voucher,

P3para.Text: a transport voucher, or
a cheque voucher,

P2para.Text: but does not include a cash voucher.
For the purposes of subsection (1)(a) it does not matter whether the document or token is capable of being exchanged—

P3para.Text: singly or together with other vouchers, stamps, documents or tokens;
immediately or only after a time.

Text.Addition: In this Chapter “
” means a voucher, stamp or similar document or token intended to enable a person to obtain the provision of care for a child (whether or not in exchange for it).

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “transport voucher” means a ticket, pass or other document or token intended to enable a person to obtain passenger transport services (whether or not in exchange for it).
In this Chapter “cheque voucher” means a cheque—

P3para.Text: provided for an employee, and
intended for use by the employee wholly or mainly for payment for—

P4para.Text: particular goods or services, or
goods or services of one or more particular classes;

P3para.Text: and, in relation to a cheque voucher, references to a voucher being exchanged for goods or services are to be read accordingly.

P1group.Title: Non-cash voucher made available to public generally

P1para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a non-cash voucher if—

P3para.Text: it is of a kind made available to the public generally, and
it is provided to the employee or a member of the employee’s family on no more favourable terms than to the public generally.

P1group.Title: Transport vouchers under pre-26th March 1982 arrangements

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a transport voucher provided for an employee of a passenger transport undertaking under arrangements in operation on 25th March 1982 which meet the condition in subsection (2).
The condition is that the arrangements are intended to enable the employee or a member of the employee’s family to obtain passenger transport services provided by—

P3para.Text: the employer,
a subsidiary of the employer,
a body corporate of which the employer is a subsidiary, or
another passenger transport undertaking.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “passenger transport undertaking” means an undertaking whose business consists wholly or mainly in the carriage of passengers or a subsidiary of such an undertaking, and
“subsidiary” means a wholly-owned subsidiary within the meaning of section 1159 of and Schedule 6 to the Companies Act 2006.

Title.Emphasis: Benefit of non-cash voucher treated as earnings

P1group.Title: Benefit of non-cash voucher treated as earnings

P2para.Text: The cash equivalent of the benefit of a non-cash voucher to which this Chapter applies is to be treated as earnings from the employment for the tax year in which the voucher is received by the employee.
The cash equivalent is the difference between—

P3para.Text: the cost of provision, and
any part of that cost made good by the employee , to the person incurring it, on or before 6 July following the relevant tax year.

Text.Addition: If the voucher is a non-cash voucher other than a cheque voucher, the relevant tax year is—
the tax year in which the cost of provision is incurred, or
if later, the tax year in which the employee receives the voucher.
If the voucher is a cheque voucher, the relevant tax year is the tax year in which the voucher is handed over in exchange for money, goods or services.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter the “cost of provision” means, in relation to a non-cash voucher, the expense incurred in or in connection with the provision of—

P3para.Text: the voucher, and
the money, goods or services for which it is capable of being exchanged,

P2para.Text: by the person at whose cost they are provided.

Text.Addition: In the case of a childcare voucher, the reference in subsection (3)(b) to the services for which the voucher is capable of being exchanged is to the provision of care for a child which may be obtained by using it.

P2para.Text: In the case of a transport voucher, the reference in subsection (3)(b) to the services for which the voucher is capable of being exchanged is to the passenger transport services which may be obtained by using it.

If a person incurs expense in or in connection with the provision of non-cash vouchers for two or more employees as members of a group or class, the expense incurred in respect of one of them is to be such part of that expense as is just and reasonable.

Title.Addition: Benefit of non-cash voucher treated as earnings: optional remuneration arrangements

Text.Addition: Where a non-cash voucher to which this Chapter applies is provided pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements—
the relevant amount is to be treated as earnings from the employment for the tax year in which the voucher is received by the employee, and
section 87(1) does not apply.
To find the relevant amount, first determine which (if any) is the greater of—
the cost of provision (see section 87(3)), and
the amount foregone with respect to the benefit of the voucher (see section 69B).
If the cost of provision is greater than or equal to the amount foregone, the “relevant amount” is the cash equivalent of the benefit of the non-cash voucher (see section 87(2)).
Otherwise, the “relevant amount” is the difference between—
the amount foregone, and
any part of the cost of provision that is made good by the employee, to the person incurring it, on or before 6 July following the relevant tax year.
If the voucher is a non-cash voucher other than a cheque voucher, the relevant tax year is—
the tax year in which the cost of provision is incurred, or
if later, the tax year in which the employee receives the voucher.
If the voucher is a cheque voucher, the relevant tax year is the tax year in which the voucher is handed over in exchange for money, goods or services.
For the purposes of subsections (2) and (3), assume that the cost of provision is zero if the condition in subsection (8) is met.
The condition is that the non-cash voucher would be exempt from income tax but for section 228A (exclusion of certain exemptions).

P1group.Title: Year in which earnings treated as received

P2para.Text: In the case of a non-cash voucher other than a cheque voucher, the amount treated as earnings under section 87 or 87A is to be treated as received—

P3para.Text: in the tax year in which the cost of provision is incurred, or
if later, in the tax year in which the voucher is received by the employee.

P2para.Text: In the case of a cheque voucher, the amount treated as earnings under section 87 or 87A is to be treated as received in the tax year in which the voucher is handed over in exchange for money, goods or services.
For the purposes of subsection (2) and sections 87(2B) and 87A(6), Where a cheque voucher is posted it is to be treated as handed over at the time of posting.

P1group.Title: Reduction for meal vouchers
Credit-tokens to which this Chapter applies

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to a credit-token provided for an employee by reason of the employment which is used by the employee to obtain money, goods or services.
A credit-token provided for an employee by the employer is to be regarded as provided by reason of the employment unless—

P3para.Text: the employer is an individual, and
the provision is made in the normal course of the employer’s domestic, family or personal relationships.

P1group.Title: Provision for, or use by, member of employee’s family

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter—

P3para.Text: any reference to a credit-token being provided for an employee includes a reference to it being provided for a member of the employee’s family, and
use of a credit-token by a member of an employee’s family is to be treated as use of the token by the employee.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “credit-token”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “credit-token” means a credit card, debit card or other card, a token, a document or other object given to a person by another person (“X”) who undertakes—

P3para.Text: on the production of it, to supply money, goods or services on credit, or
if a third party (“Y”) supplies money, goods or services on its production, to pay Y for what is supplied.

P2para.Text: A card, token, document or other object can be a credit-token even if—

P3para.Text: some other action is required in addition to its production in order for the money, goods or services to be supplied;
X in paying Y may take a discount or commission.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: the use of an object given by X to operate a machine provided by X is to be treated as its production to X, and
the use of an object given by X to operate a machine provided by Y is to be treated as its production to Y.

P2para.Text: A “credit-token” does not include a cash voucher or a non-cash voucher.

P1group.Title: Credit-token made available to public generally

P1para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a credit-token if—

P3para.Text: it is of a kind made available to the public generally, and
it is provided to the employee or a member of the employee’s family on no more favourable terms than to the public generally.

Title.Emphasis: Benefit of credit-token treated as earnings

P1group.Title: Benefit of credit-token treated as earnings

P2para.Text: On each occasion on which a credit-token to which this Chapter applies is used by the employee in a tax year to obtain money, goods or services, the cash equivalent of the benefit of the token is to be treated as earnings from the employment for that year.
The cash equivalent is the difference between—

P3para.Text: the cost of provision, and
any part of that cost made good by the employee—

Text.Substitution: to the person incurring it, and
on or before 6 July following the tax year which contains the occasion in question.

P2para.Text: In this section the “cost of provision” means the expense incurred—

P3para.Text: in or in connection with the provision of the money, goods or services obtained on the occasion in question, and
by the person at whose cost they are provided.

P2para.Text: If a person incurs expense in or in connection with the provision of credit-tokens for two or more employees as members of a group or class, the expense incurred in respect of one of them is to be such part of that expense as is just and reasonable.

Title.Addition: Benefit of credit-token treated as earnings: optional remuneration arrangements

Text.Addition: If the conditions in subsections (2) and (3) are met in relation to any occasions on which a credit-token to which this Chapter applies is used by the employee in a tax year to obtain money, goods or services—
the relevant amount is to be treated as earnings from the employment for that year, and
section 94(1) does not apply in relation to the use of the credit-token on those occasions.
The condition in this subsection is that the credit-token is used pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements.
The condition in this subsection is that AF is greater than the relevant cost of provision for the tax year.
In this section “

” means so much of the amount foregone (see section 69B) as is attributable on a just and reasonable basis to the use of the credit-token by the employee in the tax year pursuant to the optional remuneration arrangements to obtain money, goods or services.
The “relevant amount” is the difference between—
AF, and

any part of the relevant cost of provision for the tax year that is made good by the employee, to the person incurring it, on or before 6 July following the tax year which contains the occasion of use of the credit-token to which the making good relates.
But the relevant amount is taken to be zero if the amount given by paragraph (b) of subsection (4) exceeds AF.
For the purposes of this section the “relevant cost of provision for the tax year” is determined as follows—

Find the cost of provision with respect to each occasion of use of the credit-token by the employee in the tax year pursuant to the optional remuneration arrangements to obtain money, goods or services.
The total of those amounts is the relevant cost of provision for the tax year.
But the relevant cost of provision for the tax year is to be taken to be zero if the condition in subsection (8) is met.

The condition is that use of the credit token by the employee in the tax year pursuant to the optional remuneration arrangements to obtain money, goods or services would be exempt from income tax but for section 228A (exclusion of certain exemptions).
In this section “
” has the same meaning as in section 94.

P1group.Title: Disregard for money, goods or services obtained

P2para.Text: This section applies if the cash equivalent of the benefit of a cash voucher, a non-cash voucher or a credit-token or the relevant amount in respect of a cash voucher, a non-cash voucher or a credit-token —

P3para.Text: is to be treated as earnings from an employee’s employment under this Chapter, ...

P2para.Text: Money, goods or services obtained—

P3para.Text: by the employee or another person in exchange for the cash voucher or non-cash voucher, or
by the employee or a member of the employee’s family by use of the credit-token,

P2para.Text: are to be disregarded for the purposes of the Income Tax Acts.
But the goods or services are not to be disregarded for the purposes of applying sections 362 and 363 (deductions where non-cash voucher or credit-token provided).

Text.Addition: In the case of a childcare voucher, the reference in subsection (2)(a) to the services obtained in exchange for the voucher is to the provision of care for a child obtained by using it.

P2para.Text: In the case of a transport voucher, the reference in subsection (2)(a) to the services obtained in exchange for the voucher is to the passenger transport services obtained by using it.

P1group.Title: Dispensations relating to vouchers or credit-tokens

Title.Addition: Power to exempt use of non-cash vouchers or credit-tokens to obtain exempt benefits

Text.Addition: The Treasury may by regulations provide for exemption from any liability that would otherwise arise by virtue of this Chapter in respect of—
non-cash vouchers which are or can be used to obtain specified exempt benefits, or which evidence an employee's entitlement to specified exempt benefits;
credit-tokens which are used to obtain specified exempt benefits.
In this section—
” means a benefit the direct provision of which is exempted from liability to income tax by a provision of Part 4 (employment income: exemptions), and
” means specified in the regulations.
Regulations under this section may operate by amending section 266 (exemption of non-cash vouchers for exempt benefits) or section 267 (exemption of credit-tokens used for exempt benefits).

P1group.Title: Living accommodation to which this Chapter applies

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to living accommodation provided for—

P3para.Text: an employee, or
a member of an employee’s family or household,

P2para.Text: by reason of the employment.

Text.Addition: Where this Chapter applies to any living accommodation—

the living accommodation is a benefit for the purposes of this Chapter (and accordingly it is immaterial whether the terms on which it is provided to any of those persons constitute a fair bargain), and
sections 102 to 108 provide for
the benefit of the living accommodation to be treated as earnings.

P2para.Text: Living accommodation provided for any of those persons by the employer is to be regarded as provided by reason of the employment unless—

P3para.Text: the employer is an individual, and
the provision is made in the normal course of the employer’s domestic, family or personal relationships.

P1group.Title: Accommodation provided by local authority

P1para.Text: In section 102 (benefit of accommodation treated as earnings) subsection (1A) (accommodation provided otherwise than pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements) does not apply to living accommodation provided for an employee if—

P3para.Text: the employer is a local authority,
it is provided for the employee by the authority, and

the terms on which it is provided are no more favourable than those on which similar accommodation is provided by the authority for persons who are not their employees but whose circumstances are otherwise similar to those of the employee.

P1group.Title: Accommodation provided for performance of duties

P2para.Text: In section 102 (benefit of accommodation treated as earnings) subsection (1A) (accommodation provided otherwise than pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements) does not apply to living accommodation provided for an employee if it is necessary for the proper performance of the employee’s duties that the employee should reside in it.
In section 102 (benefit of accommodation treated as earnings) subsection (1A) does not apply to living accommodation provided for an employee if—

P3para.Text: it is provided for the better performance of the duties of the employment, and
the employment is one of the kinds of employment in the case of which it is customary for employers to provide living accommodation for employees.

P2para.Text: But if the accommodation is provided by a company and the employee (“E”) is a director of the company or of an associated company, the exception in subsection (1) or (2) only applies if, in the case of each company of which E is a director—

P3para.Text: E has no material interest in the company, and
either—

P4para.Text: E’s employment is as a full-time working director, or
the company is non-profit-making or is a charitable company.

P2para.Text: “Non-profit-making” means that the company does not carry on a trade and its functions do not consist wholly or mainly in the holding of investments or other property.
A company is “associated” with another if—

P3para.Text: one has control of the other, or
both are under the control of the same person.

P1group.Title: Accommodation provided as result of security threat

P1para.Text: In section 102 (benefit of accommodation treated as earnings) subsection (1A) (accommodation provided otherwise than pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements) does not apply to living accommodation provided for an employee if—

P3para.Text: there is a special threat to the security of the employee,
special security arrangements are in force, and
the employee resides in the accommodation as part of those arrangements.

Addition.Substitution: In section 102 (benefit of accommodation treated as earnings) subsection (1A) (accommodation provided otherwise than pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements)

Text.Addition: does not apply to living accommodation outside the United Kingdom provided by a company for a director or other officer of the company (“D”) or a member of D's family or household if—
the company is wholly owned by D or D and other individuals (and no interest in the company is partnership property), and
the company has been the holding company of the property at all times after the relevant time.
The company is “the holding company of the property” when—
it owns a relevant interest in the property,
its main or only asset is that interest, and
the only activities undertaken by it are ones that are incidental to its ownership of that interest.
The company is also “the holding company of the property” when—
a company (“the subsidiary”) which is wholly owned by the company meets the conditions in paragraphs (a) to (c) of subsection (2),
the company's main or only asset is its interest in the subsidiary, and
the only activities undertaken by the company are ones that are incidental to its ownership of that interest.
” means an interest under the law of any territory that confers (or would but for any inferior interest confer) a right to exclusive possession of the property at all times or at certain times.
“The relevant time” is the time the company first owned a relevant interest in the property; but this is subject to subsection (6).
If—
none of D's interest in the company was acquired directly or indirectly from a person connected with D, and
the company owned a relevant interest in the property at the time D first acquired an interest in the company,
“the relevant time” is the time D first acquired such an interest.
Section 100A(1) does not apply if subsection (2), (3) or (4) applies.
This subsection applies if—
the company's interest in the property was acquired directly or indirectly from a connected company at an undervalue, or
the company's interest in the property derives from an interest that was so acquired.
This subsection applies if, at any time after the relevant time—
expenditure in respect of the property has been incurred directly or indirectly by a connected company, or
any borrowing of the company directly or indirectly from a connected company has been outstanding (but see subsection (7)).

This subsection applies if the living accommodation is provided in pursuance of an arrangement the main purpose, or one of the main purposes, of which is the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions.
In subsection (2) references to the acquisition of an interest include the grant of an interest.

For the purposes of that subsection, an interest is acquired at an undervalue if the total consideration for it is less than that which might reasonably have been expected to be obtained on a disposal of the interest on the open market; and “consideration” here means consideration provided at any time (and, for example, includes payments by way of rent).
For the purposes of subsection (3)(b), no account is to be taken of—
any borrowing at a commercial rate, or
any borrowing which results in D being treated under Chapter 7 (taxable benefits: loans) as receiving earnings.
In subsection (4) “
” includes any scheme, agreement or understanding, whether or not enforceable.
In this section “
” means—
a company connected with D, with a member of D's family or with an employer of D, or
a company connected with such a company.

P1group.Title: Chevening House

P1para.Text: In section 102 (benefit of accommodation treated as earnings) subsection (1A) (accommodation provided otherwise than pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements) does not apply to living accommodation provided for an employee if the accommodation is—

P3para.Text: Chevening House, or
any other premises held on the trusts of the trust instrument set out in the Schedule to the Chevening Estate Act 1959 (c. 49),

P1para.Text: and the employee is a person nominated in accordance with those trusts.

Title.Emphasis: Benefit of living accommodation treated as earnings

P1group.Title: Benefit of living accommodation treated as earnings

Text.Substitution: This section applies if living accommodation to which this Chapter applies is provided in any period (“the taxable period”) —

P3para.Text: which consists of the whole or part of a tax year, and
throughout which the employee holds the employment,

Text.Addition: the cash equivalent of the benefit of the accommodation is to be treated as earnings from the employment for that year.
If the benefit of the accommodation is provided pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements—
subsection (1A) does not apply, and
the relevant amount is to be treated as earnings from the employment for that tax year.

P2para.Text: Section 103 indicates how the cash equivalent is calculated.

Text.Addition: Section 103A indicates how the relevant amount is determined.

P1group.Title: Method of calculating cash equivalent

P2para.Text: The cash equivalent is calculated—

P3para.Text: under section 105 if the cost of providing the living accommodation does not exceed £75,000; and
under section 106 if the cost of providing the living accommodation exceeds £75,000.

P2para.Text: Section 104 (general rule) sets out how to calculate the cost of providing living accommodation for the purpose of determining whether or not it exceeds £75,000.
In this Chapter—

Para.Text: “annual value”,
“person involved in providing accommodation”, and
“the property”,
have the meaning given by sections 110 to 113, and “the taxable period” has the meaning given by section 102(1) .

Title.Addition: Accommodation provided pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements: relevant amount

Text.Addition: To find the relevant amount, first determine which (if any) is the greater of—
the modified cash equivalent of the benefit of the accommodation (see sections 105(2A) and 106(2A)), and
the amount foregone with respect to the benefit of the accommodation (see section 69B).

If the amount mentioned in subsection (1)(a) is greater than or equal to the amount mentioned in subsection (1)(b), the “relevant amount” is the cash equivalent of the benefit of the accommodation (see section 103).
Otherwise, the “relevant amount” is the difference between—
the amount foregone with respect to the benefit of the accommodation, and
the deductible amount (see subsections (7) and (8)).
If the amount foregone with respect to the benefit of the accommodation does not exceed the deductible amount, the relevant amount is taken to be zero.
For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2), assume that the modified cash equivalent of the benefit of the accommodation is zero if the condition in subsection (6) is met.
The condition is that the benefit of the accommodation would be exempt from income tax but for section 228A (exclusion of certain exemptions).
If the cost of providing the living accommodation does not exceed £75,000, the “

” means any sum made good, on or before 6 July following the tax year which contains the taxable period, by the employee to the person at whose cost the accommodation is provided that is properly attributable to its provision.
If the cost of providing the living accommodation exceeds £75,000, the “
” means the total of amounts A and B where—
A is equal to so much of MG as does not exceed
B is the amount of any excess rent paid by the employee in respect of the taxable period;

MG is the total of any sums made good, on or before 6 July following the tax year which contains the taxable period, by the employee to the person at whose cost the accommodation is provided that are properly attributable to its provision (in the taxable period);
RV
is the rental value of the accommodation for the taxable period as set out in section 105(3) or (4A)(b) (as applicable).
In subsection (8) “
” means so much of the rent in respect of the taxable period paid—
by the employee,
in respect of the accommodation,
to the person providing it, and
on or before 6 July following the tax year which contains the taxable period,
as exceeds the rental value of the accommodation.

Where it is necessary for the purposes of subsection (1)(b) and (3)(a) to apportion an amount of earnings to the benefit of the accommodation in the taxable period, the apportionment is to be made on a just and reasonable basis.
In this subsection “earnings” is to be interpreted in accordance with section 69B(5).

P1group.Title: General rule for calculating cost of providing accommodation

P1para.Text: For any tax year the cost of providing living accommodation is given by the formula—

Para.Text: where—
A is any expenditure incurred in acquiring the estate or interest in the property held by a person involved in providing the accommodation,
I is any expenditure incurred on improvements to the property which has been incurred before the tax year in question by a person involved in providing the accommodation, and
P is so much of any payment or payments made by the employee to a person involved in providing the accommodation as represents—
(a) reimbursement of A or I, or
(b) consideration for the grant to the employee of a tenancy or sub-tenancy of the property.

P1group.Title: Cash equivalent: cost of accommodation not over £75,000

P2para.Text: The cash equivalent or modified cash equivalent is to be calculated under this section if the cost of providing the living accommodation does not exceed £75,000.
The cash equivalent is the difference between—

P3para.Text: the rental value of the accommodation for the taxable period, and

any sum made good , on or before 6 July following the tax year which contains the taxable period, by the employee to the person at whose cost the accommodation is provided that is properly attributable to its provision.

Text.Addition: The modified cash equivalent is equal to the rental value of the accommodation for the taxable period.

P2para.Text: The “rental value of the accommodation” for the taxable period is (subject to subsections (4) and (4A)) the rent which would have been payable for that period if the property had been let to the employee at an annual rent equal to the annual value.

Text.Substitution: Subsection (4A) applies where—
a rental amount is payable by the person (“P”) at whose cost the accommodation is provided in respect of the whole or part of the taxable period (“
”), and
the amount so payable is payable at an annual rate greater than the annual value.
Where this subsection applies—
subsection (3) does not apply to the relevant period, and
instead the “rental value of the accommodation” for the relevant period is the rental amount payable by P in respect of the relevant period.
A reference in subsection (4) or (4A) to a rental amount payable by P in respect of the relevant period is to the sum of—
any rent for the period payable by P, and
any amount attributed to the period in respect of a lease premium (see sections 105A and 105B).

P2para.Text: If the rental value of the accommodation for the taxable period does not exceed any sum made good by the employee as mentioned in subsection (2)(b), the cash equivalent is nil.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of section 105(4B)(b) an amount is attributed to the relevant period “in respect of a lease premium” if—
the property consists of premises, or a part of premises, that are subject to a lease,
the premises are not mainly used by P for a purpose other than the provision of living accommodation to which this Chapter applies,
the lease is for a term of 10 years or less, and
the net amount payable by P in relation to the lease by way of lease premium is greater than zero.
The amount so attributed is—
where—
A is the relevant period (in days),
B is the term of the lease (in days), and
C is the net amount payable by P in relation to the lease by way of lease premium.
For provision about the application of this section in relation to certain leases with break clauses, see section 105B.
For the purposes of this section the net amount payable by P in relation to a lease by way of lease premium is—
the total amount (if any) that has been paid, or is or will become payable, by P in relation to the lease by way of lease premium, less
any amount within paragraph (a) that has been repaid or is or will become repayable.
In this section and section 105B “
” means any premium payable—
under a lease, or
otherwise under the terms on which a lease is granted.
In the application of this section to Scotland “
” includes a grassum.

Title.Addition: Lease premiums in the case of leases with break clauses

Text.Addition: This section applies to a lease (“the original lease”) that contains one or more relevant break clauses.
For the purposes of this section—
” means a provision of a lease that gives a person a right to terminate it so that its term is shorter than it otherwise would be, and

a break clause contained in the original lease is “relevant” if the right to terminate the lease that it confers is capable of being exercised in such a way that the term of the original lease is 10 years or less.
For the purposes of section 105A—
the term of the original lease, and
the net amount payable by P in relation to the lease by way of lease premium,
are to be determined on the assumption that any relevant break clause is exercised in such a way that the term of the lease is as short as possible.

If a relevant break clause is not in fact exercised in such a way that the term of the original lease is as short as possible, the parties to the lease are treated for the purposes of section 105A as if they were parties to another lease (a “notional lease”) the term of which—
begins immediately after the time at which the term of the original lease would have ended, if that break clause had been so exercised, and
ends at the time mentioned in subsection (5).
The term of a notional lease ends—

at the time the term of the original lease would end, on the assumption that any relevant break clause that is exercisable only after the beginning of the term of the notional lease is exercised in such a way that the term of the original lease is as short as possible, or
if earlier, the tenth anniversary of the beginning of the term of the original lease.

For the purposes of section 105A the net amount payable by P in relation to a notional lease by way of lease premium is, in the case of a notional lease the term of which ends under paragraph (a) of subsection (5)—
the net amount that would be payable by P in relation to the original lease by way of lease premium on the assumption mentioned in that paragraph, less
any part of that amount that has already been attributed to a period in respect of a lease premium under section 105(4B)(b).

For the purposes of section 105A the net amount payable by P in relation to a notional lease by way of lease premium is, in the case of a notional lease the term of which ends under paragraph (b) of subsection (5), the relevant proportion of—
the net amount that would be payable by P in relation to the original lease by way of lease premium, on the assumption that no break clause is exercised, less
any part of that amount that has already been attributed to a period in respect of a lease premium under section 105(4B)(b).
In subsection (7) “
” means—
where—
D is the term of the notional lease (in days), and
E is the sum of—
(a) the term of the notional lease (in days), and
(b) the number of days by which the term of the original lease would exceed 10 years, on the assumption that no break clause is exercised.

P1group.Title: Cash equivalent: cost of accommodation over £75,000

P2para.Text: The cash equivalent or modified cash equivalent is calculated under this section if the cost of providing the living accommodation exceeds £75,000.
To calculate the cash equivalent—
Calculate the amount that would be the cash equivalent if section 105 applied (cash equivalent: cost of accommodation not over £75,000).
Calculate the following amount (“the additional yearly rent”)—

Para.Text: where—
ORI is the official rate of interest in force for the purposes of Chapter 7 of this Part (taxable benefits: loans) on 6th April in the tax year, and
C is the cost of providing the accommodation calculated—
(a) in accordance with section 104 (general rule for calculating cost of accommodation), or
(b) in a case where section 107 applies (special rule for calculating cost of providing accommodation), in accordance with that section instead.

P2para.Text: Calculate the rent which would have been payable for the taxable period if the property had been let to the employee at the additional yearly rent calculated under step 2.
Calculate the cash equivalent by—

P3para.Text: adding together the amounts calculated under steps 1 and 3, and
(if allowed by subsection (3)) subtracting from that total the excess rent paid by the employee.

Text.Addition: To calculate the modified cash equivalent—
apply steps 1 to 3 in subsection (2), as if the words “cash equivalent” in step 1 were “modified cash equivalent (for the purposes of section 105)”;
calculate the modified cash equivalent by adding together the amounts calculated under steps 1 and 3 as applied by paragraph (a).

P2para.Text: In step 4—

P3para.Text: paragraph (b) only applies if, in respect of the taxable period, the rent paid—

Text.Substitution: by the employee,
in respect of the accommodation,
to the person providing it, and
on or before 6 July following the tax year which contains the taxable period,

P3para.Text: exceeds the rental value of the accommodation for that period as set out in section 105(3) or (4)(b), as applicable, and
“the excess rent” means the total amount of that excess.

P1group.Title: Special rule for calculating cost of providing accommodation

P2para.Text: This section contains a special rule for calculating the cost of providing living accommodation which—

P3para.Text: operates for the purposes of step 2 of section 106(2) (calculating the additional yearly rent), and
accordingly only operates where the cost of provision for the purposes of section 106(1) (as calculated under section 104) exceeds £75,000.

P2para.Text: This section applies if, throughout the period of 6 years ending with the date when the employee first occupied the accommodation (“the initial date”), an estate or interest in the property was held by a person involved in providing the accommodation.
It does not matter whether it was the same estate, interest or person throughout.
For any tax year the cost of providing the living accommodation for the purposes mentioned in subsection (1)(a) is given by the formula—

Para.Text: where—
MV is the price which the property might reasonably be expected to have fetched on a sale in the open market with vacant possession as at the initial date,
I is any expenditure incurred on improvements to the property which has been incurred during the period—
(a) beginning with the initial date, and
(b) ending with the day before the beginning of the tax year,
by a person involved in providing the accommodation, and
P is so much of any payment or payments made by the employee to a person involved in providing the accommodation as represents—
(a) reimbursement (up to an amount not exceeding MV) of any expenditure incurred in acquiring the estate or interest in the property held on the initial date,
(b) reimbursement of I, or
(c) consideration for the grant to the employee of a tenancy or sub-tenancy of the property.

P2para.Text: In estimating MV no reduction is to be made for an option in respect of the property held by—

P3para.Text: the employee,
a person connected with the employee, or
a person involved in providing the accommodation.

P1group.Title: Cash equivalent: accommodation provided for more than one employee

P2para.Text: If, for the whole or part of a tax year, the same living accommodation is provided for more than one employee at the same time, the total of the cash equivalents for all of the employees is to be limited to the amount that would be the cash equivalent if the accommodation was provided for one employee.
The cash equivalent for each of the employees is to be such part of that amount as is just and reasonable.

P1group.Title: Priority of this Chapter over Chapter 1 of this Part

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: under this Chapter an amount is to be treated as earnings from an employee’s employment for a tax year, and
under Chapter 1 of this Part an amount would, apart from this section, constitute earnings from the employment for the year in respect of the provision of the accommodation.

P2para.Text: The full amount mentioned in subsection (1)(a) is to be treated as earnings from the employment for that year under this Chapter.

The amount mentioned in subsection (1)(b) is to constitute earnings from the employment for the year under Chapter 1 of this Part only to the extent that it exceeds the amount mentioned in subsection (2).

Text.Addition: In a case where the
is nil—
subsections (2) and (3) do not apply, and
the full amount mentioned in subsection (1)(b) constitutes earnings from the employment for the year under Chapter 1.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “annual value”

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter the “annual value” of living accommodation is the rent which might reasonably be expected to be obtained on a letting from year to year if—

P3para.Text: the tenant undertook to pay all taxes, rates and charges usually paid by a tenant, and
the landlord undertook to bear the costs of the repairs and insurance and the other expenses (if any) necessary for maintaining the property in a state to command that rent.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (1) that rent—

P3para.Text: is to be taken to be the amount that might reasonably be expected to be so obtained in respect of the letting of the accommodation, and

is to be calculated on the basis that the only amounts that may be deducted in respect of services provided by the landlord are amounts in respect of the cost to the landlord of providing any relevant services.

P2para.Text: If living accommodation is of a kind that might reasonably be expected to be let on terms under which—

P3para.Text: the landlord is to provide any services which are either—

P4para.Text: relevant services, or
the repair, insurance or maintenance of any premises which do not form part of the accommodation but belong to or are occupied by the landlord, and

P3para.Text: amounts are payable in respect of the services in addition to the rent,

P2para.Text: the rent to be established under subsection (1) in respect of the accommodation is to be increased under subsection (4).
That rent is to include—

P3para.Text: where the services are relevant services, so much of the additional amounts as exceeds the cost to the landlord of providing the services;
where the services are within subsection (3)(a)(ii), the whole of the additional amounts.

P2para.Text: In this section “relevant service” means a service other than the repair, insurance or maintenance of the accommodation or of any other premises.

P1group.Title: Disputes as to annual value

P2para.Text: This section applies if there is a dispute as to the amount of the annual value of living accommodation for the purposes of this Chapter.

Text.Substitution: An application for the tribunal to determine the question is to be subject to the relevant provisions of Part 5 of
(see, in particular, section 48(2)(b) of that Act), and each of the persons concerned is entitled to be a party to the proceedings on the application.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “person involved in providing the accommodation”

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter “person involved in providing the accommodation” means any of the following—

P3para.Text: the person providing the accommodation;
the employee’s employer (if not within paragraph (a));
any person, other than the employee, who is connected with a person within paragraph (a) or (b).

P1group.Title: Meaning of “the property”

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter “the property”, in relation to living accommodation, means the property consisting of that accommodation.

Chapter.Title: Taxable benefits: cars, vans and related benefits

P1group.Title: Cars, vans and related benefits

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to a car or a van in relation to a particular tax year if in that year the car or van—

P3para.Text: is made available (without any transfer of the property in it) to an employee or a member of the employee’s family or household,
is so made available by reason of the employment (see section 117), and
is available for the employee’s or member’s private use (see section 118).

Text.Addition: Where this Chapter applies to a car or van, the car or van is a benefit for the purposes of this Chapter (and accordingly it is immaterial whether the terms on which it is made available to the employee or member constitute a fair bargain).

P2para.Text: Where this Chapter applies to a car or van—

P3para.Text: sections 120 to 148 provide for an amount in respect of the benefit of the car to be treated as earnings,
sections 149 to 153 provide for an amount in respect of the benefit of any fuel provided for the car to be treated as earnings, ...
sections 154 to 159 provide for an amount in respect of the benefit of the van to be treated as earnings; and

Text.Addition: sections 160 to 164 provide for
the benefit of any fuel provided for the van to be treated as earnings in certain circumstances.
This Chapter does not apply to a van in relation to a tax year if the private use of the van during the tax year by the employee or member of the employee’s family or household is insignificant.

P2para.Text: The following provisions of this Chapter provide for further exceptions—

Para.Text: section 167 (pooled cars);
section 168 (pooled vans);
section 169 (car available to more than one member of family or household employed by same employer).

Text.Addition: section 169A (van available to more than one member of family or household employed by same employer).

P1group.Title: Meaning of “car” and “van”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter—

Para.Text: “car” means a mechanically propelled road vehicle which is not—
a goods vehicle,
a motor cycle,
an invalid carriage, or
a vehicle of a type not commonly used as a private vehicle and unsuitable to be so used;
“van” means a mechanically propelled road vehicle which—
is a goods vehicle, and
has a design weight not exceeding 3,500 kilograms,
and which is not a motor cycle.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (1)—

Para.Text: “design weight” means the weight which a vehicle is designed or adapted not to exceed when in normal use and travelling on a road laden;
“goods vehicle” means a vehicle of a construction primarily suited for the conveyance of goods or burden of any description;
“invalid carriage” has the meaning given by section 185(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 (c. 52);
“motor cycle” has the meaning given by section 185(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988.

P1group.Title: Meaning of when car or van is available to employee

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter a car or van is available to an employee at a particular time if it is then made available, by reason of the employment and without any transfer of the property in it, to the employee or a member of the employee’s family or household.
References in this Chapter to—

P3para.Text: the time when a car or van is first made available to an employee are to the earliest time when the car or van is made available as mentioned in subsection (1), and
the last day in a year on which a car or van is available to an employee are to the last day in the year on which the car or van is made available as mentioned in subsection (1).

P2para.Text: This section does not apply to section 124A or 138 (automatic car or van for a disabled employee).

P1group.Title: Meaning of car or van made available by reason of employment

Text.Substitution: For the purposes of this Chapter a car or van made available by an employer to an employee or member of an employee's family or household is to be regarded as made available by reason of the employment unless subsection (2)
excludes the application of this subsection.
Subsection (1) does not apply where—
the employer is an individual, and
the car or van in question is made available in the normal course of the employer's domestic, family or personal relationships.
Subsection (1) does not apply where—
the employer carries on a vehicle hire business under which cars or vans of the same kind are made available to members of the public for hire,
the car or van in question is hired to the employee or member in the normal course of that business, and
in hiring that car or van the employee or member is acting as an ordinary member of the public.

Substitution.Addition: the employer carries on a business under which cars or vans of the same kind are made available to members of the public for sale or lease,
the car or van in question is sold or leased to the employee or member in the normal course of that business, and

the terms on which the car or van is sold or leased to the employee or member might reasonably be expected to be agreed between the employer and a member of the public with whom the employer deals at arm’s length.

P1group.Title: Availability for private use

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter a car or van made available in a tax year to an employee or a member of the employee’s family or household is to be treated as available for the employee’s or member’s private use unless in that year—

P3para.Text: the terms on which it is made available prohibit such use, and
it is not so used.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “private use”, in relation to a car or van made available to an employee or a member of the employee’s family or household, means any use other than for the employee’s business travel (see section 171(1)).

P1group.Title: Where alternative to benefit of low emission car or van offered

Text.Substitution: This section applies where in a tax year—
a car is made available as mentioned in section 114(1),
the car's CO
emissions figure (see sections 133 to 138) does not exceed 75 grams per kilometre, and
an alternative to the benefit of the car is offered.

P2para.Text: The mere fact that the alternative is offered does not result in an amount in respect of the benefit constituting earnings by virtue of Chapter 1 of this Part (earnings).

P1group.Title: Benefit of car treated as earnings

P2para.Text: If this Chapter applies to a car in relation to a particular tax year, the cash equivalent of the benefit of the car is to be treated as earnings from the employment for that year.
In such a case (including a case where the cash equivalent of the benefit of the car is nil) the employee is referred to in this Chapter as being chargeable to tax in respect of the car in that year.

Text.Addition: Any reference in this Act to a case where the cash equivalent of the benefit of a car is treated as the employee's earnings for a year by virtue of this section includes a case where the cash equivalent is nil.
This section is subject to section 120A.

Title.Addition: Benefit of car treated as earnings: optional remuneration arrangements

Text.Addition: Where this Chapter applies to a car in relation to a particular tax year and the conditions in subsection (3) are met—
the relevant amount (see section 121A) is to be treated as earnings from the employment for that tax year, and
section 120(1) does not apply.
In such a case (including a case where the relevant amount is nil) the employee is referred to in this Chapter as being chargeable to tax in respect of the car in the tax year.
The conditions are that—
the car is made available to the employee or member of the employee's household pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements,

Addition.Substitution: the total foregone amount in connection with the car for the tax year is

Text.Addition: is greater than the modified cash equivalent of the benefit of the car for the tax year (see section 121B), and
the car's CO
emissions figure (see sections 133 to 138) exceeds 75 grams per kilometre.

Addition.Addition: In this section, and in section 121A, the total foregone amount in connection with the car for a tax year is the total of—
the amount foregone (see section 69B) with respect to the benefit of the car for that year, and
the amount foregone (see section 69B) with respect to each other benefit that—
