If a journey made by a member of a relevant authority is a qualifying journey and a qualifying payment is made to the member for carrying a passenger on the journey, the member's journey is not to be treated as business travel in respect of that passenger for the purposes of sections 233 and 234 unless the passenger is also a member of the authority.
A journey made by a member of a relevant authority is a “
” for the purposes of this section if—
it is a journey between the member's home and permanent workplace, and
the member's home is situated in the area of the authority, or no more than 20 miles outside the boundary of the area.
In this section “
” has the same meaning as in Part 5 (see section 339).
The Treasury may by regulations—

provide for bodies specified in the regulations (which must be local authorities or bodies that have similar or related functions or purposes) to be relevant authorities for the purposes of this section,
provide for references in this section to a member of a relevant authority to be read as references to a member of a description prescribed in the regulations, and
define what is meant by “
” for the purposes of this section.
The regulations may contain transitional provision and savings.

P1group.Title: Interpretation of this Chapter

P2para.Text: In this Chapter—

Para.Text: “business travel” means travelling the expenses of which, if incurred and paid by the employee in question, would (if this Chapter did not apply) be deductible under sections 337 to 342;
“mileage allowance payments” has the meaning given by section 229(2);
“passenger payments” has the meaning given by section 233(3).

Text.Addition: For journeys that are treated as business travel for the purposes of certain provisions of this Chapter, see section 235A (journeys made by members of local authorities
etc

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter a vehicle is a “company vehicle” in a tax year if in that year—

P3para.Text: the vehicle is made available to the employee by reason of the employment and is not available for the employee’s private use, or
an amount in respect of the benefit of the vehicle is to be treated as the employee’s earnings for the tax year by virtue of—

P4para.Text: section 120 or 120A (benefit of car treated as earnings),
section 154 or 154A (benefit of van treated as earnings), or
section 203 or 203A (residual liability to charge: benefit treated as earnings), or

P3para.Text: in the case of a car or van, an amount in respect of the benefit of the car or van would be required to be so treated if sections 167 and 168 (exceptions for pooled cars and vans) and section 248A (emergency vehicles) did not apply, or

in the case of a cycle, the cash equivalent of the benefit of the cycle would be required to be treated as the employee’s earnings for the tax year under Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) if section 244(1) (exception for cycles made available) did not apply.

P2para.Text: Sections 117 and 118 (when cars and vans are made available by reason of employment and are made available for private use) apply for the purposes of subsection (2).

Chapter.Title: Exemptions: other transport, travel and subsistence

P1group.Title: Parking provision and expenses

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision of workplace parking for an employee.
No liability to income tax arises by virtue of the payment or reimbursement of expenses incurred in connection with the provision for or the use by an employee of workplace parking.
In this section “workplace parking” means—

P3para.Text: a parking space for a car or van,
a motor cycle parking space, or
facilities for parking a cycle other than a motor cycle,

P2para.Text: at or near the employee’s workplace.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision, at or near an employee's workplace, of facilities for charging a battery of a vehicle used by the employee (including a vehicle used by the employee as a passenger).
Subsection (1) applies only if the facilities are made available generally to the employer's employees at that workplace.
In this section—
“facilities”—
includes electricity, but
does not include workplace parking,
”, in relation to a car or van, has the meaning given by section 239(6),
” means a vehicle—
to which Chapter 2 applies (see section 235), and
which is neither a taxable car nor a taxable van, and
” has the meaning given by section 237(3).

P1group.Title: Modest private use of heavy goods vehicles

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises where a heavy goods vehicle is made available to an employee for the employee’s private use if conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that there is no transfer of the property in the vehicle to the employee.
Condition B is that the employee’s use of the vehicle in the tax year is not wholly or mainly private use.
In this section—

Para.Text: “heavy goods vehicle” means a mechanically propelled road vehicle which—
is of a construction primarily suited for the conveyance of goods or burden of any kind, and
is designed or adapted to have a maximum weight exceeding 3,500 kilograms when in normal use and travelling on a road laden, and
“private use” means use other than for travel which the employee is necessarily obliged to do in the performance of the duties of the employment.

P1group.Title: Payments and benefits connected with taxable cars and vans and exempt heavy goods vehicles

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the discharge of any liability of an employee in connection with a taxable car or van or an exempt heavy goods vehicle.
No liability to income tax arises in respect of a payment to an employee in respect of expenses incurred by the employee in connection with a taxable car or van or an exempt heavy goods vehicle.

Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply to liability arising by virtue of section 120A (optional remuneration arrangements: benefit of a car), section 149 or 149A (benefit of car fuel treated as earnings) , section 154A (optional remuneration arrangements: benefit of a van) or section 160 or 160A (benefit of van fuel treated as earnings).

No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of a benefit connected with a taxable car or van or an exempt heavy goods vehicle.
Subsection (4) does not apply to the provision of a driver.

For the purposes of this section a car or van is “taxable” if under Chapter 6 of Part 3 an amount (whether the cash equivalent or the relevant amount) in respect of the benefit of it is to be treated as the employee’s earnings for the tax year.
For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: “heavy goods vehicle” has the same meaning as in section 238(4) (modest private use of heavy goods vehicles), and
a heavy goods vehicle is “exempt” if it is made available in the tax year to the employee in such circumstances that section 238 applies.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2), a heavy goods vehicle is also “exempt” if it is so made available in such circumstances that section 238 would apply if the employee were not in lower-paid employment as a minister of religion (see section 290D).

P1group.Title: Incidental overnight expenses and benefits

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a sum if or to the extent that it is paid wholly and exclusively for the purpose of paying or reimbursing expenses which—

P3para.Text: are incidental to the employee’s absence from the place where the employee normally lives,
relate to a continuous period of such absence in relation to which the overnight stay conditions are met (a “qualifying period”), and
would not be deductible under Part 5 if the employee incurred and paid them and Chapter 2 of this Part (mileage allowances and passenger payments) did not apply.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of a benefit provided for an employee if—

P3para.Text: its provision is incidental to such an absence during a qualifying period, and
no amount would be deductible in respect of it under Part 5.

P2para.Text: Subsections (1) and (2) are subject to section 241 (incidental overnight expenses and benefits: overall exemption limit).
The overnight stay conditions are that—

P3para.Text: the employee is obliged to stay away from the place where the employee normally lives throughout the period,
the period includes at least one overnight stay away from that place, and
each such overnight stay during the period is at a place the expenses of travelling to which meet condition A or B.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the expenses are deductible under Part 5 (otherwise than under any of the excepted foreign travel provisions) or would be if the employee incurred and paid them and Chapter 2 of this Part did not apply.
Condition B is that the expenses are within section 250 or 255 (exemption of work-related and individual learning account training provision) or would be if the employer paid or reimbursed them.
In this section “excepted foreign travel provisions” means—

P3para.Text: section 371 (travel costs and expenses where duties performed abroad: visiting spouse’s civil partner's or child’s travel),
section 374 (non-domiciled employee’s spouse’s civil partner's or child’s travel costs and expenses where duties performed in UK), and
section 376 (foreign accommodation and subsistence costs and expenses (overseas employments)).

P1group.Title: Incidental overnight expenses and benefits: overall exemption limit

P2para.Text: Section 240(1) and (2) do not apply if the exemption provisions total in respect of the qualifying period in question exceeds the permitted amount.
In this section “the exemption provisions total”, in respect of a period, means the aggregate of—

P3para.Text: the amounts that would be exempted under section 240(1) and (2) in respect of the period, apart from this section, and
the amounts that would be exempted under section 268 (exemption of vouchers and tokens for incidental overnight expenses) in respect of the period, apart from the condition in section 268(5).

P2para.Text: In this section “the permitted amount”, in respect of a period, means the aggregate of the following amounts—

P3para.Text: £5 for each night during the period spent wholly in the United Kingdom, and
£10 for each night during the period spent wholly or partly outside the United Kingdom.

Title.Addition: Travel by unpaid directors of not-for-profit companies

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a sum if or to the extent that it is paid wholly and exclusively for the purpose of paying or reimbursing travel expenses in respect of which conditions A to C are met.
Condition A is that—
the employee is obliged to incur the expenses as holder of the employment, and
the expenses are attributable to the employee’s necessary attendance at any place in the performance of the duties of the employment.
Condition B is that the employment is employment as a director of a not-for-profit company.
Condition C is that the employment is one from which the employee receives no employment income other than sums to which Chapter 3 of Part 3 applies (expenses payments).
In this section—
“director” has the same meaning as in the benefits code (see section 67), and
“not-for-profit company” means a company that does not carry on activities for the purpose of making profits for distribution to its members or others.

Title.Addition: Travel where directorship held as part of trade or profession

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a sum if or to the extent that it is paid wholly and exclusively for the purpose of paying or reimbursing travel expenses in respect of which conditions A to D are met.
Condition A is that the employee is obliged to incur the expenses as holder of the employment.
Condition B is that the employment is employment as a director of a company.
Condition C is that the employee carries on a trade, profession or vocation (alone or in partnership).
Condition D is that, in calculating the profits of that trade, profession or vocation for income tax purposes, a deduction is allowed under
ITTOIA
2005 for the expenses, but no such deduction is to be made.
In this section “director” has the same meaning as in the benefits code (see section 67).

P1group.Title: Works transport services

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision for employees of a works transport service if—

P3para.Text: the service is available generally to employees of the employer (or each employer) concerned,
the main use of the service is for qualifying journeys by those employees, and
the service—

P4para.Text: is used only by the employees for whom it is provided or their children, or
is substantially used only by those employees or children.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “children” includes stepchildren and illegitimate children but does not include children aged 18 or over, and
“works transport service” means a service which is provided by means of a bus or a minibus for conveying employees of one or more employers on qualifying journeys.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: “bus” means a road passenger vehicle which has a seating capacity of 12 or more, and
“minibus” means a vehicle constructed or adapted for the carriage of passengers which has a seating capacity of 9, 10 or 11.

P2para.Text: But a vehicle which falls within the definition in subsection (3)(b) is not a minibus for the purposes of this section if—

P3para.Text: it has one or more disqualified seats, and
excluding the disqualified seats, it has a seating capacity of 8 or less.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsections (3) and (4) the seating capacity of a vehicle is determined in the same way as for the purposes of Part 3 of Schedule 1 to VERA 1994 (vehicle excise duty on buses).
This applies whether or not the vehicle is a bus within the meaning of that Part of that Schedule.
For the purposes of subsection (4) a seat is disqualified if relevant construction and use requirements are not met in relation to it.

In this subsection “construction and use requirements” has the same meaning as in Part 2 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 (c. 52) or, in Northern Ireland, Part III of the Road Traffic (Northern Ireland) Order 1995 (S.I. 1995/2994 (N.I. 18)).

P1group.Title: Support for public bus services

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision of financial or other support for a public transport road service if—

P3para.Text: in the case of a local bus service, conditions A and B are met, or
in any other case, conditions A to C are met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the service is used by employees of one or more employers for qualifying journeys.
Condition B is that the service is available generally to employees of the employer (or each employer) concerned.
Condition C is that the terms on which the service is available to the employees of the employer (or each employer) concerned are not more favourable than those available to other passengers.
In this section—

Para.Text: “local bus service” means a local service (as defined in section 2 of the Transport Act 1985 (c. 67)), and
“public transport road service” means a public passenger transport service provided by means of a road vehicle.

P1group.Title: Cycles and cyclist’s safety equipment

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision for an employee of a cycle or cyclist’s safety equipment if conditions A to C are met.
Condition A is that there is no transfer of the property in the cycle or equipment in question.
Condition B is that the employee uses the cycle or equipment in question mainly for qualifying journeys.
Condition C is that cycles are available generally to employees of the employer concerned or, as the case may be, cyclist’s safety equipment is so available to them.
In this section “cycle” has the meaning given by section 192(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 (c. 52), and “cyclist” has a corresponding meaning.

P1group.Title: Travelling and subsistence during public transport strikes

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the following benefits and payments where a strike or other industrial action disrupts a public transport service normally used by an employee.
They are—

P3para.Text: the provision for the employee of overnight accommodation at or near the employee’s permanent workplace,
a payment to the employee in respect of expenses incurred by the employee in connection with such accommodation,
the provision for the employee of transport for the purpose of ordinary commuting or travel between any two places that is for practical purposes substantially ordinary commuting, and
a payment to the employee in respect of expenses incurred on such transport.

P1group.Title: Transport between work and home for disabled employees: general

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of—

P3para.Text: the provision of transport for a disabled employee, or
the payment or reimbursement of expenses incurred on such transport,

P2para.Text: if the condition in subsection (2) is met.

The condition is that the transport is provided or the expenses are incurred for the purpose of ordinary commuting or travel between any two places that is for practical purposes substantially ordinary commuting.
Subsection (1) does not apply in a case where a car is made available to a disabled employee (but see section 247).

In this section “disabled employee” means an employee who has a physical or mental impairment with a substantial and long-term adverse effect on the employee’s ability to carry out normal day to day activities.

P1group.Title: Provision of cars for disabled employees

P2para.Text: This section applies where a car is made available to a disabled employee without any transfer of the property in it.
No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 6 or 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: cars, vans etc. and residual liability to charge) in respect of the benefit if conditions A to C are met.
No liability to income tax arises in respect of—

P3para.Text: the provision of fuel for the car, or
the payment or reimbursement of expenses incurred in connection with it,

P2para.Text: if conditions A to C are met.

Condition A is that the car has been adapted for the employee’s special needs or, in the case of an employee who because of disability can only drive a car that has automatic transmission, it is such a car.
Condition B is that the car is made available on terms prohibiting its use otherwise than for—

P3para.Text: the employee’s business travel, or
transport for the employee for the purpose of—

P4para.Text: ordinary commuting or travel between any two places that is for practical purposes substantially ordinary commuting, or
travel to a place the expenses of travelling to which would be within one of the training exemption provisions if the employer paid them.

P2para.Text: Condition C is that in the tax year the car is only used in accordance with those terms.
In this section—

Para.Text: “business travel” has the same meaning as in Chapter 6 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: cars, vans and related benefits) (see section 171(1)),
“disabled employee” has the same meaning as in section 246 (see subsection (4)), and
“the training exemption provisions” means—
section 250 (exemption of work-related training provision),
section 255 (exemption for contributions to individual learning account training), and
section 311 (retraining courses).

P2para.Text: Section 138(4) (when a car has automatic transmission) applies for the purposes of this section as it applies for the purposes of section 138.

P1group.Title: Transport home: late night working and failure of car-sharing arrangements

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision of transport or the payment or reimbursement of expenses incurred on transport if—

P3para.Text: the transport is for a journey from the employee’s workplace to the employee’s home,
the late working conditions or the car-sharing failure conditions are met, and
the number of previous occasions in the tax year on which the provision of transport within this section or the payment or reimbursement of expenses within this section has occurred is lower than 60.

P2para.Text: The late working conditions are that—

P3para.Text: the journey is made on an occasion when the employee is required to work later than usual and until at least 9 p.m.,
such occasions occur irregularly,
by the time when the employee ceases work—

P4para.Text: public transport has ceased to be available for the journey, or
it would not be reasonable to expect the employee to use it, and

P3para.Text: the transport is by taxi or similar private road transport.

P2para.Text: The car-sharing failure conditions are that—

P3para.Text: the employee regularly travels to work in a car with one or more other employees of the employee’s employer under arrangements for the sharing of the car with them, and
the journey is made on an occasion when the employee is unable to use the car because of unforeseen and exceptional circumstances.

Text.Addition: This section applies where—
an emergency vehicle is made available to a person employed in an emergency service

Addition.Substitution: mainly for use for the person's business travel

Text.Addition: the terms on which it is made available prohibit its private use otherwise than when the person is on call or
... commuting, and
the person does not make private use of it otherwise than in such circumstances.
No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 6 or 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: cars, vans
etc.
and residual liability to charge) in respect of the benefit.
” means a vehicle which is used to respond to emergencies and which either—
has fixed to it a lamp designed to emit a flashing light for use in emergencies, or

would have such a lamp fixed to it but for the fact that (if it did) a special threat to the personal physical security of those using it would arise by reason of it being apparent that they were employed in an emergency service.
The following are “
constables and other persons employed for police purposes,
persons employed for the purposes of a fire, or fire and rescue, service, and
persons employed in the provision of ambulance or paramedic services.
The Treasury may by order amend subsection (4).
”, in relation to a person, means any use other than for the person’s business travel; and “
” has the same meaning as in Chapter 6 of Part 3 (see section 171(1)).
A person to whom an emergency vehicle is made available is on call when liable, as part of normal duties, to be called on to use the emergency vehicle to respond to emergencies.
A person to whom an emergency vehicle is made available is
... commuting when the person—
is using
for ordinary commuting or for travel between two places that is for practical purposes substantially ordinary commuting, and

P1group.Title: Interpretation of this Chapter

P1para.Text: In this Chapter—

Para.Text: “car” and “van” have the same meaning as in Chapter 6 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: cars, vans and related benefits) (see section 115), except that for the purposes of sections 246 and 247 (transport for the disabled) any adaptation of a car for the employee’s special needs is to be disregarded,
“ordinary commuting” has the same meaning as in section 338 (travel for necessary attendance) (see subsection (3)),
“qualifying journey”, in relation to an employee, means the whole or part of a journey—
between the employee’s home and workplace,
between one workplace and another,
in connection with the performance of the duties of the employment, and
“workplace” and “permanent workplace” have the meaning given by section 339.

P1group.Title: Exemption of work-related training provision

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of—

P3para.Text: the provision for an employee of work-related training or any benefit incidental to such training, or
the payment or reimbursement to or in respect of an employee of—

P4para.Text: the cost of work-related training or of any benefit incidental to such training, or
any costs of a kind specified in subsection (2) in respect of such training.

P2para.Text: The costs are—

P3para.Text: costs which are incidental to the employee undertaking the training,
expenses incurred in connection with an examination or other assessment of what the employee has gained from the training, and
the cost of obtaining any qualification, registration or award to which the employee becomes or may become entitled as a result of the training or such an examination or other assessment.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “work-related training”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “work-related training”, in relation to an employee, means a training course or other activity designed to impart, instil, improve or reinforce any knowledge, skills or personal qualities which—

P3para.Text: are likely to prove useful to the employee when performing the duties of the employment or a related employment, or
will qualify or better qualify the employee—

P4para.Text: to perform those duties, or
to participate in any charitable or voluntary activities that are available to be performed in association with the employment or a related employment.

P2para.Text: For this purpose “related employment”, in relation to an employee, means another employment with the same employer, or with a person connected with the employer, which the employee—

P3para.Text: is to hold,
has a serious opportunity of holding, or
can realistically expect to have a serious opportunity of holding in due course.

P1group.Title: Exception for non-deductible travel expenses

P2para.Text: Where travel or subsistence is provided or the costs of travel or subsistence are paid or reimbursed, section 250 does not apply except to the extent that the travel meets condition A or B or the subsistence meets condition B.
Condition A is that, on the assumptions in subsection (4), mileage allowance relief under Chapter 2 of this Part would be available for the travel if no mileage allowance payments had been made.
Condition B is that, on those assumptions, the expenses of the travel or subsistence would be deductible under Part 5.
The assumptions are—

P3para.Text: that the employee undertook the training as one of the duties of the employment, and
that the employee incurred and paid the expenses.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “mileage allowance payments” has the meaning given by section 229(2), and
“subsistence” includes food, drink and temporary living accommodation.

P1group.Title: Exception where provision for excluded purposes

P2para.Text: Section 250 does not apply if or to the extent that the facilities or other benefits that are provided or the costs of which are paid or reimbursed are provided to the employee for one or more of the following purposes.
They are—

P3para.Text: enabling the employee to enjoy the facilities or benefits for entertainment or recreational purposes which are unconnected,
providing the employee with an unconnected inducement to remain in or accept an employment with the employer or a person connected with the employer, and
rewarding the employee for performing duties of the employment or performing them in a particular way.

P2para.Text: In subsection (2)(a) the reference to enjoying facilities or benefits for entertainment or recreational purposes includes a reference to enjoying them in the course of a leisure activity.
In subsection (2)(a) and (b) “unconnected” means unconnected with imparting, instilling, improving or reinforcing knowledge, skills or personal qualities within section 251(1).

P1group.Title: Exception where unrelated assets are provided

P2para.Text: Section 250 does not apply if the benefit that is provided or the cost of which is paid or reimbursed is, or is the use of, an asset that is not a training-related asset.
“Training-related asset”, in relation to work-related training provided to an employee, means—

P3para.Text: an asset provided for use only—

P4para.Text: in the course of the training, or
in the course of the training and in the performance of the duties of the employee’s employment,

P3para.Text: training materials provided in the course of the training, or
something made by the employee in the course of the training or incorporated into something so made.

P2para.Text: For this purpose, “training materials” includes stationery, books or other written material, audio or video tapes, compact disks or floppy disks.

Title.Addition: Apprenticeship bursaries paid to persons leaving local authority care

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a care leaver's apprenticeship bursary payment.
A care leaver's apprenticeship bursary payment is a payment—
payable out of the public revenue,
to a care leaver (see subsection (3)),
made in connection with the person's employment as an apprentice (see subsection (4)), and
in respect of which any conditions specified in regulations made by the Treasury are met.
A person is a care leaver if they are a person—
who is, or was, a child looked after—
by a local authority in England within the meaning of section 22 of the Children Act 1989 (general duty of local authority in relation to children looked after by them);

by a local authority in Wales within the meaning of the Social Services and Well-being (Wales) Act 2014 (anaw 4) (see section 74 of that Act (child or young person looked after by a local authority));
by a local authority in Scotland within the meaning of Chapter 1 of Part 2 of the Children (Scotland) Act 1995 (see section 17(6) of that Act (duty of local authority to child looked after by them));

by an authority in Northern Ireland within the meaning of the Children (Northern Ireland) Order 1995 (S.I. 1995/755 (N.I. 2)) (see Article 25 of that Order (children looked after by an authority: interpretation)), and
in respect of whom any other conditions specified in regulations made by the Treasury are met.
” has the meaning specified in regulations made by the Treasury.
Regulations under this section—
may make provision framed by reference to a scheme (however described or named), or document, as it has effect from time to time,
may make different provision for different purposes,
may make different provision for different areas, and
may make retrospective provision.

P1group.Title: Exemption for contributions to individual learning account training

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax in respect of income from a current or former employment arises by virtue of—

P3para.Text: the provision to a person within subsection (2) (“the employee”) of individual learning account training that is given by a person who is not the employee’s employer or former employer,
any payment to the person giving the training in respect of the cost of that provision,
the provision to the employee of any benefit incidental to such training, or
the payment or reimbursement of any costs in respect of such training of a kind specified in subsection (3).

P2para.Text: A person is within this subsection if the person either—

P3para.Text: holds an account that qualifies under section 104 of the Learning and Skills Act 2000 (c. 21), or
is a party to arrangements that qualify under section 105 or 106 of that Act or section 2 of the Education and Training (Scotland) Act 2000 (asp. 8).

P2para.Text: The costs are—

P3para.Text: costs which are incidental to the employee undertaking the training,
expenses incurred in connection with an examination or other assessment of what the employee has gained from the training, and
the cost of obtaining any qualification, registration or award to which the employee becomes or may become entitled as a result of the training or such an examination or other assessment.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “individual learning account training”

P1para.Text: In this Chapter “individual learning account training” means training or education of a kind that qualifies for grants authorised by—

P3para.Text: regulations under section 108 or 109 of the Learning and Skills Act 2000 (c. 21), or
regulations under section 1 of the Education and Training (Scotland) Act 2000.

P1group.Title: Exception for non-deductible travel expenses

P2para.Text: Where travel or subsistence is provided or the costs of travel or subsistence are paid or reimbursed, section 255 does not apply except to the extent that the travel meets condition A or B or the subsistence meets condition B.
Condition A is that, on the assumptions in subsection (4), mileage allowance relief under Chapter 2 of this Part would be available for the travel if no mileage allowance payments had been made.
Condition B is that, on those assumptions, the expenses of the travel or subsistence would be deductible under Part 5.
The assumptions are—

P3para.Text: that the employee undertook the training as one of the duties of the employment, and
that the employee incurred and paid the expenses.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “mileage allowance payments” has the meaning given by section 229(2), and
“subsistence” includes food, drink and temporary living accommodation.

P1group.Title: Exception where provision for excluded purposes

P2para.Text: Section 255 does not apply if or to the extent that the facilities or other benefits that are provided or made available, or the costs of which are paid or reimbursed, are provided or made available for either or both of the following purposes.
They are—

P3para.Text: enabling the employee or former employee to enjoy the facilities or benefits for entertainment or recreational purposes, and
rewarding the employee or former employee for performing duties of the employment or former employment or performing them in a particular way.

P2para.Text: In subsection (2)(a) the reference to enjoying facilities or benefits for entertainment or recreational purposes includes a reference to enjoying them in the course of a leisure activity.

P1group.Title: Exception where unrelated assets are provided

P2para.Text: Section 255 does not apply if the benefit that is provided, or the use of which is provided, or the cost of which is paid or reimbursed is an asset that is not a training-related asset.
“Training-related asset”, in relation to individual learning account training provided to an employee or former employee, means—

P3para.Text: an asset provided—

P4para.Text: for use only in the course of the training, or
for use in the course of the training and in the performance of the duties of the employee’s employment, but not to any significant extent for any other use, or

P3para.Text: training materials provided in the course of the training, or
something made by the employee or former employee in the course of the training or incorporated into something so made.

P2para.Text: For this purpose “training materials” includes stationery, books or other written material, audio or video tapes, compact disks or floppy disks.

P1group.Title: Exception where training not generally available to staff

P2para.Text: Section 255(1) only applies if any expenditure involved in making the provision, the payment or the reimbursement is incurred in giving effect to existing arrangements providing—

P3para.Text: for the person incurring it to contribute to costs arising from the undertaking of individual learning account training by the employer’s employees or former employees, and
for such contributions to be generally available, on similar terms, to the employer’s employees at that time.

P2para.Text: In subsection (1) “existing arrangements” means arrangements in place when the agreement to incur the expenditure was made.
The Treasury may by regulations make provision specifying the persons or other entities under whom Crown servants are to be treated for the purposes of this section as holding employment.
Such regulations may—

P3para.Text: treat a description of Crown servants (or two or more such descriptions taken together) as an entity for the purposes of the regulations, and
make different provision for different descriptions of Crown servants.

P2para.Text: In this section “Crown servant” means a person holding an employment under the Crown.

P1group.Title: Exemption of recreational benefits

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision to an employee or a member of an employee’s family or household of benefits within subsection (2).
The benefits are—

P3para.Text: sporting or other recreational facilities which meet conditions A to C, and
a right or opportunity to make use of such facilities.
This is subject to section 262.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the facilities are available generally to the employees of the employer in question.
Condition B is that they are not available to members of the public generally.
Condition C is that they are used wholly or mainly by persons whose right or opportunity to use them is employment-related (whether or not by reference to the same employer).
A person’s right or opportunity to use facilities is “employment-related” if and only if—

P3para.Text: it derives from the person being—

P4para.Text: an employee or former employee, or
a member or former member of the family or household of an employee or former employee,

P3para.Text: of a particular employer, and
the facilities are provided so as to be available generally to that employer’s employees.

P1group.Title: Benefits not exempted by section 261

P2para.Text: Section 261 (exemption of recreational benefits) does not apply to the following benefits—

P3para.Text: an interest in or the use of any of the following—

P4para.Text: a mechanically propelled vehicle,
holiday or other overnight accommodation, or
facilities which include, or are provided in association with, a right or opportunity to make use of holiday or overnight accommodation,

P3para.Text: facilities provided on domestic premises, or
a right or opportunity to make use of facilities within paragraph (a) or (b).

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “domestic premises” means—
premises used wholly or mainly as a private dwelling, or
land or other premises belonging to, or enjoyed with, premises so used, and
“vehicle” includes a ship, boat or other vessel, an aircraft and a hovercraft.

P1group.Title: Power to alter benefits to which section 261 applies

P1para.Text: The Treasury may by regulations provide that section 261—

P3para.Text: does not apply to a benefit specified in the regulations,
applies to a benefit so specified only where such conditions as the regulations specify are met in relation to the terms on which, and the persons to whom, it is provided, or
applies in such cases as are so specified to—

P4para.Text: facilities that do not meet the conditions in section 261(3) to (5), or
a benefit within section 262.

P1group.Title: Annual parties and functions

P2para.Text: This section applies to an annual party or similar annual function provided for an employer’s employees and available to them generally or available generally to those at a particular location.

Where in the tax year only one annual party or similar annual function to which this section applies is provided for the employer’s employees, or the employees in question, no liability to income tax arises in respect of its provision if the cost per head of the party or function does not exceed £150.

Where in the tax year two or more such parties or functions are so provided, no liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision of one or more of them (“the exempt party or parties”) if the cost per head of the exempt party or parties does not exceed £150 or £150 in aggregate.
For the purposes of this section, the cost per head of a party or function is the total cost of providing—

P3para.Text: the party or function, and
any transport or accommodation incidentally provided for persons attending it (whether or not they are the employer’s employees),

P2para.Text: divided by the number of those persons.
That total cost includes any value added tax on the expenses incurred in providing the party, function, transport or accommodation.

P1group.Title: Third party entertainment

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision of entertainment for an employee or a member of the employee’s family or household if conditions A to C are met.
Condition A is that the person providing the entertainment is not the employer or a person connected with the employer.
Condition B is that neither the employer nor a person connected with the employer has directly or indirectly procured its provision.
Condition C is that it is not provided—

P3para.Text: in recognition of particular services performed by the employee in the course of the employment, or
in anticipation of particular services to be so performed.

P2para.Text: In this section “entertainment” includes hospitality of any kind.

Title.Emphasis: General exemptions: use for exempt benefits

P1group.Title: Exemption of non-cash vouchers for exempt benefits

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) in respect of a non-cash voucher if or to the extent that the voucher is used to obtain anything the direct provision of which would fall within—

P3para.Text: section 237(1) (parking provision),
section 246 (transport between home and work for disabled employees: general),
section 247 (provision of cars for disabled employees),
section 248 (transport home: late night working and failure of car-sharing arrangements), ...
section 265 (third party entertainment), or

Text.Addition: section 320C (recommended medical treatment);

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) in respect of a non-cash voucher if the voucher evidences the employee’s entitlement to use anything the direct provision of which would fall within—

P3para.Text: section 242 (works transport services),
section 243 (support for public bus services), ...
section 244 (cycles and cyclist’s safety equipment), or

Text.Addition: section 319 (mobile telephones).

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) in respect of a non-cash voucher if the voucher can only be used to obtain anything the direct provision of which would fall within—

P3para.Text: section 245 (travelling and subsistence during public transport strikes),
section 261 (exemption of recreational benefits),
section 264 (annual parties and functions),
section 296 (armed forces' leave travel facilities), ...
section 317 (subsidised meals) , ...

Text.Addition: section 320A (eye tests and special corrective appliances)
section 320B (health screening and medical check-ups)
, or
section 320D (flu vaccinations).

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) in respect of a non-cash voucher if the voucher evidences the employee’s entitlement to a benefit in respect of which no charge arises by virtue of Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) because of regulations under section 210 (power to exempt minor benefits).
For the purposes of this section direct provision is taken to fall within a section if it would do so if the employee were not in lower-paid employment as a minister of religion.

P1group.Title: Exemption of credit-tokens used for exempt benefits

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) in respect of a credit-token if or to the extent that the token is used to obtain anything the direct provision of which—

P3para.Text: would fall within one of the provisions specified in subsection (2), or
would do so if the employee were not in lower-paid employment as a minister of religion.

P2para.Text: Those provisions are—

P3para.Text: section 237(1) (parking provision),
section 245 (travelling and subsistence during public transport strikes),
section 246 (transport between home and work for disabled employees: general),
section 247 (provision of cars for disabled employees),
section 248 (transport home: late night working and failure of car-sharing arrangements), ...
section 265 (third party entertainment).
section 319 (mobile telephones). , ...

Text.Addition: section 320A (eye tests and special corrective appliances)
section 320B (health screening and medical check-ups)
, and
section 320D (flu vaccinations).

Title.Emphasis: Exemptions for particular non-cash vouchers and credit-tokens

P1group.Title: Exemption of vouchers and tokens for incidental overnight expenses

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) in respect of a non-cash voucher or a credit-token if or to the extent that the voucher or token is used by an employee to obtain goods, services or money if conditions A to C are met.
In the case of goods or services, condition A is that—

P3para.Text: obtaining them is incidental to the employee’s absence from the place where the employee normally lives, and
that absence is for a continuous period in relation to which the overnight stay conditions are met (“the qualifying period”).

P2para.Text: In the case of money, condition A is that—

P3para.Text: it is obtained for the purpose of obtaining goods or services, and
obtaining them is incidental to such an absence during such a period.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that an amount would not be deductible under section 362 or 363 (deductions where non-cash voucher or credit-token provided) in respect of the cost of obtaining the goods or services.
Condition C is that the exemption provisions total in respect of the qualifying period does not exceed the permitted amount.
In this section—

Para.Text: “the overnight stay conditions” has the same meaning as in section 240 (exemption of incidental overnight expenses and benefits) (see section 240(4)), and
“the exemption provisions total” and “the permitted amount” have the same meaning as in section 241 (incidental overnight expenses and benefits: overall exemption limit) (see section 241(2) and (3)).

P1group.Title: Exemption where benefits or money obtained in connection with taxable car or van or exempt heavy goods vehicle

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) in respect of a non-cash voucher or a credit-token if or to the extent that the voucher or token is used by the employee or a member of the employee’s family for obtaining—

P3para.Text: goods or services in connection with a taxable car or van or an exempt heavy goods vehicle, or
money which is spent on such goods or services.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) applies where the goods in question are fuel for a car, or van, but see section 149(3) or section 160(3) (by virtue of which such use of a voucher or token is treated as the provision of the fuel for the purposes of section 149 (benefit of car fuel treated as earnings) or section 160 (benefit of van fuel treated as earnings)).
For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: “car” and “van” have the meaning given by section 115, and

a car or van is “taxable” if the cash equivalent of the benefit of it is treated as the employee’s earnings for the tax year in which the voucher or token is used under Chapter 6 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: cars, vans and related benefits).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: “heavy goods vehicle” has the same meaning as in section 238 (modest private use of heavy goods vehicles), and

a heavy goods vehicle is “exempt” if it is made available in the tax year to the employee in such circumstances that section 238 applies or would apply if the employee were not in lower-paid employment as a minister of religion.

P1group.Title: Exemption for small gifts of vouchers and tokens from third parties

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) in respect of a non-cash voucher or a credit-token if conditions A to C are met.
Condition A is that the voucher or token is provided as a gift.
Condition B is that it is only capable of being used to obtain goods.
Condition C is that it meets conditions A to C and E in section 324 (general exemption of small gifts from third parties).

Title.Addition: Limited exemption for qualifying childcare vouchers

Text.Addition: If qualifying childcare vouchers are provided for an

Addition.Substitution: no liability to income tax arises by virtue of section 62 (general definition of earnings), and

liability to income tax by virtue of Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit tokens) arises only in respect of so much of the cash equivalent of the benefit as exceeds the exempt amount.

Addition.Addition: For the meaning of “eligible employee”, see section 270AA.

Text.Addition: A “
” means a non-cash voucher in relation to which Conditions A to
are met.
Condition A is that the voucher is provided to enable an employee to obtain care for a child who—
is a child or stepchild of the employee and is maintained (wholly or partly) at the employee’s expense, or
is resident with the employee and is a person in respect of whom the employee has parental responsibility.
Condition B is that the voucher can only be used to obtain qualifying child care.
Condition C is that the vouchers are provided under a scheme that is open—
to the employer’s
employees generally, or
generally to those at a particular location.

Addition.Addition: Where the scheme under which the vouchers are provided involves—
Condition C is not prevented from being met by reason only that the scheme is not open to relevant low-paid employees.

” means arrangements (whenever made) under which the employees for whom the vouchers are provided give up the right to receive an amount of general earnings or specific employment income in return for the provision of the vouchers;

” means arrangements (whenever made) under which the employees for whom the vouchers are provided agree with the employer that they are to be provided with the vouchers rather than receive some other description of employment income;

” means any of the employer's employees who are remunerated by the employer at a rate such that, if the relevant salary sacrifice arrangements or relevant flexible remuneration arrangements applied to them, the rate at which they would then be so remunerated would be likely to be lower than the national minimum wage.

Condition D is that the employer has, at the required time, made an estimate of the employee's relevant earnings amount for the tax year in respect of which the voucher is provided (see section 270B).

Text.Addition: For the purposes of this section the “exempt amount”, in any tax year, is

Addition.Substitution: for each qualifying week in that year, and
the voucher administration costs for that year.

Addition.Addition: In subsection (6)(a) “the appropriate amount”, in the case of an employee, means—
if the relevant earnings amount in the case of the employee for the tax year, as estimated in accordance with subsection (5C), exceeds the higher rate limit for the tax year,

if the relevant earnings amount in the case of the employee for the tax year, as so estimated, exceeds the basic rate limit for the tax year but does not exceed the higher rate limit for the tax year, £28, and
” for any tax year in respect of which qualifying childcare vouchers are provided for an employee means the difference between the cost of provision of the vouchers and their face value.
The face value of a voucher is the amount stated on or recorded in the voucher as the value of the provision of care for a child that may be obtained by using it.

Text.Addition: A “
” means a tax week in respect of which a qualifying childcare voucher is received.
A “

” means one of the successive periods in a tax year beginning with the first day of that year and every seventh day after that (so that the last day of a tax year or, in the case of a tax year ending in a leap year, the last two days is treated as a separate week).
An employee is only entitled to one exempt amount even if care is provided for more than one child.
But it does not matter that another person may also be entitled to an exempt amount in respect of the same child.
An employee is not entitled to an exempt amount under this section and under section 318A (limited exemption for employer-contracted childcare) in respect of the same tax week.
In this section “
” and “
” have the same meaning as in section 318A (see sections 318B and 318C).

Addition.Addition: ”, in relation to a childcare voucher, has the meaning given in section 87(3) and (3A).

Text.Addition: The powers conferred by section 318D (childcare: power to vary
and qualifying conditions) are exercisable—
in relation to the
specified in subsection
as in relation to the
specified in section
, and
in relation to the qualifying conditions for the exemption conferred by this section as in relation to the qualifying conditions for the exemption conferred by section 318A.
An employee is an eligible employee for the purposes of section 270A if conditions A to C are met in relation to the employee.
Condition A is that the employee—
was employed by the employer immediately before the relevant day, and
has not ceased to be employed by the employer on or after that day.
” means the day specified by the Treasury in regulations for the purposes of this section.
Condition B is that there has not been a period of 52 tax weeks ending on or after the relevant day which has not included at least one qualifying week.
In subsection (4)—
” means a tax week in respect of which a qualifying childcare voucher has been provided for the employee under the scheme by the employer in respect of a child, and
” has the meaning given by section 270A(7).
Condition C is that the employee has not given the employer a childcare account notice.

A “childcare account notice” is a written notice informing the employer that the employee wishes to leave the scheme in order to be able to open a childcare account under section 17 of the Childcare Payments Act 2014 or enable the employee's partner to do so.
In subsection (7) “
” is to be read in accordance with regulations made under section 3(5) of that Act.

Title.Addition: Meaning of “relevant earnings amount” and “required time”

Text.Addition: For the purposes of section 270A, the “relevant earnings amount”, in the case of an employee provided with vouchers by an employer for any qualifying week in a tax year, means—
the aggregate of—
the amount of any relevant earnings for the tax year from employment by the employer, and
any amounts treated under Chapters 2 to 12 of Part 3 as earnings from such employment, less
the aggregate of any excluded amounts.

But if the employee becomes employed by the employer during the tax year, what would otherwise be the amount of the aggregate mentioned in subsection (1)(a) is the relevant multiple of that amount; and the relevant multiple is—
where RD is the number of days in the period beginning with the day on which the employee becomes employed by the employer and ending with the tax year.
In subsection (1)(a) “
” means—
salary, wages or fees, and
any other earnings specified in regulations made by the Treasury under this paragraph.
In subsection (1)(b) “
” means amounts specified in regulations made by the Treasury under this subsection.
In section 270A “the required time”, in the case of an employee, means—
if the employee joins the scheme under which the vouchers are provided at a time during the tax year, that time, and
otherwise, the beginning of the tax year.
For the purposes of subsection (5)(a) the employee is taken to join the scheme as soon as—
the employer has agreed that vouchers will be provided under the scheme for the employee, and
there is a child falling within section 270A(3)(a) or (b) in relation to the employee.
The Treasury may by order amend this section.

Title.Emphasis: Exemption of removal benefits and expenses: general

P1group.Title: Limited exemption of removal benefits and expenses: general

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax in respect of earnings or by virtue of Part 7A arises by virtue of—

P3para.Text: the provision of removal benefits to which this section applies, or
the payment or reimbursement of removal expenses to which this section applies.

P2para.Text: In relation to earnings, subsection (1) does not apply if (disregarding this section) the earnings are general earnings to which either of the following sections applies—

P3para.Text: section 22 (chargeable overseas earnings for year when remittance basis applied and employee outside section 26 ), or
section 26 (foreign earnings for year when remittance basis applied and employee met section 26A requirement ).

Text.Addition: In relation to Part 7A, subsection (1) does not apply to any amount so far as the amount (disregarding this section and section 554P) would count as employment income to which section 554Z9 or 554Z10 would apply.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) is subject to section 287 (limit on exemption).

P1group.Title: Removal benefits and expenses to which section 271 applies

P2para.Text: Benefits are removal benefits to which section 271 applies if—

P3para.Text: they are reasonably provided in connection with a change of the employee’s residence which meets the conditions in section 273,
they are provided on or before the limitation day (see section 274), and
they are within subsection (2) or one of the following provisions—

P4para.Text: section 277 (acquisition benefits and expenses),
section 278 (abortive acquisition benefits and expenses),
section 279 (disposal benefits and expenses),
section 280 (transporting belongings),
section 281 (travelling and subsistence),
section 285 (replacement of domestic goods).

P2para.Text: A benefit is within this subsection if it is a non-cash voucher, cash voucher or credit-token used—

P3para.Text: to obtain goods or services the direct provision of which would be a benefit within one of the provisions specified in subsection (1)(c)(i) to (vi), or
to obtain money for the purpose of obtaining such goods or services or meeting expenses within one of those provisions or section 284 (bridging loan expenses).

P2para.Text: Expenses are removal expenses to which section 271 applies if—

P3para.Text: they are reasonably incurred by the employee in connection with a change of the employee’s residence which meets the conditions in section 273,
they are incurred on or before the limitation day, and
they are within one of the provisions referred to in subsection (1)(c)(i) to (vi) or within section 284 (bridging loan expenses).

P1group.Title: Conditions applicable to change of residence

P2para.Text: The conditions referred to in section 272(1)(a) and (3)(a) which apply to the change of the employee’s residence are conditions A to C.
Condition A is that the change of residence results from one of the following changes—

P3para.Text: the employee becoming employed,
an alteration of the duties of the employment, or
an alteration of the place where the employee is normally to perform those duties.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that the change of residence is made wholly or mainly to allow the employee to reside within a reasonable daily travelling distance of the place where the employee normally performs or is normally to perform the duties of the employment after the employment change (see section 275).
Condition C is that the employee’s former residence is not within a reasonable daily travelling distance of that place.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “the limitation day”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “the limitation day”, in relation to an employee’s change of residence, means the last day of the tax year after that in which the employee begins to perform the duties of the employment after the employment change, but this is subject to any direction under subsection (2).

An officer of Revenue and Customs may direct that the last day of a later tax year is the limitation day in relation to any particular change of residence if it appears to them reasonable to do so having regard to all the circumstances of that change.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “the employment change”

P1para.Text: In this Chapter “the employment change”, in relation to an employee’s change of residence, means whichever of the changes specified in section 273(2) results in the change of residence.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “residence”, “former residence” and “new residence” etc.

P2para.Text: If an employee has more than one residence, references in this Chapter to the employee’s residence are references to the employee’s main residence.
In this Chapter, in relation to a change of the employee’s residence—

P3para.Text: references to the former residence are references to the employee’s residence before the change, and
references to the new residence are references to the employee’s residence after the change.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter references to an interest in a residence are, in the case of a building, references to an estate or interest in the land concerned.

Title.Emphasis: Benefits and expenses within this Chapter

P1group.Title: Acquisition benefits and expenses

P2para.Text: This section applies if an interest in the employee’s new residence is acquired by—

P3para.Text: the employee,
one or more members of the employee’s family or household, or
the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household.

P2para.Text: The following benefits are within this section—

P3para.Text: legal services connected with the acquisition of the interest, including legal services connected with any loan raised by the employee to acquire it,
the waiving of any procurement fees connected with any such loan,

the waiving of any amount payable in respect of insurance effected to cover risks incurred by the maker of any such loan because the loan equals the whole, or a substantial part, of the value of the interest,
any survey or inspection of the residence undertaken in connection with the acquisition, and
the connection of any utility serving the new residence for use by the employee or by the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household.

P2para.Text: The following expenses are within this section—

P3para.Text: sums paid for any services within subsection (2)(a), (d) or (e),
any procurement fees connected with any loan raised by the employee to acquire the interest,
the costs of any insurance within subsection (2)(c),
fees payable to an appropriate registry or appropriate register in connection with the acquisition, and
stamp duty or stamp duty land tax charged on the acquisition.

P2para.Text: In this section references to a loan raised by the employee include a loan raised by—

P3para.Text: one or more members of the employee’s family or household, or
the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “appropriate registry” means—
Her Majesty’s Land Registry,
the Land Registry in Northern Ireland, or
the Registry of Deeds for Northern Ireland, and
“appropriate register” means any register under the management and control of the Keeper of the Registers of Scotland.

P1group.Title: Abortive acquisition benefits and expenses

P1para.Text: Benefits or expenses are within this section if—

P3para.Text: they are benefits provided or expenses incurred with a view to the acquisition of an interest in a residence,
the interest is not acquired—

P4para.Text: because of circumstances outside the control of the person seeking to acquire it, or
because that person reasonably declines to proceed, and

P3para.Text: the benefits or expenses would have fallen within section 277 if the interest had been acquired.

P1group.Title: Disposal benefits and expenses

P2para.Text: This section applies if the employee has an interest in the former residence and because of the change of residence it is disposed of or is intended to be disposed of.
The following benefits are within this section—

P3para.Text: legal services connected with the disposal or intended disposal, including legal services connected with the redemption of a related loan,
the waiving of any penalty for redeeming a related loan for the purpose of the disposal or intended disposal,
the services of an estate agent or auctioneer engaged in the disposal or intended disposal,
services connected with the advertisement of the disposal or intended disposal,
the disconnection, for the purpose of the disposal or intended disposal, of any utility serving the former residence, and
services connected with maintaining, insuring, or preserving the security of, the former residence at any time when it is unoccupied pending the disposal or intended disposal.

P2para.Text: The following expenses are within this section—

P3para.Text: sums paid for any services within subsection (2)(a), (c), (d) or (e),
any penalty for redeeming a related loan for the purpose of the disposal or intended disposal,
rent paid in respect of the former residence at any time when it is unoccupied pending the disposal or intended disposal, and
expenses of maintaining, insuring, or preserving the security of the former residence at any time when it is unoccupied pending the disposal or intended disposal.

P2para.Text: In this section references to the employee having an interest in a residence include—

P3para.Text: one or more members of the employee’s family or household having such an interest, or
the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household having such an interest.

P2para.Text: A loan is a “related loan” for this purpose if—

P3para.Text: it was raised to obtain an interest in the former residence, or
it is secured on such an interest, or
part of it was so raised and the rest of it is so secured.

P1group.Title: Transporting belongings

P2para.Text: The following benefits are within this section—

P3para.Text: the transportation of domestic belongings from the employee’s former residence to the employee’s new residence, and
the effecting of insurance to cover such transportation.

P2para.Text: The following expenses are within this section—

P3para.Text: expenses connected with such transportation, and
the costs of any such insurance.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “domestic belongings” means belongings of the employee or of members of the employee’s family or household, and
“transportation” includes—
packing and unpacking belongings,
temporarily storing them, where there is not a direct move from the former to the new residence,
detaching domestic fittings from the former residence, where they are to be taken to the new residence, and
attaching domestic fittings to the new residence and adapting them, where they are brought from the former residence.

P1group.Title: Travelling and subsistence

P2para.Text: The following benefits are within this section—

P3para.Text: subsistence and facilities for travel provided for the employee and members of the employee’s family or household for temporary visits to the new area for purposes connected with the change of residence,
any other subsistence provided for the employee,
facilities provided for the employee for travel between the employee’s former residence and—

P4para.Text: the place where the employee’s new duties are normally performed, or
the new place where the duties of the employee’s employment are normally performed, or
temporary living accommodation of the employee,

P3para.Text: where the employment change is within section 273(2)(b) or (c) (change of duties or place of performance), facilities provided for the employee for travel before the change between the employee’s new residence and—

P4para.Text: the place where the employee normally performs the duties of the employment before the change, or
temporary living accommodation of the employee,

P3para.Text: facilities provided for the employee and members of the employee’s family or household for travel from the employee’s former residence to the employee’s new residence in connection with the change of residence,
subsistence provided for a relevant child while the child stays in education-linked living accommodation,
facilities provided for a relevant child for travel between education-linked living accommodation and the employee’s accommodation.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section, “education-linked living accommodation”, in relation to a relevant child, means living accommodation where the child stays for the purpose of securing continuity in education, being—

P3para.Text: accommodation in the new area where the child stays before the employee’s change of residence,
accommodation in the former area where the child stays after that change,
accommodation in the new area where the child stays while the employee is living in temporary living accommodation in the former area, or
accommodation in the former area where the child stays while the employee is living in temporary living accommodation in the new area.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (1)(g) “the employee’s accommodation”, in relation to travel to or from education-linked accommodation, means—

P3para.Text: if that accommodation is within subsection (2)(a), the employee’s former residence,
if that accommodation is within subsection (2)(b), the employee’s new residence, and
if that accommodation is within subsection (2)(c) or (d), the employee’s temporary accommodation.

P2para.Text: The cost of providing subsistence or travel of a kind described in subsection (1) is an expense within this section.

Subsections (1) and (4) are subject to section 282 (exclusion from this section of benefits and expenses where deduction allowed), and subsection (1) is also subject to section 283 (exclusion from this section of taxable car and van facilities).
In this section—

Para.Text: “new duties” means—
if the employment change is within section 273(2)(a) (change of employer), the duties of the employee’s new employment, and
if the employment change is within section 273(2)(b) (change of duties), the new duties of the employment,
“former area” means the area round or near the former residence of the employee,
“new area” means—
if the employment change is within section 273(2)(a) or (b) (change of employer or duties), the area round or near the place where the employee’s new duties normally are or are to be performed, and

if the employment change is within section 273(2)(c) (change of place of performance), the area round or near the new place where the duties of the employee’s employment normally are or are to be performed,
“relevant child” means a person who is a member of the employee’s family or household and is aged under 19 at the beginning of the tax year in which the employment change occurs, and
“subsistence” means food, drink and temporary living accommodation.

P1group.Title: Exclusion from section 281 of benefits and expenses where deduction allowed

P2para.Text: Benefits and expenses are excluded from section 281 (travelling and subsistence) if or to the extent that an amount is deductible in respect of the cost of the benefits or of the expenses under any of the following provisions.
They are—

P3para.Text: section 341 (travel at start or finish of overseas employment),
section 342 (travel between employments where duties performed abroad), and
Chapter 5 of Part 5 except section 376 (deductions for earnings representing benefits or reimbursed expenses in respect of certain foreign travel).

P2para.Text: If an amount is so deductible in respect of part only of the cost of a benefit, the part of the benefit excluded by this section is to be determined on a just and reasonable basis.

P1group.Title: Exclusion from section 281 of taxable car and van facilities

P2para.Text: A car or van is not treated as a facility for the purposes of section 281(1) if in the tax year in which it is provided it is also made available—

P3para.Text: to the employee or members of the employee’s family or household for private use not falling within section 281(1),
by reason of the employee’s employment, and
without any transfer of the property in it.

P2para.Text: The following sections apply for the purposes of this section as they apply for the purposes of Chapter 6 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: cars, vans and related benefits)—

P3para.Text: section 115 (meaning of “car” and “van”),
section 117 (meaning of car or van made available by reason of employment), and
section 118 (availability for private use).

P1group.Title: Bridging loan expenses

P2para.Text: Expenses are within this section if—

P3para.Text: the employee has an interest in the former residence and disposes of it because of the change of residence,
the employee acquires an interest in the new residence, and

the expenses are interest payable by the employee in respect of a loan raised by the employee wholly or partly because expenditure is incurred in connection with that acquisition before the proceeds of that disposal become available.
This is subject to subsections (2) and (3).

P2para.Text: Interest is only within this section if or to the extent that the loan is used—

P3para.Text: for acquiring the employee’s interest in the new residence, or
for redeeming a loan—

P4para.Text: which was raised by the employee to obtain an interest in the former residence,
which is secured on such an interest, or
which was partly so raised and the rest of which is so secured.

P2para.Text: If the loan exceeds the market value of the employee’s interest in the former residence at the time of acquisition of the new residence, the interest on the excess is not within this section.

If subsection (3) applies in a case where the loan is used partly for purposes within subsection (2) and partly for other purposes, the amount of the interest within this section is the appropriate fraction of the total interest.
The appropriate fraction is—
or, if it is smaller—

Para.Text: where—
MV is the market value of the employee’s interest in the former residence at the time of acquisition of the new residence,
PL is the part of the loan used for purposes within subsection (2), and
L is the amount of the loan.

P2para.Text: In this section—

P3para.Text: references to a loan raised by the employee include a loan raised by—

P4para.Text: one or more members of the employee’s family or household, or
the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household, and

P3para.Text: references to the employee having, disposing of or acquiring an interest in a residence include—

P4para.Text: one or more members of the employee’s family or household having, disposing of or acquiring such an interest, or
the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household having, disposing of or acquiring such an interest.

P1group.Title: Replacement of domestic goods

P2para.Text: Benefits and expenses are within this section if—

P3para.Text: the employee has an interest in the former residence and disposes of it because of the change of residence,
the employee acquires an interest in the new residence,
in the case of benefits, they are domestic goods provided to replace goods used at the former residence which are unsuitable for use at the new residence, and
in the case of expenses, they are incurred on the purchase of domestic goods intended for such replacement.

P2para.Text: In this section references to the employee having, disposing of or acquiring an interest in a residence include—

P3para.Text: one or more members of the employee’s family or household having, disposing of or acquiring such an interest, or
the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household having, disposing of or acquiring such an interest.

P1group.Title: Power to amend sections 277 to 285

P2para.Text: The Treasury may by regulations amend sections 277 to 285 so as to secure that benefits or expenses which would not otherwise fall within any of those sections do so.
The regulations may include such supplementary, incidental or consequential provisions as appear to the Treasury to be necessary or expedient.
Those provisions may be made by amending this Chapter or otherwise.
The regulations apply to a change of an employee’s residence resulting from an employment change occurring on or after the day specified in the regulations for this purpose.

P1group.Title: Limit on exemption

P2para.Text: If in the case of any change of residence the value of the exemption exceeds £8,000, section 271 (exemption of removal benefits and expenses) does not apply to the excess.
The value of the exemption is an amount equal to the sum of—

P3para.Text: the section 62 earnings, ...
the benefits code earnings (after taking account of section 64(2)(b) where otherwise an amount that falls within paragraph (a) would be included), and

Text.Addition: the Part 7A employment income

P2para.Text: In this section “the section 62 earnings” means all earnings within section 62 (earnings) in respect of which section 271 would prevent liability to income tax from arising if this section were disregarded.
In this section “the benefits code earnings” means all earnings—

P3para.Text: which are treated as such under the benefits code (except earnings so treated under Chapter 7 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: loans)), and
in respect of which section 271 would prevent liability to income tax from arising if this section were disregarded.

P2para.Text: In the case of living accommodation, the amount that would be so treated is to be taken to be equal to—

Para.Text: where—

CE is the cash equivalent of the accommodation under Chapter 5 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: living accommodation) for the period in which the accommodation is provided (calculated as mentioned in section 103), and
D is any amount deductible under section 364 (deductions where living accommodation provided).

Text.Addition: In this section “
” means the amount in respect of which section 271 (when read with section 554P) would prevent liability to income tax arising if this section were to be disregarded.

Title.Emphasis: Special exemption and relief for bridging loans

P1group.Title: Limited exemption of certain bridging loans connected with employment moves

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 7 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: loans) in respect of a loan if—

P3para.Text: it is a removal benefit (see subsection (2)),
the unused removal benefit exemption condition is met (see subsection (3)), and
the loan is discharged before the end of the exempted loan discharge period (see subsection (4)).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section and section 289, a loan is a removal benefit if—

P3para.Text: it is raised by the employee in connection with a change of residence meeting the conditions in section 273 (conditions applicable to change of residence),
the employee has an interest in the former residence and disposes of it in consequence of the change of residence,
the employee acquires an interest in the new residence,
