the loan is raised wholly or partly because expenditure is incurred in connection with that acquisition before the proceeds of that disposal become available, and
the loan is made before the limitation day.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section and section 289 the unused removal benefit exemption condition is that, in the case of the particular change of residence—

P3para.Text: the sum specified in section 287(1) (limit on exemption), exceeds
the amount referred to in section 287(2) (the value of the exemption);

P2para.Text: and for those purposes that excess is “the unused exemption”.

In this section and section 289 “the exempted loan discharge period”, in relation to a loan, means the period of N days beginning with the day on which it is made, taking N as the number obtained by applying the following formula and, if that does not give a whole number, rounding up the result to the nearest whole number—

Para.Text: where—
A is the unused exemption,
B is the maximum amount of the loan outstanding in the period beginning with the time when the loan is made and ending with the limitation day, and
C is the official rate of interest in force when the loan is made (expressed as a percentage).

P2para.Text: In this section—

P3para.Text: references to a loan raised by the employee include a loan raised by—

P4para.Text: one or more members of the employee’s family or household, or
the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household, and

P3para.Text: references to the employee having, disposing of or acquiring an interest in a residence include—

P4para.Text: one or more members of the employee’s family or household having, disposing of or acquiring such an interest, or
the employee and one or more members of the employee’s family or household having, disposing of or acquiring such an interest.

P2para.Text: The tax payable in respect of a loan for a tax year ending before the limitation day may be decided on the basis that the unused removal benefit exemption condition will not be met.

P1group.Title: Relief for certain bridging loans not qualifying for exemption under section 288

P2para.Text: This subsection applies to a loan if—

P3para.Text: it is a removal benefit (see section 288(2)),
the unused removal benefit exemption condition is met (see section 288(3)), and
the loan is not discharged before the end of the exempted loan discharge period (see section 288(4)).

P2para.Text: A loan to which subsection (1) applies is to be treated for the purposes of Chapter 7 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: loans) as if it was made on the day after the last day of the exempted loan discharge period.
Subsection (2) does not apply for the purposes of sections 176, 177, 180, 189 and 190.

The tax payable in respect of a loan for a tax year ending before the limitation day may be decided on the basis that subsections (1) and (2) will not apply because the unused removal benefit exemption condition will not be met.

Title.Addition: Exemptions: amounts which would otherwise be deductible
Exemption for paid or reimbursed expenses

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 3 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: expenses payments) in respect of an amount (“amount A”) paid or reimbursed by a person to an employee (whether or not an employee of the person) in respect of expenses if—
an amount equal to or exceeding amount A would (ignoring this section) be allowed as a deduction from the employee's earnings under Chapter 2 or 5 of Part 5 in respect of the expenses, and
the payment or reimbursement is not provided pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements.
No liability to income tax arises in respect of an amount paid or reimbursed by a person (“the payer”) to an employee (whether or not an employee of the payer) in respect of expenses if—
the amount has been calculated and paid or reimbursed in an approved way (see subsection (6)),
the payment or reimbursement is not provided pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements, and
conditions A and B are met.

Addition.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of an amount paid or reimbursed by a person (“the payer”) to an employee (whether or not an employee of the payer) for expenses in the course of qualifying travel if—
the amount has been calculated and paid or reimbursed in accordance with regulations made by the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs,
the payment or reimbursement is not provided pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements, and

Text.Addition: Condition A is that the payer or another person operates a system for checking—
that the employee is, or employees are, in fact incurring and paying amounts in respect of expenses of the same kind, and
that a deduction would (ignoring this section) be allowed under Chapter 2 or 5 of Part 5 in respect of those amounts.
Condition B is that neither the payer nor any other person operating the system knows or suspects, or could reasonably be expected to know or suspect—
that the employee has not incurred and paid an amount in respect of the expenses, or
that a deduction from the employee's earnings would not be allowed under Chapter 2 or 5 of Part 5 in respect of the amount.

Addition.Addition: the payer or another person operates a system for checking that the employee has undertaken the qualifying travel in relation to which the amount is paid or reimbursed, and
neither the payer nor any other person operating the system knows or suspects, or could reasonably be expected to know or suspect, that the travel was not undertaken.

Text.Addition: , in relation to an employee to whom an amount is paid or reimbursed
in respect of expenses, means arrangements (whenever made, whether before or after the employment began) under which—
the employee gives up the right to receive an amount of general earnings or specific employment income in return for the payment or reimbursement, or
the amount of other general earnings or specific employment income received by the employee depends on the amount of the payment or reimbursement.

Addition.Addition: ” means travel for which a deduction from the employee's earnings would be allowed under Chapter 2 or 5 of Part 5.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of
, a sum is calculated and paid or reimbursed in an approved way if—
it is calculated and paid or reimbursed in accordance with regulations made by the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs, or
it is calculated and paid or reimbursed in accordance with an approval given under section 289B.
Regulations made under subsection
(6)(a) may make different provision for different purposes.

Addition.Addition: Regulations made under subsection (2A)(a) may contain provision about calculating amounts that is framed by reference to rates (for expenses) published from time to time by the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs.

Title.Addition: Approval to pay or reimburse expenses at a flat rate

Text.Addition: A person (“

”) may apply to Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs for approval to pay or reimburse expenses of the applicant's employees, or employees of another person, at a rate set out in the application (“the proposed rate”).

An officer of Revenue and Customs may give the approval if satisfied that any calculation of a payment or reimbursement of expenses in accordance with the proposed rate, or such other rate as is agreed between the applicant and the officer, would be a reasonable estimate of the amount of expenses actually incurred.
An approval under subsection (2) takes effect in accordance with a notice (an “approval notice”) given to the applicant by an officer of Revenue and Customs.
An approval notice must specify—
the rate at which expenses may be paid or reimbursed,
the day from which the approval takes effect, that day not being earlier than the day on which the approval notice is given,
the day on which the approval ceases to have effect, that day not being later than the end of the period of 5 years beginning with the day on which the approval takes effect, and
the type of expenses to which the approval relates.
An approval notice may specify that the approval is subject to conditions specified or described in the notice.
An application for an approval under this section must be in such form and manner, and contain such information, as is specified by Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs.

An officer of Revenue and Customs may, if in the officer's opinion there is reason to do so, revoke an approval given under section 289B by giving a further notice (a “revocation notice”) to either or both of the following—
the person who applied for the approval, and
the person who is paying or reimbursing expenses in accordance with the approval.
A revocation notice may revoke the approval from—
the day on which the approval took effect, or
a later day specified in the notice.
A revocation under subsection (1) may be in relation to all expenses or expenses of a description specified in the revocation notice.
If the revocation notice revokes the approval from the day on which the approval took effect—

any liability to tax that would have arisen in respect of the payment or reimbursement of expenses if the approval had never been given in relation to such expenses is to be treated as having arisen, and

any person who has made, and any employee who has received, a payment or reimbursement of expenses calculated in accordance with the approval must make all the returns which they would have had to make if the approval had never been given in relation to such expenses.
If the revocation notice revokes the approval from a later day—

any liability to tax that would have arisen in respect of the payment or reimbursement of expenses if the approval had ceased to have effect on that day in relation to such expenses is to be treated as having arisen, and

any person who has made, and any employee who has received, a payment or reimbursement of expenses calculated in accordance with the approval must make all the returns which they would have had to make if the approval had ceased to have effect in relation to such expenses on that day.
No liability to income tax arises by virtue of any provision of the benefits code in respect of an amount (“amount A”) treated as earnings of an employee as a result of the provision of a benefit if—
an amount equal to amount A would (ignoring this section) be allowed as a deduction from the employee's earnings under Chapter 3 of Part 5 in respect of the provision of the benefit, and
the benefit is not provided pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements.
”, in relation to an employee to whom a benefit is provided, means arrangements (whenever made, whether before or after the employment began) under which—
the employee gives up the right to receive an amount of general earnings or specific employment income in return for the provision of the benefit, or
the amount of other general earnings or specific employment income received by the employee depends on the provision of the benefit.
This section applies if conditions A to C are met.
Condition A is that, pursuant to arrangements, an amount—
is paid or reimbursed to an employee in respect of expenses, or
is treated as earnings of an employee as a result of the provision of a benefit,
which, in the absence of this section, would have been exempt from income tax.
Condition B is that, in the absence of those arrangements, the employee would have received a greater amount of general earnings or specific employment income in respect of which—
tax would have been chargeable, or
national insurance contributions would have been payable (whether by the employee or another person).
Condition C is that the main purpose, or one of the main purposes, of the arrangements is the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions.
If this section applies—
the exemption conferred by section 289A does not apply in respect of the amount paid or reimbursed as mentioned in subsection (2)(a), and
the exemption conferred by section 289D does not apply in respect of the amount treated as earnings as mentioned in subsection (2)(b).
In this section “
” includes any scheme, transaction or series of transactions, agreement or understanding, whether or not legally enforceable.

P1group.Title: Accommodation benefits of ministers of religion

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax in respect of a person employed as a full-time minister arises by virtue of—

P3para.Text: the payment or reimbursement of a statutory amount payable in connection with qualifying premises, or
the reimbursement of a statutory deduction made in connection with qualifying premises.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax in respect of a person employed as a full-time minister arises by virtue of the payment or reimbursement of expenses incurred in connection with providing living accommodation in qualifying premises if the employment is lower-paid employment as a minister of religion (see section 290D).
Subsection (1) does not apply if or to the extent that the amount or deduction is properly attributable to a part of the premises for which the minister receives rent.
Premises are qualifying premises in relation to a person employed as a minister if—

P3para.Text: an interest in them belongs to a charity or an ecclesiastical corporation, and
because of that interest and by reason of holding the employment, the minister has a residence in them from which to perform the duties of the employment.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “full-time minister” means a person in full-time employment as a minister of a religious denomination,
“statutory amount” means an amount paid in pursuance of a provision in, or having the force of, an Act, and
“statutory deduction” means a deduction made in pursuance of such a provision.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a person in lower-paid employment as a minister of
by virtue of the payment or reimbursement of accommodation outgoings.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the minister is paid an allowance intended to be used, wholly or in part, for paying accommodation outgoings (as to which see section 290B).
In this section—
“accommodation outgoings” means amounts incurred by the minister in—
heating, lighting or cleaning qualifying premises; or
maintaining a garden forming part of qualifying premises;
“qualifying premises” has the same meaning as in section 290.

Title.Addition: ministers of religion in respect of accommodation outgoings

Text.Addition: This section applies where a person in lower-paid employment as a minister of
is paid an allowance intended to be used, wholly or in part, for paying accommodation outgoings.
No liability to tax arises by virtue of the payment of the allowance to the extent that it is used for paying accommodation outgoings.
In this section—
“accommodation outgoings”
as in section 290A;
“qualifying premises” has the same meaning as in section 290.

Title.Addition: Provisions of benefits code not applicable to lower-paid ministers of religion

Text.Addition: This section applies where a person is in employment which is lower-paid employment as a minister of religion in relation to a tax year.
No liability to income tax arises in respect of the person in relation to the tax year by virtue of any of the following Chapters of the benefits code—
Chapter 3 (taxable benefits: expenses payments);
Chapter 6 (taxable benefits: cars, vans and related benefits);
Chapter 7 (taxable benefits: loans);
Chapter 10 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge).
Subsection (2)—

means that in any of those Chapters a reference to an employee does not include an employee whose employment is within the exclusion in that subsection, if the context is such that the reference is to an employee in relation to whom the Chapter applies, but
does not restrict the meaning of references to employees in other contexts.
Subsection (2) has effect subject to—
section 188(2) (discharge of loan: where employment becomes lower-paid), and
section 290G (employment in two or more related employments).

Title.Addition: Meaning of “lower-paid employment as a minister of religion”

Text.Addition: For the purposes of this Part an employment is “

Term.Addition: lower-paid employment as a minister of religion

Text.Addition: ” in relation to a tax year if—
the employment is direct employment as a minister of a religious denomination, and
the earnings rate for the employment for the year (calculated under section 290E) is less than £8,500.
An employment is not “
” for the purposes of subsection (1)(a) if—
it is an employment which is treated as existing under—
section 56(2) (deemed employment of worker by intermediary), or
section 61G(2) (deemed employment of worker by managed service company), or
an amount counts as employment income in respect of it by virtue of section 554Z2(1) (treatment of relevant step under Part 7A (employment income provided through third parties)).
Subsection (1) is subject to section 290G.

Title.Addition: Calculation of earnings rate for a tax year

Text.Addition: For any tax year the earnings rate for an employment is to be calculated as follows—
Find the total of the following amounts—
the total amount of the earnings from the employment for the year within Chapter 1 of Part 3 (earnings),
the total of any amounts that are treated as earnings from the employment for the year under the benefits code (see subsections (2) and (3)), and
the total of any amounts that are treated as earnings from the employment for the year under Chapter 12 of Part 3 (other amounts treated as earnings),
excluding any exempt income, other than any attributable to section 290A or 290B (accommodation outgoings of ministers of religion).
Add to that total any extra amount required to be added for the year by section 290F (extra amounts to be added in connection with a car).
Subtract the total amount of any authorised deductions (see subsection (4)) from the result of step 2.
The earnings rate for the employment for the year is given by the formula—
where—
R is the result of step 3,
Y is the number of days in the year, and
E is the number of days in the year when the employment is held.
Section 290C(2) (provisions of benefits code not applicable to lower-paid ministers of religion) is to be disregarded for the purpose of determining any amount under step 1.

If the benefit of living accommodation is to be taken into account under step 1, the cash equivalent is to be calculated in accordance with section 105 (even if the cost of providing the accommodation exceeds £75,000).
For the purposes of step 3 “
” means any deduction that would (assuming it was an amount of taxable earnings) be allowed from any amount within step 1 under—
section 346 (employee liabilities),
section 370 (travel costs and expenses where duties performed abroad: employee's travel),
section 371 (travel costs and expenses where duties performed abroad: visiting spouse's, civil partner's or child's travel),
section 373 (
employee's travel costs and expenses where duties performed in
UK
section 374 (
employee's spouse's, civil partner's or child's travel costs and expenses where duties performed in
UK
section 376 (foreign accommodation and subsistence costs and expenses (overseas employments)),
section 713 (payroll giving to charities),
sections 188 to 194 of FA 2004 (contributions to registered pension schemes), or
section 262 of
CAA
2001 (capital allowances to be given effect by treating them as deductions).

Title.Addition: Extra amounts to be added in connection with a car

Text.Addition: The provisions of this section apply for the purposes of section 290E in the case of a tax year in which a car is made available as mentioned in section 114(1) (cars, vans and related benefits) by reason of the employment.
Subsection (3) applies if in the tax year—
an alternative to the benefit of the car is offered, and

the amount that would be earnings within Chapter 1 of Part 3 if the benefit of the car were to be determined by reference to the alternative offered exceeds the benefit code earnings (see subsection (4)).
The amount of the excess is an extra amount to be added under step 2 in section 290E(1).
For the purposes of subsection (2) “the benefit code earnings” is the total for the year of—
the cash equivalent of the benefit of the car (calculated in accordance with Chapter 6 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: cars, vans
etc
)), and
the cash equivalent (calculated in accordance with that Chapter) of the benefit of any fuel provided for the car by reason of the employment.
Section 290C(2) (provisions of benefits code not applicable to lower-paid ministers of religion) is to be disregarded for the purpose of determining any amount under this section.
This section applies if a person is employed in two or more related employments.
None of the employments is to be regarded as lower-paid employment as a minister of religion in relation to a tax year if—
the total of the earnings rates for the employments for the year (calculated in each case under section 290E) is £8,500 or more, or
any of them is an employment falling outside the exclusion contained in section 290C(2) (provisions of benefits code not applicable to lower-paid ministers of religion).
For the purposes of this section two employments are “related” if—
both are with the same employer, or
one is with a body or partnership (“A”) and the other is either—
with an individual, partnership or body that controls A (“B”), or
with another partnership or body also controlled by B.
Section 69 (extended meaning of “control”) applies for the purposes of this section as it applies for the purposes of the benefits code.

P1group.Title: Termination payments to MPs and others ceasing to hold office

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax in respect of earnings arises by virtue of any grant or payment to which this section applies (but see Chapter 3 of Part 6: payments and benefits on termination of employment etc.).
This section applies to grants and payments—

Text.Substitution: made under section 5(1) of the Parliamentary Standards Act 2009 in connection with a person's ceasing to be a member of the House of Commons,

P3para.Text: made under section 4 of the Ministerial and other Pensions and Salaries Act 1991 (c. 5) (grants to persons ceasing to hold certain ministerial and other offices),

made under section 3 of the European Parliament (Pay and Pensions) Act 1979 (c. 50) (resettlement grants for persons ceasing to be Representatives), or under Article 13 of the Statute for Members of the European Parliament (transitional allowances),
made under section 81(3) of the Scotland Act 1998 (c. 46) to a person—

P4para.Text: ceasing to be a member of the Scottish Parliament on its dissolution, or
ceasing to hold an office corresponding to a relevant office,

Text.Substitution: made under section 20(3) of the Government of Wales Act 2006 to a person—
ceasing to be a member of the National Assembly for Wales; or
ceasing to hold office as the Presiding Officer, Deputy Presiding Officer, or such other office in connection with the Assembly as the Assembly may determine, but continuing to be an Assembly Member,
made under section 53(3) of the Government of Wales Act 2006 to a person ceasing to be a member of the Welsh Assembly Government

P3para.Text: made under section 48(1) of the Northern Ireland Act 1998 (c. 47) to a person—

P4para.Text: ceasing to be a member of the Northern Ireland Assembly on its dissolution, or
ceasing to hold an office corresponding to a relevant office, or

Text.Addition: made under section 26A of the Greater London Authority Act 1999 (payments on ceasing to hold office as Mayor of London or as a member of the London Assembly).

P2para.Text: In this section “a relevant office” has the same meaning as in section 4 of the Ministerial and other Pensions and Salaries Act 1991.

Text.Substitution: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a payment made to a member of the House of Commons under section 5(1) of the Parliamentary Standards Act 2009 if the payment is—
expressed to be made in respect of accommodation expenses, or
related to or in consequence of a payment expressed to be so made.

” means expenses necessarily incurred on overnight accommodation that is required for the performance of the member's parliamentary duties in or about the Palace of Westminster or the member's constituency.

But the cost of an overnight stay in a hotel that was required only because, on that night, the member had been required to be at the House of Commons because the House was sitting late does not count as accommodation expenses for the purposes of this section, unless the member had been required to be at the House because it was sitting beyond 1 a.m.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a loan for a deposit payable at the commencement of a tenancy.

Substitution.Addition: The reference in subsection (1) to a payment made to a member of the House of Commons under section 5(1) of the Parliamentary Standards Act 2009 includes a payment made under that section to another person at the direction of a member (see section 6(7) of that Act).

P1group.Title: Overnight expenses of other elected representatives

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a payment to which this section applies if it is expressed to be made in respect of a member’s necessary overnight expenses.
This section applies to payments—

P3para.Text: made to members of the Scottish Parliament under section 81(2) of the Scotland Act 1998 (c. 46),
made to members of the National Assembly for Wales under section 20(2) of the Government of Wales Act 2006 or to a member of the Welsh Assembly Government under section 53(2) of that Act, or
made to members of the Northern Ireland Assembly under section 47(2) of the Northern Ireland Act 1998 (c. 47).

P2para.Text: In this section “a member’s necessary overnight expenses” means additional expenses necessarily incurred by a member for the purpose of performing duties as a member in staying overnight away from the member’s only or main residence—

P3para.Text: in the area in which the Parliament or Assembly to which the member belongs sits, or
in the constituency or region which the member represents.

Title.Addition: travel and subsistence expenses of MPs

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a payment made to a member of the House of Commons under section 5(1) of the Parliamentary Standards Act 2009 if the payment is expressed to be made—
in respect of relevant
UK
travel expenses, or
in respect of relevant subsistence expenses.
” means expenses necessarily incurred on journeys of the following kinds within the United Kingdom—
journeys made by the member that are necessary for the performance of the member's parliamentary duties, and
if the member shares caring responsibilities with a spouse or partner, journeys made by the spouse or partner between the member's London Area residence and the member's constituency residence.

” means expenses necessarily incurred on an evening meal (excluding alcoholic drinks) eaten on the Parliamentary Estate, where the member is required to be at the House of Commons because the House is sitting beyond 7.30 p.m.
” and “
” have the same meaning in subsection (2)(b) as they have in the scheme in effect for the time being under section 5 of the Parliamentary Standards Act 2009.

Title.Addition: travel expenses of other elected representatives

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a payment to which this section applies if it is expressed to be made in respect of relevant
UK
travel expenses.
This section applies to payments—
made to members of the Scottish Parliament under section 81(2) of the Scotland Act 1998,
made to members of the National Assembly for Wales under section 20(2) of the Government of Wales Act 2006 or to a member of the Welsh Assembly Government under section 53(2) of that Act, or
made to members of the Northern Ireland Assembly under section 47(2) of the Northern Ireland Act 1998.
In this section “
” means expenses necessarily incurred on journeys of the following kinds within the United Kingdom—
journeys within subsection (4) made by the member that are necessary for the performance of his or her duties as a member;
if the member shares caring responsibilities with a spouse or partner, journeys made by the spouse or partner between the constituency or region and the member's parliamentary home.
The journeys referred to in subsection (3)(a) are those—
between the constituency or region and the Parliament or Assembly to which the member belongs,
between the constituency or region and the member's parliamentary home, or
within the constituency or region, but not excluded by subsection (5).
A journey is excluded if—
in the case of a member who has only one local office, it is between the member's local home and that office, and
in any other case, it is between the member's local home and the principal local office.
In this section—
”, in relation to a member, means the constituency or region which the member represents and the area within 20 miles of the boundary of that constituency or region;
”, in relation to a member, means an office which is situated in the constituency or region and occupied by the member for the purposes of performing duties as a member;
” means a residence of the member situated in the constituency or region;
” means the member's only or main residence in the area comprising—
the main site of the Parliament or Assembly to which the member belongs, and
the area within 20 miles of that site;
”, in relation to a member, means the local office most frequently occupied by the member for the purposes of performing duties as a member.
A person has “caring responsibilities” if the person—
has parental responsibility for a dependent child aged under 17 or for a child aged 17 or 18 who is in full-time education, or
is the primary carer for a family member in receipt of—
attendance allowance,
disability living allowance at the middle or highest rate for personal care,
the daily living component of personal independence payment, or
constant attendance allowance at or above the maximum rate with an industrial injuries disablement benefit, or the basic (full day) rate with a war disablement pension.
The Treasury may by order amend the definition of “caring responsibilities” in subsection (7).

P1group.Title: European travel expenses of MPs and other representatives

Text.Substitution: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a sum that is paid to—
a member of the House of Commons under section 5(1) of the Parliamentary Standards Act 2009,
a member of the Scottish Parliament under section 81(2) of the Scotland Act 1998,
a member of the National Assembly for Wales under section 20(2) of the Government of Wales Act 2006 or a member of the Welsh Assembly Government under section 53(2) of that Act, or
a member of the Northern Ireland Assembly under section 47(2) of the Northern Ireland Act 1998,
and expressed to be made in respect of European travel expenses.
” means the cost of, and any additional expenses incurred in, travelling between the United Kingdom and a relevant European location.
” means—
a European Union institution or agency, or
the national parliament of—
another member State,
a candidate or applicant country, or

Substitution.Substitution: any other country that is a member of the Council of Europe.

Text.Substitution: The Treasury may by order amend subsection (3) by—
adding a European location,
removing a European location, or
varying the description of a European location.

P1group.Title: Transport and subsistence for Government ministers etc.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision of transport or subsistence provided or made available by or on behalf of the Crown to—

P3para.Text: the holder of a ministerial office, or
a member of the family or household of the holder of a ministerial office.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of payments and reimbursements by or on behalf of the Crown of expenses incurred in connection with the provision of transport or subsistence to a person within subsection (1).
“Ministerial office” means—

P3para.Text: an office in Her Majesty’s Government in the United Kingdom,
any other office which is one of the offices and positions in respect of which salaries are payable under section 1 of the Ministerial and other Salaries Act 1975 (c. 27), and
an office under one of the following Acts which corresponds to an office within paragraph (a) or (b)—

P4para.Text: the Scotland Act 1998 (c. 46),
the Government of Wales Act 2006, or
the Northern Ireland Act 1998 (c. 47).

P2para.Text: In determining whether a particular person holds an office within subsection (3)(b), it is irrelevant whether or not a salary is paid or payable to that person under the Ministerial and other Salaries Act 1975.
In this section references to the provision of transport to a person include references to—

P3para.Text: the provision or making available to that person of a vehicle with or without a driver,
the provision of fuel for a vehicle provided or made available to that person, and
the provision of any other benefit in connection with such a vehicle.

P2para.Text: In this section—

P3para.Text: “subsistence” includes food and drink and temporary living accommodation, and
“vehicle” means a mechanically propelled road vehicle.

Title.Addition: Travel expenses of members of local authorities

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a qualifying payment made to a member of a relevant authority for travel expenses incurred by the member if—
the payment is for expenses other than those related to the member's use of a vehicle to which Chapter 2 applies, and
the expenses are not excluded by subsection (2).
Expenses are excluded by this subsection if—
they are incurred on a journey between the member's home and permanent workplace, and
the member's home is situated more than 20 miles outside the boundary of the area of the relevant authority.
In this section “
” has the same meaning as in Part 5 (see section 339).
The Treasury may by regulations—

provide for bodies specified in the regulations (which must be local authorities or bodies that have similar or related functions or purposes) to be relevant authorities for the purposes of this section,
provide for references in this section to a member of a relevant authority to be read as references to a member of a description prescribed in the regulations, and
define what is meant by “
” for the purposes of this section.
The regulations may contain transitional provision and savings.

P1group.Title: Armed forces' leave travel facilities

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of—

P3para.Text: the provision of travel facilities for a member of the armed forces of the Crown going on or returning from leave, or
a payment made in respect of such travel.

P2para.Text: In subsection (1) “travel facilities” does not include a vehicle.

P1group.Title: Armed forces' food, drink and mess allowances

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of allowances if—

P3para.Text: they are payable out of the public revenue to any description of members of the armed forces of the Crown, and
the Treasury certifies that they are payable to them instead of food or drink normally supplied to members of the armed forces.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of allowances if—

P3para.Text: they are payable out of the public revenue in respect of any description of members of the armed forces of the Crown, and
the Treasury certifies that they are so payable as a contribution to the expenses of a mess.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of payments to members of the armed forces of the Crown of the Operational Allowance.
The Operational Allowance is an allowance designated as such

Addition.Substitution: under a Royal Warrant made under section 333 of the Armed Forces Act 2006

Title.Addition: Armed forces: the Council Tax Relief

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of payments of the Council Tax Relief to members of the armed forces of the Crown.
Payments of the Council Tax Relief are payments designated as such

Addition.Substitution: under a Royal Warrant made under section 333 of the Armed Forces Act 2006

Title.Addition: Armed forces: Continuity of Education Allowance

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of payments of the Continuity of Education Allowance to or in respect of members of the armed forces of the Crown during their employment under the Crown or after their deaths.
The Continuity of Education Allowance is an allowance designated as such under a Royal Warrant made under section 333 of the Armed Forces Act 2006.
No liability to income tax arises in respect of payments of accommodation allowances to, or in respect of, a member of the armed forces of the Crown.
An “accommodation allowance” is an allowance—
payable out of the public revenue,
for, or towards, costs of accommodation, and
in respect of which any conditions specified in regulations made by the Treasury are met.
The provision that may be made by regulations under subsection (2)(c) includes provision framed by reference to a scheme (by whatever name called), or document, as it has effect from time to time.
Regulations under this section may make—
different provision for different cases, and
different provision for different areas.
Regulations under this section that do not increase any person's liability to income tax may have effect in relation to times before they are made.

P1group.Title: Reserve and auxiliary forces' training allowances

P1para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the following sums if they are payable out of the public revenue to members of the reserve and auxiliary forces of the Crown—

P3para.Text: training expenses allowances, and
bounties payable in consideration of the members undertaking certain training and attaining a particular standard of efficiency.

P1group.Title: Crown employees' foreign service allowances

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of an allowance paid to a person in employment under the Crown if it is certified to represent compensation for the extra cost of being obliged to live outside the United Kingdom in order to perform the duties of the employment.
A certificate under subsection (1) may only be given by—

P3para.Text: the Treasury,
the Secretary of State,
the Lord Chancellor,
the Chancellor of the Exchequer,
the Minister for the Civil Service,
the Lord President of the Council,
the Lord Privy Seal, or
the Attorney General.

Title.Addition: Voluntary office-holders: compensation for lost employment income

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a payment made by a relevant authority to a person if—
the person holds a voluntary office with the authority,
the person carries out duties of the office in a period in which he or she is also employed, and
the payment is made solely to compensate the person for lost employment income for the period (and accordingly does not exceed the amount of that income).
For the purposes of subsection (1) a person holds a voluntary office if, at the time the payment referred to in that subsection is made, the person—
is not entitled to any payment or benefit in connection with carrying out the duties of the office,
has not received any such payment or benefit, and
does not expect to receive any such payment or benefit.
For the purposes of subsection (2)(a), (b) and (c) disregard—
a payment

Addition.Addition: (whether an advance payment or a reimbursement)

Text.Addition: in respect of reasonable expenses incurred in carrying out the duties of the office, and
a payment to which subsection (1) or section 16A of
ITTOIA
2005 applies.
In subsection (1)(c) “lost employment income” means the difference between—

the amount of employment income, after deduction of tax and national insurance contributions, that the person would have received from the employment for the period if he or she had not carried out the duties of the office, and
the amount of employment income, after deduction of tax and national insurance contributions, that the person did receive from the employment for the period.
In subsection (1) “relevant authority” means any of the following—
A government department
The Welsh Ministers and the Counsel General to the Welsh Government
The Scottish Ministers
The holder of an office in the Scottish Administration which, for the purposes of the Scotland Act 1998, is not a ministerial office (see section 126(8) of that Act)
A Northern Ireland department
A county, district or parish council in England
The council of a London borough
The Common Council of the City of London
The Greater London Authority
The Council of the Isles of Scilly
A county, county borough or community council in Wales
A council constituted under section 2 of the Local Government
etc.
(Scotland) Act 1994 or community council in Scotland
A district council in Northern Ireland
An organisation the name of which is entered in the list maintained by the Certification Officer under section 2 of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992
An organisation the name of which is entered in the list maintained by the Certification Officer for Northern Ireland under Article 5 of the Industrial Relations (Northern Ireland) Order 1992 (
A Local Medical Committee (see section 97(4) of the National Health Service Act 2006)
A body (other than a company) that is established by or under a statutory provision for the purpose of carrying out functions conferred on it by or under a statutory provision.
In this section—
“company” means a company as defined by section 1 of the Companies Act 2006;
references to a relevant authority include a company the activities of which consist solely of carrying out some or all of the functions of that authority, otherwise than for profit;

“statutory provision” includes any provision made by or under an Act of Parliament, an Act of the Scottish Parliament, any Northern Ireland legislation, or any Act or Measure of the National Assembly for Wales.
Section 16A of
ITTOIA
2005 (voluntary office-holders: compensation for lost profits) contains equivalent provision for holders of a voluntary office who carry on a trade, profession or vocation.

Title.Addition: Voluntary office-holders: payments in respect of expenses

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a payment to a person who holds a voluntary office if the payment is in respect of reasonable expenses incurred in carrying out the duties of that office.
It does not matter whether—
the payment is an advance payment or a reimbursement;
the person who makes the payment is the person with whom the office is held.
Subsections (2) and (3) of section 299A apply for the purposes of subsection (1) of this section as they apply for the purposes of subsection (1) of that section.

P1group.Title: Consuls

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of income arising from the office of a consul in the United Kingdom in the service of a foreign state.
Such income is also to be disregarded in estimating the amount of income for any income tax purposes.
In this section “consul” means a person recognised by Her Majesty as being a consul-general, consul, vice-consul or consular agent.

P1group.Title: Official agents

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of income arising from employment as an official agent in the United Kingdom for a foreign state if conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that the employee is neither—

P3para.Text: a Commonwealth citizen, nor
a citizen of the Republic of Ireland.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that the functions of the employment are not exercised in connection with a trade, business or other undertaking carried on for the purposes of profit.
Such income is also to be disregarded in estimating the amount of income for any income tax purposes.
In this section “official agent” means a person who is not a consul (as defined in section 300) but is employed on the staff of—

P3para.Text: a consulate, or
an official department or agency of a foreign state.

P2para.Text: Subsection (5)(b) does not apply to a department or agency which carries on a trade, business or other undertaking for the purposes of profit.

P1group.Title: Consular employees

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of income arising from employment in the United Kingdom as a consular employee for a foreign state if—

P3para.Text: Her Majesty by Order in Council directs that this section applies to the foreign state for the purpose of giving effect to a reciprocal arrangement with that state, and
condition A or B is met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the employee is a national of the foreign state.
Condition B is that the employee is not a British citizen, a British overseas territories citizen, a British National (Overseas) or a British Overseas citizen.
In this section—

Para.Text: “consular employee” includes any person employed for the purposes of the official business of a consular officer at—
any consulate,
any consular establishment, or
any other premises used for those purposes, and

“reciprocal arrangement” means a consular convention or other arrangement with a foreign state, making similar provision to that made by this section , sections 646A and 681A of this Act and section 771 of ITTOIA 2005 (relevant foreign income of consular officers and employees) in the case of Her Majesty’s consular officers or employees in that state.

P2para.Text: An Order in Council under subsection (1) may limit the operation of this section in relation to a state in any way appearing to Her Majesty necessary or expedient having regard to the arrangement with the state.
Such an Order—

P3para.Text: may be made so as to have effect from a date earlier than that on which it is made, but not earlier than the arrangement in question comes into force, and
may contain such transitional provisions as appear to Her Majesty necessary or expedient.

P2para.Text: A statutory instrument containing such an Order is subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of the House of Commons.
This section does not affect section 301 (official agents).

Title.Emphasis: Visiting forces and staff of designated allied headquarters

P1group.Title: Visiting forces etc

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of earnings if—

P3para.Text: they are paid by the government of a designated country to a member of a visiting force of that country or of a civilian component of such a force, and
that person is not a British citizen, a British overseas territories citizen, a British National (Overseas) or a British Overseas citizen.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (1)—

P3para.Text: members of the armed forces of a designated country who are attached to a designated international military headquarters are treated as a visiting force of that country, and
whether a person is a member of a civilian component of such a force is to be determined accordingly.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of earnings if they are paid by a designated allied headquarters to an employee of a category for the time being agreed between Her Majesty’s government in the United Kingdom and the other members of the North Atlantic Council.

But where the employee is a British citizen, a British overseas territories citizen, a British National (Overseas) or a British Overseas citizen, subsection (3) only applies if it is necessary for it to do so to give effect to an agreement between parties to the North Atlantic Treaty.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of earnings if—
they are paid by the government of a designated country to a person belonging to the EU civilian staff, and
that person is not a British citizen, a British overseas territories citizen, a British National (Overseas) or a British Overseas citizen.

P2para.Text: Subsections (1) and (2) are to be interpreted as if—

P3para.Text: they were in Part 1 of the Visiting Forces Act 1952 (c. 67), and
references in that Act to a country to which a provision of that Act applies were references to a designated country.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “allied headquarters” means an international military headquarters established under the North Atlantic Treaty, ...
“designated” means designated for the purpose in question by or under an Order in Council made for giving effect to an international agreement, and

Text.Addition: ” means designated for the purpose in question by or under an Order in Council made for giving effect to an international agreement.

civilian personnel seconded by a member State to an EU institution for the purposes of activities (including exercises) relating to the preparation for, and execution of, tasks mentioned in Article 43(1) of the Treaty on European Union (tasks relating to a common security and defence policy), as amended from time to time, and
civilian personnel (other than locally hired personnel)—
made available to the EU by a member State to work with designated international military headquarters or a force of a designated country, or
otherwise made available to the EU by a member State for the purposes of activities of the kind referred to in paragraph (a).

P1group.Title: Experts seconded to European Commission

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of daily subsistence allowances paid by the European Commission to persons whose services are made available to the Commission by their employers under the detached national experts scheme.
“The detached national experts scheme” means—

P3para.Text: the scheme relating to national experts seconded to the European Commission which was established by the Commission on 26th July 1988, as it has effect for the time being, or
any scheme having effect for the time being which replaces that scheme.

Title.Addition: Experts seconded to other European Union bodies

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of any subsistence allowances paid by a relevant
body to persons who, because of their expertise in matters relating to the subject matter of the functions of the relevant
EU
body, have been seconded to the body by their employers.
Each of the following is a “relevant
EU
body”—
the European Medicines Agency, established as the European Agency for the Evaluation of Medicinal Products by Council Regulation
of 22 July 1993,
the European Police College, established by Council Decision of 20 September 2005 (2005/681/
the European Banking Authority, established by Regulation (
EU
) No 1093/2010 of 24 November 2010, and
any other body established by an
EU
instrument which is designated as a relevant
EU
body for the purposes of this section by an order made by the Treasury.

P1group.Title: Offshore oil and gas workers: mainland transfers

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of—

P3para.Text: the provision for an employee who has a permanent workplace at an offshore installation of—

P4para.Text: transfer transport,
related accommodation and subsistence, or
local transport, or

P3para.Text: the payment or reimbursement of reasonable expenses incurred by such an employee on such transport or accommodation and subsistence.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1)(a)(ii) only applies if the related accommodation and subsistence is provided at reasonable cost.
In this section “transfer transport” means transport by sea or air between the mainland of Great Britain or Northern Ireland and the offshore installation, which meets conditions A and B.
Condition A is that the place of arrival or departure on the mainland is one to or from which transport between the mainland and the offshore installation is provided for employees generally.
Condition B is that the cost of the transport would not be deductible under Part 5 if the employee incurred and paid it.
In this section—

Para.Text: “related accommodation and subsistence” means overnight accommodation and subsistence in the vicinity of the place of departure or arrival on the mainland, which is necessary because of the time at which transfer transport is to be taken,
“local transport” means transport between a place where the employee is provided with related accommodation and subsistence and the place of departure or arrival on the mainland,
“workplace” and “permanent workplace” have the meaning given by section 339.

P1group.Title: Miners etc: coal and allowances in lieu of coal

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision of coal or smokeless fuel or an allowance paid in lieu of such provision if the employee is a colliery worker and the condition in subsection (2) is met.
That condition is that the amount of coal or fuel provided or in respect of which the allowance is paid does not substantially exceed the amount reasonably required for personal use.
That condition is assumed to be met unless the contrary is shown.
In this section “colliery worker” means a coal miner or any other person employed at or about a colliery otherwise than in clerical, administrative or technical work.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of this section an individual is employed as a home care worker if the duties of the employment consist wholly or mainly of the provision of personal care to another individual (“
”) at the recipient's home, in a case where the recipient is in need of personal care because of—
old age,
mental or physical disability,
past or present dependence on alcohol or drugs,
past or present illness, or
past or present mental disorder.

No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of the provision of board or lodging (or both) to an individual employed as a home care worker if the provision is—
on a reasonable scale,
at the recipient's home, and
by reason of the individual's employment as a home care worker.

Title.Addition: Limited exemption for sporting testimonial payments

Text.Addition: This section applies to any sporting testimonial payments which are—
made out of money raised by a sporting testimonial (“the sporting testimonial”), and
treated by virtue of section 226E as earnings of a person (“S”).
No liability to income tax arises in respect of sporting testimonial payments to which this section applies.
Subsection (2) has effect subject to and in accordance with the following provisions.
It only applies—
if the controller of the relevant event or activity (or of all the relevant events or activities in a series) constituting the sporting testimonial is an independent person,
if S has not already benefitted from an exemption under this section in relation to one or more sporting testimonial payments made out of money raised by another sporting testimonial, and

where the sporting testimonial consists of a series of relevant events or activities taking place over more than a year, if the sporting testimonial payment is made out of money raised by events or activities taking place within the period of one year beginning with the day on which the first event or activity in the series took place.
It only applies to the first £100,000 of sporting testimonial payments made out of money raised by the sporting testimonial.

If sporting testimonial payments are made (out of money raised by the sporting testimonial) in two or more tax years, any part of the exempt amount that is not used in the first of those years is to be carried forward to the next tax year (and so on).

This section applies to sporting testimonial payments made to or to the order of the personal representatives of S (where S has died) but only if the payments are made within the period of 24 months beginning with the date of death.
In subsection (4)(a) “
” means a person who is not (or where the controller is a committee, a committee none of whose members are)—
S or a person connected with S,
an employer or former employer of S or a person connected with an employer or former employer of S, or
a person acting for or on behalf of a person mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b).
If the first relevant event or activity in a series took place before 6 April 2017, subsection (4)(c) has effect as if it referred to the year beginning with 6 April 2017.
Section 993 of ITA 2007 (meaning of “connected” persons) has effect for the purposes of this section.
Terms used in this section and section 226E have the same meaning as in that section.

P1group.Title: Death or retirement benefit provision

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of provision made by an employee’s employer under a registered pension scheme or otherwise for a retirement or death benefit.

Text.Addition: Subsection (1) does not apply to provision made for insuring against the risk that a retirement or death benefit under an employer-financed retirement benefits scheme cannot be paid or given because of the employer’s insolvency.

In subsection (1A)
“
” has the same meaning as in Chapter 2 of Part 6 (see section 393A).

P2para.Text: In this section “retirement or death benefit” means a pension, annuity, lump sum, gratuity or other similar benefit which will be paid or given to the employee , or paid or given in respect of the employee to any other individual or to a charity, in the event of the employee’s retirement or death.

Title.Substitution: Exemption of contributions to registered pension scheme

Text.Substitution: No liability to income tax arises in respect of earnings where an employee’s employer makes contributions under a registered pension scheme

Title.Addition: Exemption of contributions to overseas pension scheme

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of earnings where an employer makes contributions under a qualifying overseas pension scheme in respect of an employee who is a relevant migrant member of the pension scheme.
In subsection (1)—
”, and
have the same meaning as in Schedule 33 to FA 2004 (overseas pension schemes: migrant member relief).

Title.Addition: Independent advice in respect of conversions and transfers of pension scheme benefits

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of—
the provision to an employee or former employee of appropriate independent advice, or
the payment or reimbursement, to or in respect of an employee or former employee, of the cost of such advice,
if conditions A to C are met.

Condition A is that the provision, payment or reimbursement is required by regulations under section 49 or 52 of the Pension Schemes Act 2015 (power to require employer to arrange independent advice in respect of conversions and transfers).

If condition A is met only as respects part of the payment or reimbursement because the amount of the payment or reimbursement exceeds the amount required to be paid or reimbursed, subsection (1) applies in respect of that part.
Condition B is that the provision, payment or reimbursement is not pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements.
Condition C is that such other requirements as may be specified in regulations made by the Treasury are satisfied in relation to the provision, payment or reimbursement.
In this section—
“appropriate independent advice”—
in relation to England and Wales and Scotland, has the meaning given by regulations under section 48 of the Pension Schemes Act 2015;
in relation to Northern Ireland, has the meaning given by regulations under section 51 of that Act;

” means arrangements (whenever made, whether before or after the employment began) under which an employee gives up the right to receive an amount of general earnings or specific employment income in return for the provision of appropriate independent advice or the payment or reimbursement of the cost of such advice.

Title.Addition: Provision of pensions advice: limited exemption

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of—
the provision of relevant pensions advice to an employee or former or prospective employee, or
the payment or reimbursement of costs incurred, by or in respect of an employee or former or prospective employee, in obtaining relevant pensions advice,
if Condition A or B is met.
But subsection (1) does not apply in relation to a person in a tax year so far as the value of the exemption in the person's case in that year exceeds £500.
The “
”, in relation to a person and a tax year, is the amount exempted by subsection (1) from income tax in the person's case in that year, disregarding subsection (2) for this purpose.

If in a tax year there is in relation to an individual more than one person who is an employer or former employer, subsections (1) to (3) apply in relation to the individual as employee or former or prospective employee of any one of those persons separately from their application in relation to the individual as employee or former or prospective employee of any other of those persons.
”, in relation to a person, means information, or advice, in connection with—
the person's pension arrangements, or
the use of the person's pension funds.
Condition A is that the relevant pensions advice, or payment or reimbursement, is provided under a scheme that is open—
to the employer's employees generally, or
generally to the employer's employees at a particular location.

Condition B is that the relevant pensions advice, or payment or reimbursement, is provided under a scheme that is open generally to the employer's employees, or generally to those of the employer's employees at a particular location, who—
have reached the minimum qualifying age, or
meet the ill-health condition.
The “
”, in relation to an employee, means the employee's relevant pension age less 5 years.
”, in relation to an employee, means—

Addition.Substitution: of Schedule 36 to FA 2004 apply in relation to the employee, the lowest protected pension age that applies as a result of those paragraphs (in relation to the employee or, as the case may be, to sums or assets that relate to the employee), or

Text.Addition: in any other case, the employee's normal minimum pension age, as defined by section 279(1) of FA 2004.

The “ill-health condition” is met by an employee if the employer is satisfied, on the basis of evidence provided by a registered medical practitioner, that the employee is (and will continue to be) incapable of carrying on his or her occupation because of physical or mental impairment.

P1group.Title: Limited exemptions for statutory redundancy payments

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax in respect of earnings arises by virtue of a redundancy payment or an approved contractual payment, except where subsection (2) applies.
Where an approved contractual payment exceeds the amount which would have been due if a redundancy payment had been payable, the excess is liable to income tax.

No liability to income tax in respect of employment income other than earnings arises by virtue of a redundancy payment or an approved contractual payment, except where it does so by virtue of Chapter 3 of Part 6 (payments and benefits on termination of employment etc.).
For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: a statutory payment in respect of a redundancy payment is to be treated as paid on account of the redundancy payment, and
a statutory payment in respect of an approved contractual payment is to be treated as paid on account of the approved contractual payment.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “approved contractual payment” means a payment to a person on the termination of the person’s employment under an agreement in respect of which an order is in force under section 157 of ERA 1996 or Article 192 of ER(NI)O 1996,
“redundancy payment” means a redundancy payment under Part 11 of ERA 1996 or Part 12 of ER(NI)O 1996, and
“statutory payment” means a payment under section 167(1) of ERA 1996 or Article 202(1) of ER(NI)O 1996.

P2para.Text: In subsection (5) “employment”, in relation to a person, has the meaning given in section 230(5) of ERA 1996 or Article 3(5) of ER(NI)O 1996.

P1group.Title: Counselling and other outplacement services

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of—

P3para.Text: the provision of services to a person in connection with the cessation of the person’s employment, or
the payment or reimbursement of—

P4para.Text: fees for such provision, or
travelling expenses incurred in connection with such provision,

P3para.Text: if conditions A to D and, in the case of travel expenses, condition E are met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the only or main purpose of the provision of the services is to enable the person to do either or both of the following—

P3para.Text: to adjust to the cessation of the employment, or
to find other gainful employment (including self-employment).

P2para.Text: Condition B is that the services consist wholly of any or all of the following—

P3para.Text: giving advice and guidance,
imparting or improving skills,
providing or making available the use of office equipment or similar facilities.

P2para.Text: Condition C is that the person has been employed ... in the employment which is ceasing throughout the period of 2 years ending—

P3para.Text: at the time when the services begin to be provided, or
if earlier, at the time when the employment ceases.

P2para.Text: Condition D is that the opportunity to receive the services, on similar terms as to payment or reimbursement of any expenses incurred in connection with their provision, is available—

P3para.Text: generally to employees or former employees of the person’s employer in that employment, or
to a particular class or classes of them.

P2para.Text: Condition E is that the travel expenses are expenses—

P3para.Text: in respect of which, on the assumptions in subsection (7), mileage allowance relief under Chapter 2 of this Part would be available if no mileage allowance payments had been made, or
which, on those assumptions, would be deductible under Part 5.

P2para.Text: The assumptions are—

P3para.Text: that receiving the services is one of the duties of the employee’s employment,
that the employee incurs and pays the expenses, and
if the employment has in fact ceased, that it continues.

P2para.Text: In this section “mileage allowance payments” has the meaning given by section 229(2).

P1group.Title: Retraining courses

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the payment or reimbursement of retraining course expenses by a person (“the employer”) if the course conditions, the employment conditions and, in the case of travel expenses, the conditions in subsection (5) are met.
In subsection (1) “retraining course expenses” means—

P3para.Text: fees for the attendance of another person (“the employee”) at a training course,
travelling expenses incurred in connection with it,
fees for an examination taken during or at the end of it, or
the cost of any books which are essential for a person attending it.

P2para.Text: The course conditions are that—

P3para.Text: the course provides training designed to impart or improve skills or knowledge relevant to, and intended to be used in the course of, gainful employment (including self-employment) of any description,
it is entirely devoted to the teaching or practical application (or both) of the skills or knowledge, and
it lasts no more than two years. ...

P2para.Text: The employment conditions are that—

P3para.Text: the employee begins the course while employed by the employer or within the period of one year after the employment ceases,

the employee ceases to be employed by the employer before the end of the period of 2 years beginning at the end of the course and is not re-employed by the employer within the period of 2 years after so ceasing,
the employee is employed ... in the employment which is ceasing throughout the period of 2 years ending—

P4para.Text: when the employee begins the course, or
if earlier, when the employment ceases, and

P3para.Text: the opportunity to undertake the course, on similar terms as to payment or reimbursement of amounts within subsection (1), is available—

P4para.Text: generally to the employee’s fellow employees or former fellow employees in that employment, or
to a particular class or classes of them.

P2para.Text: The travel expenses must be—

P3para.Text: expenses in respect of which, on the assumptions in subsection (6), mileage allowance relief under Chapter 2 of this Part would be available if no mileage allowance payments had been made, or
expenses which, on those assumptions, would be deductible under Part 5.

P2para.Text: The assumptions are—

P3para.Text: that attendance at the course is one of the duties of the employee’s employment,
that the employee incurs and pays the expenses, and
if the employee has in fact ceased to be employed by the employer, that the employee continues to be employed by the employer.

P2para.Text: In this section “mileage allowance payments” has the meaning given by section 229(2).

P1group.Title: Recovery of tax

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: a person’s liability to tax for a tax year has been determined on the assumption that section 311(1) applies, and
subsequently—

P4para.Text: the condition in section 311(4)(a) is not met because of the person’s failure to begin the course within the period of one year after ceasing to be employed, or
the condition in section 311(4)(b) is not met because of the person’s continued employment or re-employment.

P2para.Text: An assessment of an amount or further amount of tax due as a result of the condition not being met may be made under section 29(1) of TMA 1970.
Such an assessment must be made before the end of the period of 6 years immediately following the end of the tax year in which subsection (1) first applies.

If subsection (1)(b)(i) or (ii) applies, the person’s employer or former employer must give an officer of Revenue and Customs a notice containing particulars of the person’s failure to begin the course or continued employment or re-employment within 60 days of coming to know of it.

If an officer of Revenue and Customs has reason to believe that a person has failed to give such a notice, the officer may by notice require the person to provide such information as the officer may reasonably require for the purposes of this section about—

P3para.Text: the failure to begin the course,
the continued employment, or
the re-employment.

P2para.Text: A notice under subsection (5) may specify a time (not less than 60 days) within which the required information must be provided.

Title.Addition: Exemptions: bonus payments by certain employers
Limited exemption for qualifying bonus payments

Text.Addition: This section applies in relation to qualifying bonus payments made, in a tax year (“the tax year”), by an employer which is a company to an employee or former employee of the employer.

No liability to income tax arises in respect of the qualifying bonus payments if, or to the extent that, the total chargeable amount in respect of those payments does not exceed £3,600 (“the exempt amount”).

If qualifying bonus payments are made to the same person by two or more employers in the tax year, subsection (2) applies separately in relation to the total payments made by each employer, unless subsection (4) applies.

If two or more employers are members of the same group at the time each of them first makes a qualifying bonus payment to the employee or former employee in the tax year, subsection (2) applies as if the reference to the qualifying bonus payments were to all the qualifying bonus payments made by those employers to the employee or former employee in that tax year.
If, in a tax year—
an employer makes a payment when it is a member of a group, and
later in that tax year the employer ceases to be a member of that group,
the employer is treated for the purposes of this section as remaining a member of that group for the remainder of the tax year (without prejudice to it also being a member of any other group).
In applying subsection (2)—
the exempt amount is set against payments in the order in which they are made, and

if two or more payments are made on the same day, which together take the total payments made in the tax year over the exempt amount, subsection (7) applies to determine the amount of each of those payments which is exempt.
In a case within subsection (6)(b), the amount of a payment which is exempt is given by the formula—
where—
P is the amount of the payment,
SP is the sum of that payment and the other payments made on the same day, and
REA is so much of the exempt amount as remains after taking account of any qualifying bonus payments previously made in the tax year.
Where subsection (2) applies separately to different payments by virtue of subsection (3), subsections (6) and (7) also apply to those payments separately.
The Treasury may by order increase or reduce the sum of money specified in subsection (2).

A statutory instrument containing an order under this section which reduces the sum of money specified may not be made unless a draft of it has been laid before and approved by a resolution of the House of Commons.

In this section “chargeable amount”, in respect of a qualifying bonus payment, means the amount of employment income which would be charged to tax in respect of that qualifying bonus payment, apart from this section.
A payment made by an employer (“E”) to an employee or former employee is a qualifying bonus payment if—
it does not consist of regular salary or wages,
it is awarded under a scheme which meets the participation requirement and the equality requirement (see section 312C),
E meets the trading requirement (see section 312D) throughout the qualifying period,
E meets the indirect employee-ownership requirement (see section 312E) throughout the qualifying period,

E meets the office-holder requirement (see section 312F) at the time the payment is made and on at least the requisite number of days in the qualifying period (whether or not those days are consecutive),
E is not a service company (see section 312G),
the payment is not excluded (see section 312H), and
where it is a payment to a former employee, it is made in the period of 12 months beginning with the day the employment ceased.
In this section “
”, in relation to a payment, means the period of 12 months ending with the day on which the payment is made.
But in a case where E meets the indirect employee-ownership requirement on the day on which the payment is made—
if the controlling interest requirement was first met during that 12 month period, the qualifying period does not include any time before it was met, and
if the all-employee benefit requirement was first met during that 12 month period, the qualifying period does not include any time before that requirement was met.
In this section “
” means—
if the qualifying period is 12 months, the number of days in that period reduced by 90, and
if the qualifying period is a shorter period by virtue of subsection (3), the number of days in that period reduced by the corresponding fraction of 90 days.

Title.Addition: Section 312B: the participation and equality requirements

Text.Addition: For the purposes of section 312B—
the participation requirement is that all persons in relevant employment when the award is determined must be eligible to participate in that and any other award under the scheme, and
the equality requirement is that every employee who participates in an award under the scheme must do so on the same terms.
A person is in “relevant employment” if—
where E is a member of a group, the person is employed by any company which is a member of the group, and
in any other case, the person is employed by E.

Addition.Addition: The participation requirement is not infringed by reason of the exclusion of directors of the company from participating in an award.

Text.Addition: The participation requirement is not infringed by reason of a person in relevant employment being excluded from participating in an award because, at the time the award is determined, the person has less than the minimum period of continuous service in relevant employment required by E.
But the minimum period required by E for this purpose must not exceed 12 months.
The participation requirement is not infringed—
by reason of a person being excluded from participating in an award where—
disciplinary proceedings have been taken against the person by E which have resulted in a finding of gross misconduct against the person, and
that finding was made in the period of 12 months immediately before the time the award is determined,

by reason of a person's eligibility to participate in an award being conditional, in a case where the person is at the time of the award subject to disciplinary proceedings taken by E, upon those proceedings being concluded and no finding of gross misconduct being made against that person, or
by a person being treated as never having been eligible to participate in an award where, after the award was made but before the payment is made—
a finding of gross misconduct is made against that person in disciplinary proceedings taken by E after the award was made, or
that person is summarily dismissed from the employment.
The equality requirement is infringed if the amount of an award to an employee under the scheme is determined by reference to factors other than those mentioned in subsection (6).
The equality requirement is not infringed by reason of the amount of an award under the scheme to employees participating in the award being determined by reference to—
an employee's remuneration,
an employee's length of service, or
hours worked by an employee;
but this is subject to subsections (7) and (8).
The equality requirement is infringed if an award is made on terms such that some (but not all) of the employees participating in the award receive nothing.
If the amount of an award is determined by reference to more than one of the factors mentioned in subsection (6), the equality requirement is infringed unless—
each factor gives rise to a separate entitlement related to the level of remuneration, length of service or (as the case may be) hours worked, and
the total entitlement is the sum of those separate entitlements.

Subject to subsection (6), the equality requirement is infringed if any feature of the scheme has, or is likely to have, the effect of conferring benefits wholly or mainly on those participating in the award who are—
directors or former directors, or
employees receiving the higher or highest levels of remuneration, or
employees who—
are employed in a particular part of the business carried on by E or, if E is a member of a group, the group, or
carry on particular kinds of activities.

In subsections (1)(b), (5), (6), (7) and (9) references to an employee include a former employee, so, when applying those subsections in relation to a former employee, any reference to remuneration, length of service, hours worked, being employed in a particular part of a business or carrying on particular activities is to be read as relating to that former employment.
For the purposes of section 312B, a company meets the trading requirement if—
it is a trading company which is not a member of a group, or
