it is a member of a trading group.
” means a company carrying on trading activities whose activities do not include to a substantial extent activities other than trading activities.
” means a group—
one or more of whose members carry on trading group activities, and
the activities of whose members, taken together, do not include to a substantial extent activities other than trading group activities.
In this section—
” means activities carried on by the company in the course of, or for the purposes of, a trade being carried on by it;
” means activities carried on by a member of the group in the course of, or for the purposes of, a trade being carried on by any member of the group.
For the purposes of determining whether a company is a trading company or a member of a trading group—
the activities of the members of a group are to be treated as one business (with the result that activities are disregarded to the extent that they are intra-group activities), and
a business carried on by a company in partnership with one or more other persons is to be treated as not being a trading activity.
For the purposes of section 312B, a company meets the indirect employee-ownership requirement if—
a settlement meets the controlling interest requirement in respect of—
the company, or
if the company is a member of a trading group, but not the principal company, that principal company, and
the settlement meets the all-employee benefit requirement.
For this purpose—
section 236M of
TCGA
1992 applies to determine if a settlement meets the controlling interest requirement in respect of the company mentioned in subsection (1)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be), and
sections 236J and 236K of that Act apply to determine if the settlement meets the all-employee benefit requirement (but see subsection (3)).
If a settlement would not otherwise meet the all-employee benefit requirement at any time during the qualifying period, section 236L of
TCGA
1992 applies for the purposes of subsection (1)(b), unless the all-employee benefit requirement has (ignoring that section) previously been met at any time in the period—
beginning with 10 December 2013, and
ending immediately before that time.
For the purposes of subsections (2) and (3)—
in sections 236I to 236M of
TCGA
1992 references to C are to be read as references to the company in respect of which the settlement is required to meet the controlling interest requirement (see subsection (1)(a)), and

section 236L of that Act applies as if the reference in subsection (1)(c) of that section to the period of 12 months ending with the time in question were a reference to the period of 12 months ending with the date the payment is made (even if the qualifying period is a period of less than 12 months by virtue of section 312B(3)).
For the purposes of section 312B, a company meets the officer-holder requirement if the appropriate fraction does not exceed 2/5.
” means—
where—
ND is the number of persons who are one or both of the following—
a director or other office-holder of the company;
an employee of the company connected with a person within paragraph (a);
NE is the number of persons who are employees (or office-holders) of the company.
For the purposes of section 312B, “
” means—
a managed service company within the meaning of section 61B, or
a company (“SC”) in respect of which Conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that the business carried on by SC consists substantially of the provision of the services of persons employed by it.
Condition B is that the majority of those services are provided to persons—
to whom subsection (4) applies, but
who are not members of the same group as the company which makes the payment.
This subsection applies to—
a person who controls or has controlled, or two or more persons who together control or have controlled, SC or any company of which SC is a 51% subsidiary at the time the payment is made,
a person who, or two or more persons who together, at any time before the time the payment is made—
employed all or a majority of the employees of SC, or
employed all or a majority of the employees of SC and other companies which are members of the same group as SC at the time the payment is made (taken together), and
any company which is a 51% subsidiary of, controlled by or connected or associated with, any person within paragraph (a) or (b).
For the purposes of subsection (4)—
a partnership is to be treated as a single person, and
where a partner (alone or together with others) has control of a company, the partnership is to be treated as having (in the same way) control of that company.
The following provisions apply for the purposes of this section—
section 449 of CTA 2010 (“associated company”);
section 995 of ITA 2007 (meaning of “control”);
section 286 of
TCGA
1992 (connected persons: interpretation).
For the purposes of section 312B, a payment is “excluded” if the employee is a party to arrangements (whether made before or after the beginning of the employee's employment) under which—
the employee gives up the right to receive an amount of general earnings or specific employment income in return for the provision of the payment, or
the employee and employer agree that the employee is to receive the payment rather than receive some other description of employment income.
In this section references to an employee include a former employee.
In this Chapter—
” has the meaning given by section 170(9) of
TCGA
” means any trade which is conducted on a commercial basis and with a view to the realisation of profits.
In this Chapter—
references to a group, to membership of a group, to the principal company of a group or to being members of the same group, are to be construed in accordance with section 170 of
TCGA
references to a group are to be construed with any necessary modifications where applied to a company incorporated under the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom.
For the purposes of this Chapter, a payment is treated as made when it would be treated as received for the purposes of Chapter 4 of Part 2 if it were not a qualifying bonus payment (see section 18).

In this Chapter references to a payment to an employee or former employee include a payment to the personal representatives of an employee or former employee who has died if the payment is made within the period of 12 months beginning with the date of death.

P1group.Title: Repairs and alterations to living accommodation

P2para.Text: This section applies where living accommodation is provided by reason of a person’s employment.
No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of—

P3para.Text: alterations and additions to the premises which are of a structural nature, or
landlord’s repairs to the premises.

P2para.Text: In this section “landlord’s repairs” means repairs of a kind which are the obligation of the lessor under the covenants implied by section 11(1) of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 (c. 70) (lessor’s repairing obligations in short leases) where premises are let under a lease to which that section applies.

P1group.Title: Council tax etc. paid for certain living accommodation

P2para.Text: This section applies if living accommodation provided for an employee falls within the exception in one of the following provisions—

Para.Text: section 99(1) (accommodation necessary for proper performance of duties),
section 99(2) (accommodation provided for better performance of duties), or
section 100 (accommodation provided as a result of security threat).

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of—

P3para.Text: any payment to, for or on behalf of the employee, or
any reimbursement of any payment by the employee,

P2para.Text: in respect of council tax or rates, or water or sewerage charges, in respect of the accommodation.

P1group.Title: Limited exemption for expenses connected with certain living accommodation

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: living accommodation is provided for an employee in a tax year, and
conditions A and B are met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the accommodation falls within the exception in one of the following provisions—

Para.Text: section 99(1) (accommodation necessary for proper performance of duties),
section 99(2) (accommodation provided for better performance of duties), or
section 100 (accommodation provided as a result of security threat).

P2para.Text: Condition B is that there is an amount of earnings from the employment in the tax year by virtue of expenditure, or the reimbursement to the employee of expenditure, on—

P3para.Text: heating, lighting or cleaning the premises,
repairs to the premises, their maintenance or decoration, or
the provision in the premises of furniture, equipment or other items which are normal for domestic occupation.

P2para.Text: If this section applies, no liability to income tax arises in respect of the earnings mentioned in subsection (3) to the extent that they exceed—

Para.Text: where—
DA is the number of reckonable days in the tax year (a “reckonable day” being a day on which—
(a) the accommodation is provided, and
(b) the employment is held by the employee),
DE is—
(a) the number of days in that year, or
(b) if the employment is held for only part of that year, the number of days in that part,
NE is the net amount of the earnings from the employment in the tax year (see subsection (5)),
SMG is, where the expenses are incurred by a person other than the employee, so much of any sum made good by the employee to that other person as is properly attributable to the expenses.

P2para.Text: To calculate the net amount of the earnings from the employment—
Take the earnings from the employment, leaving out of account the expenses in question.
Add, in the case of employment by a company, the earnings from any employment by an associated company.
A company is “associated” with another for this purpose if one has control of the other or both are under the control of the same person.
Deduct any deductions allowable under—

P3para.Text: section 232 (giving effect to mileage allowance relief) or Part 5 of this Act,

Text.Substitution: sections 188 to 194 of FA 2004 (contributions to registered pension schemes), or

P3para.Text: section 262 of CAA 2001 (capital allowances to be given effect by treating them as deductions from earnings).

P1group.Title: Accommodation, supplies and services used in employment duties

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of the provision for an employee of accommodation, supplies or services used by the employee in performing duties of the employment if conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that any use of the accommodation, supplies or services for private purposes by the employee or members of the employee’s family or household is not significant.
For this purpose, use “for private purposes” means—

P3para.Text: use that is not use in performing the duties of the employee’s employment, and
use that is at the same time both use in performing the duties of an employee’s employment and other use.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that where the provision is otherwise than on premises occupied by the person making it—

P3para.Text: its sole purpose is to enable the employee to perform the duties of the employee’s employment, and
what is provided is not an excluded benefit.

P2para.Text: The following are excluded benefits unless regulations under subsection (6) provide otherwise—

P3para.Text: a motor vehicle, boat or aircraft, and
a benefit that involves—

P4para.Text: the extension, conversion or alteration of living accommodation, or
the construction, extension, conversion or alteration of a building or other structure on land adjacent to and enjoyed with such accommodation.

P2para.Text: The Treasury may make provision by regulations as to what is an excluded benefit for the purposes of subsection (4)(b).
The regulations may provide that a benefit is an excluded benefit only if such conditions as may be prescribed are met as to the terms on which, and persons to whom, it is provided.

Title.Addition: Accommodation, supplies and services used in employment duties: payment or reimbursement of expenses

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the payment or reimbursement of expenses incurred by an employee on behalf of the employer in respect of the provision for the employee of accommodation, supplies or services if conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that, at the time the accommodation, supplies or services are first provided, the intention of the employer is that—
they will be used by the employee in performing duties of the employment, and
any use of them for private purposes by the employee or members of the employee’s family or household will not be significant.
Condition B is that where the provision is otherwise than on premises occupied by the employer—
its sole purpose is to enable the employee to perform the duties of the employee’s employment, and
what is provided is not an excluded benefit.
In this section “
” and “
” have the same meaning as in section 316.

This section applies where an employer makes a payment to an employee in respect of reasonable additional household expenses which the employee incurs in carrying out duties of the employment at home under homeworking arrangements.
No liability to income tax arises in respect of the payment.
In this section, in relation to an employee—
” means arrangements between the employee and the employer under which the employee regularly performs some or all of the duties of the employment at home; and
” means expenses connected with the day to day running of the employee’s home.

P1group.Title: Subsidised meals

Text.Substitution: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision for an employee by the employer of free or subsidised meals if they are provided—
in a canteen, or
on the employer’s business premises,
and conditions A to
are met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the meals are provided on a reasonable scale.
Condition B is that all the employer’s employees or all of them at a particular location may obtain one or both of the following—

P3para.Text: a free or subsidised meal, or
a free or subsidised meal voucher or token.

P2para.Text: Condition C is that if the meals are provided in the restaurant or dining room of a hotel or a catering or similar business at a time when meals are being served to the public—

P3para.Text: part of the restaurant or dining room is designated for the use of employees only, and
the meals are taken in that part.

Text.Addition: Condition D is that the provision is not pursuant to—
relevant salary sacrifice arrangements, or
relevant flexible remuneration arrangements.

P2para.Text: In this section “free or subsidised meal voucher or token” means a voucher, ticket, pass or other document or token which—

P3para.Text: is intended to enable a person to obtain a meal, and
is provided to the employee free of charge or for less than the cost of the meals to be obtained by it.

Text.Addition: In this section—

” means arrangements (whenever made, whether before or after the employment began) under which the employee gives up the right to receive an amount of general earnings or specific employment income in return for the provision of free or subsidised meals;

” means arrangements (whenever made, whether before or after the employment began) under which the employee and employer agree that the employee is to be provided with free or subsidised meals rather than receive some other description of employment income.

P2para.Text: In this section “meals” includes light refreshments.

P1group.Title: Childcare: exemption for employer-provided care

Substitution.Substitution: No liability to income tax arises

For the meaning of “care” and “child”, see section 318B.
If those conditions are met only as respects part of the provision, no such liability arises in respect of that part.
Condition A is that the child—
is a child or stepchild of the employee and is maintained (wholly or partly) at the employee’s expense,
is resident with the employee, or
is a person in respect of whom the employee has parental responsibility.
For the meaning of “parental responsibility”, see section 318B.
Condition B is that—
the premises on which the care is provided are not used wholly or mainly as a private dwelling, and
any applicable registration requirement is met.
The registration requirements are—
in

Condition C is that—
the premises on which the care is provided are made available by the scheme employer alone, or
the partnership requirements are met.
In this section “
” means the employer operating the scheme under which the care is provided (who need not be the employer of the employee).
The partnership requirements are—
that the care is provided under arrangements made by persons who include the scheme employer,
that the premises on which it is provided are made available by one or more of those persons, and
that under the arrangements the scheme employer is wholly or partly responsible for financing and managing the provision of the care.
Condition D is that the care is provided under a scheme that is open—
to the scheme employer’s employees generally, or
generally to those of the scheme employer’s employees at a particular location,

and that the employee to whom it is provided is either an employee of the scheme employer or is an employee working at the same location as employees of the scheme employer to whom the scheme is open.

Title.Addition: Eye tests and special corrective appliances

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision for an employee of—
an eye and eyesight test, or
special corrective appliances that an eye and eyesight test shows are necessary,
if conditions A and B are met.

Addition.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the payment or reimbursement of expenses incurred by an employee in respect of the provision for the employee of a test or appliances of the kind mentioned in subsection (1) if conditions A and B are met.

Text.Addition: Condition A is that the provision of the test or appliances is required by regulations made under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974.

Condition B is that tests and appliances of the kind mentioned in subsection (1) are made available generally to those employees of the employer in question for whom they are required to be provided by the regulations

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision for an employee, on behalf of an employer, of a health-screening assessment or a medical check-up.
Subsection (1) does not apply—
to more than one health-screening assessment provided in a tax year by any one employer or by any of a number of persons who are employers of the employee at the same time, or
to more than one medical check-up so provided.
In this section—
” means an assessment to identify employees who might be at particular risk of ill-health, and
” means a physical examination of the employee by a health professional for (and only for) determining the employee's state of health.
No liability to income tax arises in respect of—
the provision to an employee of recommended medical treatment, or
the payment or reimbursement, to or in respect of an employee, of the cost of such treatment,
if that provision, payment or reimbursement is not pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements or relevant flexible remuneration arrangements.
But subsection (1) does not apply in a tax year if, and to the extent that, the value of the exemption in that year exceeds £500.
Medical treatment is “recommended” if it is provided to the employee in accordance with a recommendation which—
is made to the employee as part of occupational health services provided to the employee by a service provided—
under section 2 of the Employment and Training Act 1973 (arrangements for the purpose of assisting persons to retain employment
etc
), or
by, or in accordance with arrangements made by, the employer,
is made for the purpose of assisting the employee to return to work after a period of absence due to injury or ill health, and
meets any other requirements specified in regulations made by the Treasury.
Regulations under subsection (3)(c) may, in particular, specify that the recommendation must be one given after the employee has been assessed as unfit for work—
for at least the specified number of consecutive days, and
in the specified manner by a person of a specified description.
The Treasury may by order amend subsection (3)(a) so as to add, amend or remove a reference to any enactment.
“The value of the exemption”, in a tax year, is an amount equal to the sum of—
all earnings within section 62 (earnings), and
all earnings which are treated as such under the benefits code,
in respect of which subsection (1) would prevent liability to income tax from arising in the tax year disregarding subsection (2).
In this section—
” means all procedures for diagnosing or treating any physical or mental illness, infirmity or defect;

” means arrangements (whenever made, whether before or after the employment began) under which the employee and employer agree that the employee is to be provided with recommended medical treatment or the cost of such treatment is to be paid or reimbursed, rather than the employee receiving some other description of employment income;
” means specified in regulations under subsection (3)(c).
No liability to income tax arises in respect of the provision for an employee of an influenza vaccination if the provision is not made pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements.

No liability to income tax arises in respect of the payment or reimbursement of expenses incurred by an employee in respect of the provision for the employee of an influenza vaccination if the payment or reimbursement is not made pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements.
In this section “

” means arrangements (whenever made, whether before or after the employment began) under which the employee gives up the right to receive an amount of general earnings or specific employment income in return for the provision of an influenza vaccination or the payment or reimbursement of the cost of such a vaccination.

P1group.Title: Suggestion awards

P2para.Text: This section applies where an employer establishes a scheme for the making of suggestions that is open on the same terms—

P3para.Text: to employees of the employer generally, or
to a particular description of them.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of an encouragement award or financial benefit award made under the scheme for a suggestion which meets conditions A to C if, or to the extent that, it does not exceed the permitted maximum for the award under section 322.
Condition A is that the suggestion relates to the activities carried on by the employer.
Condition B is that the suggestion is made by an employee who could not reasonably be expected to make it in the course of the duties of the employment, having regard to the employee’s experience.
Condition C is that the suggestion is not made at a meeting held for the purpose of proposing suggestions.
In this section and section 322—

Para.Text: “encouragement award” means an award, other than a financial benefit award, made for a suggestion with intrinsic merit or showing special effort, and

“financial benefit award” means an award for a suggestion relating to an improvement in efficiency or effectiveness which the employer has decided to adopt and reasonably expects will result in a financial benefit.

P1group.Title: Suggestion awards: “the permitted maximum”

P2para.Text: The permitted maximum for an encouragement award for the purposes of section 321 (suggestion awards) is £25.
The permitted maximum for a financial benefit award where no such award for the suggestion has been made before is—

P3para.Text: if only one such award is made for the suggestion, the suggestion maximum, and
if two or more such awards are made on the same occasion to different persons for the suggestion, the appropriate proportion of the suggestion maximum.

P2para.Text: If on a later occasion or occasions one or more further such awards are made for the same suggestion, the permitted maximum for each is—

P3para.Text: if only one such award is made for the suggestion on that occasion, the residue of the suggestion maximum, and
if two or more such awards are made on the same occasion to different persons for the suggestion, the appropriate proportion of that residue.

P2para.Text: The suggestion maximum for a financial benefit award is the financial benefit share or £5000 if that is less.
In subsection (4) “the financial benefit share” means the greater of—

P3para.Text: half the financial benefit reasonably expected to result from the adoption of the suggestion for the first year after its adoption, and
one-tenth of the financial benefit reasonably expected to result from its adoption for the first 5 years after its adoption.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “the appropriate proportion” means such proportion as the award bears to the total of the financial benefit awards made on the same occasion for the suggestion,
“the residue of the suggestion maximum” means the suggestion maximum less the total previous exemption, and
“the total previous exemption” means the total of the amounts exempted from income tax under section 321 in respect of financial benefit awards for the suggestion made on previous occasions.

P1group.Title: Long service awards

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a long service award which meets the condition in subsection (3) if or to the extent that the chargeable amount does not exceed the permitted maximum.
In subsection (1)—

Para.Text: “chargeable amount” means the amount of employment income which would be charged to tax in respect of the award apart from subsection (1),
“long service award” means an award made to an employee to mark not less than 20 years' service with the same employer, and
“permitted maximum” means £50 for each year of service in respect of which the award is made.

P2para.Text: The condition is that the award must take the form of—

P3para.Text: tangible moveable property,
shares in a company which is, or belongs to the same group as, the employer, or
the provision of any other benefit except—

P4para.Text: a payment,
a cash voucher,
a credit-token,
securities,
shares not within paragraph (b), or
an interest in or rights over securities or shares.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) does not apply to an award (“the later award”) if another award to mark a particular period of service with the same employer has been made to the employee in the period of 10 years ending with the date on which the later award is made.
For the purposes of this section, service is treated as being with the same employer if it is with two or more employers—

P3para.Text: each of whom is a successor or predecessor of the others, or
one of whom is a company which belongs or has belonged to the same group as the others or a predecessor or successor of the others.

P2para.Text: In this section “group” means a body corporate and its 51% subsidiaries.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a benefit provided by, or on behalf of, an employer to an employee or a member of the employee's family or household if—
conditions A to D are met, or
in a case where subsection (2) applies, conditions A to E are met.
This subsection applies where—
the employer is a close company, and
the employee is—
a person who is a director or other office-holder of the employer, or
a member of the family or household of such a person.
Condition A is that the benefit is not cash or a cash voucher within the meaning of section 75.
Condition B is that the benefit cost of the benefit does not exceed £50.
In this section “
”, in relation to a benefit, means—
the cost of providing the benefit, or

if the benefit is provided to more than one person and the nature of the benefit or the scale of its provision means it is impracticable to calculate the cost of providing it to each person to whom it is provided, the average cost per person of providing the benefit.

For the purposes of subsection (5)(b), the average cost per person of providing a benefit is found by dividing the total cost of providing the benefit by the number of persons to whom the benefit is provided.
Condition C is that the benefit is not provided pursuant to relevant salary sacrifice arrangements or any other contractual obligation.

”, in relation to the provision of a benefit to an employee or to a member of an employee's family or household, means arrangements (whenever made, whether before or after the employment began) under which the employee gives up the right to receive an amount of general earnings or specific employment income in return for the provision of the benefit.
Condition D is that the benefit is not provided in recognition of particular services performed by the employee in the course of the employment or in anticipation of such services.
Condition E is that—
the benefit cost of the benefit provided to the employee, or

in a case where the benefit is provided to a member of the employee's family or household who is not an employee of the employer, the amount of the benefit cost allocated to the employee in accordance with section 323B(4),
does not exceed the employee's available exempt amount (see section 323B).

Title.Addition: Section 323A: calculation of available exempt amount

Text.Addition: The “
”, in relation to an employee of an employer, is the amount found by deducting from the annual exempt amount the aggregate of—
the benefit cost of eligible benefits provided earlier in the tax year by, or on behalf of, the employer to the employee, and

any amounts allocated to the employee in accordance with subsection (4) in respect of eligible benefits provided earlier in the tax year by, or on behalf of, the employer to a member of the employee's family or household who was not at that time an employee of the employer.
The annual exempt amount is £300.
For the purposes of subsection (1) “
” means benefits in respect of which conditions A to D in section 323A are met.
The amount allocated to an employee of an employer in respect of a benefit provided to a person (“P”) who—
is a member of the employee's family or household, and
is not an employee of the employer,
is the benefit cost of that benefit divided by the number of persons who meet the condition in subsection (5) and are members of P's family or household.
This condition is met if the person is—
a director or other office-holder of the employer,
an employee of the employer who is a member of the family or household of a person within paragraph (a), or
a former employee of the employer who—
was a director or other office-holder at any time when the employer was a close company, or
is a member of the family or household of such a person.
In this section “
” has the same meaning as in section 323A.
The Treasury may by regulations amend section 323A so as to alter the conditions which must be met for the exemption conferred by section 323A(1) to apply.
Regulations under subsection (1) may include any amendment of section 323B that is appropriate in consequence of an amendment made under subsection (1).
The Treasury must not make regulations under subsection (1) unless a draft of the regulations has been laid before and approved by a resolution of the House of Commons.

P1group.Title: Small gifts from third parties

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a gift provided for an employee or a member of the employee’s family or household if conditions A to E are met.
Condition A is that the gift is not provided by the employer or a person connected with the employer.
Condition B is that neither the employer nor a person connected with the employer has directly or indirectly procured the gift.
Condition C is that the gift is not made in recognition of particular services performed by the employee in the course of the employment or in anticipation of such services.
Condition D is that the gift is not cash or securities or the use of a service.
Condition E is that the total cost to the donor of all the eligible gifts in respect of the employee in question during the tax year does not exceed £250.

For the purposes of condition E, the total cost to the donor includes any value added tax payable on the supply of the gifts to the donor, whether or not the donor is entitled to a credit or repayment in respect of that tax.
In this section “eligible gifts” means all gifts which—

P3para.Text: meet conditions A to D, or
are non-cash vouchers or credit-tokens and meet—

P4para.Text: conditions A to C, and
conditions A and B in section 270 (exemption for small gifts of vouchers and tokens from third parties).

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) does not apply to non-cash vouchers and credit-tokens (but see section 270 which makes provision for a corresponding exemption for them).

P1group.Title: Overseas medical treatment

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of—

P3para.Text: providing an employee with medical treatment outside the United Kingdom where the need for it arises while the employee is outside the United Kingdom for the purpose of performing the duties of the employment, or
providing an employee with insurance against the cost of providing such treatment.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: “medical treatment” includes all procedures for diagnosing or treating any physical or mental illness, infirmity or defect, and
providing a person with medical treatment includes providing for the person to be an in-patient so that such treatment can be given.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax in respect of employment income arises on any payment if or to the extent that—
were the payment an annual payment falling within Chapter 7 of Part 5 of
ITTOIA
2005, it would be exempt from income tax under section 735 of that Act (health and employment insurance payments), and
it meets conditions A and B.
Condition A is that the payments are made—
to a person (“
”) who made payments or contributions in respect of premiums under an insurance policy which another person took out wholly or partly for the employee's benefit, or
to the employee's
Condition B is that the payments are attributable on a just and reasonable basis to the payments or contributions in respect of premiums.

Title.Emphasis: Expenses incidental to sale etc. of asset

P1group.Title: Expenses incidental to transfer of a kind not normally met by transferor

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of the payment or reimbursement of expenses which—

P3para.Text: are incidental to, and incurred wholly and exclusively as a result of, an employment-related asset transfer, and
are of a kind not normally met by the transferor.

P2para.Text: There is an “employment-related asset transfer” if—

P3para.Text: an asset or the beneficial interest in an asset is transferred to an employee’s employer or a person nominated by the employer, and
the right or opportunity to make the transfer arose by reason of the employment.

P2para.Text: In this section references to a transfer are to a sale or any other kind of disposal.

Title.Addition: Fees relating to monitoring schemes relating to vulnerable persons

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of the payment or reimbursement of a fee in respect of

an application to join the scheme administered under section 44 of the Protection of Vulnerable Groups (Scotland) Act 2007 (asp 14) (scheme to collate and disclose information about individuals working with vulnerable persons).

Addition.Addition: a fee paid by virtue of section 116A(4)(b) or (5)(b) of the Police Act 1997 (“the Police Act”) (fee for up-dating certificates);
section 113A(1)(b) of the Police Act (fee for criminal record certificates);
section 113B(1)(b) of the Police Act (fee for enhanced criminal record certificates);
iii)section 114(1)(b) of the Police Act (fee for criminal record certificates: Crown employment); or
iv)section 116(1)(b) of the Police Act (fee for enhanced criminal record certificates: judicial appointments and Crown employment);
where the application is made at the same time as an application under section 116A(4) or (5) of the Police Act for the certificate to be subject to up-date arrangements.
The Treasury may by order amend subsection (1) so as—

to add to the fees covered by that subsection a fee of a specified kind payable in connection with a scheme for England and Wales or Northern Ireland which corresponds to the scheme administered under section 44 of the Protection of Vulnerable Groups (Scotland) Act 2007, or
to amend or remove a reference to a fee added under paragraph (a).

Title.Addition: Advice relating to proposed employee shareholder agreements

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of—
the provision of relevant advice by a relevant independent adviser, or
the payment or reimbursement, in accordance with section 205A(7) of the Employment Rights Act 1996, of any reasonable costs incurred in obtaining relevant advice.
” means—
advice, other than tax advice, which is provided for the purposes of section 205A(6)(a) of that Act (advice as to terms and effect of employee shareholder agreement), and
tax advice which is so provided and consists only of an explanation of the tax effects of employee shareholder agreements generally.
In this section—
” means an agreement by virtue of which an employee is an employee shareholder (see section 205A(1)(a) to (d) of that Act);
” has the meaning that it has for the purposes of section 203(3)(c) of that Act.

Part.Title: Employment income: deductions allowed from earnings

Chapter.Title: Deductions allowed from earnings: general rules

P1group.Title: Deductions from earnings: general

P2para.Text: This Part provides for deductions that are allowed from the taxable earnings from an employment in a tax year in calculating the net taxable earnings from the employment in the tax year for the purposes of Part 2 (see section 11(1)).
In this Part, unless otherwise indicated by the context—

P3para.Text: references to the earnings from which deductions are allowed are references to the taxable earnings mentioned in subsection (1), and
references to the tax year are references to the tax year mentioned there.

P2para.Text: The deductions for which this Part provides are those allowed under—

Para.Text: Chapter 2 (deductions for employee’s expenses),
Chapter 3 (deductions from benefits code earnings),
Chapter 4 (fixed allowances for employee’s expenses),
Chapter 5 (deductions for earnings representing benefits or reimbursed expenses), and
Chapter 6 (deductions from seafarers' earnings).

P2para.Text: Further provision about deductions from earnings is made in—

Para.Text: section 232 (giving effect to mileage allowance relief),
... and
section 262 of CAA 2001 (capital allowances to be given effect by treating them as deductions from earnings).

P2para.Text: Further provision about deductions from income including earnings is made in—

Para.Text: Part 12 (payroll giving), and

Text.Substitution: sections 188 to 194 of FA 2004 (contributions to registered pension schemes).

P1group.Title: The income from which deductions may be made

P2para.Text: The general rule is that deductions under this Part are allowed—

P3para.Text: from any earnings from the employment in question, and
not from earnings from any other employment.
This is subject to subsections (2) to (4).

P2para.Text: Deductions under section 351 (expenses of ministers of religion) are allowed from earnings from any employment as a minister of a religious denomination.
Deductions under section 368 (fixed sum deductions from earnings payable out of public revenue) are allowed only from earnings payable out of the public revenue.
Deductions limited to specified earnings (see subsection (5)) are allowed—

P3para.Text: only from earnings from the employment that are taxable earnings under certain of the charging provisions of Chapters 4 and 5 of Part 2, and
not from other earnings from it.

P2para.Text: “Deductions limited to specified earnings” are deductions under—

Para.Text: sections 336 to 342 (deductions from earnings charged on receipt: see sections 335(2) and 354),
section 353 (deductions from earnings charged on remittance),
sections 370 to 374 (travel deductions from earnings charged on receipt),

P1group.Title: Deductions from earnings not to exceed earnings

P2para.Text: The amount of a deduction allowed under this Part may not exceed the earnings from which it is deductible.

Text.Addition: If the earnings from which a deduction allowed under this Part is deductible include earnings that are “excluded” within the meaning of section 15(1A)—
the amount of the deduction allowed is a proportion of the amount that would be allowed under this Part if the tax year were not a split year, and
that proportion is equal to the proportion that the part of the earnings that is not “excluded” bears to the total earnings.

P2para.Text: If two or more deductions allowed under this Part are deductible from the same earnings, the amounts deductible may not in aggregate exceed those earnings (or, in a case within subsection (1A), the part of those earnings that is not “excluded”) .

If deductions allowed otherwise than under this Part fall to be allowed from the same earnings as amounts deductible under this Part, the amounts deductible under this Part may not exceed the earnings (or, in a case within subsection (1A), the part of the earnings that is not “excluded”) remaining after the other deductions.

Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply to a deduction under section 351 (expenses of ministers of religion), and subsection (3) applies as if such a deduction were allowed otherwise than under this Part.
This section is to be disregarded for the purposes of the deductibility provisions (see section 332).
See also section 128 of ITA 2007 (which provides that where a loss in an employment is sustained, relief may be given against other income).

P1group.Title: Prevention of double deductions

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings under this Part is not allowed more than once in respect of the same costs or expenses.
If apart from this subsection—

P3para.Text: a deduction would be allowed under Chapter 4 of this Part (fixed allowances for employee’s expenses) for a sum fixed by reference to any kind of expenses, and
the employee would be entitled under another provision to a deduction for an amount paid in respect of the same kind of expenses,

P2para.Text: only one of those deductions is allowed.

P1group.Title: Order for making deductions

P2para.Text: This Part needs to be read with section 25(1) to (3) of ITA 2007 (general rule that deductions are to be allowed in the order resulting in the greatest reduction of liability to income tax).
In the case of deductions under this Part, the general rule in that section is subject to—

P3para.Text: section 23(3) (which requires certain deductions to be made in order to establish “chargeable overseas earnings”), and
section 381 (which requires deductions under other provisions to be taken into account before deductions under Chapter 6 of this Part (seafarers)).

P1group.Title: Meaning of “the deductibility provisions”

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Part, “the deductibility provisions” means the following provisions (which refer to amounts or expenses that would be deductible if they were incurred and paid by an employee)—

Para.Text: the definition of “business travel” in section 171(1) (definitions for Chapter 6 of Part 3),
section 179(6) (exception for certain advances for necessary expenses),
the definition of “business travel” in section 236(1) (definitions for Chapter 2 of Part 4),
section 240(1)(c) and (5) (exemption of incidental overnight expenses and benefits),
section 252(3) (exception from exemption of work-related training provision for non-deductible travel expenses),
section 257(3) (exception from exemption for individual learning account training provision for non-deductible travel expenses),
section 305(5) (offshore oil and gas workers: mainland transfers),
section 310(6)(b) (counselling and other outplacement services),
section 311(5)(b) (retraining courses),
section 361(b) (scope of Chapter 3 of this Part: cost of benefits deductible as if paid by employee),
section 362(1)(c) and (2)(b) (deductions where non-cash voucher provided),
section 363(1)(b) and (2)(b) (deductions where credit-token provided),
section 364(1)(b) and (2) (deductions where living accommodation provided),
section 365(1)(b) and (2) (deductions where employment-related benefit provided).

P1group.Title: Scope of this Chapter: expenses paid by the employee

P2para.Text: A deduction from a person’s earnings for an amount is allowed under the following provisions of this Chapter only if the amount—

P3para.Text: is paid by the person, or
is paid on the person’s behalf by someone else and is included in the earnings.

P2para.Text: In the following provisions of this Chapter, in relation to a deduction from a person’s earnings, references to the person paying an amount include references to the amount being paid on the person’s behalf by someone else if or to the extent that the amount is included in the earnings.
Subsection (1)(b) does not apply to the deductions under—

P3para.Text: section 351(2) and (3) (expenses of ministers of religion), and
section 355 (deductions for corresponding payments by qualifying new resident employees with foreign employers),

P2para.Text: and subsection (2) does not apply in the case of those deductions.
Chapter 3 of this Part provides for deductions where—

P3para.Text: a person’s earnings include an amount treated as earnings under Chapter 4, 5 or 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers etc., living accommodation and residual liability to charge), and
an amount in respect of the benefit in question would be deductible under this Chapter if the person had incurred and paid it.

P1group.Title: Effect of reimbursement etc.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter, a person may be regarded as paying an amount despite—

P3para.Text: its reimbursement, or
any other payment from another person in respect of the amount.

P2para.Text: But where a reimbursement or such other payment is made in respect of an amount, a deduction for the amount is allowed under the following provisions of this Chapter only if or to the extent that—

P3para.Text: the reimbursement, or
so much of the other payment as relates to the amount,

P2para.Text: is included in the person’s earnings.
This section does not apply to a deduction allowed under section 351 (expenses of ministers of religion).
This section is to be disregarded for the purposes of the deductibility provisions.

P1group.Title: Application of deductions provisions: “earnings charged on receipt” and “earnings charged on remittance”

P2para.Text: The availability of certain deductions under this Chapter depends on whether the earnings are earnings charged on receipt or earnings charged on remittance.
Sections 336 to 342—

P3para.Text: only apply if the earnings from which the deduction is to be made are earnings charged on receipt, and
apply subject to section 354(1) if the earnings from the employment also include other earnings.

P2para.Text: Section 353 (which provides for a deduction for expenses of the kind to which sections 336 to 342 apply)—

P3para.Text: only applies if the earnings from which the deduction is to be made are earnings charged on remittance, and
applies subject to section 354(2) if the earnings from the employment also include other earnings.

P2para.Text: In this Part—

Para.Text: “earnings charged on receipt” means earnings which are taxable earnings under section 15... or 27, and
“earnings charged on remittance” means earnings which are taxable earnings under section 22 or 26.

Title.Emphasis: General rule for deduction of employee’s expenses

P1group.Title: Deductions for expenses: the general rule

P2para.Text: The general rule is that a deduction from earnings is allowed for an amount if—

P3para.Text: the employee is obliged to incur and pay it as holder of the employment, and
the amount is incurred wholly, exclusively and necessarily in the performance of the duties of the employment.

P2para.Text: The following provisions of this Chapter contain additional rules allowing deductions for particular kinds of expenses and rules preventing particular kinds of deductions.
No deduction is allowed under this section for an amount that is deductible under sections 337 to 342 (travel expenses).

P1group.Title: Travel in performance of duties

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings is allowed for travel expenses if—

P3para.Text: the employee is obliged to incur and pay them as holder of the employment, and
the expenses are necessarily incurred on travelling in the performance of the duties of the employment.

P2para.Text: This section needs to be read with section 359 (disallowance of travel expenses: mileage allowances and reliefs).

P1group.Title: Travel for necessary attendance

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings is allowed for travel expenses if—

P3para.Text: the employee is obliged to incur and pay them as holder of the employment, and
the expenses are attributable to the employee’s necessary attendance at any place in the performance of the duties of the employment.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) does not apply to the expenses of ordinary commuting or travel between any two places that is for practical purposes substantially ordinary commuting.
In this section “ordinary commuting” means travel between—

P3para.Text: the employee’s home and a permanent workplace, or
a place that is not a workplace and a permanent workplace.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) does not apply to the expenses of private travel or travel between any two places that is for practical purposes substantially private travel.
In subsection (4) “private travel” means travel between—

P3para.Text: the employee’s home and a place that is not a workplace, or
two places neither of which is a workplace.

P2para.Text: This section needs to be read with section 359 (disallowance of travel expenses: mileage allowances and reliefs).

P1group.Title: Meaning of “workplace” and “permanent workplace”

P2para.Text: In this Part “workplace”, in relation to an employment, means a place at which the employee’s attendance is necessary in the performance of the duties of the employment.
In this Part “permanent workplace”, in relation to an employment, means a place which—

P3para.Text: the employee regularly attends in the performance of the duties of the employment, and
is not a temporary workplace.
This is subject to subsections (4) and (8).

P2para.Text: In subsection (2) “temporary workplace”, in relation to an employment, means a place which the employee attends in the performance of the duties of the employment—

P3para.Text: for the purpose of performing a task of limited duration, or
for some other temporary purpose.
This is subject to subsections (4) and (5).

P2para.Text: A place which the employee regularly attends in the performance of the duties of the employment is treated as a permanent workplace and not a temporary workplace if—

P3para.Text: it forms the base from which those duties are performed, or
the tasks to be carried out in the performance of those duties are allocated there.

P2para.Text: A place is not regarded as a temporary workplace if the employee’s attendance is—

P3para.Text: in the course of a period of continuous work at that place—

P4para.Text: lasting more than 24 months, or
comprising all or almost all of the period for which the employee is likely to hold the employment, or

P3para.Text: at a time when it is reasonable to assume that it will be in the course of such a period.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (5), a period is a period of continuous work at a place if over the period the duties of the employment are performed to a significant extent at the place.

An actual or contemplated modification of the place at which duties are performed is to be disregarded for the purposes of subsections (5) and (6) if it does not, or would not, have any substantial effect on the employee’s journey, or expenses of travelling, to and from the place where they are performed.
An employee is treated as having a permanent workplace consisting of an area if—

P3para.Text: the duties of the employment are defined by reference to an area (whether or not they also require attendance at places outside it),
in the performance of those duties the employee attends different places within the area,
none of the places the employee attends in the performance of those duties is a permanent workplace, and
the area would be a permanent workplace if subsections (2), (3), (5), (6) and (7) referred to the area where they refer to a place.

Title.Addition: Travel for necessary attendance: employment intermediaries

Text.Addition: This section applies where an individual (“the worker”)—
personally provides services (which are not excluded services) to another person (“
”), and
the services are provided not under a contract directly between the client or a person connected with the client and the worker but under arrangements involving an employment intermediary.
This is subject to the following provisions of this section.
Where this section applies, each engagement is for the purposes of sections 338 and 339 to be regarded as a separate employment.
This section does not apply if it is shown that the manner in which the worker provides the services is not subject to (or to the right of) supervision, direction or control by any person.
Subsection (3) does not apply in relation to an engagement if—
Chapter 8 of Part 2 applies in relation to the engagement,
the conditions in section 51, 52 or 53 are met in relation to the employment intermediary, and
the employment intermediary is not a managed service company.
This section does not apply in relation to an engagement if—
Chapter 8 of Part 2 does not apply in relation to the engagement merely because the circumstances in section 49(1)(c) are not met,
assuming those circumstances were met, the conditions in section 51, 52 or 53 would be met in relation to the employment intermediary, and
the employment intermediary is not a managed service company.
In determining for the purposes of subsection (4) or (5) whether the conditions in section 51, 52 or 53 are or would be met in relation to the employment intermediary—
in section 51(1)—
disregard “either” in the opening words, and
disregard paragraph (b) (and the preceding or), and
read references to the intermediary as references to the employment intermediary.

Addition.Addition: Subsection (3) does not apply in relation to an engagement if—
sections 61N to 61R in Chapter 10 of Part 2 apply in relation to the engagement,
one of Conditions A to C in section 61N is met in relation to the employment intermediary, and
the employment intermediary is not a managed service company.
This section does not apply in relation to an engagement if—
sections 61N to 61R in Chapter 10 of Part 2 do not apply in relation to the engagement because the circumstances in section 61M(1)(d) are not met,
assuming those circumstances were met, one of Conditions A to C in section 61N would be met in relation to the employment intermediary, and
the employment intermediary is not a managed service company.

In determining for the purposes of subsection (6A) or (6B) whether one of Conditions A to C in section 61N is or would be met in relation to the employment intermediary, read references to the intermediary as references to the employment intermediary.

Text.Addition: Subsection (8) applies if—

the client or a relevant person provides the employment intermediary (whether before or after the worker begins to provide the services) with a fraudulent document which is intended to constitute evidence that, by virtue of subsection (3), this section does not or will not apply in relation to the services,
that section is taken not to apply in relation to the services, and
in consequence, the employment intermediary does not under
PAYE
regulations deduct and account for an amount that would have been deducted and accounted for under those regulations if this section had been taken to apply in relation to the services.
For the purpose of recovering the amount referred to in subsection (7)(c) (“the unpaid tax”)—
the worker is to be treated as having an employment with the client or relevant person who provided the document, the duties of which consist of the services, and
the client or relevant person is under
PAYE
regulations to account for the unpaid tax as if it arose in respect of earnings from that employment.
In subsections (7) and (8) “
” means a person, other than the client, the worker or a person connected with the employment intermediary, who—
is resident, or has a place of business, in the United Kingdom, and
is party to a contract with the employment intermediary or a person connected with the employment intermediary under or in consequence of which—
the services are provided, or
the employment intermediary, or a person connected with the employment intermediary, makes payments in respect of the services.

In determining whether this section applies, no regard is to be had to any arrangements the main purpose, or one of the main purposes, of which is to secure that this section does not to any extent apply.
In this section—
” includes any scheme, transaction or series of transactions, agreement or understanding, whether or not enforceable, and any associated operations;
” means a person, other than the worker or the client, who carries on a business (whether or not with a view to profit and whether or not in conjunction with any other business) of supplying labour;
” means any such provision of service as is mentioned in subsection (1)(a);
” means services provided wholly in the client's home;
” means a company which—
is a managed service company within the meaning given by section 61B, or
would be such a company disregarding subsection (1)(c) of that section.

P1group.Title: Travel between group employments

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings from an employment is allowed for travel expenses if conditions A to D are met.
Condition A is that the employee is obliged to incur and pay the expenses.
Condition B is that the travel is for the purpose of performing duties of the employment at the destination.
Condition C is that the employee has performed duties of another employment at the place of departure.
Condition D is that the employments are with companies in the same group.
In this section “group” means a company and its 51% subsidiaries.
For the purposes of sections 353 and 354 (special rules for earnings with a foreign element), the expenses are treated as incurred in the performance of the duties to be performed at the destination.
This section needs to be read with section 359 (disallowance of travel expenses: mileage allowances and reliefs).

Text.Addition: A deduction from earnings from an employment is allowed for travel expenses if conditions A to E are met.
Condition A is that the employee is obliged to incur and pay the expenses.
Condition B is that the travel—
takes place within the United Kingdom, and
is for the purpose of performing duties of the employment at the destination.
Condition C is that the employee has performed duties of another employment at the place of departure.
Condition D is that—
at least one of the employments is as a director of a company (“company X”), and
the other employment is also with a company (“company Y”) but not necessarily as a director of it.
Condition E is that the employee was appointed as a director of company X because company Y, or a company in the same group as company Y, has a shareholding or other financial interest in company
This section needs to be read with section 359 (disallowance of travel expenses: mileage allowances and reliefs).
In this section—
“director” has the same meaning as in the benefits code (see section 67), and
“group” means a company and its 51% subsidiaries.

P1group.Title: Travel at start or finish of overseas employment

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings from an employment is allowed for starting travel expenses and finishing travel expenses if conditions A to C are met.
Condition A is that the duties of the employment are performed wholly outside the United Kingdom.
Condition B is that the employee is UK resident.

Condition C is that in a case where the employer is a foreign employer, the employee is not a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 of this Act or Chapter 5 of Part 8 of ITTOIA 2005 (see section 845B of that Act).
If the travel is only partly attributable to the taking up or termination of the employment, this section applies only to the part of the expenses properly so attributable.
Subsection (7) applies if in the tax year the employment is in substance one whose duties fall to be performed outside the United Kingdom.

Duties of the employment performed in the United Kingdom, whose performance is merely incidental to the performance of duties outside the United Kingdom, are to be treated for the purposes of subsection (2) as performed outside the United Kingdom.
In this section—

Para.Text: “starting travel expenses” means expenses incurred by the employee in travelling from a place in the United Kingdom to take up the employment,
“finishing travel expenses” means expenses incurred by the employee in travelling to a place in the United Kingdom on the termination of the employment, and
“employee” includes a person who is to be, or has ceased to be, an employee.

P2para.Text: This section needs to be read with section 359 (disallowance of travel expenses: mileage allowances and reliefs).

P1group.Title: Travel between employments where duties performed abroad

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings from an employment is allowed for travel expenses incurred by the employee if conditions A to F are met.
Condition A is that the travel is for the purpose of performing duties of the employment at the destination.
Condition B is that the employee has performed duties of another employment at the place of departure.
Condition C is that the place of departure or the destination or both are outside the United Kingdom.
Condition D is that the duties of one or both of the employments are performed wholly or partly outside the United Kingdom.
Condition E is that the employee is UK resident.

Condition F is that in a case where the employer is a foreign employer, the employee is not a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 of this Act or Chapter 5 of Part 8 of ITTOIA 2005 (see section 845B of that Act).
If the travel is only partly attributable to the purpose of performing duties of the employment at the destination, this section applies only to the part of the expenses properly so attributable.
This section needs to be read with section 359 (disallowance of travel expenses: mileage allowances and reliefs).

P1group.Title: Deduction for professional membership fees

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings from an employment is allowed for an amount paid in respect of a professional fee if—

P3para.Text: the duties of the employment involve the practice of the profession to which the fee relates, and

the registration, certification, licensing or other matter in respect of which the fee is payable is a condition, or one of alternative conditions, which must be met if that profession is to be practised in the performance of those duties.

P2para.Text: In this section “professional fee” means a fee mentioned in the following Table.

P3para.Text: Fee payable for entry or retention of a name in any of the following—

P4para.Text: the register maintained by the Registrar of Chiropractors,

Text.Substitution: the dental care professionals register,

P4para.Text: the dentists register,
the register of dispensing opticians,
the register maintained by the Health and Care Professions Council ,
the register of medical practitioners,
the register maintained by the Nursing and Midwifery Council,
either of the registers of opthalmic opticians,
the register maintained by the Registrar of Osteopaths,

Text.Substitution: the register maintained under article 19 of the Pharmacy Order 2010 so far as relating to pharmacists or pharmacy technicians,

Text.Addition: the register of pharmaceutical chemists kept under Articles 6 and 9 of the Pharmacy (Northern Ireland) Order 1976.
the register maintained by the Care Council for Wales,
the register maintained by the Scottish Social Services Council,
the register maintained by the Northern Ireland Social Care Council,
the register of social workers in England kept under section 39(1) of the Children and Social Work Act 2017,
the register kept under the Anaesthesia Associates and Physician Associates Order 2024.

Trainee registration fee payable by a specialty registrar to a body which recommends specialty registrars to the registrar of the General Medical Council for the award of a certificate of completion of training under section 34L of the Medical Act 1983.

Trainee registration fee payable by a person listed in the dentists register to a body which provides evidence to the General Dental Council relating to a person’s suitability to be awarded a Certificate of Completion of Specialist Training in a specialist branch of dentistry pursuant to regulations made under section 26(3) and (4) of the Dentists Act 1984

P3para.Text: Fee payable for entry or retention of a name in any of the following—

P4para.Text: the register maintained by the registrar appointed by the Farriers Registration Council,
the supplementary veterinary register,
the register of veterinary surgeons.

Text.Addition: any list or register of veterinary nurses maintained by the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons,
the register maintained by the Animal Medicines Training Regulatory Authority pursuant to paragraph 13 of Schedule 3 to the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2006.

P3para.Text: Fee payable to the Council for Licensed Conveyancers on the issue of a licence to practise as a licensed conveyancer.
Fee and contribution to the compensation fund or Guarantee Fund payable on the issue of a solicitor’s practising certificate.

Text.Addition: Fee payable to the Costs Lawyer Standards Board on applying for a costs lawyer practising certificate.

P3para.Text: Fee payable for entry or retention of a name in the Register of Architects.
Fee payable for entry or retention of a name in any of the following—

P4para.Text: the register maintained by the General Teaching Council for Scotland,
the register maintained by the Education Workforce Council.

Text.Addition: the register maintained by the General Teaching Council for Northern Ireland.

Text.Emphasis: Patent attorneys and trade mark attorneys

P3para.Text: Registration fee payable by—

P4para.Text: a registered patent attorney,
a registered trade mark attorney.

P3para.Text: Practising fee payable by—

P4para.Text: a registered patent attorney,
a registered trade mark attorney.

P3para.Text: Fee payable by a driving instructor for entry or retention of a name in the register of approved instructors or on the issue or renewal of a licence authorising its holder to give paid instruction in the driving of a motor car.
Fee (including any related medical or technical examination fee) payable, on the issue or renewal of a licence by the Civil Aviation Authority, by—

P4para.Text: an aircraft maintenance engineer,
an air traffic controller or student air traffic controller,
a member of the flight crew of an aircraft registered in the United Kingdom,
a flight information service officer.

P3para.Text: Fee (including any related medical examination fee) payable—

P4para.Text: on the issue or renewal of a licence authorising its holder to drive a large goods vehicle or a passenger-carrying vehicle,
by an officer or other seaman on the issue, renewal or endorsement of a certificate, licence or other document which is required as evidence of his qualification or competence to serve in a ship.

P3para.Text: Fee payable by a seafarer employed in a sea-going United Kingdom ship on the issue or renewal of a medical fitness certificate.

Text.Addition: Fee payable by a person employed or to be employed at a United Kingdom airport for a criminal records check required for the issue of a security pass authorising him to enter areas within the airport.

Emphasis.Addition: Occupations in the private security industry

Text.Addition: Fee payable on applying for a licence from the Security Industry Authority under the Private Security Industry Act 2001.
Fee payable—
on applying for a personal licence from the Gambling Commission under the Gambling Act 2005, or
on applying to vary such a licence.
Any fee payable to the Gambling Commission under section 132 of that Act.

P2para.Text: The Board of Inland Revenue may make an order adding such fee as is specified in the order to the Table of fees mentioned in subsection (2).

The Commissioners may make an order if they consider that such fee is payable in respect of any registration, certification, licensing or other matter if it is required as a condition, or one of alternative conditions, of the practice of a profession.

P1group.Title: Deduction for annual subscriptions

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings from an employment is allowed for an amount paid in respect of an annual subscription if—

P3para.Text: it is paid to a body of persons approved under this section, and

the activities of the body which are directed to one or more of the objects within subsection (2) are of direct benefit to, or concern the profession practised in, the performance of the duties of the employment.

P2para.Text: The objects are—

P3para.Text: the advancement or dissemination of knowledge (whether generally or among persons belonging to the same or similar professions or occupying the same or similar positions),
the maintenance or improvement of standards of conduct and competence among the members of a profession,
the provision of indemnity or protection to members of a profession against claims in respect of liabilities incurred by them in the exercise of their profession.

P2para.Text: An officer of Revenue and Customs may approve a body of persons under this section if, on an application by the body, the officer is satisfied that—

P3para.Text: the body is not of a mainly local character,
its activities are carried on otherwise than for profit, and
its activities are wholly or mainly directed to objects within subsection (2).

P2para.Text: An officer of Revenue and Customs must give notice to the body of their decision on the application.
If the activities of the body are to a significant extent directed to objects other than objects within subsection (2), an officer of Revenue and Customs may—

P3para.Text: determine the proportion of the activities directed to objects within subsection (2), and
determine that only such corresponding part of the subscription as is specified by an officer of Revenue and Customs is allowable under this section.

P2para.Text: In determining that part, an officer of Revenue and Customs must have regard to the proportion of expenditure of the body attributable to objects other than objects within subsection (2) and all other relevant circumstances.
If a body applies for approval under this section and is approved, a subscription paid to it—

P3para.Text: before it has applied but in the same tax year as the application, or
after it has applied but before it is approved,

P2para.Text: is treated for the purposes of this section as having been paid to an approved body.

P1group.Title: Decisions of an officer of Revenue and Customs under section 344

P2para.Text: An officer of Revenue and Customs may by notice to the body in question—

P3para.Text: withdraw an approval given under section 344, and
withdraw or vary a determination made under that section,

P2para.Text: to take account of any change in circumstances.
A body aggrieved by a decision of an officer of Revenue and Customs under section 344 or subsection (1) may appeal ....
The notice of appeal must be given to an officer of Revenue and Customs within 30 days after the date on which notice of their decision was given to the body.

P1group.Title: Deduction for employee liabilities and expenses

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings from an employment is allowed for any or all of the following—
A. Payment in or towards the discharge of a liability related to the employment.
B. Payment of any costs or expenses incurred in connection with—

P3para.Text: a claim that the employee is subject to a liability related to the employment, or
proceedings relating to or arising out of a claim that the employee is subject to a liability related to the employment.

Text.Addition: BA. Payment of any costs or expenses not falling within paragraph B which are incurred in connection with the employee giving evidence about matters related to the employment in, or for the purposes of—
a proceeding or other process (whether or not involving the employee), or
an investigation (whether or not likely to lead to any proceeding or other process involving the employee).
BB. Payment of any costs or expenses not falling within paragraph B or BA which are incurred in connection with a proceeding or other process, or an investigation, in which—
acts of the employee related to the employment, or
any other matters related to the employment,
are being or are likely to be considered.

P2para.Text: C. Payment of a premium under a qualifying insurance contract, but only to the extent that the premium relates to—

P3para.Text: provision in the contract for the employee to be indemnified against a payment falling within paragraph A, or
provision in the contract for the payment of any costs or expenses falling within paragraph B , BA or BB .

P2para.Text: But a deduction is not allowed for a payment which falls within paragraph A B, BA or BB if it would be unlawful for the employer to enter into a contract of insurance in respect of the liability, or costs or expenses, in question.

Text.Addition: Nor is a deduction allowed for a payment which falls within

Addition.Substitution: any of paragraphs A to C

Text.Addition: if the payment is made in pursuance of arrangements the main purpose, or one of the main purposes, of which is the avoidance of tax.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter—

P3para.Text: “premium”, in relation to a qualifying insurance contract, means an amount payable to the insurer under the contract, and

where a qualifying insurance contract relates to more than one person, employment or risk, the part of the premium to be treated as relating to each of them is to be determined by apportionment on a just and reasonable basis.

Text.Addition: In this section and section 349—
” includes failures to act and acts are “related to the employment” if the employee was acting—
in the employee's capacity as holder of the employment, or
in any other capacity in which the employee was acting in the performance of the duties of the employment,
” includes making a formal or informal statement or answering questions,
” includes any civil, criminal or arbitration proceedings, any disciplinary or regulatory proceedings of any kind and any process operated for resolving disputes or adjudicating on complaints, and
references to a proceeding or other process or an investigation include a reference to a proceeding or other process or an investigation that is likely to take place.

P1group.Title: Payments made after leaving the employment

P2para.Text: A deduction for a payment is not allowed under section 346 if—

P3para.Text: the employee has ceased to hold the employment, and
the payment is made after the day on which the employee ceased to hold the employment.

P2para.Text: If subsection (1) applies, see section 555 (former employee entitled to deduction in calculating net income).

P1group.Title: Liabilities related to the employment

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter each of the following kinds of liability is related to the employment— A. Liability imposed upon the employee because he did an act, or failed to do an act—

P3para.Text: in his capacity as holder of the employment, or
in any other capacity in which he acted in the performance of the duties of the employment.

P1para.Text: B. Liability imposed upon the employee in connection with any proceedings relating to, or arising from, a claim that he is subject to a liability because he did an act, or failed to do an act—

P3para.Text: in his capacity as holder of the employment, or
in any other capacity in which he acted in the performance of the duties of the employment.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “qualifying insurance contract”

P2para.Text: In section 346 “qualifying insurance contract” means a contract of insurance which meets conditions A, B, C and D.
Condition A is that, so far as the risks insured against are concerned, the contract only relates to one or more of the following—

P3para.Text: the indemnification of an employee against a liability related to the employment,
the indemnification of a person against vicarious liability in respect of a liability related to another person’s employment,
the payment of costs or expenses incurred—

P4para.Text: in connection with a claim that a person is subject to a liability to which the insurance relates, or
in connection with any proceedings relating to or arising out of a claim that a person is subject to a liability to which the insurance relates,

Text.Addition: the payment of costs or expenses incurred in connection with an employee giving evidence about matters related to the employee's employment in, or for the purposes of—
a proceeding or other process (whether or not involving the employee), or
an investigation (whether or not likely to lead to any proceeding or other process involving the employee),
the payment of any costs or expenses incurred in connection with a proceeding or other process, or an investigation, in which—
acts of an employee related to the employment, or
any other matters related to the employment of an employee,
are being or are likely to be considered,

P3para.Text: the indemnification of an employer against loss from a payment made by the employer to an employee in respect of—

P4para.Text: a liability related to the employment, or
any costs or expenses incurred as mentioned in paragraph (c) , (ca) or (cb).

P2para.Text: Condition B is that—

P3para.Text: the period of insurance under the contract does not exceed 2 years or, if it does, it does so only because of one or more renewals, each for a period of 2 years or less, and
the insured is not required to renew the contract for any period.

P2para.Text: Condition C is—

P3para.Text: that the insured is not entitled under the contract to receive any payment or other benefit in addition to—

P4para.Text: cover for the risks insured against, and
any right to renew the contract, or
