P3para.Text: if the insured is so entitled, that the part of the premium reasonably attributable to the entitlement is not a significant part of the whole premium.

P2para.Text: Condition D is that the contract is not connected with another contract.

P1group.Title: Connected contracts

P2para.Text: An insurance contract is connected with another contract for the purposes of section 349 if conditions E and F are met—

P3para.Text: at the time when both contracts are first in force, or
at any time after that time.

P2para.Text: Condition E is that one of the contracts was entered into—

P3para.Text: by reference to the other, or
with a view to enabling or facilitating entry into the other on particular terms.

P2para.Text: Condition F is that the terms on which one of the contracts was entered into are significantly different from what they would have been if—

P3para.Text: it had not been entered into in anticipation of the other being entered into, or
the other had not also been entered into.

P2para.Text: If—

P3para.Text: there is only one such significant difference in terms, and
the contracts meet conditions A, B and C specified in section 349,

P2para.Text: the difference may be disregarded in the following cases.
The first case is where the difference is a reduction in premiums under the contract that is reasonably attributable only to the contract—

P3para.Text: containing a right to renew, or
being entered into by way of renewal.

P2para.Text: The second case is where—

P3para.Text: two or more contracts have been entered into as part of a single transaction, and

the difference is reductions in their premiums that are reasonably attributable only to the premium under each of them having been fixed by reference to the appropriate proportion of the combined premium.

P2para.Text: In subsection (6) “the combined premium” means the amount that would have been the total premium under a single contract relating to all the risks covered by the contracts.

P1group.Title: Expenses of ministers of religion

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from any earnings from any employment as a minister of a religious denomination for amounts incurred by the minister wholly, exclusively and necessarily in the performance of duties of such an employment.

If a minister of a religious denomination pays rent in respect of a dwelling-house, part of which is used mainly and substantially for the purposes of such duties, a deduction is allowed from the minister’s earnings from any employment as such a minister for—

P3para.Text: one quarter of the rent, or
if less, the part of the rent that, on a just and reasonable apportionment, is attributable to that part of the dwelling-house.

P2para.Text: If—

P3para.Text: an interest in premises belongs to a charity or an ecclesiastical corporation, and

because of that interest and by reason of holding an employment as a minister of a religious denomination, the minister has a residence in the premises from which to perform the duties of the employment,

P2para.Text: a deduction is allowed from the minister’s earnings from any such employment for part of any expenses borne by the minister on the maintenance, repair, insurance or management of the premises.
The amount of the deduction is—

Para.Text: where—
A is the amount of the expenses borne by the minister on the maintenance, repair, insurance or management of the premises, and
B is the amount of those expenses that are allowed under subsection (1).

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) needs to be read with section 359 (disallowance of travel expenses: mileage allowances and reliefs).

P1group.Title: Limited deduction for agency fees paid by entertainers

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from earnings from an employment as an entertainer for agency fees (and any value added tax on them) if the fees are calculated as a percentage of the whole or part of the earnings from the employment.
This is subject to the limit in subsection (2).

Amounts may be deducted under this section in calculating the net taxable earnings from an employment in a tax year only to the extent that, in aggregate, they do not exceed 17.5% of the taxable earnings from the employment in the tax year.
Subsections (4) and (5) apply for the purposes of this section.
“Entertainer” means an actor, dancer, musician, singer or theatrical artist.
“Agency fees”, in relation to an employment, means—

P3para.Text: fees paid under a contract between the employee and another person, to whom the fees are paid, who—

P4para.Text: agrees under the contract to act as an agent of the employee in connection with the employment, and
at the time the fees are paid is carrying on an employment agency with a view to profit, and

P3para.Text: fees paid under an arrangement under which a co-operative society or the members of such a society agree to act as the employee’s agent in connection with the employment.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (5)—

Para.Text: “co-operative society” does not include a society which carries on or intends to carry on business with the object of making profits mainly for the payment of interest, dividends or bonuses on money invested or deposited with or lent to the society or any other person, and
“employment agency” has the meaning given by section 13(2) of the Employment Agencies Act 1973 (c. 35).

Title.Emphasis: Special rules for earnings with a foreign element

P1group.Title: Deductions from earnings charged on remittance

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from earnings charged on remittance for expenses within subsection (2) if the condition in subsection (3) is met.
The expenses are—

P3para.Text: any expenses—

P4para.Text: paid by the employee out of the earnings, or
paid on the employee’s behalf by another person and included in the earnings, and

P3para.Text: any other expenses paid in the United Kingdom in the tax year or an earlier tax year in which the employee has been resident in the United Kingdom.

P2para.Text: The condition is that the expenses would have been deductible under sections 336 to 342 if the earnings had been earnings charged on receipt in the tax year in which the expenses were incurred.
Where—

P3para.Text: any of the deductibility provisions refers to amounts or expenses that would be deductible from earnings if they were paid by a person, and
the earnings in question are earnings charged on remittance,

P2para.Text: it is assumed for the purposes of those provisions that the person pays the amounts or expenses out of those earnings.

P1group.Title: Disallowance of expenses relating to earnings taxed on different basis or untaxed

P2para.Text: If the earnings from an employment for a tax year include both earnings charged on receipt and other earnings (except earnings charged under section 22), no deduction is allowed under sections 336 to 342 from the earnings charged on receipt for an amount paid in respect of duties of the employment to which the other earnings relate.

If the earnings from an employment for a tax year include both earnings charged on remittance under section 26 and other earnings, no deduction is allowed under section 353 from the earnings charged on remittance for an amount paid in respect of duties of the employment to which the other earnings relate.
This section is to be disregarded for the purposes of the deductibility provisions.

P1group.Title: Deductions for corresponding payments by qualifying new resident employees with foreign employers

P2para.Text: An employee may make a claim to the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs under this section if conditions A to D are met.
Condition A is that the employee is a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 of this Act or Chapter 5 of Part 8 of ITTOIA 2005 (see section 845B of that Act).
Condition B is that the employment is with a foreign employer.
Condition C is that the employee has made a payment out of earnings from the employment.
Condition D is that the payment does not reduce the employee’s liability to United Kingdom income tax, but was made in circumstances corresponding to those in which it would do so.
If the Commissioners are satisfied that conditions A to D are met, they may allow the payment as a deduction under this Chapter.

Title.Emphasis: Disallowance of business entertainment and gifts expenses

P1group.Title: Disallowance of business entertainment and gifts expenses

P2para.Text: No deduction from earnings is allowed under this Part for expenses incurred in providing entertainment or a gift in connection with the employer’s trade, business, profession or vocation.
Subsection (1) is subject to the exceptions in—

P3para.Text: section 357 (exception where employer’s expenses disallowed), and
section 358 (other exceptions).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section and those sections—

P3para.Text: “entertainment” includes hospitality of any kind, and
expenses incurred in providing entertainment or a gift include expenses incurred in providing anything incidental to the provision of entertainment or a gift.

P1group.Title: Business entertainment and gifts: exception where employer’s expenses disallowed

P2para.Text: The prohibition in section 356 on deducting expenses does not apply if—

P3para.Text: the earnings include an amount in respect of the expenses,
the employer—

P4para.Text: paid the amount to, or on behalf of, the employee, or
put it at the employee’s disposal,

P3para.Text: exclusively for meeting expenses incurred or to be incurred by the employee in providing the entertainment or gift, and
condition A, B or C is met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the deduction of the amount falls to be disallowed under section 45 or 867 of ITTOIA 2005 or under section 1298 of CTA 2009 in calculating the employer’s profits from the trade, profession or vocation in question for the purposes of the Tax Acts (or it would do so apart from the exemption in ... section 524 of ITA 2007 or section 478 of CTA 2010 or any relief applying in respect of those profits).

Text.Substitution: Condition B is that the inclusion of the amount falls to be disallowed (or would be disallowed apart from some other relief applying to the employer) under
in calculating—
the employer’s expenses of management for the purposes of giving relief under the Tax Acts, or

Substitution.Substitution: the ordinary BLAGAB management expenses of the employer for the purposes of section 76 of FA 2012.

P2para.Text: Condition C is that—

P3para.Text: the employer is a tonnage tax company during the whole or part of the tax year, and
apart from the tonnage tax election, the deduction of the amount included in the employee’s earnings would fall to be disallowed in calculating the employer’s relevant shipping profits.

P2para.Text: In subsection (4) “tonnage tax company”, “tonnage tax election” and “relevant shipping profits” have the same meaning as in Schedule 22 to FA 2000.

P1group.Title: Business entertainment and gifts: other exceptions

P2para.Text: The prohibition in section 356 on deducting expenses does not apply if the expenses are incurred in providing entertainment or gifts for the employer’s employees unless—

P3para.Text: they are also provided for others, and
their provision for the employees is incidental to their provision for the others.

P2para.Text: For this purpose directors and persons engaged in the management of a company are regarded as employed by it.

The prohibition in section 356 on deducting expenses does not apply if the expenses are incurred in providing a gift which incorporates a conspicuous advertisement for the employer or, if the employer is a company, another company which belongs to the same group as the employer, unless—

P3para.Text: the gift is food, drink, tobacco or a token or voucher exchangeable for goods, or

the cost of the gift to the donor, together with any other gifts (except food, drink, tobacco or tokens or vouchers exchangeable for goods) given to the same person in the same tax year, is more than £50.

P2para.Text: In subsection (3) “group” means a body corporate and its 51% subsidiaries.

Title.Emphasis: Other rules preventing deductions of particular kinds

P1group.Title: Disallowance of travel expenses: mileage allowances and reliefs

P2para.Text: No deduction may be made under the travel deductions provisions in respect of travel expenses incurred in connection with the use by the employee of a vehicle that is not a company vehicle if condition A or B is met.
Condition A is that mileage allowance payments are made to the employee in respect of the use of the vehicle.
Condition B is that mileage allowance relief is available in respect of the use of the vehicle by the employee (see section 231).
In this section—

Para.Text: “company vehicle” has the meaning given by section 236(2),
“mileage allowance payments” has the meaning given by section 229(2), and
“the travel deductions provisions” means sections 337 to 342, 370, 371, 373 and 374 (travel expenses) and section 351 (expenses of ministers of religion).

P1group.Title: Disallowance of certain accommodation expenses of MPs and other representatives

P2para.Text: No deduction from earnings is allowed under this Chapter or section 373 (non-resident or qualifying new resident employee’s travel costs and expenses where duties performed in UK) for accommodation expenses incurred by a member of—

P3para.Text: the House of Commons,
the Scottish Parliament,
the National Assembly for Wales, or
the Northern Ireland Assembly.

P2para.Text: In this section “accommodation expenses” means expenses incurred in, or in connection with, the provision or use of residential or overnight accommodation to enable the member to perform duties as a member of the Parliament or Assembly in or about—

P3para.Text: the place where it sits, or
the constituency or region which the member represents.

Text.Addition: In relation to a member of the House of Commons, subsection (3) of section 292 applies for the purposes of this section as it applies for the purposes of that section.
No deduction from earnings is allowed under this Chapter for any contribution paid by any person under Part 1 of
SSCBA
1992 or Part 1 of SSCB(
NI
But this prohibition does not apply to an employer's contribution (see subsection (3)) which is allowable as a deduction—
under section 336 (the general rule),
under any of sections 337 to 342 (travel expenses), or

under section 351(1)
(expenses of ministers of religion).
For this purpose “
” means—
a secondary Class 1 contribution,
a Class 1A contribution, or
a Class 1B contribution,
within the meaning of Part 1 of
SSCBA
1992 or Part 1 of SSCB(
NI
No deduction from earnings is allowed under this Chapter for additional household expenses which the employee incurs in the performance of the duties of the employment at home.
In this section, “
” has the same meaning as in section 316A.

P1group.Title: Scope of this Chapter: cost of benefits deductible as if paid by employee

P1para.Text: A deduction from a person’s earnings is allowed under the following provisions of this Chapter where—

P3para.Text: the earnings include an amount treated as earnings under—

P4para.Text: Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens),
Chapter 5 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: living accommodation), or
Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge), and

P3para.Text: an amount in respect of the benefit in question would be deductible under Chapter 2 or 5 of this Part if the person had incurred and paid it.

Title.Emphasis: Deductions where amounts treated as earnings under the benefits code

P1group.Title: Deductions where non-cash voucher provided

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings is allowed if—

P3para.Text: the earnings include an amount treated as earnings under section 87(1) or 87A(1) (amount in respect of benefit of non-cash voucher treated as earnings),
the voucher is exchanged for goods or services (whether in the tax year or a later year), and

had the employee incurred and paid the cost of the goods or services in the tax year, the whole or part of the amount paid would have been deductible from the earnings under Chapter 2 or 5 of this Part.

P2para.Text: The deduction is equal to the lesser of—

P3para.Text: the amount treated as earnings, and
the amount that would have been so deductible.

P1group.Title: Deductions where credit-token provided

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings is allowed if—

P3para.Text: the earnings include an amount treated as earnings under section 94(1) or 94A(1) (amount in respect of benefit of credit-token treated as earnings), and

had the employee incurred and paid the cost of the goods or services obtained by using the token, the whole or part of the amount paid would have been deductible from the earnings under Chapter 2 or 5 of this Part.

P2para.Text: The deduction is equal to the lesser of—

P3para.Text: the amount treated as earnings, and
the amount that would have been so deductible.

P1group.Title: Deductions where living accommodation provided

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings is allowed if—

P3para.Text: the earnings include an amount treated as earnings under Chapter 5 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: living accommodation), and

had the employee incurred and paid an amount equal to that amount for the accommodation in the tax year, the whole or part of the amount paid would have been deductible under Chapter 2 or 5 of this Part.

P2para.Text: The deduction is equal to the amount that would have been so deductible.

P1group.Title: Deductions where certain employment-related benefits provided

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings is allowed if—

P3para.Text: the earnings include an amount treated as earnings under Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of a benefit, ...

Text.Addition: the cost of the benefit was determined under section 204 or 206, and

P3para.Text: had the employee incurred and paid the cost of the benefit, the whole or part of the amount paid would have been deductible under Chapter 2 or 5 of this Part.

P2para.Text: The deduction is equal to the amount that would have been so deductible.
For the purposes of this section, the cost of the benefit is determined in accordance with section 204 or 206 .

P1group.Title: Scope of this Chapter: amounts fixed by Treasury

P1para.Text: A deduction from an employee’s earnings for an amount is allowed under this Chapter where the amount has been fixed by the Treasury by reference to the employee’s employment.

P1group.Title: Fixed sum deductions for repairing and maintaining work equipment

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed for the sum, if any, fixed by the Treasury as in their opinion representing the average annual expenses incurred by employees of the class to which the employee belongs in respect of the repair and maintenance of work equipment.
The Treasury may only fix such a sum for a class of employees if they are satisfied that—

P3para.Text: the employees are generally responsible for the whole or part of the expense of repairing and maintaining the work equipment, and
the expenses for which they are generally responsible would be deductible from the employees' earnings under section 336 if paid by them.

P2para.Text: No deduction is allowed under this section if the employer pays or reimburses the expenses in respect of which the sum is fixed or would do so if requested.
If the employer pays or reimburses part of those expenses or would do so if requested, the amount of the deduction is reduced by the amount which is or would be paid or reimbursed.
In this section “work equipment” means tools or special clothing.
This section needs to be read with section 330(2) (prevention of double deductions).

P1group.Title: Fixed sum deductions from earnings payable out of public revenue

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from earnings payable out of the public revenue for the employee’s fixed sum expenses in respect of the duties to which the earnings relate.

“Fixed sum expenses” means the sum, if any, fixed by the Treasury as in their opinion representing the average annual expenses which employees of the employee’s description are obliged to pay wholly, exclusively and necessarily in the performance of duties to which such earnings relate.
This section needs to be read with section 330(2) (prevention of double deductions).

Chapter.Title: Deductions for earnings representing benefits or reimbursed expenses

P1group.Title: Scope of this Chapter: earnings representing benefits or reimbursed expenses

P2para.Text: A deduction from a person’s earnings for an amount is allowed under the following provisions of this Chapter where the amount is included in the earnings in respect of—

P3para.Text: provision made for the person, or
expenses reimbursed by another person.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter references to “the included amount” are references to the amount so included.
If the included amount is an amount treated as earnings under—

P3para.Text: Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens),
Chapter 5 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: living accommodation), or
Chapter 10 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge),

P2para.Text: a deduction may be allowed instead in respect of the benefit in question under Chapter 3 of this Part (deductions from benefits code earnings).

Title.Emphasis: Travel costs and expenses where duties performed abroad

P1group.Title: Travel costs and expenses where duties performed abroad: employee’s travel

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from earnings which are relevant taxable earnings if—

P3para.Text: the earnings include an amount in respect of—

P4para.Text: the provision of travel facilities for a journey made by the employee, or
the reimbursement of expenses incurred by the employee on such a journey, and

P3para.Text: the circumstances fall within Case A, B or C.

P2para.Text: The deduction is equal to the included amount.
Case A is where—

P3para.Text: the employee is absent from the United Kingdom wholly and exclusively for the purpose of performing the duties of one or more employments,
the duties concerned can only be performed outside the United Kingdom, and
the journey is—

P4para.Text: a journey from a place outside the United Kingdom where such duties are performed to a place in the United Kingdom, or
a return journey following such a journey.

P2para.Text: Case B is where—

P3para.Text: the duties of the employment are performed partly outside the United Kingdom,
those duties are not performed on a vessel,
the journey is between a place in the United Kingdom and a place outside the United Kingdom where duties of the employment are performed,
the duties performed outside the United Kingdom can only be performed there, and
the journey is made wholly and exclusively for the purpose of performing them or returning after performing them.

P2para.Text: Case C is where—

P3para.Text: the duties of the employment are performed partly outside the United Kingdom,
those duties are performed on a vessel,
the journey is between a place in the United Kingdom and a place outside the United Kingdom where duties of the employment are performed,
the duties performed outside the United Kingdom can only be performed there, and
the journey is made wholly and exclusively for the purpose of performing those duties, or those duties and other duties of the employment, or returning after performing them.

Text.Addition: In this section “relevant taxable earnings” means general earnings for a tax year
... that—
are taxable earnings under section 15, and

Addition.Substitution: if the tax year is tax year 2024-2025 or an earlier tax year, would be taxable earnings under section 15 even if the employee made a claim under section 809B of ITA 2007 (claim for remittance basis) for that year, or

if the tax year is tax year 2025-2026 or a later tax year and the employee is a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 for that tax year, are not qualifying foreign general earnings within the meaning of section 41T (qualifying foreign general earnings).

P1group.Title: Travel costs and expenses where duties performed abroad: visiting spouse’s , civil partner's or child’s travel

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from earnings which are relevant taxable earnings if—

P3para.Text: the earnings include an amount in respect of—

P4para.Text: the provision of travel facilities for a journey made by the employee’s spouse , civil partner or child, or
the reimbursement of expenses incurred by the employee on such a journey, and

P3para.Text: conditions A to C are met.

P2para.Text: The deduction is equal to the included amount.
Condition A is that the employee is absent from the United Kingdom for a continuous period of at least 60 days for the purpose of performing the duties of one or more employments.
Condition B is that the journey is between a place in the United Kingdom and a place outside the United Kingdom where such duties are performed.
Condition C is that the employee’s spouse , civil partner or child is—

P3para.Text: accompanying the employee at the beginning of the period of absence,
visiting the employee during that period, or
returning to a place in the United Kingdom after so accompanying or visiting the employee.

P2para.Text: A deduction is not allowed under this section for more than two outward and two return journeys by the same person in a tax year.
In this section “child” includes a stepchild and an illegitimate child, but not a person who is 18 or over at the beginning of the outward journey.

Text.Addition: In this section “
” has the meaning given by section 370(6).

P1group.Title: Where seafarers' duties are performed

P1para.Text: For the purposes of—

P3para.Text: section 370 (employee’s travel costs and expenses where duties performed abroad), and
section 371 (visiting spouse’s , civil partner's or child’s travel costs and expenses where duties performed abroad),

P1para.Text: whether duties performed on a vessel are performed in or outside the United Kingdom is determined without regard to section 40(2) (certain duties treated as performed in UK).

Title.Emphasis: Travel costs and expenses of non-resident or qualifying new resident employees where duties performed in UK

P1group.Title: Non-resident or qualifying new resident employee’s travel costs and expenses where duties performed in UK

P2para.Text: This section applies if a person (“the employee”) who is non-UK resident or a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 of this Act or Chapter 5 of Part 8 of ITTOIA 2005 (see section 845B of that Act)—

P3para.Text: receives earnings from an employment for duties performed in the United Kingdom, and
an amount is included in the earnings in respect of—

P4para.Text: the provision of travel facilities for a journey made by the employee, or
the reimbursement of expenses incurred by the employee on such a journey.

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from earnings from the employment which are earnings charged on receipt if the journey meets conditions A and B.
Condition A is that the journey ends on, or during the period of 5 years beginning with, a date that is a qualifying arrival date in relation to the employee (see section 375).
Condition B is that the journey is made—

P3para.Text: from a country outside the United Kingdom in which the employee normally lives at the time the journey is made to a place in the United Kingdom in order to perform duties of the employment, or
to such a country from a place in the United Kingdom in order to return to such a country after performing such duties.

P2para.Text: If the journey is wholly for a purpose specified in subsection (4), the deduction is equal to the included amount.
If the journey is only partly for such a purpose, the deduction is equal to so much of the included amount as is properly attributable to that purpose.

P1group.Title: Non-resident or qualifying new resident employee’s spouse’s , civil partner's or child’s travel costs and expenses where duties performed in UK

P2para.Text: This section applies if a person (“the employee”) who is non-UK resident or a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 of this Act or Chapter 5 of Part 8 of ITTOIA 2005 (see section 845B of that Act)—

P3para.Text: receives earnings from an employment for duties performed in the United Kingdom, and
an amount is included in the earnings in respect of—

P4para.Text: the provision of travel facilities for a journey made by the employee’s spouse , civil partner or child, or
the reimbursement of expenses incurred by the employee on such a journey.

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from earnings from the employment which are earnings charged on receipt if conditions A to C are met.
Condition A is that the journey—

P3para.Text: is made between a country outside the United Kingdom in which the employee normally lives at the time the journey is made and a place in the United Kingdom, and
ends on, or during the period of 5 years beginning with, a date that is a qualifying arrival date in relation to the employee (see section 375).

P2para.Text: Condition B is that the employee is in the United Kingdom for a continuous period of at least 60 days for the purpose of performing the duties of one or more employments from which the employee receives earnings for duties performed in the United Kingdom.
Condition C is that the employee’s spouse , civil partner or child is—

P3para.Text: accompanying the employee at the beginning of that period,
visiting the employee during that period, or
returning to a country outside the United Kingdom in which the employee normally lives at the time the journey is made, after so accompanying or visiting the employee.

P2para.Text: If the journey is wholly for the purpose of so accompanying or visiting the employee or so returning, the deduction is equal to the included amount.
If the journey is only partly for that purpose, the deduction is equal to so much of the included amount as is properly attributable to that purpose.
A deduction is not allowed under this section for more than two inward journeys and two return journeys by the same person in a tax year.
In this section “child” includes a stepchild and an illegitimate child, but not a person who is 18 or over at the beginning of the inward journey.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “qualifying arrival date”

P2para.Text: For the purposes of sections 373(3) and 374(3), a date is a qualifying arrival date in relation to a person if—

P3para.Text: it is a date on which the person arrives in the United Kingdom to perform duties of an employment from which the person receives earnings for duties performed in the United Kingdom, and
condition A or B is met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the person has not been in the United Kingdom for any purpose during the period of 2 years ending with the day before the date.
Condition B is that the person was not resident in the United Kingdom in either of the 2 tax years preceding the tax year in which the date falls.

If, in a case where condition B applies, there are 2 or more dates in the tax year on which the person arrives in the United Kingdom to perform duties of an employment from which the person receives earnings for duties performed in the United Kingdom, the qualifying arrival date is the earliest of them.

Title.Emphasis: Foreign accommodation and subsistence costs and expenses

P1group.Title: Foreign accommodation and subsistence costs and expenses (overseas employments)

P2para.Text: A deduction from earnings from an employment is allowed if—

P3para.Text: the duties of the employment are performed wholly outside the United Kingdom,
the employee is UK resident,

in a case where the employer is a foreign employer, the employee is not a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 of this Act or Chapter 5 of Part 8 of ITTOIA 2005 (see section 845B of that Act), and
the earnings include an amount in respect of—

P4para.Text: the provision of accommodation or subsistence outside the United Kingdom for the employee for the purpose of enabling the employee to perform the duties of the employment, or
the reimbursement of expenses incurred by the employee on such accommodation or subsistence for that purpose.

P2para.Text: If the accommodation or subsistence is wholly for that purpose, the deduction is equal to the included amount.
If the accommodation or subsistence is only partly for that purpose, the deduction is equal to so much of the included amount as is properly attributable to that purpose.
Subsection (5) applies if in the tax year the employment is in substance one whose duties fall to be performed outside the United Kingdom.

Duties of the employment performed in the United Kingdom, whose performance is merely incidental to the performance of duties outside the United Kingdom, are to be treated for the purposes of subsection (1)(a) as performed outside the United Kingdom.

P1group.Title: Costs and expenses in respect of personal security assets and services

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: there is a special threat to an employee’s personal physical security which arises wholly or mainly because of the employee’s employment,
an asset or service which improves personal security is provided for or used by the employee to meet the threat,
the employee’s earnings include an amount in respect of—

P4para.Text: the provision or use, or
expenses connected with it,

P3para.Text: because the whole or part of the cost of the provision or use is borne, or the expenses are reimbursed to the employee, by or on behalf of another person (“the provider”), and
the provider’s sole object in bearing the whole or part of the cost or reimbursing the expenses is meeting the threat.

P2para.Text: In the case of such an asset, if the provider intends it to be used solely for the purpose of improving personal physical security, a deduction equal to the included amount is allowed.
If the provider intends the asset to be used solely to improve personal physical security, any use of the asset incidental to that purpose is ignored.

If the provider intends the asset to be used only partly to improve personal physical security, a deduction equal to the proportion of the included amount attributable to the intended use for that purpose is allowed.
In determining whether or not this section applies in relation to an asset, it does not matter if—

P3para.Text: the asset becomes fixed to land (even a dwelling or grounds), or
the employee is or becomes entitled—

P4para.Text: to the property in the asset, or
if the asset is a fixture, to any estate or interest in the land concerned.

P2para.Text: In the case of a service within subsection (1), if the benefit resulting to the employee consists wholly or mainly of an improvement of the employee’s personal physical security, a deduction equal to the included amount is allowed.

The fact that an asset or a service improves the personal physical security of a member of the employee’s family or household, as well as that of the employee, does not prevent a deduction being allowed.
In this section—

Para.Text: “asset” includes equipment or a structure (such as a wall), but not a car, ship or aircraft or a dwelling or grounds appurtenant to a dwelling, and
“service” does not include a dwelling or grounds appurtenant to a dwelling.

P1group.Title: Deduction from seafarers' earnings: eligibility

P2para.Text: A deduction is allowed from earnings from an employment as a seafarer if—

P3para.Text: the earnings are relevant general earnings,
the duties of the employment are performed wholly or partly outside the United Kingdom, and
any of those duties are performed in the course of an eligible period.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “eligible period” means a period consisting of at least 365 days which is either—

P3para.Text: a period of consecutive days of absence from the United Kingdom, or
a combined period.

P2para.Text: A combined period is a period—

P3para.Text: at least half of the days in which are days of absence from the United Kingdom, and
which consists of 3 consecutive periods, A, B and C, where—

Para.Text: A is a period of consecutive days of absence from the United Kingdom or a period which is itself a combined period,
B is a period of not more than 183 days, and
C is a period of consecutive days of absence from the United Kingdom.

P2para.Text: For this purpose a person is only regarded as being absent from the United Kingdom on any day if absent at the end of the day.

Text.Substitution: Relevant general earnings” means—
taxable earnings under section 15, 22 or 26, or
general earnings—
to which section 27 applies, and
which are for a period in which the employee is liable under the law of an
State (other than the United Kingdom) to tax in that State by reason of domicile or residence.

P1group.Title: Calculating the deduction

P2para.Text: The deduction under section 378—

P3para.Text: is allowed from the amount of the earnings from the employment attributable to the eligible period, and
is equal to that amount.

P2para.Text: Earnings from the employment for a period of leave immediately after the eligible period are to be regarded as earnings attributable to the eligible period if or to the extent that they are earnings for the tax year in which the eligible period ends.
This section is subject to section 380 (limit on deduction where UK duties etc. make amount unreasonable).

P1group.Title: Limit on deduction where UK duties etc. make amount unreasonable

P2para.Text: If—

P3para.Text: section 378 (deduction from seafarers' earnings: eligibility) applies to earnings for a tax year, and
in the tax year the employee performs some of the duties of the employment as a seafarer or of any associated employments in the United Kingdom,

P2para.Text: the amount of earnings in respect of which the deduction under this Chapter is allowed is subject to the following limitation.
The amount is restricted to the proportion of the aggregate earnings for that year from the employment as a seafarer and all associated employments that is reasonable having regard to—

P3para.Text: the nature of and time devoted to the duties performed outside and in the United Kingdom, and
all other relevant circumstances.

P2para.Text: In this section “associated employments” means employments with the same employer or with associated employers.

The same rules for determining whether employers are associated apply for the purposes of this section as apply for section 24(4) (limit on chargeable overseas earnings where duties of associated employment performed in UK) (see section 24(5)).

P1group.Title: Taking account of other deductions

P1para.Text: For the purposes of sections 379 and 380, the amount of the earnings from an employment for a tax year is the amount remaining after any deductions under—

P3para.Text: section 232 (giving effect to mileage allowance relief),
Chapter 2, 3, 4 or 5 of this Part,

Text.Substitution: section 262 of
CAA
2001 (capital allowances to be given effect by treating them as deductions from earnings), and
sections 188 to 194 of FA 2004 (contributions to registered pension schemes).

P1group.Title: Duties on board ship

P2para.Text: Duties which a person performs on a ship engaged—

P3para.Text: on a voyage beginning or ending outside the United Kingdom (but excluding any part of it beginning and ending in the United Kingdom), or
on a part beginning or ending outside the United Kingdom of any other voyage,

P2para.Text: are treated as performed outside the United Kingdom for the purposes of this Chapter.
Duties which a person performs on a vessel engaged on a voyage not extending to a port outside the United Kingdom are treated for the purposes of this Chapter as performed in the United Kingdom.
For the purposes of subsection (1) the areas designated under section 1(7) of the Continental Shelf Act 1964 (c. 29) are treated as part of the United Kingdom.
Subsection (1) applies despite anything to the contrary in section 40 (duties on board vessel or aircraft).

P1group.Title: Place of performance of incidental duties

P2para.Text: For the purposes of section 378(1)(b) (deduction from seafarers' earnings: eligibility), duties of an employment as a seafarer which are performed outside the United Kingdom are treated as performed in the United Kingdom if conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that in the tax year in which the duties are performed the employment is in substance one whose duties fall to be performed in the United Kingdom.
Condition B is that the performance of the duties performed outside the United Kingdom is merely incidental to the performance of duties in the United Kingdom.
Section 39 (duties in UK merely incidental to duties outside UK) does not affect the question—

P3para.Text: where any duties are performed, or
whether a person is absent from the United Kingdom,

P2para.Text: for the purposes of section 378(1) to (3).

P1group.Title: Meaning of employment “as a seafarer”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter employment “as a seafarer” means an employment (other than Crown employment) consisting of the performance of duties on a ship or of such duties and others incidental to them.
In this section “Crown employment” means employment under the Crown—

P3para.Text: which is of a public nature,
which is not employment in the Royal Fleet Auxiliary Service, and
the earnings from which are payable out of the public revenue of the United Kingdom or of Northern Ireland.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “ship”

Text.Substitution: In this Chapter “
” does not include an offshore installation.

Part.Title: Employment income: income which is not earnings or share-related

P1group.Title: Charge on payments to non-approved retirement benefits schemes
Meaning of “non-approved retirement benefits scheme”
Apportionment of payments in respect of more than one employee
Exception: employments where earnings charged on remittance
Exception: non-domiciled employees with foreign employers
Exception: seafarers with overseas earnings
Relief where no benefits are paid or payable
Application of this Chapter

Text.Substitution: This Chapter applies to relevant benefits provided under an employer-financed retirement benefits scheme.
Section 393A defines “employer-financed retirement benefits scheme” and section 393B defines “relevant benefits”.

Text.Addition: In this Chapter “
” means a scheme for the provision of benefits consisting of or including relevant benefits to or in respect of employees or former employees of an employer.
But neither—
a registered pension scheme, nor
a section 615(3) scheme,
is an employer-financed retirement benefits scheme.
” means a superannuation fund to which section 615(3) of
ICTA
applies.
” includes a deed, agreement, series of agreements, or other arrangements.
In this Chapter “
” means any lump sum, gratuity or other benefit (including a non-cash benefit) provided (or to be provided)—
on or in anticipation of the retirement of an employee or former employee,
on the death of an employee or former employee,
after the retirement or death of an employee or former employee in connection with past service,
on or in anticipation of, or in connection with, any change in the nature of service of an employee, or
to any person by virtue of a pension sharing order or provision relating to an employee or former employee.
But—
benefits charged to tax under Part 9 (pension income)

Addition.Addition: , or that would be charged to tax under that Part but for section 573(2A) or (2B), 646D or 646E

Text.Addition: benefits chargeable to tax by virtue of Schedule 34 to FA 2004 (which applies certain charges under Part 4 of that Act in relation to non-UK schemes), and
excluded benefits,
are not relevant benefits.
The following are “excluded benefits”—
benefits in respect of ill-health or disablement of an employee during service,
benefits in respect of the death by accident of an employee during service,
benefits under a relevant life policy, and
benefits of any description prescribed by regulations made by the Board of Inland Revenue.

In subsection (3)(c)
“
” means—

Addition.Substitution: an excepted group life policy as defined in section 480 of

Text.Addition: a policy of life insurance the terms of which provide for the payment of benefits on the death of a single individual and with respect to which

Addition.Substitution: condition A in section 481 of that Act would be met if paragraph (a) in that condition referred to the death, in any circumstances or except in specified circumstances, of that individual (rather than the death in any circumstances of each of the individuals insured under the policy) and if the condition did not include paragraph (b), and
conditions C and D in that section and conditions A and C in section 482 of that Act are met, or

Text.Addition: a policy of life insurance that would be within paragraph (a) or (b) but for the fact that it provides for a benefit which is an excluded benefit under or by virtue of paragraph (a), (b) or (d) of subsection (3).

Addition.Addition: Regulations under subsection (3)(d) may include provision having effect in relation to times before they are made.

Text.Addition:
In subsection (1)(e)
“
” means any such order or provision as is mentioned in section 28(1) of
1999 or Article 25(1) of WRP(
NI

P1group.Title: Charge on benefit to which this Chapter applies

P2para.Text: If a benefit to which this Chapter applies is received by an individual, the amount of the benefit counts as employment income of the individual for the relevant tax year.

Text.Addition: Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to the benefit if the total amount of the benefits to which this Chapter applies received by the individual in the relevant tax year does not exceed £100.

P2para.Text: If a benefit to which this Chapter applies is received by a person who is not an individual, the person who is (or persons who are) the responsible person in relation to the scheme under which the benefit is provided is chargeable to income tax on the amount of the benefit for the relevant tax year.
In this section the “relevant tax year” is the tax year in which the benefit is received.
For the purposes of subsection (2), the rate of tax is 45% or such other rate as may for the time being be specified by the Treasury by order.

Text.Addition: Subsection (4B) applies if the receipt of a benefit to which this Chapter applies gives rise to other relevant income of the employee, or the former employee, to or in respect of whom the benefit is provided.
Subsection (1) or (2) (as the case may be) applies to the amount of the benefit only so far as that amount exceeds the other relevant income.
In subsections (4A) and (4B) “
” means—
general earnings of the employee or former employee which are chargeable to income tax,
an amount which counts as employment income of the employee or former employee under Chapter 2 of Part 7A,

Addition.Addition: an amount which would count as employment income of the employee or former employee under that Chapter but for the application of section 554Z5 (overlap with earlier relevant step), or

Addition.Substitution: an amount which would be within paragraph (a), (b) or (ba) apart from—
the employee or former employee having been non-UK resident for any tax year, or
any tax year having been a split year as respects the employee or former employee.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises by virtue of any other provision of this Act in respect of a benefit to which this Chapter applies.

Text.Addition: Subsection (5) does not affect—
any liability to income tax on general earnings, or
any liability to income tax on an amount which counts as employment income under Chapter 2 of Part 7A.
This section applies if an individual is temporarily non-resident.
Any benefits within subsection (3) are to be treated for the purposes of section 394(1) as if they were received by the individual in the period of return.
A benefit is within this subsection if—
this Chapter applies to it,
it is in the form of a lump sum,
it is received by the individual in the temporary period of non-residence, and
ignoring this section—
no charge to tax arises by virtue of section 394(1) in respect of it, but
such a charge would arise if the existence of any double taxation relief arrangements were disregarded.
Subsection (3)(d)(i) includes a case where the charge could be prevented by making a DTR claim, even if no claim is in fact made.
Subsection (2) does not affect the operation of section 394(1A) (and, accordingly, “
” for the purposes of section 394(1A) remains the tax year in which the benefit is actually received).

Nothing in any double taxation relief arrangements is to be read as preventing the individual from being chargeable to income tax in respect of any benefit treated by virtue of this section as received in the period of return (or as preventing a charge to that tax from arising as a result).
Part 4 of Schedule 45 to FA 2013 (statutory residence test: anti-avoidance) explains—
when an individual is to be regarded as “temporarily non-resident”, and
what “the temporary period of non-residence” and “the period of return” mean.
In this section—
” means arrangements that have effect under section 2(1) of TIOPA 2010;
” means a claim for relief under section 6 of that Act.

Text.Substitution: This section applies in relation to a relevant benefit under an employer-financed retirement benefits scheme in the form of a lump sum where, under the scheme, an employee has paid any sum or sums by way of contribution to the provision of the lump sum.
The amount which, by virtue of section 394, counts as employment income, or is chargeable to tax under
, is the amount of the lump sum reduced by the sum, or the aggregate of the sums, paid by the employee by way of contribution to the provision of the lump sum.
A reduction under this section may not be claimed in respect of the same contribution in relation to more than one lump sum.
It is to be assumed, unless the contrary is shown, that no reduction is applicable under this section.

Title.Addition: Benefits under old section 222 schemes not taxed by virtue of section 394

Text.Addition: Section 394 does not apply to a benefit provided under an employer–financed retirement benefits scheme if—
immediately before 6th April 1980 the scheme was approved under section 222 of

Abbreviation.Expansion: Income and Corporation Taxes Act 1970 c. 10

Text.Addition: the scheme was not approved under Chapter
of Part II of
no material changes have been made to the terms on which benefits are provided under the scheme after 5th April 1980, and
no contributions have been paid under the scheme after that date.

Title.Addition: Exemption or reduction for foreign service

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
a benefit to which this Chapter applies is provided to or in respect of an employee or former employee in the form of a lump sum,
the employer-financed retirement benefits scheme under which the lump sum is provided is established in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom,
the lump sum is received by the employee or former employee or a related person,

Addition.Addition: the recipient is not resident in the United Kingdom in the tax year in which the lump sum is received,

Text.Addition: all or part of the lump sum (“the relevant part”) would, but for this section, count as employment income by virtue of section 394(1) or be chargeable to income tax under section 394(2) (account having been taken of section 394(4B) and section 395), and
the service in respect of which rights to receive the relevant part of the lump sum accrued (referred to as “reckonable service”) is or includes foreign service.
Section 394(1) or, as the case may be, section 394(2) does not apply to the relevant part of the lump sum if the condition in subsection (3) is met.
The condition is that—
three-quarters or more of the period of reckonable service is made up of foreign service,
if the period of reckonable service exceeds 10 years, the whole of the last 10 years of that period is made up of foreign service, or
if the period of reckonable service exceeds 20 years, one-half or more of that period, including any 10 of the last 20 years, is made up of foreign service.

If the condition in subsection (3) is not met, the amount that counts as employment income by virtue of section 394(1) or, as the case may be, is chargeable to income tax under section 394(2) is to be reduced by the appropriate proportion.

The appropriate proportion is a proportion of the relevant part of the lump sum equal to the proportion that the period of foreign service included in the reckonable service bears to the period of reckonable service.
In determining the service in respect of which rights to receive the relevant part of the lump sum accrued—
service in a previous employment or with a previous employer is to be taken into account if rights to receive the relevant part of the lump sum also accrued in respect of that service, and

it does not matter if the rights originally accrued under a different employer-financed retirement benefits scheme (whether one established in the United Kingdom or in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom).
“Related person”, in relation to an employee or former employee (E), means any of the following—
E’s spouse or civil partner or E’s widow or widower or surviving civil partner,

a person who is financially dependent on E, whose financial relationship with E is one of mutual dependence or who is dependent on E because of physical or mental impairment (or, if the lump sum is paid after E’s death, anyone who was such a person at the time of E’s death), and
E’s personal representatives.
In this section “foreign service” has the meaning given by section
In section 395B “
” means service to which subsection (2), (3), (6) or (8) applies.
This subsection applies to service in or after the tax year 2013–14—
to the extent that it consists of duties performed outside the United Kingdom in respect of which earnings would not be relevant earnings, or
if a deduction equal to the whole amount of the earnings from the employment was or would have been allowable under Chapter 6 of Part 5 (deductions from seafarers' earnings).
This subsection applies to service in or after the tax year 2003–04 but before the tax year 2013–14 such that—
any earnings from the employment would not be relevant earnings, or
a deduction equal to the whole amount of the earnings from the employment was or would have been allowable under Chapter 6 of Part 5 (deductions from seafarers' earnings).

Addition.Substitution: for service in or after the tax year 2025-26, earnings—

if the employee is a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 for that tax year, which are not qualifying foreign general earnings within the meaning of section 41T (qualifying foreign general earnings), and

for service before tax year 2025-26, earnings to which section 15 applies and to which that section would apply even if the employee made a claim under section 809B of ITA 2007 (claim for remittance basis) for that year.

Text.Addition: In subsection (3) “
” means—
for service in or after the tax year 2008–09, earnings—
which are for a tax year in which the employee is ordinarily UK resident,
to which section 15 applies, and
to which that section would apply even if the employee made a claim under section 809B of ITA 2007 (claim for remittance basis) for that year, and
for service before the tax year 2008–09, general earnings to which section 15 or 21 as originally enacted applies.
This subsection applies to service before the tax year 2003–04 and after the tax year 1973–74 such that—
the emoluments from the employment were not chargeable under Case I of Schedule E, or would not have been so chargeable had there been any, or
a deduction equal to the whole amount of the emoluments from the employment was or would have been allowable under a foreign earnings deduction provision.
In subsection (6) “
” means—
paragraph 1 of Schedule 2 to FA 1974,
paragraph 1 of Schedule 7 to FA 1977, or
section 192A or 193(1) of ICTA.
This subsection applies to service before the tax year 1974-75 such that tax was not chargeable in respect of the emoluments of the employment—
in the tax year 1956–57 or later, under Case I of Schedule E, or
in earlier tax years, under Schedule E,
or it would not have been so chargeable had there been any such emoluments.

P1group.Title: Certain lump sums not taxed by virtue of section 394
Certain lump sums: calculation of amount taxed by virtue of section 394
Valuation of benefits

P2para.Text: In the case of a cash benefit, for the purposes of this Chapter the amount of a benefit is taken to be the amount received.
In the case of a non-cash benefit, for the purposes of this Chapter the amount of a benefit is taken to be the greater of—

P3para.Text: the amount of earnings (as defined in Chapter 1 of Part 3) that the benefit would give rise to if it were received for performance of the duties of an employment (money’s worth), and
the cash equivalent of the benefit under the benefits code if it were so received and the code applied to it.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (2) the benefits code has effect with the modifications in subsections (4) to (6).
References in the benefits code to the employee are to be taken as references to the person by whom the benefit is received.
References in the benefits code to the employer are to be taken as including references to the former employer.
Where—

P3para.Text: section 106 (cash equivalent: cost of accommodation over £75,000) applies, and
the amount referred to in section 105(2)(b) (the sum made good) exceeds the amount referred to in section 105(2)(a) (the rental value),

P2para.Text: the amount to be subtracted under paragraph (b) of step 4 of the calculation in section 106(2) is that excess (and not only the excess rent referred to there).

P1group.Title: Employment-related loans: interest treated as paid

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: an amount consisting of, or including, an amount representing the benefit of a loan (“a taxable amount”) counts as employment income of an individual in a tax year under section 394(1), or
the person who is (or any of the persons who are) the responsible person in relation to a scheme is charged to tax on a taxable amount ... under section 394(2).

P2para.Text: The individual or the responsible person is to be treated for all purposes of the Tax Acts (other than this Chapter) as having paid interest on the loan in the tax year equal to the amount representing the cash equivalent of the loan.
The interest is to be treated—

P3para.Text: as accruing during the period in the tax year during which the loan is outstanding, and
as paid at the end of the period.

P2para.Text: The interest is not to be treated—

P3para.Text: as income of the person making the loan, or
as relevant loan interest to which section 369 of ICTA applies (mortgage interest payable under deduction of tax).

Text.Addition: The following heads specify the person who is, or persons who are, the responsible person in relation to an employer-financed retirement benefits scheme for the purposes of this Chapter.

But if a person is, or persons are, the responsible person in relation to the scheme by virtue of being specified under one head, no-one is the responsible person in relation to the scheme by virtue of being specified under a later head.
If there are one or more trustees of the scheme who are resident in the United Kingdom, that trustee or each of those trustees.
If there are one or more persons who control the management of the scheme, that person or each of those persons.

If alive or still in existence, the employer, or any of the employers, who established the scheme and any person by whom that employer, or any of those employers, has been directly or indirectly succeeded in relation to the provision of benefits under the scheme.
Any employer of employees to or in respect of whom benefits are, or are to be, provided under the scheme.
If there are one or more trustees of the scheme who are not resident in the United Kingdom, that trustee or each of those trustees.

Text.Substitution: In this Chapter—
” has the meaning given by section 393A;
” has the meaning given by section 393B; and
” has the meaning given by section 399A.

Chapter.Title: Payments and benefits on termination of employment etc.

P1group.Title: Application of this Chapter

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to payments and other benefits which are received directly or indirectly in consideration or in consequence of, or otherwise in connection with—

P3para.Text: the termination of a person’s employment,
a change in the duties of a person’s employment, or
a change in the earnings from a person’s employment,

P2para.Text: by the person, or the person’s spouse or civil partner, blood relative, dependant or personal representatives.
Subsection (1) is subject to subsection (3) and sections 405 to 414A (exceptions for certain payments and benefits).
This Chapter does not apply to any payment or other benefit chargeable to income tax apart from this Chapter.
For the purposes of this Chapter—

P3para.Text: a payment or other benefit which is provided on behalf of, or to the order of, the employee or former employee is treated as received by the employee or former employee, and
in relation to a payment or other benefit—

P4para.Text: any reference to the employee or former employee is to the person mentioned in subsection (1), and
any reference to the employer or former employer is to be read accordingly.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “benefit”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “benefit” includes anything in respect of which, were it received for performance of the duties of the employment, an amount—

P3para.Text: would be taxable earnings from the employment, or
would be such earnings apart from an earnings-only exemption.
This is subject to subsections (2) to (4).

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “benefit” does not include a benefit received in connection with the termination of a person’s employment that is a benefit which, were it received for performance of the duties of the employment, would fall within—

P3para.Text: section 239(4) (exemption of benefits connected with taxable cars and vans and exempt heavy goods vehicles), so far as that section applies to a benefit connected with a car or van,
section 269 (exemption where benefits or money obtained in connection with taxable car or van or exempt heavy goods vehicle),
section 319 (mobile telephones), or
section 320 (limited exemption for computer equipment).

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “benefit” does not include a benefit received in connection with any change in the duties of, or earnings from, a person’s employment to the extent that it is a benefit which, were it received for performance of the duties of the employment, would fall within section 271(1) (limited exemption of removal benefits and expenses).
The right to receive a payment or benefit is not itself a benefit for the purposes of this Chapter.

Title.Emphasis: Payments and benefits treated as employment income

Title.Addition: Split of payments and other benefits between sections 402B and 403

Text.Addition: In this Chapter “
” means a payment or other benefit to which this Chapter applies because of section 401(1)(a).
Section 402B (termination awards not benefiting from threshold treated as earnings) applies to termination awards to the extent determined under section 402C.
Section 403 (charge on payment or benefit where threshold applies) applies to termination awards so far as they are not ones to which section 402B applies.
Section 403 also applies to payments and other benefits to which this Chapter applies because of section 401(1)(b) or (c) (change in duties or earnings).

Title.Addition: Termination awards not benefiting from threshold to be treated as earnings

Text.Addition: The amount of a termination award to which this section applies—
is treated as an amount of earnings of the employee, or former employee, from the employment ,
See also section 7(3)(b) and (5)(ca) (which cause amounts treated as earnings under this section to be included in general earnings).
Section 403(3) (when benefits are received) does not apply in relation to payments or other benefits to which this section applies.

Title.Addition: The termination awards to which section 402B applies

Text.Addition: This section has effect for the purpose of identifying the extent to which section 402B applies to termination awards in respect of the termination of the employment of the employee.
In this section “
” means a termination award that is neither—
a redundancy payment, nor
so much of an approved contractual payment as is equal to or less than the amount which would have been due if a redundancy payment had been payable.

If the post-employment notice pay (see section 402D) in respect of the termination is greater than, or equal to, the total amount of the relevant termination awards in respect of the termination, section 402B applies to all of those relevant termination awards.
If the post-employment notice pay in respect of the termination is less than the total amount of the relevant termination awards in respect of the termination but is not nil—
section 402B applies to a part of those relevant termination awards, and
the amount of that part is equal to the post-employment notice pay.
Section 309(4) to (6) (meaning of “redundancy payment” and “approved contractual payment”
etc
) apply for the purposes of subsection (2) as they apply for the purposes of section 309.
“The post-employment notice pay” in respect of a termination is (subject to subsection (11)) given by—
where—
BP, D and P are given by subsections (3) to (7), and
T is the total of the amounts of any payment or benefit received in connection with the termination which—
would fall within section 401(1)(a) but for section 401(3),
is taxable as earnings under Chapter 1 of Part 3,
is not pay in respect of holiday entitlement for a period before the employment ends, and
is not a bonus payable for termination of the employment.
If the amount given by the formula in subsection (1) is a negative amount, the post-employment notice pay is nil.
Subject to subsections (5)
BP is the employee's basic pay (see subsection (7)) from the employment in respect of the last pay period of the employee to end before the trigger date,
P is the number of days in that pay period, and
D is the number of days in the post-employment notice period.
See section 402E for the meaning of “trigger date” and “post-employment notice period”.
If there is no pay period of the employee which ends before the trigger date then—
BP is the employee's basic pay from the employment in respect of the period starting with the first day of the employment and ending with the trigger date,
P is the number of days in that period, and
D is the number of days in the post-employment notice period.
If the last pay period of the employee to end before the trigger date is a month,

Addition.Addition: the employee's basic pay is paid in equal monthly instalments,

Text.Addition: the minimum notice (see section 402E) is given by contractual terms and is expressed to be a whole number of months, and the post-employment notice period is equal in length to the minimum notice or is otherwise a whole number of months, then—
BP is the employee's basic pay from the employment in respect of the last pay period of the employee to end before the trigger date,
P is 1, and
D is the length of the post-employment notice period expressed in months.

Addition.Addition: In any other case where the last pay period of the employee to end before the trigger date is a month and the employee's basic pay is paid in equal monthly instalments, then—
BP is the employee's basic pay from the employment in respect of the last pay period of the employee to end before the trigger date,
D is the number of days in the post-employment notice period.

Text.Addition: In this section “
” means—
employment income of the employee from the employment but disregarding—
any amount received by way of overtime, bonus, commission, gratuity or allowance,
any amount received in connection with the termination of the employment,
any amount treated as earnings under Chapters 2 to 10 of Part 3 (the benefits code) or which would be so treated apart from section 64,
any amount which is treated as earnings under Chapter 12 of Part 3 (amounts treated as earnings),
any amount which counts as employment income by virtue of Part 7 (income relating to securities and securities options), and
any employment-related securities that constitute earnings under Chapter 1 of Part 3 (earnings), and
any amount which the employee has given up the right to receive but which would have fallen within paragraph (a) had the employee not done so.
In subsection (7) “
” has the same meaning as it has in Chapter 1 of Part 7 (see section 421B).
The Treasury may by regulations amend this section for the purpose of altering the meaning of “basic pay”.
A statutory instrument containing regulations under subsection (9) may not be made unless a draft of it has been laid before, and approved by a resolution of, the House of Commons.

Where the purpose, or one of the purposes, of any arrangements is the avoidance of tax by causing the post-employment notice pay calculated under subsection (1) to be less than it would otherwise be, the post-employment notice pay is to be treated as the amount which the post-employment notice pay would have been but for the arrangements.
In subsection (11) “
” includes any scheme, arrangement or understanding of any kind, whether or not legally enforceable, involving a single transaction or two or more transactions.

Title.Addition: Meaning of “trigger date” and “post-employment notice period” in section 402D

Text.Addition: Subsections (2) and (4) to (6) have effect for the purposes of section 402D (and subsection (4) has effect also for the purposes of this section).
The “trigger date” is—
if the termination is not a notice case, the last day of the employment, and
if the termination is a notice case, the day the notice is given.
For the purposes of this section, the termination is a “notice case” if the employer or employee gives notice to the other to terminate the employment, and here it does not matter—
whether the notice is more or less than, or the same as, the minimum notice, or
if the employment ends before the notice expires.
The “minimum notice” is the minimum notice required to be given by the employer to terminate the employee's employment by notice in accordance with the law and contractual terms effective—
where the termination is not a notice case—
immediately before the employment ends, or
where the employment ends by agreement entered into after the start of the employment, immediately before the agreement is entered into, and
where the termination is a notice case, immediately before the notice is given.
The “post-employment notice period” is the period—
beginning at the end of the last day of the employment, and
ending with the earliest lawful termination date.
(But see subsection (8) for provision about limited-term contracts.)
If the earliest lawful termination date is, or precedes, the last day of the employment, the number of days in the post-employment notice period is nil.
“The earliest lawful termination date” is the last day of the period which—
is equal in length to the minimum notice, and
begins at the end of the trigger date.

In the case of a contract of employment which is a limited-term contract and which does not include provision for termination by notice by the employer, the post-employment notice period is the period—
beginning at the end of the last day of the employment, and
ending with the day of the occurrence of the limiting event.

If, in a case to which subsection (8) applies, on the last day of the employment the day of the occurrence of the limiting event is not ascertained or ascertainable (because, for example, the limiting event is the performance of a task), then subsection (8) has effect as if for paragraph (b) there were substituted—

ending with the day on which notice would have expired if the employer had, on the last day of the employment, given to the employee the minimum notice required to terminate the contract under section 86 of the Employment Rights Act 1996 (assuming that that section applies to the employment).
In this section “
” and “
” have the same meaning as in the Employment Rights Act 1996 (see section 235(2A) and (2B)).

P1group.Title: Charge on payment or other benefit where threshold applies

P2para.Text: The amount of a payment or benefit to which this section applies counts as employment income of the employee or former employee for the relevant tax year if and to the extent that it exceeds the £30,000 threshold.
In this section “the relevant tax year” means the tax year in which the payment or other benefit is received.
For the purposes of this Chapter (but see section 402B(3)) —

P3para.Text: a cash benefit is treated as received—

P4para.Text: when it is paid or a payment is made on account of it, or
when the recipient becomes entitled to require payment of or on account of it, and

P3para.Text: a non-cash benefit is treated as received when it is used or enjoyed.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter the amount of a payment or benefit in respect of an employee or former employee exceeds the £30,000 threshold if and to the extent that, when aggregated with—

Text.Substitution: other payments or benefits in respect of the employee or former employee that are payments or benefits to which this section applies, and
other payments or benefits in respect of the employee or former employee that are payments or benefits—
received in the tax year 2017-18 or an earlier tax year, and
to which this Chapter applied in the tax year of receipt,

P2para.Text: it exceeds £30,000 according to the rules in section 404 (how the £30,000 threshold applies).
If it is received after the death of the employee or former employee—

P3para.Text: the amount of a payment or benefit to which this section applies counts as the employment income of the personal representatives for the relevant year if or to the extent that it exceeds £30,000 according to the rules in section 404, and
the tax is accordingly to be assessed and charged on them and is a debt due from and payable out of the estate.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter references to the taxable person are to the person in relation to whom subsection (1) or (5) provides for an amount to count as employment income or, as the case may be, in relation to whom section 402B(1) provides for an amount to be treated as an amount of earnings .

P1group.Title: How the £30,000 threshold applies

P2para.Text: For the purpose of the £30,000 threshold in section 403(4) and (5), the payments and other benefits provided in respect of an employee or former employee which are to be aggregated are those provided—

P3para.Text: in respect of the same employment,
in respect of different employments with the same employer, and
in respect of employments with employers who are associated.

P2para.Text: For this purpose employers are “associated” if on a termination or change date—

P3para.Text: one of them is under the control of the other, or
one of them is under the control of a third person who on that termination or change date or another such date controls or is under the control of the other.

P2para.Text: In subsection (2)—

P3para.Text: references to an employer, or to a person controlling or controlled by an employer, include the successors of the employer or person, and

“termination or change date” means a date on which a termination or change occurs in connection with which a payment or other benefit to which section 403 applies is received in respect of the employee or former employee.

P2para.Text: If payments and other benefits are received in different tax years, the £30,000 is set against the amount of payments and other benefits received in earlier years before those received in later years.
If more than one payment or other benefit is received in a tax year in which the threshold is exceeded—

P3para.Text: the £30,000 (or the balance of it) is set against the amounts of cash benefits as they are received, and
any balance at the end of the year is set against the aggregate amount of non-cash benefits received in the year.

Text.Addition: In subsection (3)(b), the reference to a payment or other benefit to which section 403 applies includes a reference to a payment or other benefit—
received in the tax year 2017-18 or an earlier tax year, and
to which this Chapter applied in the tax year of receipt.

Title.Addition: Amounts charged to be treated as highest part of total income

Text.Addition: A payment or other benefit which counts as a person's employment income as a result of section 403 is treated as the highest part of the person's total income.
Subsection (1) has effect for all income tax purposes except the purposes of sections 535 to 537 of
ITTOIA
2005 (gains from contracts for life insurance
etc
: top slicing relief).
See section 1012 of ITA 2007 (relationship between highest part rules) for the relationship between—
the rule in subsection (1), and
other rules requiring particular income to be treated as the highest part of a person's total income.
The Treasury may by regulations amend the listed provisions by substituting, for the amount for the time being mentioned in those provisions, a different amount.
The listed provisions are—
subsections (1), (4) and (5) of section 403, and
subsections (1), (4) and (5) of section 404 and its heading.
Regulations under this section may include transitional provision.

A statutory instrument containing regulations under this section which reduce the mentioned amount may not be made unless a draft of it has been laid before, and approved by a resolution of, the House of Commons.

P1group.Title: Exception for certain payments exempted when received as earnings

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to any payment received in connection with the termination of a person’s employment which, were it received for the performance of the duties of the employment, would fall within section 308 (exemption of contributions to approved personal pension arrangements).

This Chapter does not apply to any payment received in connection with any change in the duties of, or earnings from, a person’s employment to the extent that, were it received for the performance of the duties of the employment, it would fall within section 271(1) (limited exemption of removal benefits and expenses).

P1group.Title: Exception for death or disability payments and benefits

Text.Addition: This Chapter does not apply to a payment or other benefit provided—
in connection with the termination of employment by the death of an employee, or
on account of injury to, or disability of, an employee.
Although “injury” in subsection (1) includes psychiatric injury, it does not include injured feelings.

P1group.Title: Exception for payments and benefits under tax-exempt pension schemes

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a payment or other benefit provided under a tax-exempt pension scheme if—

P3para.Text: the payment or other benefit is by way of compensation—
