P4para.Text: for loss of employment, or
for loss or diminution of earnings, and

P3para.Text: the loss or diminution is due to ill-health, or
the payment or other benefit is properly regarded as earned by past service.

P2para.Text: For this purpose “tax-exempt pension scheme” means—

Text.Substitution: a registered pension scheme,
a scheme set up by a government outside the United Kingdom for the benefit of employees or primarily for their benefit, or

P3para.Text: any such scheme or fund as was described in section 221(1) and (2) of ICTA 1970 (schemes to which payments could be made without charge to tax under section 220 of ICTA 1970).

P1group.Title: Exception for contributions to registered pension schemes

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a contribution to a registered pension scheme or an employer-financed retirement benefit scheme if the contribution is made—

P3para.Text: as part of an arrangement relating to the termination of a person’s employment, and
in order to provide benefits for the person in accordance with the terms of the scheme or approved personal pension arrangements.

P1group.Title: Exception for payments and benefits in respect of certain legal expenses etc and indemnity insurance

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a payment or other benefit received by an individual if or to the extent that—

P3para.Text: in the case of a cash benefit, it is provided for meeting the cost of a deductible amount, or
in the case of a non-cash benefit, it is or represents a benefit equivalent to the cost of paying a deductible amount.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section “deductible amount” means an amount which meets conditions A to C.
Condition A is that the amount is paid by the individual or by the employer or former employer on behalf of the individual.

Condition B is that a deduction for the amount would have been allowed under section 346 from earnings from the relevant employment, if the individual still held the employment when the amount was paid.
Condition C is that the amount is paid at a time which falls within the run-off period.
In this section and section 410—

Para.Text: “relevant employment” means the employment mentioned in section 401(1);
“run-off period” means the period which—
starts with the day on which the relevant employment terminated, and
ends with the last day of the sixth tax year following the tax year in which the period started.

P1group.Title: Exception for payments and benefits in respect of certain legal expenses etc and indemnity insurance: individual deceased

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a payment or other benefit received by an individual’s personal representatives if or to the extent that—

P3para.Text: in the case of a cash benefit, it is provided for meeting the cost of a deductible amount, or
in the case of a non-cash benefit, it is or represents a benefit equivalent to the cost of paying a deductible amount.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section “deductible amount” means an amount which meets conditions A to C.
Condition A is that the amount is paid by the individual’s personal representatives or by the former employer on behalf of the individual's personal representatives .
Condition B is that a deduction for the amount would have been allowed under section 346 from earnings from the relevant employment, if—

P3para.Text: the individual had not died,
the amount had been paid by the individual, and
the individual still held the employment when the amount was paid.

P2para.Text: Condition C is that the amount is paid at a time which falls within the run-off period.

P1group.Title: Exception for payments and benefits for forces

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to a payment or other benefit provided—

P3para.Text: under a Royal Warrant, Queen’s Order or Order in Council relating to members of Her Majesty’s forces, or
by way of payment in commutation of annual or other periodical payments authorised by any such Warrant or Order.

Text.Addition: This Chapter does not apply to a payment or other benefit provided under a scheme established by an order under section 1(1) of the Armed Forces (Pensions and Compensation) Act 2004.

P1group.Title: Exception for payments and benefits provided by foreign governments etc.

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply to—

P3para.Text: a benefit provided under a pension scheme administered by the government of an overseas territory within the Commonwealth, or
a payment of compensation for loss of career, interruption of service or disturbance made—

P4para.Text: in connection with any change in the constitution of any such overseas territory, and
to a person who was employed in the public service of the territory before the change.

P2para.Text: References in subsection (1) to—

P3para.Text: an overseas territory,
the government of such a territory, and
employment in the public service of such a territory,

P2para.Text: have the meanings given in section 615 of ICTA.

P1group.Title: Exception in certain cases of foreign service

Text.Addition: This section applies to a payment or other benefit if—
the payment or other benefit is within section 401(1)(a), and the employee or former employee is non-UK resident for the tax year in which the employment terminates, or
the payment or other benefit is within section 401(1)(b) or (c).

P2para.Text: This Chapter does not apply if the service of the employee or former employee in the employment in respect of which the payment or other benefit is received included foreign service comprising—

P3para.Text: three-quarters or more of the whole period of service ending with the date of the termination or change in question, or
if the period of service ending with that date exceeded 10 years, the whole of the last 10 years, or
if the period of service ending with that date exceeded 20 years, one-half or more of that period, including any 10 of the last 20 years.

P2para.Text: In subsection (1) “foreign service” means service to which subsection (2A), (3), (4) or (6) applies.

Text.Addition: This subsection applies to service in or after the tax year 2013-14—
to the extent that it consists of duties performed outside the United Kingdom in respect of which earnings would not be relevant earnings, or
if a deduction equal to the whole amount of the earnings from the employment was or would have been allowable under Chapter 6 of Part 5 (deductions from seafarers' earnings).

P2para.Text: This subsection applies to service in or after the tax year 2003-04 but before the tax year 2013-14 such that—

Text.Substitution: any earnings from the employment would not be relevant earnings, or

P3para.Text: a deduction equal to the whole amount of the earnings from the employment was or would have been allowable under Chapter 6 of Part 5 (deductions from seafarers' earnings).

Text.Substitution: In subsection (2A)(a) “
” means—
for service in or after the tax year 2025-26, earnings—
to which section 15 applies, and

if the employee is a qualifying new resident for the purposes of Chapter 5C of Part 2 for that tax year, which are not qualifying foreign general earnings within the meaning of section 41T (qualifying foreign general earnings), and

for service before tax year 2025-26, earnings to which section 15 applies and to which that section would apply even if the employee made a claim under section 809B of ITA 2007 (claim for remittance basis) for that year.

Text.Addition: In subsection (3)(a) “
” means—
for service in or after the tax year 2008-09, earnings—
which are for a tax year in which the employee is ordinarily UK resident,
to which section 15 applies, and
to which that section would apply, even if the employee made a claim under section 809B of ITA 2007 (claim for remittance basis) for that year, and
for service before the tax year 2008-09, general earnings to which section 15 or 21 as originally enacted applies.

P2para.Text: This subsection applies to service before the tax year 2003-04 and after the tax year 1973-74 such that—

P3para.Text: the emoluments from the employment were not chargeable under Case I of Schedule E, or would not have been so chargeable had there been any, or
a deduction equal to the whole amount of the emoluments from the employment was or would have been allowable under a foreign earnings deduction provision.

P2para.Text: In subsection (4) “foreign earnings deduction provision” means—

P3para.Text: paragraph 1 of Schedule 2 to FA 1974,
paragraph 1 of Schedule 7 to FA 1977, or
section 192A or 193(1) of ICTA.

P2para.Text: This subsection applies to service before the tax year 1974-75 such that tax was not chargeable in respect of the emoluments of the employment—

P3para.Text: in the tax year 1956-57 or later, under Case I of Schedule E, or
in earlier tax years, under Schedule E,

P2para.Text: or it would not have been so chargeable had there been any such emoluments.

Title.Addition: Exception for payment of certain legal costs

Text.Addition: This Chapter does not apply to a payment which meets conditions A and B.
Condition A is that the payment meets the whole or part of legal costs incurred by the employee exclusively in connection with the termination of the employee’s employment.
Condition B is that either—
the payment is made pursuant to an order of a court or tribunal, or
the termination of the employee’s employment results in a
agreement between the employer and the employee and —
the
agreement provides for the payment to be made by the employer, and
the payment is made directly to the employee’s lawyer.
In this section—
“lawyer” has the same meaning as “qualified lawyer” in section 203(4) of the Employment Rights Act 1996 or article 245(4) of the Employment Rights (Northern Ireland) Order 1996;
“legal costs” means fees payable for the services and disbursements of a lawyer.

P1group.Title: Reduction in other cases of foreign service

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

Text.Addition: either—
the payment or other benefit is within section 401(1)(a), and the employee or former employee is non-UK resident for the tax year in which the employment terminates, or
the payment or other benefit is within section 401(1)(b) or (c),

P3para.Text: the service of the employee or former employee in the employment in respect of which the payment or other benefit is received includes foreign service, and

Text.Substitution: section 413(1) does not except the payment or other benefit from the application of this Chapter.

P2para.Text: The taxable person may claim relief in the form of a proportionate reduction of the amount that would otherwise—

Text.Substitution: be treated as earnings by section 402B(1), or
count as employment income as a result of section 403

P2para.Text: The proportion is that which the length of the foreign service bears to the whole length of service in the employment before the date of the termination or change in question.
A person’s entitlement to relief under this section is limited as mentioned in subsection (5) if the person is entitled—

P3para.Text: to deduct, retain or satisfy income tax out of a payment which the person is liable to make, or
to charge any income tax against another person.

P2para.Text: The relief must not reduce the amount of income tax for which the person is liable below the amount the person is entitled so to deduct, retain, satisfy or charge.
In this section “foreign service” has the same meaning as in section 413(2).

Title.Addition: Exception for payments and benefits under section 615(3) schemes

Text.Addition: This Chapter does not apply to a payment or other benefit provided in the form of a lump sum under a section 615(3) scheme.
In this section, “section 615(3) scheme” means a superannuation fund to which section 615(3) of

Abbreviation.Expansion: Income and Corporation Taxes Act 1988 c.1

Text.Addition: applies.

Title.Addition: Exception in certain cases of foreign service as seafarer

Text.Addition: This section applies to a payment or other benefit if—
the payment or other benefit is within section 401(1)(a), and
the employee or former employee is
UK
resident for the tax year in which the employment terminates.

This Chapter does not apply if the service of the employee or former employee in the employment in respect of which the payment or other benefit is received included foreign seafaring service comprising—
three-quarters or more of the whole period of service ending with the date of the termination in question, or
if the period of service ending with that date exceeded 10 years, the whole of the last 10 years, or
if the period of service ending with that date exceeded 20 years, one-half or more of that period, including any 10 of the last 20 years.
In subsection (2) “
” means service to which subsection (4), (5) or (7) applies.

This subsection applies to service in or after the tax year 2003-04 such that a deduction equal to the whole amount of the earnings from the employment was or would have been allowable under Chapter 6 of Part 5 (deductions from seafarers' earnings).

This subsection applies to service before the tax year 2003-04 and after the tax year 1973-74 such that a deduction equal to the whole amount of the emoluments from the employment was or would have been allowable under a seafarers' earnings deduction provision.
In subsection (5) “seafarers' earnings deduction provision” means—
paragraph 1 of Schedule 2 to FA 1974 so far as relating to employment as a seafarer,
paragraph 1 of Schedule 7 to FA 1977 so far as relating to employment as a seafarer,
section 192A of
ICTA
, or
section 193(1) of
ICTA
so far as relating to employment as a seafarer.
This subsection applies to service before the tax year 1974-75 in an employment as a seafarer such that tax was not chargeable in respect of the emoluments of the employment—
in the tax year 1956-57 or later, under Case I of Schedule E, or
in earlier tax years, under Schedule E,
or it would not have been so chargeable had there been any such emoluments.
In this section “
” is to be read in accordance with section 384.

Title.Addition: Reduction in other cases of foreign service as seafarer

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
the payment or other benefit is within section 401(1)(a),
the employee or former employee is
UK
resident for the tax year in which the employment terminates,
the service of the employee or former employee in the employment in respect of which the payment or other benefit is received includes foreign service, and
section 414B(2) does not except the payment or other benefit from the application of this Chapter.
The taxable person may claim relief in the form of a proportionate reduction of the amount that would otherwise—
be treated as earnings by section 402B(1), or
count as employment income as a result of section 403.
The proportion is that which the length of the foreign seafaring service bears to the whole length of service in the employment before the date of the termination in question.
A person's entitlement to relief under this section is limited as mentioned in subsection (5) if the person is entitled—
to deduct, retain or satisfy income tax out of a payment which the person is liable to make, or
to charge any income tax against another person.
The relief must not reduce the amount of income tax for which the person is liable below the amount the person is entitled so to deduct, retain, satisfy or charge.
In this section “
” has the same meaning as in section 414B(2).

P1group.Title: Valuation of benefits

P2para.Text: In the case of a cash benefit, for the purposes of this Chapter the amount of a payment or other benefit is taken to be the amount received.
In the case of a non-cash benefit, for the purposes of this Chapter the amount of a payment or other benefit is taken to be the greater of—

P3para.Text: the amount of earnings (as defined in Chapter 1 of Part 3) that the benefit would give rise to if it were received by an employee within section 15 for performance of the duties of an employment (money’s worth), and
the cash equivalent of the benefit under the benefits code if it were so received and the code applied to it.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (2), the benefits code has effect with the modifications in subsections (4), (6) and (7).
References in the benefits code to the employee are to be taken as references to the taxable person and any other person by whom the benefit is received.
For the purposes of subsection (4), section 401(4)(a) is to be disregarded.
References in the benefits code to the employer are to be taken as including references to the former employer.
Where—

P3para.Text: section 106 (cash equivalent: cost of accommodation over £75,000) applies, and
the sum referred to in section 105(2)(b) (the sum made good) exceeds the amount referred to in section 105(2)(a) (the rental value),

P2para.Text: the amount to be subtracted under paragraph (b) of step 4 of the calculation in section 106(2) is that excess (and not only the excess rent referred to there).

P1group.Title: Notional interest treated as paid if amount charged for beneficial loan

P2para.Text: This section applies if an amount (“the taxable amount”) consisting of, or including, an amount representing the benefit of a loan counts as a person’s employment income in a tax year under section 403.
That person is to be treated for the purposes of the Tax Acts (other than this Chapter) as having paid interest on the loan in the tax year equal to the lesser of—

P3para.Text: the amount representing the cash equivalent of the loan, and
the taxable amount.

P2para.Text: The interest is to be treated—

P3para.Text: as accruing during the period in the tax year during which the loan is outstanding, and
as paid at the end of the period.

P2para.Text: The interest is not to be treated—

P3para.Text: as income of the person making the loan, or
as relevant loan interest to which section 369 of ICTA applies (mortgage interest payable under deduction of tax).

Title.Substitution: Consideration for acquisition of employment-related securities

This section applies if a person fails to give a return under section 421JA for a tax year (containing, or accompanied by, all required information) on or before the date mentioned in section 421JA(4)(b) (“the date for delivery”).

Title.Addition: Shares in research institution spin-out companies

Text.Addition: This Chapter applies where—
an agreement is made for one or more transfers of intellectual property (an “
”) from one or more research institutions to a company (a “

a person acquires shares (or an interest in shares) in the spin-out company before the intellectual property agreement is made or within the period of 183 days beginning with the date on which it is made,
the right or opportunity to acquire the shares (or interest in shares) was available by reason of employment by the research institution (or any of them) or by the spin-out company, and
the person is involved in research in relation to any of the intellectual property that is the subject of the intellectual property agreement.

But this Chapter does not apply if the avoidance of tax or national insurance is the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) of the arrangements under which the right or opportunity to acquire the shares (or interest in shares) is made available.

For the relevant tax purposes the market value of the shares (or interest in shares) at the time of the acquisition is to be calculated disregarding the effect on that market value of the intellectual property agreement and any transfer of intellectual property pursuant to it.

For the purposes of subsection (1)
“the relevant tax purposes” are—
determining any amount that is to constitute earnings from the employment under Chapter 1 of Part 3 (earnings),

determining the amount of any gain realised on the occurrence of an event that is a chargeable event by virtue of section 439(3)(a)
(conversion),
operating Chapter 3C of this Part (acquisition of securities for less than market value),
determining any amount that counts as employment income of the employee under Chapter 5 of this Part (securities acquired pursuant to securities option)
, and
determining any amount that counts as employment income of the employee in respect of the employment under Chapter 2 of Part 7A (employment income provided through third parties)

If the shares are (or interest in shares is) acquired before the intellectual property agreement is made, or before any transfer of intellectual property pursuant to it, and any benefit deriving from the intellectual property agreement or any such transfer is received by the employee in connection with the shares (or interest in shares), the taxable amount determined under section 448 (post-acquisition benefits from securities: amount of charge) is to be treated as nil.

But this section does not apply if something which affects the shares (or interest in shares) has been done (at or before the time when the intellectual property agreement is made or intellectual property is transferred) as part of a scheme or arrangement the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) of which is the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions.

(election for disapplication of Chapter 2) in relation to the shares (or interest in shares).

must be made in a form approved by the Board of the Inland Revenue, and
may not be made more than 14 days after the acquisition.

(amount of charge) what would have been the market value of the shares (or interest in shares) at the time of the acquisition but for any restrictions (IUMV), that market value is to be calculated disregarding the effect on that market value of the intellectual property agreement and any transfer of intellectual property pursuant to it.

For the purposes of Chapter 3B (securities with artificially enhanced market value) neither the intellectual property agreement nor any transfer of intellectual property pursuant to it are things done otherwise than for genuine commercial purposes.

Title.Substitution: Options to which this Chapter applies

Text.Substitution: This Chapter applies to a securities option acquired by a person where the right or opportunity to acquire the securities option is available by reason of an employment of that person or any other person.

For the purposes of subsection (1)
“
” includes a former or prospective employment.

A right or opportunity to acquire a securities option made available by a person’s employer, or a person connected with a person’s employer, is to be regarded for the purposes of subsection (1) as available by reason of an employment of that person unless—
the person by whom the right or opportunity is made available is an individual, and
the right or opportunity is made available in the normal course of the domestic, family or personal relationships of that person.

A right or opportunity to acquire a securities option available by reason of holding employment-related securities is to be regarded for the purposes of subsection (1) as available by reason of the same employment as that by reason of which the right or opportunity to acquire the employment-related securities was available.
In this Chapter—

” means a securities option to which this Chapter applies.
For the purposes of this Chapter the following are “

the person who acquired the employment-related securities option on the acquisition,
(if different) the employee, and
any relevant linked person.
A person is a relevant linked person if—
that person (on the one hand), and
either the person who acquired the employment-related securities option on the acquisition or the employee (on the other),

Chapter 1 of Part 3 (earnings), or
Chapter 10 of that Part (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge),
when an employment-related securities option is acquired.
Liability to tax may arise, when securities are acquired pursuant to the employment-related securities option, under—
section 446B (charge on acquisition where market value of securities or interest artificially depressed),
Chapter 3C of this Part (acquisition of securities for less than market value), or
section 476 (acquisition of securities pursuant to securities option).
Liability to tax may also arise by virtue of section 476 when—
the employment-related securities option is assigned or released, or
a benefit is received in connection with the employment-related securities option.

SAYE
option schemes (see Chapter 7 of this Part),
CSOP
schemes (see Chapter 8 of this Part), or
enterprise management incentives (see Chapter 9 of this Part).

Text.Substitution: any amount that was treated as earnings from the employment under Chapter 10 of that Part (taxable benefits: residual liability to charge) in respect of the acquisition of the employment-related securities option,

the amount of any gain by a previous holder on an assignment of the employment-related securities option which would have been a deductible cost by virtue of subsection (2)(c) of section 479 (as originally enacted) on an exercise of the option at a time when that section was in force

Substitution.Addition: any amount that has counted as employment income of the employee in respect of the employment under Chapter 2 of Part 7A in relation to the employment-related securities option or to any sum of money or asset held solely for the purposes of the option.

In subsection (5)(a) the reference to an amount of exempt income, in a case in which the amount that constituted earnings in respect of the acquisition was not an amount of general earnings to which any of the charging provisions of Chapters 4 and 5 of Part 2 applied, includes any amount that would have been an amount of exempt income if any of those charging provisions had applied.

Text.Substitution: If there has been a previous chargeable event in relation to the employment-related securities option (or if section 476 or 477 as originally enacted applied to the option by virtue of an earlier event), so much of any deductible amount as was deducted in calculating the taxable amount on the occasion of that event is to be regarded as not being a deductible amount.

Title.Substitution: secondary Class 1 contributions met by employee

Substitution.Substitution: Relief is available under this section against an amount counting as employment income under section 476 if

Text.Substitution: an agreement having effect under paragraph 3A of Schedule 1 to the Contributions and Benefits Act has been entered into allowing the secondary contributor to recover from the employee the whole or part of any secondary Class 1 contributions in respect of the gain, or

an election having effect under paragraph 3B of Schedule 1 to that Act is in force which has the effect of transferring to the employee the whole or part of the liability to pay secondary Class 1 contributions in respect of the gain.

Substitution.Substitution: The amount of the relief is the total of

Text.Substitution: any amount that under the agreement referred to in subsection (1)(a) is recovered in respect of the gain by the secondary contributor before 5th June in the tax year following that in which the gain is realised, and
the amount of any liability in respect of the gain that, by virtue of the election referred to in subsection (1)(b), has become the employee’s liability.

If notice of withdrawal of approval of the election is given, the amount of any liability in respect of the gain for the purposes of subsection (2)(b) is limited to the amount of the liability met before 5th June in the tax year following that in which the gain is realised.

Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a liability to pay Class 1 contributions which is prevented from arising by virtue of section 2(1)(a) of the Social Security Contributions (Share Options) Act 2001 (liability to pay Class 1 contributions in respect of gains replaced by liability to pay special contribution).

Substitution.Addition: Relief under this section is given by way of deduction from the amount otherwise counting as employment income.
Relief under this section does not affect the amount to be taken into account—
as employment income in determining contributions payable under the Contributions and Benefits Act, or
as relevant employment income for the purposes of paragraph 3A or 3B of Schedule 1 to that Act.

Text.Substitution: In this section—
”, in relation to an election, means approval by

Substitution.Substitution: the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs

Text.Substitution: under paragraph 3B of Schedule 1 to the Contributions and Benefits Act, and
” has the same meaning as in that Act (see section 7).

Substitution.Substitution: Relief is available under this section against an amount counting as employment income under section 476 if

Text.Substitution: conditions A to D are met.
Condition A is that a notice in respect the employment-related securities option was given to

Substitution.Substitution: the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs

Text.Substitution: in accordance with section 1 of the Social Security Contributions (Share Options) Act 2001 before 11th August 2001.

Condition B is that the person, or one of the persons, who gave that notice is a person who (apart from that Act) was liable, or would have become liable, by virtue of an election under paragraph 3B of Schedule 1 to the Contributions and Benefits Act, to pay secondary Class 1 contributions in respect of an event which is a chargeable event for the purposes of section 476.

Condition C is that that person became liable to pay a special contribution under section 2 of the Social Security Contributions (Share Options) Act 2001 in respect of the employment-related securities option.
Condition D is that that person met that liability before 11th August 2001 or before the end of such further period as

Substitution.Substitution: the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs

Text.Substitution: directed under section 2(5) of that Act.

Substitution.Addition: The amount of the relief is the amount of the liability referred to in subsection (4).
Relief under this section is given by way of deduction from the amount otherwise counting as employment income.

Title.Substitution: Application of this Chapter where option exchanged for another

Text.Substitution: This section applies if—
the employment-related securities option (the “
”) is assigned or released, and
the whole or part of the consideration for the assignment or release consists of or includes another securities option (the “

For the purposes of section 479(5)
(amount of gain realised by assigning or releasing option) the new option is not to be treated as consideration given for the assignment or release of the old option.
This Chapter applies to the new option as it applies to the old option.

For the purposes of section 480(2)
(consideration for acquisition of option) the amount of the consideration given for the acquisition of the new option is to be treated as being the sum of—

the amount by which the amount of the consideration given for the acquisition of the old option exceeds the amount of any consideration given for the assignment or release of the old option, apart from the new option, and
any valuable consideration given for the acquisition of the new option, apart from the old option.

Two or more transactions are to be treated for the purposes of subsection (1) as a single transaction by which one option is assigned for a consideration which consists of or includes another option if—
the transactions result in—
a person ceasing to hold an option, and
that person or a connected person coming to hold another option, and
one or more of the transactions is effected under arrangements to which two or more persons holding options, in respect of which there may be liability to tax under this Chapter, are parties.
Subsection (5) applies regardless of the order in which the assignments and the acquisition occur.
In this Chapter—
”, and
have the meaning indicated in section 420.
In this Chapter “
” has the meaning indicated in section 421(1).
For the purposes of this Chapter sections 421(2) and 421A apply for determining the amount of consideration given for anything.
In this Chapter “
” has the same meaning as in Chapter 1 of this Part (see section 421B(8)).
In this Chapter—
”, and
have the meaning indicated in section 471(5).
In this Chapter “
” has the meaning indicated in section 472.
In this Chapter—
” has the same meaning as in the Contributions and Benefits Act (see section 1 of that Act),

Acronym.Expansion: Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act

P1group.Title: Application of this Chapter where share option exchanged for another
Duty to notify matters relating to share options
Minor definitions
... Share incentive plans (SIPs)

P2para.Text: This Chapter provides—

P3para.Text: for exemptions from income tax in connection with shares obtained under share incentive plans (“SIPs”) which are Schedule 2 SIPs,
for amounts to count as employment income in certain circumstances in connection with such plans, and
for the making of PAYE deductions in connection with such amounts.

P2para.Text: The provisions of—

P3para.Text: this and the following sections of this Chapter,
Schedule 2, and
the provisions mentioned in section 515 (tax advantages and charges under other Acts),

P2para.Text: together constitute “the SIP code”.
In the SIP code—

Para.Text: “PAYE deduction” means a deduction required by PAYE regulations;

Text.Addition: ” is to be read in accordance with paragraph 1 and Part 10 of Schedule 2;

Para.Text:
a “share incentive plan”
(or “SIP” for short) means a plan established by a company providing—
for shares to be appropriated to employees without payment (“free shares”), or
for shares to be acquired on behalf of employees out of sums deducted from their salary (“partnership shares”).

P2para.Text: Other expressions used in the SIP code and contained in the index at the end of Schedule 2 have the meaning indicated by the index.

P1group.Title: Operation of tax advantages in connection with Schedule 2 SIP

P2para.Text: Sections 490 to 499 apply for income tax purposes in connection with shares awarded under a Schedule 2 SIP.

But those sections do not apply to an individual if, at the time of the award of shares in question, the earnings from the eligible employment are not (or would not be if there were any) general earnings to which any of the charging provisions of Chapter 4 or 5 of Part 2 apply.
“The eligible employment” means the employment which results in the individual meeting the employment requirement in relation to the plan.

Text.Addition: And those sections do not apply if the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) of the arrangements under which the shares in question are awarded or acquired is the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions.

Title.Emphasis: Tax advantages connected with award of shares

P1group.Title: No charge on award or acquisition of shares: general

P2para.Text: This section applies—

P3para.Text: on the award to an employee of free, matching or partnership shares under the plan, or
on the acquisition on behalf of an employee of dividend shares under the plan.

P2para.Text: The employee is not liable to income tax on the value of the beneficial interest in the shares that passes to the employee at the time of the award or acquisition.

P1group.Title: No charge on award of shares as taxable benefit
No charge on partnership share money deducted from salary

P2para.Text: An employee is not liable to income tax under Part 2 on any amount of the employee’s salary which is deducted as partnership share money under a partnership share agreement.

P1group.Title: No charge on acquisition of dividend shares

P2para.Text: Section 1105(3) of CTA 2010 (information relating to distributions to be provided by nominee) does not apply to any amount applied by the trustees in acquiring dividend shares on behalf of a participant.

Text.Addition: For the exemption of such amounts from income tax, see section 770 of
ITTOIA
2005 (amounts applied by
SIP
trustees acquiring dividend shares or retained for reinvestment).

P2para.Text: Subsection (3) is subject to paragraph 80(4)(c) of Schedule 2 (information required where dividend shares cease to be subject to plan).

Title.Emphasis: Tax advantages connected with holding of shares

P1group.Title: No charge on removal of restrictions applying to shares
No charge on increase in value of shares of dependent subsidiary

Title.Substitution: No charge on cash dividend retained for reinvestment

Text.Substitution: For the exemption from income tax of amounts retained under paragraph 68(2) of Schedule 2 (amount of cash dividend not reinvested), see section 770 of
ITTOIA
2005 (amounts applied by
SIP
trustees acquiring dividend shares or retained for reinvestment).

Title.Emphasis: Tax advantages connected with shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P1group.Title: Limitations on charges on shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on free or matching shares ceasing to be subject to the plan, except as provided by—

P3para.Text: section 505 (charge on free or matching shares ceasing to be subject to plan), or
section 507 (charge on disposal of beneficial interest during holding period).

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on partnership shares ceasing to be subject to the plan, except as provided by section 506 (charge on partnership shares ceasing to be subject to plan).

No liability to income tax arises on dividend shares ceasing to be subject to the plan, except under Chapter 3 or 4 of Part 4 of ITTOIA 2005 (dividends etc. from UK or non-UK resident companies etc.) as a result of section 394(2) or 407(2) of that Act (distribution or dividend payment when dividend shares cease to be subject to plan).

P1group.Title: No charge on shares ceasing to be subject to plan in certain circumstances

P2para.Text: A participant is not liable to income tax on shares ceasing to be subject to the plan if—

P3para.Text: they cease to be so subject on the participant ceasing to be in relevant employment, and
subsection (2) applies.

P2para.Text: This subsection applies if the participant ceases to be in relevant employment—

P3para.Text: because of injury or disability,
on being dismissed by reason of redundancy,
by reason of a relevant transfer within the meaning of the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006,

if the relevant employment is employment by an associated company (see paragraph 95(2) of Schedule 2), by reason of a change of control or other circumstances ending that company’s status as an associated company,
by reason of the participant’s retirement ..., or
on the participant’s death.

Text.Addition: A participant is not liable to income tax on shares (“the relevant shares”) in a company (“
”) being withdrawn from the plan if—
the withdrawal of the relevant shares from the plan relates to—
a transaction resulting from a compromise, arrangement or scheme falling within subsection (9),
an offer forming part of a general offer falling within subsection (10), or
the application of sections 979 to 982 or 983 to 985 of the Companies Act 2006 in the case of a takeover offer (as defined in section 974 of that Act) falling within subsection (13), and
as a result of, as the case may be—
the transaction,
the offer, or
the application of sections 979 to 982 or 983 to 985 of the Companies Act 2006,
the participant receives cash (and no other assets) in exchange for the relevant shares.
For the purposes of subsection (3)(b) it does not matter if the participant receives other assets in exchange for shares other than the relevant shares.
Subsection (3) does not apply to the relevant shares (or to a proportion of them) if in connection with, as the case may be—
the compromise, arrangement or scheme,
the general offer, or
the takeover offer,

a course of action was open to the participant which, had it been followed, would have resulted in other assets being received in exchange for the relevant shares (or the proportion of them) instead of cash.

Subsection (3) does not apply to the relevant shares (or to a proportion of them) if it is reasonable to suppose that the relevant shares (or the proportion of them) would not have been awarded to the participant—
had, as the case may be—
the compromise, arrangement or scheme,
the general offer, or
the takeover offer,
not been made, or
had any arrangements for the making of—
a compromise, arrangement or scheme which would fall within subsection (9),
a general offer which would fall within subsection (10), or
a takeover offer (as defined in section 974 of the Companies Act 2006) which would fall within subsection (13),
which were in place or under consideration at any time not been in place or under consideration.

In subsection (6) the reference to shares being awarded to the participant is to be read, in the case of dividend shares, as a reference to the shares being acquired by the trustees on the participant's behalf.
In subsection (6)(b) “
” includes any plan, scheme, agreement or understanding, whether or not legally enforceable.
A compromise, arrangement or scheme falls within this subsection if it is applicable to or affects—
all the ordinary share capital of the relevant company or all the shares of the same class as the relevant shares, or
all the shares, or all the shares of that same class, which are held by a class of shareholders identified otherwise than by reference to their employment or their participation in
SIP.
A general offer falls within this subsection if—
it is made to holders of shares of the same class as the relevant shares or to holders of shares in the relevant company, and
it is made in the first instance on a condition such that if it is satisfied the person making the offer will have control of the relevant company.
For the purposes of subsection (10) it does not matter if the general offer is made to different shareholders by different means.
In subsection (10)(b) “
” has the meaning given by sections 450 and 451 of CTA 2010.
A takeover offer falls within this subsection if—
it relates to the relevant company, and
where there is more than one class of share in the relevant company, the class or classes to which it relates is or include the class of the relevant shares.

P1group.Title: No charge in respect of incidental expenditure

P1para.Text: An employee is not liable to income tax in respect of incidental expenditure of—

P3para.Text: the trustees,
the company which established the plan, or
(if different) the employer,

P1para.Text: in operating the plan.

P1group.Title: Operation of tax charges in connection with Schedule 2 SIP

P2para.Text: Sections 501 to 508 apply for income tax purposes in connection with shares awarded under a Schedule 2 SIP.

But those sections do not apply to an individual if, at the time of the award of shares in question, the earnings from the eligible employment are not (or would not be if there were any) general earnings to which any of the charging provisions of Chapter 4 or 5 of Part 2 apply.
“The eligible employment” means the employment which results in the individual meeting the employment requirement in relation to the plan.

Title.Emphasis: Charges connected with holding of shares

P1group.Title: Charge on capital receipts in respect of plan shares

P2para.Text: This section applies if conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that a capital receipt is received by a participant in respect of, or by reference to, any of the participant’s plan shares.
Condition B is that the plan shares in respect of, or by reference to, which the capital receipt is received are—

P3para.Text: free, matching or partnership shares that were awarded to the participant less than 5 years before the participant received the capital receipt, or
dividend shares that were acquired on behalf of the participant less than 3 years before the participant received the capital receipt.

P2para.Text: If this section applies, the amount or value of the capital receipt counts as employment income of the participant for the relevant tax year.
The “relevant tax year” is the tax year in which the participant receives the capital receipt.
This section does not apply if the capital receipt is received by the participant’s personal representatives after the death of the participant.
Section 502 explains what is meant by a “capital receipt”.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “capital receipt” in section 501

P2para.Text: This section applies for determining whether any money or money’s worth is a “capital receipt” for the purposes of section 501.
The general rule is that any money or money’s worth is a “capital receipt” for the purposes of section 501.
The general rule is subject to the following exceptions.
Money or money’s worth is not a capital receipt for the purposes of section 501 to the extent that—

P3para.Text: it constitutes income in the hands of the recipient for the purposes of income tax or would do so but for sections 489 to 498 (SIPs: tax advantages) or section 770 of ITTOIA 2005 (exemption for amounts applied by SIP trustees acquiring dividend shares or retained for reinvestment),
it consists of the proceeds of disposal of the plan shares mentioned in section 501, or
it consists of new shares within the meaning of paragraph 87 of Schedule 2 (company reconstructions).

P2para.Text: If, as a result of a direction given by or on behalf of the participant for the purposes of paragraph 77 of Schedule 2 (power of trustees to raise funds to subscribe for rights issues), the trustees—

P3para.Text: dispose of some of the rights under a rights issue, and
use the proceeds of that disposal to exercise other such rights,

P2para.Text: the money or money’s worth constituting the proceeds of that disposal is not a capital receipt for the purposes of section 501.

P1group.Title: Charge on partnership share money paid over to employee

P2para.Text: Any amount paid over to an individual under any of the provisions of Schedule 2 mentioned in subsection (2) counts as employment income of the individual for the relevant tax year.
The provisions are—

Para.Text:
paragraph 46(5)
(deductions in excess of permitted maximum amount),

paragraph 50(5)(b) or paragraph 52(6)(b)
(surplus partnership share money remaining after acquisition of shares),

paragraph 52(7)
(partnership share money paid over on individual ceasing to be in relevant employment),

paragraph 52(8)
(partnership share money paid over where accumulation period brought to an end by event specified in plan),

paragraph 55(3)
(partnership share money paid over on withdrawal from partnership share agreement), or
paragraph 56 (partnership share money paid over on plan ceasing to be a Schedule 2 SIP or termination of plan).

P2para.Text: The “relevant tax year” is the tax year in which the amount is paid over.

P1group.Title: Charge on cancellation payments in respect of partnership share agreement

P2para.Text: This section applies if an individual who has entered into a partnership share agreement receives any money or money’s worth in respect of the cancellation of the agreement.
The amount of the money or the value of the money’s worth counts as employment income of the individual for the relevant tax year.
The “relevant tax year” is the tax year in which the individual receives the money or money’s worth.

Title.Emphasis: Charges connected with shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P1group.Title: Charge on free or matching shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P2para.Text: When free or matching shares cease to be subject to the plan, there may be an amount that counts as employment income of the participant depending on the period that has elapsed between—

P3para.Text: the date when the shares were awarded to the participant (“the award date”), and
the date when they cease to be subject to the plan (“the exit date”).

P2para.Text: If the period is less than 3 years, the market value of the shares at the exit date counts as employment income of the participant for the relevant tax year (see subsection (5)).
If the period is 3 years or more but less than 5 years, whichever is the lesser of—

P3para.Text: the market value of the shares at the award date, and
the market value of the shares at the exit date,

P2para.Text: counts as employment income of the participant for the relevant tax year (see subsection (5)).
Where—

P3para.Text: subsection (3) applies, and
the applicable amount is the market value of the shares at the award date,

P2para.Text: the tax due is reduced by the amount or aggregate amount of any tax paid by virtue of section 501 (charge on capital receipts in respect of plan shares) on any capital receipts in respect of the shares.

Text.Addition: Any tax due under subsection (2) or (3) is reduced by the amount or aggregate amount of any tax paid by virtue of Chapter 3B of this Part in relation to the shares.

P2para.Text: The “relevant tax year” is the tax year in which the exit date falls.
No liability to tax arises by virtue of this section—

P3para.Text: on the forfeiture of free or matching shares,
if section 498 (no charge on shares ceasing to be subject to plan in certain circumstances) applies, or
if section 507 (charge on disposal of beneficial interest in holding period) applies.

P1group.Title: Charge on partnership shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P2para.Text: When partnership shares cease to be subject to the plan, there may be an amount that counts as employment income of the participant depending on the period that has elapsed between—

P3para.Text: the acquisition date in respect of those shares (as defined by paragraph 50(4) or, as the case may be, paragraph 52(5) of Schedule 2), and
the date when they cease to be subject to the plan (“the exit date”).

P2para.Text: If the period is less than 3 years, the relevant amount counts as employment income of the participant for the relevant tax year (see subsection (5)).

Text.Addition: Subject to subsection (2B), in subsection (2) “
” means the market value of the shares at the exit date.

If the shares cease to be subject to the plan by virtue of a provision of the kind mentioned in paragraph 43(2B) of Schedule 2 (provision requiring partnership shares to be offered for sale), in subsection (2) “
” means the lesser of—
the amount of partnership share money used to acquire the shares, and
the market value of the shares at the time they are offered for sale.
Paragraph 92(2) of Schedule 2 (market value of shares subject to a restriction) applies for the purposes of subsection (2B)(b).

P2para.Text: If the period is 3 years or more but less than 5 years, whichever is the lesser of—

P3para.Text: the amount of partnership share money used to acquire the shares, and
the market value of the shares at the exit date,

P2para.Text: counts as employment income of the participant for the relevant tax year (see subsection (5)).

Text.Addition: If the shares cease to be subject to the plan by virtue of a provision of the kind mentioned in paragraph 43(2B) of Schedule 2, in subsection (3)(b) the reference to the market value of the shares at the exit date is to be read as a reference to the market value of the shares at the time they are offered for sale (as determined in accordance with paragraph 92(2) of Schedule 2 if relevant).

P2para.Text: Where—

P3para.Text: subsection (3) applies, and
the applicable amount is the amount of partnership share money used to acquire the shares,

P2para.Text: the tax due is reduced by the amount or aggregate amount of any tax paid by virtue of section 501 (charge on capital receipts in respect of plan shares) on any capital receipts in respect of the shares.

Text.Addition: Any tax due under subsection (2) or (3) is reduced by the amount or aggregate amount of any tax paid by virtue of Chapter 3B of this Part in relation to the shares.

P2para.Text: The “relevant tax year” is the tax year in which the exit date falls.
No liability to income tax arises by virtue of this section if section 498 (no charge on shares ceasing to be subject to plan in certain circumstances) applies.

P1group.Title: Charge on disposal of beneficial interest during holding period

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: free or matching shares cease to be subject to the plan at any time during the holding period for those shares, and

this occurs as a result of the participant assigning, charging or otherwise disposing of the participant’s beneficial interest in the shares in breach of obligations under paragraph 36(1)(b) of Schedule 2 (restrictions relating to disposals within holding period).

P2para.Text: The market value of the shares at the date when they cease to be subject to the plan counts as employment income of the participant for the relevant tax year.
The “relevant tax year” is the tax year in which that date falls.

P1group.Title: Identification of shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P2para.Text: For the purpose of determining any liability to tax arising by virtue of the SIP code in respect of any of a participant’s shares ceasing to be subject to the plan—

P3para.Text: shares are to be taken as ceasing to be subject to the plan in the order in which they were awarded to the participant under the plan, and

where shares are awarded to the participant on the same day, the shares are to be treated as ceasing to be subject to the plan in the order which gives rise to the lowest charge to income tax on the participant.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (1) dividend shares are “awarded” to a participant when the trustees acquire them on behalf of, or appropriate them to, the participant.

P1group.Title: Modification of section 696 where charge on shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P2para.Text: Where—

P3para.Text: as a result of shares ceasing to be subject to a Schedule 2 SIP, there is an amount that counts as employment income of a participant by virtue of the SIP code, and
the shares are readily convertible assets,

P2para.Text: section 696 (readily convertible assets) applies as follows.
Section 696 applies as if the participant (“P”) were being provided with PAYE income in the form of those shares—

P3para.Text: at the time when the shares cease to be subject to the plan, and

in respect of the relevant employment in which P is employed at that time (or, if P is not then employed in relevant employment, the relevant employment in which P was last employed before that time).

P2para.Text: In addition, subsection (2) of section 696 applies as if the reference in that subsection to the amount of income likely to be PAYE income in respect of the provision of the asset were a reference to the amount which is likely to count as employment income by virtue of the SIP code as a result of the shares ceasing to be subject to the plan.
In this section “readily convertible asset” has the same meaning as in section 696 (see sections 701 and 702), but this is subject to subsections (5) and (6).

In determining for the purposes of this section (and of section 696 in its application in accordance with this section) whether the shares are readily convertible assets, any market for the shares which—

P3para.Text: is created by virtue of the trustees acquiring shares for the purposes of the plan, and
exists solely for the purposes of the plan,

P2para.Text: is to be disregarded.

Text.Addition: In determining for the purposes of this section (and of section 696 in its application in accordance with this section) whether the shares are readily convertible assets, section 702 has effect with the omission of subsections (5A) to (5D).

P1group.Title: Payments by trustees to employer company on shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P2para.Text: This section applies if, as a result of any shares (“the relevant shares”) ceasing to be subject to a Schedule 2 SIP—

P3para.Text: there is an amount that counts as employment income of a participant by virtue of the SIP code, and
an obligation to make a PAYE deduction arises in respect of that amount.

P2para.Text: The trustees must pay to the employer company a sum which is sufficient to enable the employer company to discharge that obligation.
Subsection (2) is subject to—

P3para.Text: subsection (4), and
section 511 (PAYE deductions to be made by trustees on shares ceasing to be subject to plan).

P2para.Text: Subsection (2) only applies if, or to the extent that, the plan does not require the participant to pay the employer company a sum which is sufficient to discharge the obligation mentioned in subsection (1)(b).
Section 710(1) (notional payments: accounting for tax) has effect as if it required the deduction of income tax to be made from any sum or sums received by the employer company—

P3para.Text: from the trustees under subsection (2), or
from the participant in accordance with a requirement of the plan, as mentioned in subsection (4).

P2para.Text: After making the necessary PAYE deduction from the sum or sums received as mentioned in subsection (5), the employer company must pay any remaining amount to the participant.
In this section “the employer company” means—

P3para.Text: the company which employs the participant in relevant employment at the time when the relevant shares cease to be subject to the plan, or
if the participant is not then employed in relevant employment, the company which last employed the participant in relevant employment before that time,

P2para.Text: so long as that company is one to which PAYE regulations apply at that time.

P1group.Title: PAYE deductions to be made by trustees on shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P2para.Text: This section applies if, as a result of any shares ceasing to be subject to a Schedule 2 SIP—

P3para.Text: there is an amount that counts as employment income of a participant by virtue of the SIP code, and
condition A or B is met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that an officer of Revenue and Customs —

P3para.Text: is of the opinion that it is impracticable for the employer company (within the meaning of section 510) to make a PAYE deduction, and
accordingly directs that this section is to apply.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that there is no company that qualifies as the employer company (within the meaning of that section).
If this section applies—

P3para.Text: section 510(2) does not apply, and
the trustees must make a PAYE deduction in respect of the taxable equivalent as if the participant were a former employee of the trustees.

P2para.Text: The “taxable equivalent” means an amount equal to that mentioned in subsection (1).
If this section applies, section 689 (employee of non-UK employer) does not apply.

P1group.Title: Disposal of beneficial interest by participant

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: a participant (“P”) disposes of P’s beneficial interest in any of P’s plan shares to the trustees, and
the trustees are, as a result of paragraph 6 of Schedule 7D to TCGA 1992 (deemed disposal by trustees on disposal of beneficial interest), treated as having disposed of the shares in question.

P2para.Text: If this section applies, sections 510 and 511 apply as if the consideration payable by the trustees to the participant on the disposal had been received by the trustees as the proceeds of disposal of plan shares.

P1group.Title: Capital receipts: payments by trustees to employer company

P2para.Text: This section applies if the trustees receive a sum of money which constitutes (or forms part of) a capital receipt which, by virtue of the SIP code, counts as employment income of a participant when it is received by the participant.
Out of that sum of money the trustees must pay to the employer company an amount equal to the amount of employment income.
The employer company must then pay over that amount to the participant, but when doing so must make a PAYE deduction.
This section is subject to section 514 (capital receipts: deductions to be made by trustees).
In this section “the employer company” means—

P3para.Text: the company which employs the participant in relevant employment at the time when the trustees receive the sum mentioned in subsection (1), or
if the participant is not then employed in relevant employment, the company which last employed the participant in relevant employment before that time,

P2para.Text: so long as that company is one to which PAYE regulations apply at that time.

P1group.Title: Capital receipts: PAYE deductions to be made by trustees

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: the trustees receive a sum of money which constitutes (or forms part of) a capital receipt which, by virtue of the SIP code, counts as employment income of a participant when it is received by the participant, and
either condition A or B is met.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that an officer of Revenue and Customs —

P3para.Text: is of the opinion that it is impracticable for the employer company (within the meaning of section 513) to make a PAYE deduction, and
accordingly directs that this section is to apply.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that there is no company that qualifies as the employer company (within the meaning of that section).

If this section applies, the trustees must, when paying the capital receipt over to the participant, make a PAYE deduction in respect of the taxable equivalent as if the participant were a former employee of the trustees.
The “taxable equivalent” means an amount equal to the amount which counts as employment income as mentioned in subsection (1)(a).
If this section applies, section 689 (employee of non-UK employer) does not apply.

P1group.Title: Tax advantages and charges under other Acts

P2para.Text: SIPs are also dealt with in—

P3para.Text: Part 1 of Schedule 7D to TCGA 1992 (which provides for relief from capital gains tax for the trustees and for participants in relation to a Schedule 2 SIP in certain circumstances, including where shares cease to be subject to the plan), ...
section 95 of FA 2001 (which contains relief from stamp duty and stamp duty reserve tax for transfers of partnership or dividend shares) , ...

Text.Addition: sections 392 to 395 and 405 to 408 of
ITTOIA
2005 (SIPs: special rules for charges under Chapters 3 and 4 of Part 4 of that Act (dividends
etc.
from
UK
or non-UK resident companies
etc.
)) and section 770 of that Act (exemption for amounts applied by
SIP
trustees acquiring dividend shares or retained for reinvestment)
Chapter 5 of Part 9 of ITA 2007 (which provides for section 479 of that Act not to apply to income of the trustees of
SIP
in certain circumstances)
, and
Chapter 1 of Part 11 of CTA 2009 (share incentive plans)

P1group.Title: ... SAYE option schemes

P2para.Text: This Chapter provides—

P3para.Text: for exemptions from income tax in connection with share options granted under SAYE option schemes which are Schedule 3 SAYE option schemes.

P2para.Text: The provisions of—

P3para.Text: this and the following sections of this Chapter,
Schedule 3, and
Part 2 of Schedule 7D to TCGA 1992 (Schedule 3 SAYE option schemes: amount of consideration on exercise of option),

P2para.Text: together constitute “the SAYE code”.
In the SAYE code—

Para.Text: “SAYE option scheme” means a scheme (commonly referred to as an SAYE share option scheme) which is established by a company and provides—
for share options to be granted to employees and directors, and
for the shares acquired by the exercise of the share options to be paid for in the way mentioned in paragraph 24 of Schedule 3 (payments for shares to be linked to approved savings arrangements);

Text.Addition: ” is to be read in accordance with paragraph 1 and Part 8 of Schedule 3;

Para.Text: “share option” means a right to acquire shares in a company;
“shares” includes stock.

P2para.Text: Other expressions used in the SAYE code and contained in the index at the end of Schedule 3 have the meaning indicated by the index.

P1group.Title: Share options to which this Chapter applies

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to a share option granted to an individual—

P3para.Text: in accordance with the provisions of a Schedule 3 SAYE option scheme, and
by reason of the individual’s office or employment as a director or employee of a company.

P2para.Text: The individual may be a director or employee of the company whose shares are the subject of the share option, or of some other company.

P1group.Title: No charge in respect of receipt of option
No charge in respect of exercise of option

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the exercise of the share option if—

P3para.Text: the individual exercises it in accordance with the provisions of the SAYE option scheme at a time when the scheme is a Schedule 3 SAYE option scheme, ...
condition A or B is met and

Text.Addition: the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions is not the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) of any arrangements under which the option was granted or is exercised.

P2para.Text: Condition A is that the option is exercised on or after the third anniversary of the date on which it was granted.
Condition B is that the option—

P3para.Text: is exercised before the third anniversary of the date on which it was granted, and
is so exercised otherwise than by virtue of a provision included in the scheme under—

Para.Text: paragraph 34(5) of Schedule 3 (exercise of option where scheme-related employment ends), or
paragraph 37 of that Schedule (exercise of option where certain company events occur).

Text.Addition: In relation to any shares acquired by the exercise of the share option, no liability to income tax arises in respect of its exercise if—
the individual exercises the option before the third anniversary of the date on which the option was granted at a time when the
SAYE
option scheme is
the option is exercised by virtue of a provision included in the scheme—
under paragraph 37(1) of Schedule 3 where the relevant date is the relevant date for the purposes of paragraph 37(2)
, or
under paragraph 37(6) of Schedule 3,
as a result of, as the case may be—
the general offer,
the compromise or arrangement,

Addition.Addition: the non-UK company reorganisation arrangement, or

Text.Addition: the takeover offer,
the individual receives cash (and no other assets) in exchange for the shares,
when the decision to grant the option was taken—
the general offer,
the compromise or arrangement,

Addition.Addition: the non-UK company reorganisation arrangement, or

Text.Addition: the takeover offer,
as the case may be, had not been made,
when that decision was taken, no arrangements were in place or under consideration for—
the making of a general offer which would fall within subsection (3D),
the making of any compromise or arrangement which would fall within subsection (3H),

Addition.Addition: the making of any non-UK company reorganisation arrangement which would fall within subsection (3H), or

Text.Addition: the making of a takeover offer (as defined in section 974 of the Companies Act 2006) which would fall within subsection (3I),
if the scheme includes a provision under paragraph 38 of Schedule 3 (“the paragraph 38 provision”), in connection with—
the general offer,
the compromise or arrangement,

Addition.Addition: the non-UK company reorganisation arrangement, or

Text.Addition: the takeover offer,

as the case may be, no course of action was open to the individual which, had it been followed, would have resulted in the individual making an agreement under the paragraph 38 provision which would have prevented the individual from acquiring the shares by the exercise of the option, and
the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions is not the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) of any arrangements under which the option was granted or is exercised.
In subsection (3A)(c)(iii), (d)(iii) and (f)(iii) “
” means the takeover offer (as defined in section 974 of the Companies Act 2006) giving rise to the application of sections 979 to 982 or 983 to 985 of that Act.
In subsection (3A)(e) “
” includes any plan, scheme, agreement or understanding, whether or not legally enforceable.
A general offer falls within this subsection if it is—

a general offer to acquire the whole of the issued ordinary share capital of the relevant company which is made on a condition such that, if it is met, the person making the offer will have control of the relevant company, or
a general offer to acquire all the shares in the relevant company which are of the same class as those acquired by the exercise of the option.

In subsection (3D)(a) the reference to the issued ordinary share capital of the relevant company does not include any capital already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person and in subsection (3D)(b) the reference to the shares in the relevant company does not include any shares already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person.
For the purposes of subsection (3D)(a) and (b) it does not matter if the general offer is made to different shareholders by different means.
For the purposes of subsection (3D)(a) a person is to be treated as obtaining control of a company if that person and others acting in concert together obtain control of it.
A compromise or arrangement

Addition.Addition: or a non-UK company reorganisation arrangement

Text.Addition: falls within this subsection if it is applicable to or affects—
all the ordinary share capital of the relevant company or all the shares of the same class as those acquired by the exercise of the option, or
all the shares, or all the shares of that same class, which are held by a class of shareholders identified otherwise than by reference to their employment or directorships or their participation in
SAYE
option scheme.
A takeover offer falls within this subsection if—
it relates to the relevant company, and
where there is more than one class of share in the relevant company, the class or classes to which it relates is or include the class of the shares acquired by the exercise of the option.
In subsections (3D), (3H) and (3I) “
” means the company whose shares are acquired by the exercise of the option.

P2para.Text: In Schedule 3—

P3para.Text: paragraph 32 provides for the exercise of an option where the holder has died, and

paragraphs 40H(4) and 40I(9) provide for an SAYE option scheme to be treated as a Schedule 3 SAYE option scheme at the time when an option is exercised even though the scheme is not a Schedule 3 SAYE option scheme.

P1group.Title: No charge in respect of post-acquisition benefits
... CSOP schemes

P2para.Text: This Chapter provides—

P3para.Text: for exemptions from income tax in connection with share options granted under CSOP schemes which are Schedule 4 CSOP schemes, and
for amounts to count as employment income in certain circumstances in connection with such options.

P2para.Text: The provisions of—

P3para.Text: this and the following sections of this Chapter,
Schedule 4, and
Part 3 of Schedule 7D to TCGA 1992 (Schedule 4 CSOP schemes: amount of consideration on exercise of option),

P2para.Text: together constitute “the CSOP code”.
In the CSOP code—

Para.Text: “CSOP scheme” means a scheme (commonly referred to as a company share option plan) which—
is established by a company,
provides for share options to be granted to employees and directors, and
is not an SAYE option scheme (within the meaning of the SAYE code: see section 516(4));

Text.Addition: ” is to be read in accordance with paragraph 1 and Part 7 of Schedule 4;

Para.Text: “share option” means a right to acquire shares in a company;
“shares” includes stock.

P2para.Text: Other expressions used in the CSOP code and contained in the index at the end of Schedule 4 have the meaning indicated by the index.

P1group.Title: Share options to which this Chapter applies

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies to a share option granted to an individual—

P3para.Text: in accordance with the provisions of a Schedule 4 CSOP scheme, and
by reason of the individual’s office or employment as a director or employee of a company.

P2para.Text: The individual may be a director or employee of the company whose shares are the subject of the share option, or of some other company.

P1group.Title: No charge in respect of receipt of option
No charge in respect of receipt of option

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises in respect of the exercise of the share option if—

P3para.Text: the individual exercises it in accordance with the provisions of the CSOP scheme at a time when the scheme is a Schedule 4 CSOP scheme, ...

Text.Substitution: Condition A or B is met
Text.Addition: and
the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions is not the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) of any arrangements under which the option was granted or is exercised.

Text.Substitution: Condition A is that the option is exercised—
on or after the third anniversary of the date on which it was granted, but
not later than the tenth anniversary of that date.
Condition B is that the option—
is exercised before the third anniversary of the date on which it was granted, and

is so exercised by virtue of a provision included in the scheme under paragraph 24 of Schedule 4 (exercise of options after ceasing to be director or employee) in circumstances in which subsection (2B) applies.
This subsection applies if the individual exercising the option—

Substitution.Substitution: has ceased to be in qualifying employment because of—
a relevant transfer within the meaning of the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006, or
in the case of a group scheme where the qualifying employment is as a director or employee of a constituent company, that company ceasing to be controlled by the scheme organiser, and

Text.Substitution: exercises the option within 6 months of the day on which he ceases to be such a director or employee.

Substitution.Addition: For the purposes of subsection (2B) an individual is in “qualifying employment” if the individual is a full-time director or qualifying employee (as defined in paragraph 8(2) of Schedule 4) of—
in the case of a group scheme, a constituent company.
