the individual exercises the option before the third anniversary of the date on which the option was granted at a time when the
CSOP
scheme is
the option is exercised by virtue of a provision included in the scheme under paragraph 25A of Schedule 4,
as a result of, as the case may be—
the general offer,
the compromise or arrangement,

Addition.Addition: the non-UK company reorganisation arrangement, or

Text.Addition: the takeover offer,
the individual receives cash (and no other assets) in exchange for the shares,
when the decision to grant the option was taken—
the general offer,
the compromise or arrangement,

Addition.Addition: the non-UK company reorganisation arrangement, or

Text.Addition: the takeover offer,
as the case may be, had not been made,
when that decision was taken, no arrangements were in place or under consideration for—
the making of a general offer which would fall within subsection (2H),
the making of any compromise or arrangement which would fall within subsection (2L),

Addition.Addition: the making of any non-UK company reorganisation arrangement which would fall within subsection (2L), or

Text.Addition: the making of a takeover offer (as defined in section 974 of the Companies Act 2006) which would fall within subsection (2M),
if the scheme includes a provision under paragraph 26 of Schedule 4 (“the paragraph 26 provision”), in connection with—
the general offer,
the compromise or arrangement,

Addition.Addition: the non-UK company reorganisation arrangement, or

Text.Addition: the takeover offer,

as the case may be, no course of action was open to the individual which, had it been followed, would have resulted in the individual making an agreement under the paragraph 26 provision which would have prevented the individual from acquiring the shares by the exercise of the option, and
the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions is not the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) of any arrangements under which the option was granted or is exercised.
In subsection (2E)(c)(iii), (d)(iii) and (f)(iii) “
” means the takeover offer (as defined in section 974 of the Companies Act 2006) giving rise to the application of sections 979 to 982 or 983 to 985 of that Act.
In subsection (2E)(e) “
” includes any plan, scheme, agreement or understanding, whether or not legally enforceable.
A general offer falls within this subsection if it is—

a general offer to acquire the whole of the issued ordinary share capital of the relevant company which is made on a condition such that, if it is met, the person making the offer will have control of the relevant company, or
a general offer to acquire all the shares in the relevant company which are of the same class as those acquired by the exercise of the option.

In subsection (2H)(a) the reference to the issued ordinary share capital of the relevant company does not include any capital already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person and in subsection (2H)(b) the reference to the shares in the relevant company does not include any shares already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person.
For the purposes of subsection (2H)(a) and (b) it does not matter if the general offer is made to different shareholders by different means.
For the purposes of subsection (2H)(a) a person is to be treated as obtaining control of a company if that person and others acting in concert together obtain control of it.
A compromise or arrangement

Addition.Addition: or a non-UK company reorganisation arrangement

Text.Addition: falls within this subsection if it is applicable to or affects—
all the ordinary share capital of the relevant company or all the shares of the same class as those acquired by the exercise of the option, or
all the shares, or all the shares of that same class, which are held by a class of shareholders identified otherwise than by reference to their employment or directorships or their participation in
CSOP
scheme.
A takeover offer falls within this subsection if—
it relates to the relevant company, and
where there is more than one class of share in the relevant company, the class or classes to which it relates is or include the class of the shares acquired by the exercise of the option.
In subsections (2H), (2L) and (2M) “
” means the company whose shares are acquired by the exercise of the option.

P2para.Text: Paragraph 25 of Schedule 4 provides for the exercise of an option where the holder has died.

P1group.Title: No charge in respect of post-acquisition benefits
Charge where option granted at a discount

P2para.Text: This section applies if, at the time when the share option is granted to the individual, the aggregate of—

P3para.Text: the amount or value of any consideration given by the individual for the grant of the option, and
the amount payable by the individual, on exercising the option, in order to acquire the maximum number of shares that may be acquired under it,

P2para.Text: is less than the market value of the same quantity of issued shares of the same class.
The amount of the difference counts as employment income of the individual for the relevant tax year.
The “relevant tax year” is the tax year in which the option is granted to the individual.

Section 480(4)
(gain realised on acquisition of securities pursuant to option etc) provides for a deduction to be made to take account of amounts that count as employment income under this section.

P1group.Title: Enterprise management incentives: qualifying options

P2para.Text: This Chapter provides—

P3para.Text: for share options notified to an officer of Revenue and Customs to be qualifying options for the purposes of the EMI code, and
for exemptions and reliefs from income tax in connection with qualifying options.

P2para.Text: Schedule 5 contains the requirements that have to be met for a share option to be a qualifying option, together with the notification procedure.
The provisions of—

P3para.Text: this and the following sections of this Chapter, and
Schedule 5, ...

P2para.Text: together constitute “the EMI code”.
In the EMI code—

Para.Text: “qualifying option” means a share option—
in relation to which the requirements of Schedule 5 are met at the time when the option is granted, and
which is notified to an officer of Revenue and Customs in accordance with Part 7 of that Schedule;
“replacement option” means an option within paragraph 41(4) of that Schedule (grant of replacement option in connection with company reorganisations);
“share option” means a right to acquire shares in a company;
and any reference to the requirements of Schedule 5 is to the requirements set out in paragraph 1(3) of that Schedule.

P2para.Text: Other expressions used in the EMI code and contained in the index at the end of Schedule 5 have the meaning indicated by the index.

P1group.Title: No charge on receipt of qualifying option
Scope of tax advantages: option must be exercised by the specified anniversary

P2para.Text: Sections 530 to 540 apply in connection with the exercise of a qualifying option.
But those sections only apply in cases where the option is exercised on or before the specified anniversary of—

P3para.Text: the date of the grant of the option, or
if it is a replacement option, the date of the grant of the original option.

Text.Addition: In this section, “
” means—
in cases where the employer company is a specified Northern Ireland company, the tenth anniversary, and
otherwise, the fifteenth anniversary.

P2para.Text: In the EMI code “the original option” means—

P3para.Text: where there has been one replacement option, the option that that option replaced, or
where there have been two or more replacement options, the option that the first of them replaced.

P1group.Title: No charge on exercise of option to acquire shares at market value

P2para.Text: This section applies if the option is to acquire shares at not less than their market value—

P3para.Text: at the time when the option is granted, or
if it is a replacement option, at the time when the original option was granted.

P2para.Text: If this section applies, no liability to income tax arises by virtue of section 476 (charge on exercise etc. of option by employee) in respect of the exercise of the option.
This section has effect subject to section 532 (modified tax consequences following disqualifying events).

P1group.Title: Limitation of charge on exercise of option to acquire shares below market value

P2para.Text: This section applies if the option is to acquire shares at less than their market value—

P3para.Text: at the time when the option is granted, or
if it is a replacement option, at the time when the original option was granted,

P2para.Text: or at nil cost.
If this section applies, the section 476 gain is—

Para.Text: where—
CMV is the chargeable market value,
ACO is the amount or value of the consideration given for the grant of the option, and
ACS is the amount, if any, for which the shares are acquired.

P2para.Text: “The chargeable market value” means—

P3para.Text: the market value of the shares—

P4para.Text: at the time when the option was granted, or
if it is a replacement option, at the time when the original option was granted, or

P3para.Text: the market value of the shares at the time when the option is exercised,

P2para.Text: whichever is lower.

In this section “the section 476 gain” means the amount under section 478 (amount of charge under section 476) is to be regarded as the taxable amount for the purposes of section 476 in respect of the acquisition of the shares pursuant to the option.
This section has effect subject to section 532 (modified tax consequences following disqualifying events).

P1group.Title: Modified tax consequences following disqualifying events

P2para.Text: This section applies where—

P3para.Text: a disqualifying event (see section 533) occurs in relation to a qualifying option before the option is exercised, and
the option is exercised later than 90 days after the day on which the event occurred.

P2para.Text: If the option is within section 530(1) (option to acquire shares at market value), the section 476 gain is—
(see subsection (4)).
If the option is within section 531(1) (option to acquire shares at less than market value), the section 476 gain is—
(see subsection (4)).
For the purposes of subsections (2) and (3)—

Para.Text: ACO is the amount or value of the consideration given for the grant of the option,
ACS is the amount, if any, for which the shares are acquired,
CMV is the chargeable market value (as defined by section 531(3)), and

PEG is the post-event gain, that is the amount (if any) by which the market value of the shares at the time when the option is exercised exceeds their market value immediately before the disqualifying event.

P2para.Text: In subsections (2) and (3) “the section 476 gain” means the amount under section 478 (amount of charge under section 476) is to be regarded as the taxable amount for the purposes of section 476 in respect of the acquisition of the shares pursuant to the option.
Nothing in the following provisions—

P3para.Text: subsections (2) and (3) above, or
sections 530 and 531,

P2para.Text: applies if the amount that counts as employment income by virtue of section 476 in respect of the exercise of the option would, in the absence of those provisions, be less than the amount that counts as such income as a result of those provisions.

P1group.Title: Disqualifying events

P2para.Text: The following provisions deal with the events that are (or are to be treated as) disqualifying events in relation to a qualifying option—

P3para.Text: section 534 (events relating to the relevant company),
section 535 (events relating to the employee), and
section 536 (other disqualifying events), read with sections 537 to 539 (which contain supplementary provisions).

P2para.Text: In the provisions mentioned in subsection (1) “the employee” means the person holding the qualifying option and “the relevant company” means the company whose shares are the subject of the option (see paragraph 1(3) of Schedule 5).

P1group.Title: Disqualifying events relating to relevant company

P2para.Text: The following events relating to the relevant company are disqualifying events in relation to a qualifying option—

P3para.Text: when the relevant company becomes a 51% subsidiary of another company;
when the relevant company comes under the control of—

P4para.Text: another company, or
another company and any other person connected with that other company,

P3para.Text: without becoming a 51% subsidiary of that other company;
when the relevant company ceases to meet the trading activities requirement (see paragraphs 13 to 23 of Schedule 5).

P2para.Text: But where a replacement option has been granted, an event within subsection (1)(a) or (b) is not a disqualifying event in relation to the old option (see paragraph 41(2) of Schedule 5) if the event occurs at any time during the period—

P3para.Text: beginning at the same time as the period within which the replacement option had to be granted (see paragraph 42 of Schedule 5), and
ending with the release of the rights under the old option.

P2para.Text: A disqualifying event is to be treated as occurring in relation to a qualifying option if the circumstances mentioned in subsection (4) arise.
The circumstances are that—

P3para.Text: the relevant company was a qualifying company at the time when the option was granted as a result only of preparations to carry on a qualifying trade; and
either—

P4para.Text: the preparations cease to be carried on, or
the initial period comes to an end,

P3para.Text: without the relevant company (or, if it is a parent company, any member of the group) beginning to carry on that qualifying trade.

P2para.Text: “The initial period” means the period of two years after the date when the option was granted.
Paragraph 41(5)(b) of Schedule 5 has the effect that a replacement option is to be treated as granted on the date when the original option was granted.

Text.Addition: Subsection (1)(a) and (b) do not apply where the relevant company is subject to an employee-ownership trust (within the meaning of paragraph 27(4) to (6) of Schedule 2).

P1group.Title: Disqualifying events relating to employee

P2para.Text: The following events relating to the employee are disqualifying events in relation to a qualifying option—

P3para.Text: when the employee ceases to be an eligible employee in relation to the relevant company as a result of ceasing to meet the requirement in paragraph 25 of Schedule 5 (the employment requirement);
when the employee ceases to be such an employee as a result of ceasing to meet the requirement in paragraph 26 of that Schedule (the requirement as to commitment of working time).

P2para.Text: In addition, a disqualifying event is to be treated as occurring in relation to a qualifying option at the end of any tax year if, during that year, the average amount per week of the employee’s reckonable time in relevant employment was less than the statutory threshold.
An employee’s “reckonable time in relevant employment” means the time which the employee in fact spent, as an employee in relevant employment—

P3para.Text: on the business of the relevant company, or
if that company is a parent company, on the business of the group,

P2para.Text: together with any time which the employee would, as such an employee, have spent on that business but for any of the reasons set out in paragraph 26(3)(a) to (d) of Schedule 5 (requirement as to commitment of working time).
The “statutory threshold” means—

P3para.Text: 25 hours, or
if less, 75% of the employee’s working time.

P2para.Text: For the purpose of applying subsection (2) to the tax year in which the option was granted, any part of that year which preceded the date on which it was granted is to be disregarded in calculating the average amount mentioned in that subsection.
In this section—

P3para.Text: “relevant employment” means employment—

P4para.Text: by the relevant company, or
if that company is a parent company, by any member of the group;

P3para.Text: “working time” has the meaning given by paragraph 27 of Schedule 5 (meaning of “working time”).

P1group.Title: Other disqualifying events

P2para.Text: The following are also disqualifying events in relation to a qualifying option—

P3para.Text: any variation of the terms of the option whose effect is either—

P4para.Text: to increase the market value of the shares that are the subject of the option, or
that the requirements of Schedule 5 would no longer be met in relation to the option;

P3para.Text: any alteration to the share capital of the relevant company—

P4para.Text: to which subsection (2) (share values affected by alteration of rights or restrictions) of section 537 applies, and
whose effect is that the requirements of Schedule 5 would no longer be met in relation to the option;

P3para.Text: any alteration to the share capital of the relevant company to which—

P4para.Text: subsection (2) (share values affected by alteration of rights or restrictions), and
subsection (3) (alteration designed to increase share values),

P3para.Text: of section 537 apply;
a conversion of any of the shares to which the option relates into shares of a different class, except in a case within section 538(2); and
the grant to the employee of a relevant CSOP option, if immediately after it is granted the employee holds unexercised employee options in respect of shares with a total value of more than £250,000 .

P2para.Text: In subsection (1)(e)—

Para.Text: “relevant CSOP option”, and
“employee option”,

have the meaning given by section 539 (CSOP and other options relevant for purposes of this section); and sub-paragraphs (6) to (8) of paragraph 5 of Schedule 5 (determination of value of shares) apply for the purposes of subsection (1)(e) as they apply for the purposes of paragraph 5.

P1group.Title: Alterations of share capital for purposes of section 536

P2para.Text: This section has effect for the purposes of section 536(1)(b) and (c) (other disqualifying events: alterations of share capital of relevant company).
This subsection applies to an alteration of the share capital of the relevant company if—

P3para.Text: the alteration affects (or but for the occurrence of some other event would affect) the value of the shares to which the option relates; and
it consists of or includes—

P4para.Text: the creation, variation or removal of a right relating to any shares in the relevant company,
the imposition of a restriction relating to any such shares, or
the variation or removal of a restriction to which any such shares are subject.

P2para.Text: This subsection applies to an alteration of the share capital of the relevant company if the effect of the alteration is to increase the market value of the shares to which the option relates and either—

P3para.Text: it is not made by the relevant company for commercial reasons, or
the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) for making it is to increase the market value of those shares.

P2para.Text: In this section any reference to—

P3para.Text: a restriction relating to shares or to which shares are subject, or
a right relating to shares,

P2para.Text: is a reference to such a restriction imposed or right conferred by any contract or arrangement or in any other way.

P1group.Title: Share conversions excluded for purposes of section 536

P2para.Text: This section has effect for the purposes of section 536(1)(d) (other disqualifying events: share conversions).
A conversion of shares is not a disqualifying event if—

P3para.Text: it is a conversion of shares of one class only (“the original class”) into shares of one other class only (“the new class”);
all the shares of the original class are converted into shares of the new class; and
one of the conditions in subsection (3) is met.

P2para.Text: The conditions are—

P3para.Text: that immediately before the conversion the majority of the relevant company’s shares of the original class are held otherwise than by or for the benefit of—

P4para.Text: directors or employees of the relevant company,
an associated company of the relevant company, or
directors or employees of such an associated company;

P3para.Text: that immediately before the conversion the relevant company is employee-controlled as a result of holdings of shares of the original class.

Text.Substitution: ” has the

Substitution.Substitution: meaning given by section 449 of CTA 2010

Text.Substitution: ” has the same meaning as in the benefits code (see section 67) but also includes a person who is to be or has been a director,
” includes a person who is to be or has been an employee, and
” has the same meaning as in Chapters 1 to 4 of this Part (see section 421H(1)).

P1group.Title: CSOP and other options relevant for purposes of section 536

P2para.Text: This section has effect for the purposes of section 536(1)(e) (other disqualifying events: grant of CSOP option).
A “relevant CSOP option” means a CSOP option granted to the employee by reason of the employee’s employment—

P3para.Text: with the employer company, or
if it is a member of a group of companies, with any member of that group.

P2para.Text: A share option is an “employee option” if it is—

P3para.Text: the qualifying option mentioned in section 536(1), or
another qualifying option granted to the employee by reason of the employee’s employment as mentioned in subsection (2)(a) or (b) above, or
a relevant CSOP option.

P2para.Text: In this section a “CSOP option” means an option to acquire shares under a scheme which is a Schedule 4 CSOP scheme (see Schedule 4).

P1group.Title: No charge on acquisition of shares as taxable benefit

P2para.Text: ... Chapter 3C of this Part (taxable benefits: notional loans in respect of acquisitions of shares) does not apply in relation to the acquisition of shares by the exercise of a qualifying option.

P1group.Title: Effects on other income tax charges

Text.Substitution: Nothing in the EMI code affects—
the operation of Chapters 2 to 4 of this Part in relation to shares acquired under a qualifying option, or
the operation of Chapter 5 of this Part otherwise than in relation to the acquisition of shares under a qualifying option.

But in calculating the taxable amount for the purposes of section 426 (post-acquisition charge on restricted securities) in respect of shares acquired under a qualifying option, the amount of relief on the exercise of the option is to be regarded as a deductible amount for the purposes of section 428 (amount of charge).

P2para.Text: “The amount of relief on the exercise of the option” means the difference between—

P3para.Text: the amount that would have counted as employment income by virtue of section 476 in respect of the exercise of the option apart from the EMI code, and
the amount (if any) that in fact counts as such income in accordance with the EMI code.

Title.Emphasis: Exemption where offer made to both public and employees

P1group.Title: Exemption: offer made to public and employees

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: there is a genuine offer to the public of shares in a company at a fixed price or by tender,
a director or employee of the company, or of another company or person, is entitled by reason of the office or employment to an allocation of the shares in priority to members of the public, and
conditions A to C are met.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax in respect of earnings arises by virtue of any benefit derived by the director or employee from the entitlement.
Condition A is that the aggregate number of shares subject to the offer that may be allocated as mentioned in subsection (1)(b) (“priority shares”) does not exceed—

P3para.Text: if the offer is part of arrangements which include one or more other offers to the public of shares of the same class, either of the limits in subsection (4), or
in any other case, 10% of the shares subject to the offer (including the priority shares).

P2para.Text: The limits referred to in subsection (3)(a) are—

P3para.Text: 40% of the shares subject to the offer (including the priority shares), and
10% of all the shares of the class in question that are subject to any of the offers forming part of the arrangements (including the priority shares).

P2para.Text: Condition B is that all the persons entitled to an allocation of priority shares are entitled to it on similar terms (see section 546).
Condition C is that those persons are not restricted wholly or mainly to directors or to those whose remuneration exceeds a particular level.
This section has effect subject to section 543 (discount not covered by exemption in this section).

P1group.Title: Discount not covered by exemption in section 542

P2para.Text: This section applies if the total of—

P3para.Text: the price payable by the director or employee for the shares of the company allocated to the director or employee under the offer, and
the amount or value of any registrant discount made to the director or employee in respect of the shares,

P2para.Text: is less than the fixed price or the lowest price successfully tendered.
Section 542(2) (exemption: offer made to public and employees) does not apply to the benefit (if any) represented by the difference.

Title.Emphasis: Exemption where different offers made to public and employees

P1group.Title: Exemption: different offers made to public and employees

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: there is a genuine offer to the public of a combination of shares in two or more companies at a fixed price or by tender (“the public offer”),
there is at the same time an offer (“the employee offer”) of shares, or of a combination of shares, in one or more, but not all, of those companies—

P4para.Text: to directors or employees of any of those companies, or of any other company or person, or
to those directors or employees and to other persons,

P3para.Text: any of those directors or employees is entitled by reason of the office or employment to an allocation of shares under the employee offer in priority to any allocation to members of the public under the public offer, and
conditions A to C are met.

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax in respect of earnings arises by virtue of any benefit derived by the director or employee from the entitlement.

Condition A is that for each company whose shares are subject to the employee offer, the aggregate number of shares subject to that offer that may be allocated as mentioned in subsection (1)(c) (“priority shares”) does not exceed—

P3para.Text: if the public offer and the employee offer are part of arrangements which include one or more other offers to the public of shares in the company of the same class, either of the limits in subsection (4), or
in any other case, 10% of the shares in the company that are subject to the public offer or the employee offer (including the priority shares).

P2para.Text: The limits referred to in subsection (3)(a) are—

P3para.Text: 40% of the shares in the company that are subject to the public offer or the employee offer (including the priority shares), and
10% of all the shares in the company of the class in question that are subject to any of the offers forming part of the arrangements (including the priority shares).

P2para.Text: Condition B is that all the persons entitled to an allocation of priority shares are entitled to it on similar terms (see section 546).
Condition C is that those persons are not restricted wholly or mainly to directors or to those whose remuneration exceeds a particular level.
This section has effect subject to section 545 (discount not covered by exemption in this section).

P1group.Title: Discount not covered by exemption in section 544

P2para.Text: This section applies if the total of—

P3para.Text: the price payable by the director or employee for the shares of a company allocated to the director or employee under the employee offer, and
the amount or value of any registrant discount made to the director or employee in respect of the shares,

P2para.Text: is not the same as, or as near as reasonably practicable to, the appropriate notional price for the shares of the company.

Section 544(2) (exemption: different offers made to public and employees) does not apply to the benefit (if any) represented by the amount by which the appropriate notional price exceeds the total referred to in subsection (1).
The “appropriate notional price” for the shares of a company is—

P3para.Text: if subsection (4) applies, the amount given by the formula in subsection (6), and
in any other case, the notional price.

P2para.Text: This subsection applies if shares of the company are subject to the public offer and there is a difference between CP and AFP—

P3para.Text: CP being the price for the combination of shares subject to the public offer determined by aggregating the notional prices for each one of the shares comprised in the combination, and
AFP being the actual fixed price or (as the case may be) the lowest successfully tendered price for that combination of shares.

P2para.Text: The “notional price” for the shares of a company is the price that might reasonably have been expected to be the fixed price for the shares of the company under a separate offer of those shares if—

P3para.Text: the shares of the company, and of each of the other companies had, instead of being subject to the public offer and the employee offer, been subject to separate offers to the public in respect of each company at fixed prices, and
those separate offers had been made at the time at which the public offer was in fact made.

P2para.Text: The formula referred to in subsection (3)(a) is—

Para.Text: where—
NP is the notional price for the shares of the company, and
AFP and CP have the same meanings as in subsection (4).

P1group.Title: Meaning of being entitled “on similar terms”

P2para.Text: This section applies for the purposes of sections 542(5) and 544(5) (condition that entitlements to allocation of priority shares must be on similar terms).
The fact that different provision is made for persons according to—

P3para.Text: the levels of their remuneration,
the length of their service, or
similar factors,

P2para.Text: does not mean that they are not entitled to an allocation on similar terms.

The fact that the allocations of shares in a company to which non-company employees are entitled are smaller than those to which company employees are entitled does not mean that they are not entitled on similar terms, if conditions A and B are met.

Condition A is that each non-company employee is also entitled by reason of the office or employment and in priority to members of the public, to an allocation of shares in another company or companies which are offered to the public at a fixed price or by tender at the same time as the shares in the company.

Condition B is that in the case of each non-company employee the aggregate value of all the shares included in the allocations to which the non-company employee is entitled is the same, or as nearly the same as is reasonably practicable, as that of the shares in the company included in the entitlement of a comparable company employee.
For the purposes of subsection (5), the value of shares is to be measured by reference to the fixed price or the lowest price successfully tendered.
In this section—

Para.Text: “company employee”, in relation to a company, means a director or employee of the company, and
“non-company employee”, in relation to a company, means a director or employee of another company or person.

P1group.Title: Meaning and amount or value of “registrant discount”

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter there is a “registrant discount” in respect of the shares of a company if conditions A to C are met.

Condition A is that members of the public who comply with such requirements as may be imposed in connection with the offer or, if section 544 applies, the public offer are, or may become, entitled to a discount in respect of the whole or part of the shares of the company allocated to them.
Condition B is that at least 40% of the shares of the company allocated to members of the public are allocated to individuals who are or become entitled to—

P3para.Text: the discount, or
some other benefit of similar value for which they may elect as an alternative to the discount.

P2para.Text: Directors and employees who are entitled by reason of their office or employment to an allocation of the shares in priority to members of the public are not to be treated as members of the public for the purposes of subsection (3).

Condition C is that subscribing employees are, or may become, entitled to the same discount in respect of the shares of the company as any other members of the public to whom shares of the company are allocated under the offer.
In subsection (5) a “subscribing employee” means a director or employee who—

P3para.Text: subscribes for shares—

P4para.Text: if section 542 (offer made to public and employees) applies, under the offer as a member of the public, or
if section 544 (different offers made to public and employees) applies, under the public offer as a member of the public or under the employee offer as a director or employee, and

P3para.Text: complies (or, in the case of a requirement to register, is taken under the terms of the offer to comply) with the requirements mentioned in subsection (2).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter, the “amount or value” of any registrant discount made to a director or employee means—

P3para.Text: the amount of any such discount made to the director or employee as is mentioned in subsection (5), or
the value of any such other benefit as is mentioned in subsection (3)(b) which is conferred on the director or employee as an alternative to the discount.

P1group.Title: Minor definitions

P2para.Text: In this Chapter—

Para.Text: “director” means—
in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by a board of directors or similar body, a member of that body,
in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by a single director or similar person, that director or person, and
in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by the members themselves, a member of the company, and

includes any person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the directors of the company (as defined in paragraphs (a) to (c)) are accustomed to act and a person who is to be, or has ceased to be, a director (as so defined);
“employee” includes a person who is to be or has been an employee;
“shares” includes stock;
“the employee offer” and “the public offer” have the meanings given by section 544(1).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (1) a person is not to be regarded as a person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the directors of the company are accustomed to act merely because the directors act on advice given by that person in a professional capacity.
References in this Chapter—

P3para.Text: to the employment, in relation to an employee, are to the employment of that employee, and
to the office, in relation to a director, are to the office of that director.

Chapter.Title: Supplementary provisions about employee benefit trusts

P1group.Title: Application of this Chapter

P2para.Text: This Chapter applies for the purposes of any listed provision in circumstances where—

P3para.Text: an individual (“B”) is interested as a beneficiary of an employee benefit trust in shares or obligations of a particular company (“the company”), and
the question arises under that provision whether the trustees of the trust are, as a result of B’s being so interested, to be regarded as associates of B’s for the relevant purposes.
The relevant purposes are those of the operation, in relation to the company, of the “no material interest” requirement contained in the Schedule to this Act in which the listed provision appears.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “listed provision” means any of the following provisions (under which trustees of an employee benefit trust are not to be regarded as associates if specified limits relating to share ownership are not exceeded)—

P3para.Text: paragraph 23(2) of Schedule 2 (... SIPs),
paragraph 15(2) of Schedule 3 (... SAYE option schemes),
paragraph 13(2) of Schedule 4 (... CSOP schemes), or
paragraph 32(2) of Schedule 5 (enterprise management incentives).

P2para.Text: The general effect of this Chapter is that if the provisions of—

P3para.Text: sections 552 and 553 (attribution of interest in company to beneficiary or associate), or
section 554 (attribution of further interest),

P2para.Text: apply in relation to B or an associate of B's, B or the associate is to be treated for the purposes of the listed provision as having been the beneficial owner of a particular percentage of the company’s ordinary share capital on a particular date.
In this Chapter, in relation to an individual, “associate”—

P3para.Text: has the meaning given by section 448 of CTA 2010 (close companies: meaning of “associate”), but

does not include the trustees of an employee benefit trust as a result only of the individual’s having (as mentioned in subsection (1)(a)) an interest in shares or obligations of the company which are subject to the trust.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “employee” means the holder of a taxable employment under Part 2 (as defined in section 66(3)), and accordingly includes an office-holder whose office is within the scope of that definition as a result of section 5(1).

P1group.Title: Meaning of “employee benefit trust”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “employee benefit trust”, in relation to a company, means a trust where conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that all or most of the employees of the company are eligible to benefit under the trust.
Condition B is that after 13th March 1989 either—

P3para.Text: there has been no disposal of any of the property subject to the trust, or
any disposal of any of that property was a disposal within subsection (4).

P2para.Text: The disposals within this subsection are—

P3para.Text: disposals in the ordinary management of the trust, or
qualifying disposals (within the meaning given by section 551).

P2para.Text: In this section and section 551 “disposal” means disposal by sale, loan or otherwise.

P1group.Title: “Qualifying disposals” for purposes of section 550

P2para.Text: For the purposes of section 550 (meaning of “employee benefit trust”) a “qualifying disposal” is a disposal of property consisting of—

P3para.Text: any of the ordinary share capital of the company, or
money paid outright,

P2para.Text: where any of conditions 1, 2 and 3 is met.
Condition 1 is that the property has been applied for the benefit of—

P3para.Text: individual employees or former employees of the company,
spouses or civil partners , former spouses or civil partners , widows or widowers or surviving civil partners of employees or former employees of the company,
dependants of persons within paragraph (a), or
relatives, or spouses or civil partners of relatives, of persons within paragraph (a) or (b).

P2para.Text: In subsection (2) each reference to the company includes a reference to a company controlled by the company.
Condition 2 is that the property has been applied for charitable purposes.
Condition 3 is that the property has been transferred to—

P3para.Text: the trustees of another employee benefit trust,
the trustees of a qualifying employee share ownership trust (within the meaning of Schedule 5 to FA 1989), or
the trustees of a profit sharing scheme approved under Schedule 9 to ICTA (approved share option schemes and profit sharing schemes).

P2para.Text: In this section “relative” means—

P3para.Text: parent, child or remoter relation in the direct line, or
brother, sister, uncle, aunt, nephew or niece.

P1group.Title: Attribution of interest in company to beneficiary or associate

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: after 13th March 1989 B, or an associate of B's, has received a payment (“the relevant payment”) from the trustees of the employee benefit trust, and

at any time during the period of 3 years ending with the day on which the relevant payment was received (“the payment date”), the property subject to the trust consisted of or included any part of the ordinary share capital of the company.

P2para.Text: In such a case B or the associate is to be treated for the purposes of the listed provision as having been the beneficial owner of the appropriate percentage of the ordinary share capital of the company on the payment date.
This is in addition to any percentage of that share capital of which B or the associate was actually the beneficial owner on that date.
Section 553 explains what is meant by “the appropriate percentage”.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “appropriate percentage” for purposes of section 552

P2para.Text: For the purposes of section 552 “the appropriate percentage” is—

Para.Text: where P and D have the meaning given by the following provisions.

P2para.Text: Unless subsection (3) applies, P is the aggregate of the relevant payment and any other payments received by B or associates of B’s from the trustees of the trust during the period of 12 months ending with the payment date.
If—

P3para.Text: any distributions were made to the trustees of the trust by the company in respect of its ordinary share capital during the period of 3 years ending with the payment date, and
the aggregate of those distributions is less than the aggregate mentioned in subsection (2),

P2para.Text: P is the aggregate of those distributions.
Unless subsection (5) applies, D is the amount determined as follows—
Calculate the aggregate of—

P3para.Text: any distributions made by the company in respect of its ordinary share capital during the period of 12 months ending with the payment date,
any distributions so made during the period of 12 months immediately preceding that mentioned in paragraph (a), and
any distributions so made during the period of 12 months immediately preceding that mentioned in paragraph (b).
Divide the aggregate so calculated by the number of the periods mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (c) in which distributions were so made.

P2para.Text: If no distributions were so made during any of those periods, D is 1.
In this section “the payment date” and “the relevant payment” have the meaning indicated in section 552(1).

P1group.Title: Attribution of further interest in company

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: B or an associate of B’s is (apart from this section) to be treated by virtue of section 552(2) as having been the beneficial owner of a percentage of the ordinary share capital of the company as a result of receiving the relevant payment from the trustees of an employee benefit trust, and

B or an associate of B’s has, during the period of 12 months ending with the payment date, received one or more payments from the trustees of any other employee benefit trust or trusts connected with the company.

P2para.Text: In such a case section 552 applies to B or (as the case may be) the associate mentioned in subsection (1)(a) as if B or the associate had received—

P3para.Text: any payment from the trustees of a trust as mentioned in subsection (1)(b), or
where more than one payment has been received from the trustees of a trust, the last of the payments,

P2para.Text: on the payment date.
B or the associate is accordingly to be treated for the purposes of the listed provision as having been the beneficial owner on the payment date of both—

P3para.Text: the percentage of the ordinary share capital of the company mentioned in subsection (1)(a), and
the appropriate percentage of that share capital as determined in accordance with subsection (2).

P2para.Text: This is in addition to any percentage of that share capital of which B or the associate was actually the beneficial owner on that date.

For the purposes of this section a trust is “connected with” the company if, at any time during the period of 3 years ending with the payment date, the property subject to the trust consisted of or included any part of the ordinary share capital of the company.
In this section “the payment date” and “the relevant payment” have the meaning indicated in section 552(1).

Title.Addition: Employment income provided through third parties

Text.Addition: Chapter 2 applies if—
a person (“A”) is an employee, or a former or prospective employee, of another person (“B”),
there is an arrangement (“the relevant arrangement”) to which A is a party or which otherwise (wholly or partly) covers or relates to A,
it is reasonable to suppose that, in essence—
the relevant arrangement, or
the relevant arrangement so far as it covers or relates to A,

is (wholly or partly) a means of providing, or is otherwise concerned (wholly or partly) with the provision of, rewards or recognition or loans in connection with A's employment, or former or prospective employment, with B,
a relevant step is taken by a relevant third person, and
it is reasonable to suppose that, in essence—
the relevant step is taken (wholly or partly) in pursuance of the relevant arrangement, or
there is some other connection (direct or indirect) between the relevant step and the relevant arrangement.
In this Part “
” means a step within section 554B, 554C or 554D

Addition.Addition: (including such a step where the taking of the step, or some aspect of the taking of the step, constitutes a breach of trust or is a constituent part of a breach of trust, and even if the step or aspect

Text.Addition: is void as a result of breach of trust)..
Subsection (1) is subject to subsection (4) and sections 554E to 554Y.

Addition.Substitution: Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of—
a relevant step taken on or after A's death if—
the relevant step is within section 554B, or
the relevant step is within section 554C by virtue of subsection (1)(ab) of that section,
a relevant step within paragraph 1 of Schedule 11 to F(No.2)A 2017 which is treated as being taken on or after A's death, or

a relevant step within paragraph 1A of Schedule 11 to F(No.2)A 2017 in a case where the initial step (within the meaning given by sub-paragraph (1)(a) of that paragraph) is treated as being taken on or after A's death.

Text.Addition: In subsection (1)(b) and (c)(ii) references to A include references to any person linked with A.

Addition.Addition: a payment to a person other than A, or to A as a trustee, is of earnings from A's employment with B, and
the earnings are, in whole or part, charged to tax under the employment income Parts otherwise than by virtue of this Part,
and for this purpose it does not matter whether all or some only or none of the tax is paid (but see sections 554Z5 and 554Z11B).

For the purposes of subsection (5C), an arrangement is a “redirected-earnings arrangement” if it (wholly or partly) covers or relates to redirected earnings; and for the purposes of this subsection and subsection (5C) “
the payment mentioned in subsection (5A)(a), or
any sum or other property which (directly or indirectly)—
do not prevent a redirected-earnings arrangement being within subsection (1)(b), and

do not prevent rewards or recognition or loans being in connection with A's employment with B for the purposes of subsection (1)(c) where there is use of redirected earnings for the provision of the whole, or part, of the rewards or recognition or loans.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of subsection (1)(c) it does not matter if the relevant arrangement does not include details of the steps which will or may be taken in connection with providing, in essence, rewards or recognition or loans as mentioned (for example, details of any sums of money or assets which will or may be involved or details of how or when or by whom or in whose favour any step will or may be taken).
In subsection (1)(d) “
” means—
A acting as a trustee,
B acting as a trustee, or
any person other than A and B.

If B is a company and is a member of a group of companies at the time the relevant step is taken, in subsection (7) references to B are to be read as including references to any other company which is a member of that group at that time.

If B is a limited liability partnership, in subsection (7) references to B are to be read as including references to any company which is a wholly-owned subsidiary (as defined in section 1159(2) of the Companies Act 2006) of B at the time the relevant step is taken.
Neither subsection (8) nor subsection (9) applies if there is a connection (direct or indirect) between the relevant step and a tax avoidance arrangement.
For the purposes of subsection (1)(e)—

the relevant step is connected with the relevant arrangement if (for example) the relevant step is taken (wholly or partly) in pursuance of an arrangement at one end of a series of arrangements with the relevant arrangement being at the other end, and
it does not matter if the person taking the relevant step is unaware of the relevant arrangement.
For the purposes of subsection (1)(c) and (e) in particular, all relevant circumstances are to be taken into account in order to get to the essence of the matter.

Addition.Addition: there is an arrangement (“the relevant arrangement”) to which an individual (“A”) is a party or which otherwise (wholly or partly) covers or relates to A,
it is reasonable to suppose that, in essence—
the relevant arrangement so far as it covers or relates to A,

a relevant step is taken by a relevant third person,

that the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step represents (directly or indirectly), or has arisen or derives from, the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant transaction, or

there is a time in the relevant period when the main purpose, or one of the main purposes, of operating, implementing, maintaining or terminating the relevant arrangement so far as it covers or relates to—

is the avoidance of? income tax, national insurance contributions, corporation tax or a charge to tax under section 455 of CTA 2010.
” includes a company that would be a close company but for section 442(a) of CTA 2010 (exclusion of companies not resident in the United Kingdom).
For the purposes of subsection (1)(b), a payment or benefit or loan is “A-linked” if—
it is being provided to A, or a person chosen by A or within a class of persons chosen by A,
it is being provided to a person on A's behalf, or at A's direction or request, or
it is being provided to a person linked with A and it is reasonable to suppose that the main reason, or one of the main reasons, for it being provided is that the person is linked with A.

For the purposes of subsection (1)(i), the “relevant period” consists of the time of the relevant transaction, the time of the relevant step, the times around each of those two times, and any other times between those two times.
a payment to a person other than A, or to A as a trustee, is of earnings from—

relevant shares, or

the award of the relevant shares or sum of money would be on terms (“the deferred award terms”) the main purpose of which is to defer the receipt of the shares by A, or the payment of the sum of money to A, to a specified date (“the vesting date”) which is after the date (“the award date”) on which the award is made, while providing that the award is revoked if specified conditions are not met on or before the vesting date,

the payment represents the proceeds of the disposal of the shares, or the payment is made from another source and, correspondingly, the shares are no longer held by any person in relation to the award.

provides for A to purchase a new car from another person (“P”) using a loan (“the car loan”) to be made to A by
specifies the date (“the repayment date”) by which the car loan must be fully repaid which must be no later than four years after the date on which the car loan is made, and

permits A, in order to obtain funds to repay the car loan, to sell the car back to P on a specified date at a specified price based on an estimate (made at the time the car ownership arrangement is made) of the likely outstanding amount of the car loan on the specified date, and
as provided for by the car ownership arrangement, A purchases the car using the car loan.
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of a relevant step taken for the sole purpose of—
the purchase of the car or its sale-back as provided for by the car ownership arrangement, or
the making of the car loan as so provided,
so long as the car ownership arrangement is not a tax avoidance arrangement and there is no other connection (direct or indirect) between the relevant step and a tax avoidance arrangement.
Subsection (4) applies if—
apart from subsection (2), Chapter 2 would apply by reason of the making of the car loan, and
by the end of the repayment date, the car loan has not been fully repaid.
This Part has effect as if a relevant step within section 554C(1)(a) were taken at the end of the repayment date—
the subject of which is a sum of money of an amount equal to the outstanding amount of the car loan as at the end of the repayment date,
in relation to which the relevant person (within the meaning of section 554C(1)) is A, and
by reason of which Chapter 2 is to apply.
In this section—
” has the meaning given by section 235(2), and

Addition.Addition: has permission under Part 4A of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 to enter into, or to exercise or have the right to exercise rights and duties under, a contract of the kind mentioned in paragraph 23 of Schedule 2 to that Act, and
is not acting as a trustee.
The definition of “authorised lender” must be read with—

2)A 2017 for provision about exclusions for car loans in a case in which the relevant step is within paragraph 1 of that Schedule.
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of a relevant step taken by a person (“P”) if—
the step is acquiring a right to payment of an amount equal to the whole or part of a payment made by way of a loan to a relevant person (the “borrower”),
the loan, at the time it was made, was an employment-related loan,
at the time the relevant step is taken, the section 180 threshold is not exceeded in relation to the loan,
at the time the relevant step is taken, the borrower is an employee, or a prospective employee, of P, and
there is no connection (direct or indirect) between the relevant step and a tax avoidance arrangement.
For the purposes of this section, the section 180 threshold is not exceeded in relation to a loan if, at all times in the relevant tax year—
the amount outstanding on the loan, or
if two or more employment-related loans are made by the same employer, the aggregate of the amount outstanding on them,
does not exceed the amount specified at the end of section 180(2) (normal threshold for benefit of a loan to be treated as earnings).
two or more employment-related loans are made by the same employer, and
during the relevant tax year, a person acquires a right to payment of an amount (the “transfer amount”) equal to the whole or part of the payment made by way of any of the loans.
The transfer amount is to be treated as an “amount outstanding” on that loan for the purposes of subsection (2)(b).
” has the same meaning as it has for the purposes of Chapter 7 of Part 3;
” means the tax year in which the relevant step is taken.
See paragraph 27 of Schedule 11 to F(No. 2)A 2017 for provision about exclusions where a loan is an employment-related loan and the relevant step is within paragraph 1 of that Schedule.

Title.Addition: Exclusions: employment income exemptions under Part 4

Text.Addition: Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of a relevant step if an employment income exemption under Part 4 applies to the subject of the relevant step.
If the employment income exemption applies to the subject of the relevant step in part only, the relevant step is to be treated for the purposes of this Part as being two separate relevant steps—
one in relation to the subject of the step so far as the exemption applies to it, and
one in relation to the subject of the step so far as the exemption does not apply to it,
with subsection (1) applying only in relation to the separate relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a).

In order to give effect to subsection (2), the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step is to be apportioned between the two separate relevant steps on a just and reasonable basis.
In this section “
” includes the exemption under section 271.

Title.Addition: Exclusions: income arising from earmarked sum or asset

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
a sum of money or asset (“sum or asset R”) is held by or on behalf of a person (“P”),
income arises from sum or asset R, and
when the income arises, it—
is received by or on behalf of P, and
is the subject of a relevant step within section 554B taken by P.
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the relevant step mentioned in subsection (1)(c)(ii) if—
before the income arises, sum or asset R was the subject of a relevant step within section 554B taken by P,

Chapter 2 applied by reason of the relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a) in respect of A's employment with B or would have so applied apart from this section or section 554R or any of sections 554H to 554M or section 554T,
immediately before the income arises, sum or asset R is still earmarked or otherwise held on the basis mentioned in section 554B(1)(a) or (b), and
subsection (3) does not apply.

This subsection applies if it is reasonable to suppose that, taking into account the type of investments from which the income derives (directly or indirectly), in essence, the income represents a return from sum or asset R which exceeds the return which might be expected applying the assumption that all relevant connected persons are acting at arm's length of each other.
In subsection (3) “
” means a person with a connection (direct or indirect) to the arrangement under which the income arises.

Title.Addition: Exclusions: acquisitions out of sums or assets

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
a sum of money or asset (“sum or asset S”) is held by or on behalf of a person (“P”),
a sum of money or asset (“sum or asset T”) is acquired by or on behalf of P wholly out of sum or asset S,
sum or asset T is not acquired (directly or indirectly) from A or any person linked with A, and
subsection (2) does not apply.
This subsection applies if it is reasonable to suppose that, in essence—
at the time of the acquisition of sum or asset T, the value of sum or asset T is greater or less than the value of sum or asset S, and
the difference (or any part of the difference) in the values might not have been expected applying the assumption that all relevant connected persons are acting at arm's length of each other.
In subsection (2)—
the reference to sum or asset S is to sum or asset S so far as sum or asset T is acquired out of it, and
” means a person with a connection (direct or indirect) to the arrangement under which sum or asset T is acquired.
The cases covered by subsection (1)(b) include (in particular) cases in which sum or asset T represents the proceeds of the disposal of sum or asset S.
Subsection (6) applies if, on its acquisition, sum or asset T is the subject of a relevant step within section 554B taken by P.
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the relevant step if—
before the acquisition, sum or asset S was the subject of a relevant step within section 554B taken by P,
Chapter 2 applied by reason of the relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a) in respect of A's employment with B or would have applied apart from this section or section 554Q or 554T, and
immediately before the acquisition, sum or asset S is still earmarked or otherwise held on the basis mentioned in section 554B(1)(a) or (b).
Subsection (8) applies if—
on its acquisition, sum or asset T—
is the subject of a relevant step within section 554B taken by P by reason of which Chapter 2 applies or would apply apart from subsection (6) above or any of sections 554H to 554M, 554Q or 554T, or
if sub-paragraph (i) does not apply, is held by or on behalf of P on the same basis as that on which sum or asset S was held by or on behalf of P immediately before the acquisition, and
for the sole purpose of the acquisition, sum or asset S or sum or asset T is the subject of a relevant step within section 554C(1)(a) to (c).
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the relevant step mentioned in subsection (7)(b).

Addition.Addition: This section applies (subject to subsection (5)) if—
a right to repayment of principal under a relevant loan (the “repayment right”) is held by or on behalf of a person (“P”), and
on or after 9 December 2010, a sum of money (the “repayment sum”) is acquired by or on behalf of P by way of repayment of principal under the relevant loan.
” means a loan made on or after 6 April 1999.
on its acquisition, the repayment sum is the subject of a relevant step within section 554B taken by P, or
for the sole purpose of the acquisition, the making of the payment of the repayment sum is a relevant step within section 554C(1)(a).

Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the relevant step if, on its acquisition, the repayment sum is held by or on behalf of P on the same basis as that on which the repayment right was held by or on behalf of P immediately before the acquisition.

This section does not apply where there is any connection (direct or indirect) between the acquisition by or on behalf of P of the repayment sum and a tax avoidance arrangement (other than the arrangement under which the relevant loan was made).

Title.Addition: Exclusions: pension income chargeable under Part 9

Text.Addition: Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of a relevant step within section 554C or 554D if the step is the provision of pension income which is chargeable to income tax under Part 9 or is exempt income (within the meaning of that Part).
Sections 554T, 554U, 554V, 554W and 554X contain further provision relating to retirement benefits
etc
and are to be applied, so far as applicable, in that order.

Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of a relevant step within section 554B if the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the step arises or derives (whether wholly or partly or directly or indirectly) from an excluded pension contribution paid by A on or after 6 April 2011.

If the sum of money or asset arises or derives from the excluded pension contribution only partly, the relevant step is to be treated for the purposes of this Part as being two separate relevant steps—
one in relation to the sum of money or asset so far as it arises or derives from the excluded pension contribution, and
one in relation to the sum of money or asset so far as it does not arise or derive from the excluded pension contribution,
with subsection (1) applying only in relation to the separate relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a).
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of a relevant step within section 554C or 554D if the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the step—
represents relevant benefits, and
arises or derives (whether wholly or partly or directly or indirectly) from an excluded pension contribution paid by A.

If the sum of money or asset arises or derives from the excluded pension contribution only partly, the relevant step is to be treated for the purposes of this Part as being two separate relevant steps—
one in relation to the sum of money or asset so far as it arises or derives from the excluded pension contribution, and
one in relation to the sum of money or asset so far as it does not arise or derive from the excluded pension contribution,
with subsection (3) applying only in relation to the separate relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a).

In order to give effect to subsection (2) or (4), the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step is to be apportioned between the two separate relevant steps on a just and reasonable basis.
For the purposes of this section an excluded pension contribution is a contribution—
which is made to an arrangement by A by way of a payment of a sum of money,
by virtue of which A acquires rights to receive relevant benefits under the arrangement (and nothing else),
which is neither a relievable pension contribution nor a tax-relieved contribution, and

which is not a repayment of any loan and otherwise has nothing to do with any loan and has nothing to do with a sum of money or asset which has been the subject of a relevant step within section 554C(1)(d).
In this section—
” has the same meaning as in Chapter 2 of Part 6, but ignoring section 393B(2)(a),
” means a contribution in respect of which an individual is entitled to relief under section 188 of FA 2004, and
” has the meaning given by paragraph 3(3) of Schedule 34 to FA 2004.

Title.Addition: Exclusions: pre-6 April 2006 contributions to employer-financed retirement benefit schemes

Text.Addition: This section applies if the subject of a relevant step is a sum of money or asset which has (wholly or partly) arisen or derived (directly or indirectly) from a sum of money (“the taxed sum”)—
which was paid by B in accordance with an employer-financed retirement benefits scheme (within the meaning of Chapter 2 of Part 6) with a view to the provision of benefits under the scheme, and
in respect of which A is taxed.

For the purpose of determining whether A is taxed in respect of a sum of money, paragraph 53(3) of Schedule 36 to FA 2004 applies as it applies for the purpose of determining whether an employee is taxed for the purposes of paragraph 53(1)(b) of that Schedule.
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the relevant step.
Subsection (5) applies if the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step only partly arises or derives from the taxed sum.
The relevant step is to be treated for the purposes of this Part as being two separate relevant steps—
one in relation to the sum of money or asset so far as it arises or derives from the taxed sum, and
one in relation to the sum of money or asset so far as it does not arise or derive from the taxed sum,
with subsection (3) applying only in relation to the separate relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a).

In order to give effect to subsection (5), the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step is to be apportioned between the two separate relevant steps on a just and reasonable basis.
If B is a company and is a member of a group of companies at any time (“

”), in subsection (1)(a), in relation to any sum of money paid at the relevant time, the reference to B is to be read as including a reference to any other company which is a member of that group at the relevant time.

Title.Addition: Exclusions: purchases of annuities out of pension scheme rights

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
an annuity contract is purchased from an insurance company wholly out of rights which A has under a pension scheme, and
A's rights out of which the annuity contract is purchased are, wholly or partly, pre-6 April 2011 annuity rights.
If the purchaser—
takes a relevant step for the sole purpose of purchasing the annuity contract or transferring the beneficiary's rights under the annuity contract to A or a person linked with A, or
on the purchase of the annuity contract, otherwise takes a relevant step within section 554B the subject of which is the beneficiary's rights under the annuity contract,
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the relevant step.
If the insurance company—
takes a relevant step for the sole purpose of selling the annuity contract, or

on the sale of the annuity contract, otherwise takes a relevant step within section 554B the subject of which is a sum of money or asset representing the purchase price received for the annuity contract,
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the relevant step.

If A's rights out of which the annuity contract is purchased are only partly pre-6 April 2011 annuity rights, any relevant step mentioned in subsection (2)(a) or (b) or (3)(a) or (b) is to be treated for the purposes of this Part as being two separate relevant steps—
one in relation to the annuity contract so far as it is purchased out of rights which are pre-6 April 2011 annuity rights, and
one in relation to the annuity contract so far as it is purchased out of rights which are not pre-6 April 2011 annuity rights,
with subsection (2) or (3) (as the case may be) applying only in relation to the separate relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a) of this subsection.

In order to give effect to subsection (4), the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step mentioned in subsection (2)(a) or (b) or (3)(a) or (b) is to be apportioned between the two separate relevant steps on a just and reasonable basis.
In this section—
” means a contract for the provision of an annuity—
granted for consideration in money or money's worth in the ordinary course of a business of granting annuities on human life, and
payable for a term ending at a time ascertainable only by reference to the end of a human life,
although for this purpose it does not matter that the annuity may in some circumstances end before or after the life,
” means—
a person or
EEA
firm within section 275(1)(a) or (b) of FA 2004, or
a person resident in a territory outside the European Economic Area—
whose normal business includes the provision of annuities, and
who is regulated in the conduct of that business by the government of that territory or by a body established under the law of that territory for the purpose of regulating such business, and
” means rights, which accrued before 6 April 2011, specifically to receive an annuity.
This section applies if—
a relevant benefit is provided under a relevant scheme by way of a payment of a lump sum wholly out of rights which A has under the scheme,
A's rights out of which the lump sum is paid are, wholly or partly, pre-6 April 2011 lump sum rights, and
the payment of the lump sum is a relevant step within section 554C.
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the relevant step.

If A's rights out of which the lump sum is paid are only partly pre-6 April 2011 lump sum rights, the relevant step is to be treated for the purposes of this Part as being two separate relevant steps—
one in relation to the lump sum so far as it is paid out of rights which are pre-6 April 2011 lump sum rights, and
one in relation to the lump sum so far as it is paid out of rights which are not pre-6 April 2011 lump sum rights,
with subsection (2) applying only in relation to the separate relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a).
In order to give effect to subsection (3), the lump sum is to be apportioned between the two separate relevant steps on a just and reasonable basis.
In this section—
” means rights, which accrued before 6 April 2011, specifically to receive relevant benefits by way of lump sum payments,
” has the same meaning as in Chapter 2 of Part 6, and
” means an employer-financed retirement benefits scheme (within the meaning of that Chapter) or a superannuation fund to which section 615(3) of
ICTA
applies.

Title.Addition: Exclusions: transfers between certain foreign pension schemes

Text.Addition: This section applies if rights which A has under a section 390 scheme are transferred to another section 390 scheme or to an overseas pension scheme.
This section also applies if—
rights which A has under an overseas pension scheme are transferred to another overseas pension scheme, and
some or all of the rights transferred are section 390 scheme rights.
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of—
a relevant step within section 554C taken for the sole purpose of transferring the rights, or
a relevant step within section 554B taken by the transferee in relation to the transferred rights on their transfer.
Subsection (5) applies in relation to a transfer within subsection (2) if not all the transferred rights are section 390 scheme rights.
Any relevant step mentioned in subsection (3) is to be treated for the purposes of this Part as being two separate relevant steps—
one in relation to the section 390 scheme rights, and
one in relation to the rest of the transferred rights,
with subsection (3) applying only in relation to the separate relevant step mentioned in paragraph (a) of this subsection.

In order to give effect to subsection (5), the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step mentioned in subsection (3) is to be apportioned between the two separate relevant steps on a just and reasonable basis.
Subsection (8) applies if any of the transferred rights arise or derive (directly or indirectly) from contributions to any scheme which—
are paid by B on or after 6 April 2006, and
are neither tax-relieved contributions nor tax-exempt provision.
Any relevant step mentioned in subsection (3) is to be treated for the purposes of this Part as being two separate relevant steps—
one in relation to the rights mentioned in subsection (7), and
one in relation to the rest of the transferred rights,
with subsection (3) applying only in relation to the separate relevant step mentioned in paragraph (b) of this subsection.

In order to give effect to subsection (8), the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step mentioned in subsection (3) is to be apportioned between the two separate relevant steps on a just and reasonable basis.
If subsection (5) applies in relation to a transfer—
in subsection (7) the reference to the transferred rights is to be read as a reference to the transferred section 390 scheme rights only, and
in subsections (8) and (9) references to any relevant step mentioned in subsection (3) are to be read as references to the separate relevant step mentioned in subsection (5)(a).
If B is a company and is a member of a group of companies at any time (“

”), in subsection (7)(a), in relation to any contribution paid at the relevant time, the reference to B is to be read as including a reference to any other company which is a member of that group at the relevant time.
In this section—
” has the same meaning as in Part 4 of FA 2004 (see section 150(7) of that Act),
” means a scheme in relation to which a claim was accepted under section 390,
” means rights which A has under an overseas pension scheme and which—
have been transferred to the scheme (directly or indirectly) from a section 390 scheme, or
have arisen or derived (directly or indirectly) from rights that have been so transferred, and
“tax-exempt provision” and “tax-relieved contribution” have the meaning given by paragraph 3(3) and (4) of Schedule 34 to FA 2004.

Addition.Addition: Exclusions: payments in respect of a tax liability
Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of a relevant step which is the payment of a sum of money if—
the payment is a relevant tax payment, or
where the payment is not a relevant tax payment—
the payment is made to a person for the purpose of the person making a relevant tax payment,
the person makes a relevant tax payment of an amount equal to the amount of the first payment, and
the relevant tax payment is made before the end of the period of 60 days beginning with the day on which the first payment is made.
” means a payment made to Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs in respect of a relevant liability for—
But a provisional payment of tax (see section 554Z11D) is not a relevant tax payment.
A liability is a “relevant liability” if—
under the terms of an agreement for the discharge of the liability, or
by way of a decision on an application under this section,
an officer of Revenue and Customs agrees that the liability is to be treated as arising in respect of the relevant arrangement concerned.
A person may make an application to Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs for a liability to be treated, for the purposes of this section, as arising in respect of the relevant arrangement concerned.
An application under this section must be made in such form and manner, and contain such information, as may be specified by, or on behalf of, the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs.
An officer of Revenue and Customs must notify the applicant of the decision on an application under this section.

Title.Addition: Power to exclude other relevant steps

Text.Addition: The Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs may by regulations provide for Chapter 2 not to apply—
by reason of a relevant step falling within a specified description, or
in the cases otherwise specified in the regulations.
Regulations under this section may, in consequence of provision within subsection (1)—
provide—
for a relevant step to be treated for the purposes of this Part as if it were two or more separate relevant steps,
for the provision within subsection (1) to apply only to one or some of the separate relevant steps, and
for the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step to be apportioned between the separate relevant steps on a just and reasonable basis,
make provision, in relation to cases in which Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of a relevant step by virtue of the provision within subsection (1)—
for a relevant step to be treated as taking place if, subsequently, specified conditions are met or not met, and
for Chapter 2 to apply by reason of the relevant step treated as taking place, and
make other provision modifying the application of any provision of this Part.
Regulations under this section may contain incidental, supplemental, consequential and transitional provision and savings.
Regulations under this section may have retrospective effect.
This section applies for the purposes of this Part.

” means an arrangement which has a tax avoidance purpose.
For the purposes of subsection (13) an arrangement has a tax avoidance purpose if subsection (15) applies to a person who is a party to the arrangement.
This subsection applies to a person if the main purpose, or one of the main purposes, of the person in entering into the arrangement is the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions.
The following paragraphs apply for the purpose of determining whether any relevant step or any other step is connected with a tax avoidance arrangement—
the step is connected with a tax avoidance arrangement if (for example) the step is taken (wholly or partly) in pursuance of—
the tax avoidance arrangement, or
an arrangement at one end of a series of arrangements with the tax avoidance arrangement being at the other end, and
it does not matter if the person taking the step is unaware of the tax avoidance arrangement.
