Title.Addition: Treatment of relevant step for income tax purposes
Value of relevant step to count as employment income

Text.Addition: If this Chapter applies by reason of a relevant step, the value of the relevant step (see section 554Z3) counts as employment income of A in respect of A's employment with B—
if the relevant step is taken before A's employment with B starts, for the tax year in which the employment starts, or
otherwise, for the tax year in which the relevant step is taken.

Addition.Addition: But subsection (1) is subject to section 554Z2A (close companies).
Where the value of a relevant step would (apart from this subsection) count as employment income of more than one person—
the value of the relevant step is to be apportioned between each of those persons on a just and reasonable basis, and
subsection (1) applies as if the reference to the value of the relevant step in relation to A were a reference to so much of the value of the relevant step that is apportioned to A.

Text.Addition: If the relevant step gives rise to—
an amount which (apart from this subsection) would be treated as earnings of A under a provision of the benefits code, or
any income of A which (apart from this subsection) would be dealt with under Chapter 3 of Part 4 of

the net section 455 charge is nil.

the market value when the relevant step is taken of the asset which is the subject of the step, or

Earlier income tax liability: application of section 554Z11C
Section 554Z11C applies if the conditions in subsections (2) and (3) are met.
The first condition is that there is overlap between—
the sum of money or asset (“sum or asset P”) which is the subject of the relevant step, and

a sum of money or asset (“sum or asset Q”) by reference to which, on an occasion that occurred before the relevant step is taken, A became subject to a liability for income tax (“the earlier tax liability”).
The second condition is that at the time the relevant step is taken—
an amount is payable by a person (the “liable person”) in respect of the earlier tax liability, but the whole or part of that amount is unpaid and not otherwise accounted for, and
the liable person has not agreed any terms with an officer of Revenue and Customs for the discharge of the earlier tax liability.
For the purposes of this section there is overlap between sum or asset P and sum or asset Q so far as it is just and reasonable to conclude that—
they are the same sum of money or asset, or
sum or asset P directly, or indirectly, represents sum or asset Q.
the reference to A includes a reference to any person linked with A, and

This section applies in a case to which section 554Z11C applies (see section 554Z11B(1)).

if relevant, any of A's employment income by virtue of section 554Z2(1) is remitted to the United Kingdom on or after A's death.
But none of those subsections applies if A's employment with B never started before A's death.
In subsections (3) to (5) “
” means the relevant person (within the meaning of section 554C(1) or 554D(1) or (2)) in relation to the relevant step.
If the relevant person is A, A's personal representatives are liable for, as the case may be, the income tax on—
A's employment income by virtue of section 554Z2(1), or
so much of that income as is remitted.
If the relevant person is an individual other than A, the amount which, as the case may be—
counts as employment income of A, or
is remitted,
is to count as an amount of employment income of the relevant person for the tax year in which the relevant step is taken or the income is remitted.
If the relevant person is not an individual, the relevant taxable person is chargeable to income tax on the amount which, as the case may be—
counts as employment income of A, or
is remitted.
In subsection (5) “the relevant taxable person” is to be read as follows—
if the person (or any of the persons) who took the relevant step is
UK
resident, “the relevant taxable person” is the person (or each of the
UK
resident persons) who took the relevant step,
if paragraph (a) does not apply and B is still alive or in existence when the relevant step is taken, “the relevant taxable person” is B, or
if neither paragraph (a) nor paragraph (b) applies, “the relevant taxable person” is the non-UK resident person (or each of the non-UK resident persons) who took the relevant step.
For the purposes of subsection (5)—
the rate of tax is the rate applying for the purposes of section 394(2) (see section 394(4)) at the time of the relevant step or remittance of income, and
the tax is charged for the tax year in which the relevant step is taken or the income is remitted.
If there is more than one relevant person in relation to the relevant step, the amount which, as the case may be—
counts as employment income of A, or
is remitted,
is to be apportioned between the relevant persons on a just and reasonable basis with subsections (3) to (5) applying accordingly.

Addition.Addition: Section 554Z4A and section 554Z11A apply for the purposes of subsection (4) as for the purposes of section 554Z2 and section 554Z9(2) or 554Z10(2) respectively (reading references in sections 554Z4A and 554Z11A to “A” as references to “the relevant person”).
But those sections do not apply for the purposes of subsection (4) if the relevant person's temporary period of non-residence began before A died.

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
after the relevant step is taken, another event (“the later event”) occurs,
other than by virtue of—
this Chapter,
Chapters 2 to 5 of Part 7, or
Part 9,
the later event would (apart from this section) give rise to a liability for income tax of A or any other person on an amount (“
”), and
it is just and reasonable for this section to apply in order to avoid a double charge to income tax in respect of the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the relevant step.

So far as it is just and reasonable in order to avoid a double charge to income tax as mentioned in subsection (1)(c), there is to be no liability to income tax on the later amount by virtue of the later event.

Title.Addition: Relief where earmarking not followed by further relevant step

Text.Addition: An application for relief may be made by A (or, if A has died, A's personal representatives) to an officer of Revenue and Customs if—
this Chapter has applied by reason of a relevant step (“the original relevant step”) within section 554B taken by a person (“P”),
there occurs an event (“
”) which is not a relevant step in relation to a relevant sum or asset,
by reason of the relevant event no further relevant step is or will be taken by P or any other person in relation to any relevant sum or asset, and
there is no connection (direct or indirect) between the relevant event and a tax avoidance arrangement.
In section 554Z(15) the reference to the avoidance of tax includes (in particular) a reference to the avoidance of tax by way of obtaining relief under this section.
In subsection (1) “
” means—
the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the original relevant step, or
a sum of money or asset which (directly or indirectly) has arisen or derived, or may arise or derive, from the sum of money or asset mentioned in paragraph (a).
The application for relief must be made within four years from the time when the relevant event occurs.

If an officer of Revenue and Customs is satisfied that the requirements in subsection (1) are met, the officer must give such relief as the officer considers just and reasonable (if any) in respect of income tax paid on any previously charged amount.
In subsection (5) “
” means—
the amount which counted as employment income of A under this Chapter as a result of this Chapter applying by reason of the original relevant step, or
any amount treated by section 222 as earnings of A in relation to the notional payment (within the meaning of that section) which B is treated as having made by virtue of the original relevant step.

Subsection (8) applies if, by virtue of this Chapter having applied by reason of the original relevant step, any tax liability of A or any other person arising from another event is reduced (including to nil) by virtue of section 554Z5 or 554Z13 or otherwise.

In determining what is a just and reasonable amount of relief, the officer of Revenue and Customs must have regard (in particular) to the reduction in the tax liability and reduce the amount of relief which would otherwise have been given accordingly (including to nil).
The relief is to be given by repayment or otherwise as appropriate.
In relation to times after the relief is given, the Tax Acts have effect as if this Chapter had never applied by reason of the original relevant step.
The following provisions apply for the purposes of this Chapter—
section 38 (but as if references to general earnings were to the value of the relevant step or a part of it),
section 39(1) and (2),
section 40 (but as if in subsections (3) and (4) references to section 24(1)(b) were to section 554Z9(4)(b)), and
section 41 (but as if references to general earnings were to the value of the relevant step or a part of it).
This Chapter applies if there is an undertaking (“the relevant undertaking”) that a contribution to which subsection (2) would apply will be paid.
This subsection applies to a contribution if—
the contribution is paid to an arrangement which is not a registered pension scheme,
in connection with that arrangement (directly or indirectly), relevant benefits are to be provided (directly or indirectly) out of the contribution by a relevant third person,
the provision of the relevant benefits would be a relevant step, and
the contribution is neither a tax-relieved contribution nor tax-exempt provision.
In subsection (2)—
” has the same meaning as in Chapter 2 of Part 6, but ignoring section 393B(2)(a),
” means a person within section 554A(7)(a) to (c) (ignoring this Chapter), and
“tax-exempt provision” and “tax-relieved contribution” have the meaning given by paragraph 3(3) and (4) of Schedule 34 to FA 2004.
In this Chapter references to an undertaking include references to—
an undertaking which is not legally enforceable, and
an undertaking which is to be performed only on or following the meeting of a condition (including a condition which might never be met).

Title.Addition: to be treated as relevant third person

Text.Addition: If B takes a step within section 554Z18 or 554Z19, Chapters 1 and 2 have effect in relation to the step—
as if B were a relevant third person for the purposes of section 554A(1)(d), and
as if the step were a relevant step within section 554B (if it would not otherwise be).
For the purpose of determining whether Chapter 2 applies by reason of the step, Chapter 1 has effect—
as if sections 554F to 554O, 554S to 554U, 554W and 554X were omitted,
if the step is within section 554Z18, as if sections 554Q(2)(d), (3) and (4) and 554R(1)(c) and (d), (2) and (3) were omitted, and
if the step is within section 554Z19, as if sections 554Q and 554R were omitted.
If Chapter 2 applies by reason of the step, Chapter 2 has effect as if sections 554Z7 to 554Z12 were omitted.
If Chapter 2 does not apply by reason of the step by virtue of section 554E(3) or (6), section 554E(10) and (11) does not apply in relation to the step.
For further modifications of Chapters 1 and 2, see sections 554Z18(3) and (4), 554Z19(5) and (6), 554Z20 and 554Z21.
Regulations under section 554Y may (in particular) make provision covering cases in which Chapters 1 and 2 have effect as provided for by this section.
In this Chapter—
references to B do not include references to B acting as a trustee,
if B is a company and is a member of a group of companies, references to B are to be read as including references to any other company which is a member of that group, and

if B is a limited liability partnership, references to B are to be read as including references to any company which is a wholly-owned subsidiary (as defined in section 1159(2) of the Companies Act 2006) of B.
B takes a step within this section if—
a sum of money or asset held by or on behalf of B is earmarked (however informally) by B with a view to the relevant undertaking being performed at a later time (wholly or partly) out of—
that sum of money or asset, or
any sum of money or asset which may arise or derive (directly or indirectly) from it, or

a sum of money or asset otherwise starts being held by or on behalf of B, specifically with a view, so far as B is concerned, to the relevant undertaking being performed at a later time (wholly or partly) out of—
that sum of money or asset, or
any sum of money or asset which may arise or derive (directly or indirectly) from it.

For the purposes of subsection (1)(b) it does not matter whether or not the sum of money or asset in question has previously been held by or on behalf of B on a basis which is different to that mentioned in subsection (1)(b).
Subsection (4) applies if, in the application of section 554Q or 554R in any case, the relevant step mentioned in section 554Q(2)(a) or 554R(6)(a) is a step within this section taken by B.
In section 554Q(2)(c) or 554R(6)(c) (as the case may be) the reference to section 554B(1)(a) or (b) is to be read as a reference to subsection (1)(a) or (b) above.
B takes a step within this section if B provides security for the performance of the relevant undertaking.
For the purposes of this Part, the sum of money or asset which is the subject of the step is to be taken to be—
any sums of money which, as at the time the step is taken, are the subject of the security, and
any assets which, as at that time, are the subject of the security,
and references to the sum of money or asset which is the subject of a relevant step are to be read accordingly.

If, when the step is taken, the security covers other undertakings as well as the relevant undertaking, the sums of money and assets within subsection (2)(a) and (b) are to be apportioned between the relevant undertaking and the other undertakings on a just and reasonable basis.
Subsections (2) and (3) are subject to section 554Z20(7).
Section 554Q does not apply in any case in which the relevant step mentioned in section 554Q(2)(a) would be a step within this section taken by B.
Section 554R(6) does not apply in any case in which the relevant step mentioned in section 554R(6)(a) would be a step within this section taken by B.
In this Chapter references to providing security for the performance of an undertaking are references to providing such security in any way, however informal.
This section applies if, by virtue of section 554Z17, Chapter 2 applies by reason of a step taken by B within section 554Z19.
Section 554Z3 has effect as if subsections (3) and (4) below were substituted for subsections (1) to (6) of that section.
The value of the relevant step is—

the amount to be paid as a contribution under the relevant undertaking determined, as at the time the step is taken, on a just and reasonable basis assuming that any condition to be met before any payment is made will be met, or
if lower, the value of the security.
For the purposes of subsection (3)(b) the value of the security—
consists of—
the total amount of the sums of money included in the subject of the step (see section 554Z19(2)(a)), and
the total market value, as at the time the step is taken, of the assets included in the subject of the step (see section 554Z19(2)(b)), but

is to be subject to a just and reasonable reduction to take account of any term of the security which limits the total amount which may be made available under the security for the performance of the relevant undertaking to an amount which is lower than the amount determined under paragraph (a).

The following subsections apply if, as at the end of the day of an anniversary of the taking of the step (“the anniversary day”), B continues to provide the security for the performance of the relevant undertaking.
This Part has effect as if B's continuing to provide the security were a new step (“the anniversary step”) within section 554Z19—
which is taken by B at the end of the anniversary day, and
by reason of which Chapter 2 is to apply by virtue of section 554Z17 (subject only to section 554A(4)).

If the total amount of the sums of money which are the subject of the security (“the security sums”) varies from time to time, for the purpose of determining the sums of money included in the subject of the anniversary step, in section 554Z19(2)(a) the reference to the time the step is taken is to be read as a reference to the time during the preceding year at which the total amount of the security sums is at its highest.

For the purposes of subsection (4)(a)(ii) the market value of any asset included in the subject of the anniversary step may be determined as at any time during the preceding year (so long as the asset is the subject of the security, or one of the assets which is the subject of the security, as at that time).
In subsections (7) and (8) “
” means the year ending with the anniversary day.

Title.Addition: Relief for earmarking or security not followed by contribution or relevant benefit

Text.Addition: This section applies if, by virtue of section 554Z17, Chapter 2 applies by reason of a step taken by B within section 554Z18 or 554Z19.
Section 554Z14 has effect in relation to the step with the following modifications.
Subsection (1)(b) has effect as if for “not a relevant step in relation to a relevant sum or asset” there were substituted

InlineAmendment.Addition: “ neither the payment of the relevant contribution (or any part of it) nor the provision of any relevant benefit ”

Text.Addition: Subsection (1)(c) has effect as if for the words from “no further relevant step” to “any relevant sum or asset” there were substituted

InlineAmendment.Addition: “ the relevant contribution (or any part of it) will not be paid or a relevant benefit will not be provided ”

Text.Addition: Subsection (1) has effect as if subsection (6) below were substituted for subsection (3).
In subsection (1)—
” means the contribution to be paid under the relevant undertaking (within the meaning of Chapter 3), and
” means a relevant benefit to be provided out of the relevant contribution as mentioned in section 554Z16(2)(b) and (c).

P1group.Title: Former employee entitled to deduction in calculating net income

P2para.Text: This Part applies if—

P3para.Text: a former employee makes a deductible payment, or
a former employer makes a deductible payment on behalf of a former employee and the payment is treated—

P4para.Text: as a relevant retirement benefit, or
as post-employment earnings,

P3para.Text: of the former employee.

P2para.Text: A deduction of the amount of the deductible payment may be made in calculating the former employee's net income for the tax year in which the payment is made (see Step 2 of the calculation in section 23 of ITA 2007).
Subsection (2) applies only if the former employee makes a claim to the deduction.
The entitlement to a deduction under this section is subject to sections 556 and 557.
For the application of this Part in relation to former office-holders, see section 564.

Text.Substitution: See section 263ZA of
TCGA
1992 for relief from capital gains tax where the amount of the deduction allowed under this section exceeds the remaining total income (as defined in that section).

P1group.Title: Deductible payments made outside the time limits allowed

P2para.Text: No deduction may be made under section 555 if the deductible payment is made—

P3para.Text: on or before the day on which the former employee ceased to hold the former employment, or
after the end of the sixth tax year following the tax year in which the former employee ceased to hold the former employment.

P2para.Text: If subsection (1)(a) applies, see section 346 (deduction for employee liabilities).

Title.Addition: Deductible payments made pursuant to tax avoidance arrangements

Text.Addition: No deduction may be made under section 555 if the deductible payment is made in pursuance of arrangements the main purpose, or one of the main purposes, of which is the avoidance of tax.

P1group.Title: Deductible payments wholly or partly borne by the former employer etc.

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: a deductible payment is made by the former employee (and not by the former employer on behalf of the former employee), but
the whole or a part of the cost of making the payment is borne—

P4para.Text: by the former employer, or
out of the proceeds of a contract of insurance.

P2para.Text: No deduction of the amount of the cost borne as mentioned in subsection (1)(b) (the “relevant amount”) may be made under section 555.
But this is subject to subsection (4) if the whole or a part of the relevant amount is treated—

P3para.Text: as a relevant retirement benefit of the former employee, or
as post-employment earnings of the former employee.

P2para.Text: In such a case, a deduction of so much of the relevant amount as is treated in that way may be made under section 555.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “deductible payment”

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Part each of the following is a deductible payment—
A. Payment in or towards the discharge of a liability related to the former employment.
B. Payment of any costs or expenses incurred in connection with—

P3para.Text: a claim that the former employee is subject to a liability related to the former employment, or
proceedings relating to or arising out of a claim that the former employee is subject to a liability related to the former employment.

Text.Addition: BA Payment of any costs or expenses not falling within paragraph B which are incurred in connection with the former employee giving evidence about matters related to the former employment in, or for the purposes of—
a proceeding or other process (whether or not involving the former employee), or
an investigation (whether or not likely to lead to any proceeding or other process involving the former employee).
BB Payment of any costs or expenses not falling within paragraph B or BA which are incurred in connection with a proceeding or other process, or an investigation, in which—
acts of the former employee related to the former employment, or
any other matters related to the former employment,
are being or are likely to be considered.

P2para.Text: C. Payment of a premium under a qualifying insurance contract, but only to the extent that the premium relates to—

P3para.Text: provision in the contract for the former employee to be indemnified against a payment falling within paragraph A, or
provision in the contract for the payment of any costs or expenses falling within paragraph B , BA or BB .

P2para.Text: But a payment which falls within paragraph A B, BA or BB is not a deductible payment if it would have been unlawful for the former employer to enter into a contract of insurance in respect of the liability, or costs or expenses, in question.
In this Part—

P3para.Text: “premium”, in relation to a qualifying insurance contract, means an amount payable to the insurer under the contract, and

where a qualifying insurance contract relates to more than one person, employment or risk, the part of the premium to be treated as relating to each of them is to be determined by apportionment on a just and reasonable basis.

Text.Addition: In this section and section 560—
” includes failures to act and acts are “related to the former employment” if the former employee was acting—
in the employee's capacity as holder of the former employment, or
in any other capacity in which the former employee was acting in the performance of the duties of that employment,
” includes making a formal or informal statement or answering questions,
” includes any civil, criminal or arbitration proceedings, any disciplinary or regulatory proceedings of any kind and any process operated for resolving disputes or adjudicating on complaints, and
references to a proceeding or other process or an investigation include a reference to a proceeding or other process or an investigation that is likely to take place.

P1group.Title: Liabilities related to the former employment

P1para.Text: For the purposes of this Part each of the following kinds of liability is related to the former employment— A. Liability imposed upon the former employee because he did an act, or failed to do an act—

P3para.Text: in his capacity as holder of the former employment, or
in any other capacity in which he acted in the performance of the duties of the former employment.

P1para.Text: B. Liability imposed upon the former employee in connection with any proceedings relating to, or arising from, a claim that he is subject to a liability because he did an act, or failed to do an act—

P3para.Text: in his capacity as holder of the former employment, or
in any other capacity in which he acted in the performance of the duties of the former employment.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “qualifying insurance contract”

P2para.Text: In section 558 “qualifying insurance contract” means a contract of insurance which meets conditions A, B, C and D.
Condition A is that, so far as the risks insured against are concerned, the contract only relates to one or more of the following—

P3para.Text: the indemnification of a former employee against a liability related to the former employment,
the indemnification of a person against vicarious liability in respect of a liability related to another person’s employment,
the payment of costs or expenses incurred—

P4para.Text: in connection with a claim that a person is subject to a liability to which the insurance relates, or
in connection with any proceedings relating to or arising out of a claim that a person is subject to a liability to which the insurance relates,

Text.Addition: the payment of costs or expenses incurred in connection with a former employee giving evidence about matters related to the former employment in, or for the purposes of—
a proceeding or other process (whether or not involving the former employee), or
an investigation (whether or not likely to lead to any proceeding or other process involving the former employee).
the payment of any costs or expenses incurred in connection with a proceeding or other process, or an investigation, in which—
acts of a former employee related to the employment, or
any other matters related to the former employment of a former employee,
are being or are likely to be considered,

P3para.Text: the indemnification of an employer against loss from a payment made by the employer to a former employee in respect of—

P4para.Text: a liability related to the former employment, or
any costs or expenses incurred as mentioned in paragraph (c) , (ca) or (cb) .

P2para.Text: Condition B is that—

P3para.Text: the period of insurance under the contract does not exceed 2 years or, if it does, it does so only because of one or more renewals, each for a period of 2 years or less, and
the insured is not required to renew the contract for any period.

P2para.Text: Condition C is—

P3para.Text: that the insured is not entitled under the contract to receive any payment or other benefit in addition to—

P4para.Text: cover for the risks insured against, and
any right to renew the contract, or

P3para.Text: if the insured is so entitled, that the part of the premium reasonably attributable to the entitlement is not a significant part of the whole premium.

P2para.Text: Condition D is that the contract is not connected with another contract.

P1group.Title: Connected contracts

P2para.Text: An insurance contract is connected with another contract for the purposes of section 560 if conditions E and F are met—

P3para.Text: at the time when both contracts are first in force, or
at any time after that time.

P2para.Text: Condition E is that one of the contracts was entered into—

P3para.Text: by reference to the other, or
with a view to enabling or facilitating entry into the other on particular terms.

P2para.Text: Condition F is that the terms on which one of the contracts was entered into are significantly different from what they would have been if—

P3para.Text: it had not been entered into in anticipation of the other being entered into, or
the other had not also been entered into.

P2para.Text: If—

P3para.Text: there is only one such significant difference in terms, and
the contracts meet conditions A, B and C specified in section 560,

P2para.Text: the difference may be disregarded in the following cases.
The first case is where the difference is a reduction in premiums under the contract that is reasonably attributable only to the contract—

P3para.Text: containing a right to renew, or
being entered into by way of renewal.

P2para.Text: The second case is where—

P3para.Text: two or more contracts have been entered into as part of a single transaction, and

the difference is reductions in their premiums that are reasonably attributable only to the premium under each of them having been fixed by reference to the appropriate proportion of the combined premium.

P2para.Text: In subsection (6) “the combined premium” means the amount that would have been the total premium under a single contract relating to all the risks covered by the contracts.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “former employee” and “employment”

P2para.Text: In this Part “former employee” means an individual who has ceased to hold an employment.
In this Part “employment” includes in particular—

P3para.Text: any employment under a contract of service,
any employment under a contract of apprenticeship, and
any employment in the service of the Crown.
“Employee” and “employer” have corresponding meanings.

P1group.Title: Other interpretation

P1para.Text: In this Part each of the following expressions, when used in relation to a former employee, has the meaning given—

Para.Text: “former employment” means the employment which the former employee has ceased to hold;
“former employer” means—
the person under whom the former employee held the former employment,
a person for the time being carrying on the whole or any part of the business or other undertaking for the purposes of which the former employee held the former employment,
a person who is for the time being subject to any of the liabilities with respect to that business or other undertaking of the person mentioned in paragraph (a), and
a person who is connected with a person falling within paragraph (a), (b) or (c);

“post-employment earnings” means so much of any amount received after the former employee has ceased to hold the former employment as constitutes general earnings for the purposes of the employment income Parts;
“relevant retirement benefit” means a benefit—

Text.Substitution: which is received by the former employee under an employer-financed retirement benefits scheme, and
which, under Chapter 2 of Part 6, counts as employment income of the former employee.

P1group.Title: Application of this Part to office-holders

P2para.Text: The provisions of this Part are expressed to apply to former employees but they apply equally to former office-holders.
In those provisions as they apply to a former office-holder—

P3para.Text: references to holding a former employment are to holding the office;
“former employment” means the office held;
“former employer” means the person under whom the person held the office.

P2para.Text: In this Part “office” includes in particular any position which has an existence independent of the person who holds it and may be filled by successive holders.

P1group.Title: Structure of Part 9

P1para.Text: The structure of this Part is as follows— Chapter 2—

P3para.Text: imposes the charge to tax on pension income, and
provides for deductions to be made from the amount of income chargeable;

P1para.Text: Chapters 3 to 15 set out the types of income which are charged to tax under this Part and, for each type of income, identify—

P3para.Text: the amount of income chargeable to tax for a tax year, and
the person liable to pay any tax charged;

Text.Substitution: Chapter 15A—
provides for certain amounts paid under registered pension schemes in the form of lump sums to be subject to the charge to tax on pension income, and
deals with exemptions from the charge to tax (whether under this Part or any other provision) in relation to certain other amounts paid under registered pension schemes in the form of lump sums.

P1group.Title: Nature of charge to tax on pension income and relevant definitions

P2para.Text: The charge to tax on pension income under this Part is a charge to tax on that income excluding any exempt income.
“Pension income” means the pensions, annuities and income of other types to which the provisions listed in subsection (4) apply.
This definition applies for the purposes of the Tax Acts.
“Exempt income” means pension income on which no liability to income tax arises as a result of any provision of Chapters 15A to 18 of this Part.
This definition applies for the purposes of this Part.
These are the provisions referred to in subsection (2)—

tr.td: Annuities for the benefit of dependants
Annuities in recognition of another’s services
Certain overseas government pensions paid in the United Kingdom
The House of Commons Members' Fund

td.Addition: Pensions treated as arising from payment of pension commencement excess lump sums under registered pension schemes
Pensions treated as arising from payment of trivial commutation lump sums and winding-up lump sums under registered pension schemes
Pensions treated as arising from payment of trivial commutation lump sum death benefits

P1group.Title: Amount charged to tax

P2para.Text: The amount of pension income which is charged to tax under this Part for a particular tax year is as follows.
In relation to each pension, annuity or other item of pension income, the amount charged to tax is the “net taxable pension income” for the tax year.
The net taxable pension income for a pension, annuity or other item of pension income for a tax year is given by the formula—

Para.Text: where—
TPI means the amount of taxable pension income for that pension, annuity or item of pension income for that year (see subsection (4)), and
DPI means the total amount of any deductions allowed from the pension, annuity or item of pension income (see subsection (5)).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Act—

P3para.Text: the amount of taxable pension income for a pension, annuity or other item of pension income for a tax year is determined in accordance with Chapters 3 to 15A of this Part (which contain provisions relating to this amount for each type of pension income); and
in determining the amount of taxable pension income for a pension, annuity or other item of pension income, any exempt income is to be excluded.

P2para.Text: The deductions allowed from a pension, annuity or other item of pension income are those under—

Text.Addition: section 567A (deduction to avoid double taxation where Part 7A has applied to the source of the pension income);
section 567B (deduction where inheritance tax is paid in respect of pension death benefit);

Para.Text: section 617 (10% deduction from an overseas government pension to which section 615 applies);
Part 12 (payroll giving).

Title.Addition: Cases in which Part 7A has applied to source of pension income

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
for a tax year there is an amount (“amount TPI”) of taxable pension income for a pension, annuity or other item of pension income,

the pension, annuity or other item of pension income accrues or arises out of rights (“the relevant rights”) which represent, or have arisen or derived (directly or indirectly) from, a sum of money or asset which was the subject of a relevant step within the meaning of Part 7A, and
Chapter 2 of that Part applied by reason of the relevant step.
A deduction is allowed from amount TPI.
The amount of the deduction allowed is the amount (“amount EI”) which counted as employment income of A under Chapter 2 of Part 7A in relation to the relevant step (see section 554Z2(1)).
If amount EI exceeds amount TPI, the excess is to be carried forward to future tax years to be deducted under this section (when applicable) until all of amount EI has been deducted.

Subsection (6) applies if it is determined on a just and reasonable basis that the relevant rights represent, or have arisen or derived from, only part of the sum of money or asset which was the subject of the relevant step.
In subsection (3) the reference to the amount which counted as employment income is to be read as a reference to the corresponding proportion of that amount.

Title.Addition: Cases where inheritance tax is paid in respect of pension death benefit

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
there is an amount of taxable pension income (“amount TPI”) for a tax year for a pension, annuity or other item of pension income,
amount TPI reflects (to any extent) the payment to a person (“
”) of a benefit under a pension scheme on the death of a member of the scheme (“
the benefit is not an excluded benefit, and
at any time (whether before or after the benefit is paid)—
the beneficiary pays an amount of inheritance tax that is attributable to the value of the deceased’s notional pension property,
the deceased’s personal representatives pay an amount of inheritance tax that is so attributable and pass on the burden of that payment to the beneficiary, or
the scheme administrator pays (under section 226B of IHTA 1984) an amount of inheritance tax that is so attributable, and the payment meets the condition in subsection (2).
A payment of an amount of inheritance tax meets the condition in this subsection if (and so far as)—

in consequence of the payment, the scheme administrator makes an adjustment (under section 226B(5) of IHTA 1984) as a result of which the beneficiary’s entitlement to a benefit other than that mentioned in subsection (1) (“the other benefit”) is reduced, and
disregarding that reduction, the other benefit would not give rise to taxable pension income for any tax year.
A deduction is allowed from amount TPI equal to the lesser of—
the amount of inheritance tax paid as mentioned in subsection (1)(d)(i) or (ii), less so much (if any) of that inheritance tax as has been deducted under this subsection in an earlier tax year, and
so much of amount TPI as reflects the payment to the beneficiary of the benefit mentioned in subsection (1).
Where the deceased was under 75 on death, and the benefit mentioned in subsection (1) is a relevant lump sum death benefit, a deduction is allowed from amount TPI equal to the lesser of—

the amount of inheritance tax paid as mentioned in subsection (1)(d)(iii) so far as it meets the condition in subsection (2), less so much (if any) of that inheritance tax as has been deducted under this subsection in an earlier tax year, and
so much of amount TPI as reflects the payment to the beneficiary of the benefit mentioned in subsection (1).
Where a deduction is allowed under both of subsections (3) and (4), the deduction under subsection (4) is to be made first.
For the purposes of subsection (1)(d) the deceased’s personal representatives “pass on the burden” of a payment of inheritance tax to the beneficiary if—
the personal representatives pay a sum to the beneficiary out of the deceased’s estate that has been reduced by the amount of inheritance tax, or
the beneficiary reimburses the personal representatives that amount.
In this section—
” means the Inheritance Tax Act 1984;
” includes interest on inheritance tax;
” has the same meaning as in IHTA 1984;
” has the same meaning as in IHTA 1984;
” has the same meaning as in section 637S.

P1group.Title: Person liable for tax

P1para.Text: For the provision identifying which person is liable for any tax charged under this Part on a pension, annuity or other item of pension income, see Chapters 3 to 15A.

P1group.Title: United Kingdom pensions

P2para.Text: This section applies to any pension paid by or on behalf of a person who is in the United Kingdom.
But this section does not apply to a pension if any provision of Chapters 5 to 14 of this Part applies to it.
For pensions paid by or on behalf of a person who is outside the United Kingdom, see Chapter 4 of this Part.

P1group.Title: “Pension”: interpretation

P1para.Text: In this Chapter “pension” includes a pension which is paid voluntarily or is capable of being discontinued.

P1group.Title: Taxable pension income

P1para.Text: If section 569 applies, the taxable pension income for a tax year is the full amount of the pension accruing in that year irrespective of when any amount is actually paid.

P1group.Title: Person liable for tax

P1para.Text: If section 569 applies, the person liable for any tax charged under this Part is the person receiving or entitled to the pension.

Text.Addition: This section applies if an individual is temporarily non-resident.
Any pension within subsection (3) is to be treated for the purposes of section 571 as if it accrued in the period of return.
A pension is within this subsection if—
section 569 applies to it,
it is in the form of a lump sum,
it accrued in the temporary period of non-residence, and
ignoring this section—
it is not chargeable to tax under this Chapter, but
it would be so chargeable if the existence of any double taxation relief arrangements were disregarded.
Subsection (3)(d)(i) includes a case where the charge could be prevented by making a DTR claim, even if no claim is in fact made.

Nothing in any double taxation relief arrangements is to be read as preventing the individual from being chargeable to income tax in respect of any pension treated by virtue of this section as accruing in the period of return (or as preventing a charge to that tax from arising as a result).
Part 4 of Schedule 45 to FA 2013 (statutory residence test: anti-avoidance) explains—
when an individual is to be regarded as “temporarily non-resident”, and
what “the temporary period of non-residence” and “the period of return” mean.
In this section—
” means arrangements that have effect under section 2(1) of TIOPA 2010;
” means a claim for relief under section 6 of that Act.

P1group.Title: Foreign pensions

P2para.Text: This section applies to any pension paid by or on behalf of a person who is outside the United Kingdom to a person who is resident in the United Kingdom.
But this section does not apply to a pension if any provision of Chapters 5 to 14 of this Part applies to it.

Text.Addition: This section does not apply to pension within section 574(1)(ba) if—
the pension is paid in respect of a deceased member of a pension scheme who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of death, and
no pension payments to the person entitled to the pension were made before 6 April 2015 in respect of the deceased member out of any of the following—
the fund from which the pension is paid, and
any fund represented (to any extent) by that fund.
This section does not apply to pension within section 574(1)(bb) if the pension is paid in respect of a deceased individual who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of death.
Subsection (2A) is subject to subsection (2D).

This section does apply to pension within section 574(1)(ba) paid in respect of a deceased member of a pension scheme who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of death if the pension is paid in respect of sums or assets held for the purposes of the pension scheme under which the pension is paid (“
”) that would, if the paying scheme were a registered pension scheme, be sums or assets—
representing unused uncrystallised funds (within the meaning of paragraph 27E(4) and (5) of Schedule 28 to FA 2004) in the deceased member's case, and
designated on or after 6 April 2015 as available for the payment of dependants' drawdown pension or nominees' drawdown pension, but

not so designated before the end of the period of two years beginning with the earlier of the day on which the scheme manager of the paying scheme first knew of the member's death and the day on which the scheme manager could first reasonably have been expected to have known of it.
Chapter 17 of this Part provides exemptions for certain annuities (see sections 646D and 646E: certain beneficiaries' annuities purchased out of unused or drawdown funds).

See also paragraph 45A of Schedule 36 to FA 2004 (exemption in certain cases for payments on or after 6 April 2015 to beneficiaries under joint-life or similar annuities purchased before 6 April 2006).

P2para.Text: For pensions paid by or on behalf of a person who is in the United Kingdom, see Chapter 3 of this Part.

Text.Addition: This section also applies to a pension paid by or on behalf of a person who is outside the United Kingdom to a person who is not resident in the United Kingdom if—
the pension is a relevant lump sum paid under a pension scheme to that person in respect of a member of the scheme, and
the member is, or immediately before the member's death was, resident in the United Kingdom.

any nominees' income withdrawal paid to the person from a nominee's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of an arrangement relating to the person under a registered pension scheme,
any successors' income withdrawal paid to the person from a successor's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of an arrangement relating to the person under a registered pension scheme,

any payment to the person of a short-term annuity purchased using sums or assets out of a member's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of an arrangement relating to the person under a registered pension scheme,

any payment to the person of a dependants' short-term annuity purchased using sums or assets out of a dependant's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of an arrangement relating to the person under a registered pension scheme,

any payment to the person of a nominees' short-term annuity purchased using sums or assets out of a nominee's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of an arrangement relating to the person under a registered pension scheme,

any payment to the person of a successors' short-term annuity purchased using sums or assets out of a successor's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of an arrangement relating to the person under a registered pension scheme,

any uncrystallised funds pension lump sum paid to the person in respect of an arrangement relating to the person under a registered pension scheme, but only so far as section 579A applies in relation to the sum (see section 636A),

any income withdrawal, or dependants' income withdrawal, paid before 6 April 2015 to the person under a registered pension scheme in respect of an arrangement relating to the person under the scheme which at the time of the payment was an arrangement to which section 165(3A) or 167(2A) of FA 2004 applied (flexible drawdown arrangements),
any payment to the person of a lifetime annuity or dependants' annuity where—
the annuity is within paragraph 3(1A) or 17(1ZA), as the case may be, of Schedule 28 to FA 2004,

the terms of the contract under which the annuity is paid are such that there will or could be decreases in the amount of the annuity other than decreases from time to time allowed by regulations under paragraph 3(1)(d) or 17(1)(c), as the case may be, of Schedule 28 to FA 2004 (and any such regulations are to be treated as having effect for this purpose), and
the annuity is purchased using sums or assets held for the purposes of a registered pension scheme,
any payment to the person of a scheme pension, or dependants' scheme pension, under a money purchase arrangement under a registered pension scheme where—
the person first acquired an actual (rather than a prospective) right to receive the scheme pension on or after 6 April 2015,

when the person first acquired that actual right, fewer than 11 other individuals were entitled to the present payment of a scheme pension, or dependants' scheme pension, under the registered pension scheme, and
the scheme pension is not payable under an annuity contract treated under section 153(8) or (8A) of FA 2004 as having become a registered pension scheme

Addition.Substitution: Nothing in any double taxation relief arrangements is to be read as preventing the person from being chargeable to income tax in respect of any relevant withdrawal treated by virtue of this section as accruing in the period of return (or as preventing a charge to that tax from arising as a result).

when a person is to be regarded as “temporarily non-resident”, and

Title.Addition: Refund of overpaid inheritance tax treated as pension

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
an amount of inheritance tax that is attributable to the value of notional pension property of a deceased member of a registered pension scheme is paid,
some or all of the inheritance tax paid—
is repaid under section 241(1) of that Act to a person, other than a non-qualifying person, who is entitled to receive benefits under the scheme on the deceased’s death (a “beneficiary”), or
is repaid under that section to the deceased’s personal representatives and passed on by the personal representatives to a beneficiary,

in a case in which the payment of inheritance tax mentioned in paragraph (a) was made by the beneficiary or by the deceased’s personal representatives, a deduction is allowed under section 567B in respect of the payment, and
the deceased was aged 75 or over at the date of their death.
The relevant amount is treated for the purposes of this Part as though it were a pension paid under the registered pension scheme (and is treated as accruing in the tax year in which it is paid).
In subsection (2) “
” means—

in a case in which the payment of inheritance tax mentioned in subsection (1)(a) is made by the scheme administrator, the amount of the payment made to the beneficiary mentioned in subsection (1)(b)(i) or (ii);
in a case in which the payment of inheritance tax mentioned in subsection (1)(a) is made by a beneficiary or by the deceased’s personal representatives, the lesser of—
the amount of the payment made to the beneficiary mentioned in subsection (1)(b)(i) or (ii), and
the deduction allowed under section 567B in respect of the payment of inheritance tax mentioned in subsection (1)(a).
In this section—
” includes interest on inheritance tax;
” has the same meaning as in section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefit charge).

Substitution.Addition: “nominees' income withdrawal" has the meaning given by paragraph 27D of that Schedule;
“successors' income withdrawal" has the meaning given by paragraph 27J of Schedule 28 to FA 2004.

P2para.Text: This section applies to any annuity which was granted for consideration consisting in whole or in part of sums —

Text.Substitution: which, in the tax year 2012-13 or an earlier tax year, satisfied the conditions for relief under section 273 of ICTA or section 459 of ITA 2007 (obligatory contributions to secure an annuity for the benefit of dependants), or
which fall within subsection (3)

P2para.Text: But this section applies to an annuity which arises from a source outside the United Kingdom only if it is paid to a person resident in the United Kingdom.

Text.Addition: A sum falls within this subsection if—
in the tax year 2013-14 or a later tax year, the sum is paid by an individual, or is deducted from an individual's earnings, under an Act or the individual's terms and conditions of employment,
the sum is for the purpose of—
securing a deferred annuity after the individual's death for the individual's surviving spouse or civil partner, or
making provision after the individual's death for the individual's children, and
the individual—
is UK resident for the tax year in which the sum is paid or deducted, or
at any time in that tax year, falls within any of paragraphs (a) to (f) of section 460(3) of ITA 2007 (matters relating to residence).
Subsection (3)(a) does not cover contributions paid by a person under—
Part 1 of the Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992, or
Part 1 of the Social Security Contributions and Benefits (Northern Ireland) Act 1992.
In subsection (3)(a) “
” has the meaning given by section 62.

P1group.Title: Annuities under non-registered occupational pension schemes

P2para.Text: This section applies to—

P3para.Text: any annuity paid under an occupational pension scheme that is not a registered pension scheme, and
any annuity acquired using funds held for the purposes of such an occupational pension scheme.

P2para.Text: But this section applies to an annuity which arises from a source outside the United Kingdom only if it is paid to a person resident in the United Kingdom.
This section does not apply to an annuity to which Chapter 5A of this Part applies.

Text.Substitution: In this section “
” has the same meaning as in Part 4 of FA 2004 (see section 150(5) of that Act).

P1group.Title: Annuities in recognition of another’s services

P2para.Text: This section applies to any annuity purchased by any person in recognition of another person’s services in any office or employment.
But this section applies to an annuity which arises from a source outside the United Kingdom only if it is paid to a person resident in the United Kingdom.
This section does not apply to an annuity to which Chapter 5A of this Part applies.
For the purposes of this section “office” includes in particular any position which has an existence independent of the person who holds it and may be filled by successive holders.

Text.Addition: Chapter 17 of this Part provides exemptions for certain annuities (see sections 646B to 646E: certain beneficiaries' annuities purchased out of unused or drawdown funds).

See also paragraph 45A of Schedule 36 to FA 2004 (exemption in certain cases for payments on or after 6 April 2015 to beneficiaries under joint-life or similar annuities purchased before 6 April 2006).

P1group.Title: Taxable pension income: UK annuities

P2para.Text: The taxable pension income for an annuity to which section 609, 610 or 611 applies is determined in accordance with this section if the annuity arises from a source in the United Kingdom.
The taxable pension income for a tax year is the full amount of the annuity arising in that year.

P1group.Title: Taxable pension income: foreign annuities

P2para.Text: The taxable pension income for an annuity to which section 609, 610 or 611 applies is determined in accordance with this section if the annuity arises from a source outside the United Kingdom.
The taxable pension income for a tax year is the full amount of the annuity arising in the tax year, but subject to subsection (4).

Text.Substitution: The annuity is treated as relevant foreign income for the purposes of Chapters 2 and 3 of Part 8 of
(relevant foreign income: remittance basis and deductions and reliefs).
But if the annuity arises in the Republic of Ireland, section 839 of that Act (annual payments payable out of relevant foreign income) applies with the omission of

Substitution.Substitution: conditions B1 and B2 (and the reference to them in subsection (1))

Text.Substitution: and subsection (5)(a).
See also Chapter 4 of that Part (unremittable income).

P1group.Title: Person liable for tax

P1para.Text: If section 609, 610 or 611 applies, the person liable for any tax charged under this Part is the person receiving or entitled to the annuity.

Chapter.Title: Certain overseas government pensions paid in the UK

P1group.Title: Certain overseas government pensions paid in the United Kingdom

P2para.Text: This section applies to a pension if conditions A, B and C are met.
Condition A is that the pension—

P3para.Text: is payable—

P4para.Text: to a person who has been employed in overseas government service, or
to the widow, widower, surviving civil partner, child, relative or dependant of a person who has been employed in overseas government service, and

P3para.Text: is payable in respect of that service.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that the pension—

P3para.Text: is payable in the United Kingdom, and
is payable to a person who is resident in the United Kingdom.

P2para.Text: Condition C is that the pension is payable by or on behalf of the government of—

P3para.Text: a country which forms part of Her Majesty’s dominions,
any other country which is for the time being mentioned in Schedule 3 to the British Nationality Act 1981 (c. 61), or
any territory under Her Majesty’s protection.

P2para.Text: But condition C is not met if the pension is payable out of the public revenue of the United Kingdom or Northern Ireland.
In condition A the references to a person being employed in overseas government service are to the person being employed outside the United Kingdom—

P3para.Text: in the service of the Crown, or
in service under the government of a country or territory which falls within subsection (4).

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “pension” includes a pension which is paid voluntarily or is capable of being discontinued.

P1group.Title: Taxable pension income

P1para.Text: If section 615 applies, the taxable pension income for a tax year is the full amount of the pension accruing in that year irrespective of when any amount is actually paid.

P1group.Title: Deduction allowed from taxable pension income

P1para.Text: A deduction of 10% is allowed from an amount of taxable pension income determined under section 616 (see section 567).

P1group.Title: Person liable for tax

P1para.Text: If section 615 applies, the person liable for any tax charged under this Part is the person receiving or entitled to the pension.

P1group.Title: The House of Commons Members' Fund

P1para.Text: This section applies to any periodical payment granted out of—

P3para.Text: the House of Commons Members' Fund,
sums appropriated from that Fund, or
income from sums appropriated from that Fund.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “House of Commons Members' Fund”

P1para.Text: In this Chapter “House of Commons Members' Fund” means the fund with that name specified in section 1 of the House of Commons Members' Fund Act 2016.

P1group.Title: Taxable pension income

P1para.Text: If section 619 applies, the taxable pension income for a tax year is the total amount of the payments made in that year.

P1group.Title: Person liable for tax

P1para.Text: If section 619 applies, the person liable for any tax charged under this Part is the person receiving or entitled to the payments.
