Chapter.Title: Pre-1973 pensions paid under the Overseas Pensions Act 1973

P1group.Title: Pre-1973 pensions paid under the Overseas Pensions Act 1973

P2para.Text: This section applies to a pension if—

P3para.Text: it is paid under section 1 of OPA 1973 (whether or not paid out of a fund established under a scheme made under that section),
it is a pre-1973 pension, and
it is paid to—

P4para.Text: the original pensioner, or
the widow or widower of the original pensioner.

P2para.Text: But this section does not apply to a part of a pension which is paid because the Pensions (Increase) Act 1971 (c. 56) applies to it (and accordingly section 569 applies to that part of the pension).
Chapter 18 of this Part provides an exemption where a pension to which this section applies is paid to a person who is not resident in the United Kingdom (see sections 647 and 651).

P1group.Title: Interpretation

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter a person is the “original pensioner” in relation to a pension if—

P3para.Text: the pension is payable by virtue of the person’s service, and
the person retired from that service before 6th April 1973.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Chapter a pension is a “pre-1973 pension” if, immediately before 6th April 1973—

P3para.Text: the pension was payable to—

P4para.Text: the original pensioner, or
the widow or widower of the original pensioner, and

P3para.Text: that person was resident in the United Kingdom.

P1group.Title: Taxable pension income

P2para.Text: If section 629 applies, the taxable pension income for a tax year is the full amount of the pension income arising in the tax year .

Text.Substitution: The full amount of the pension income arising in the tax year is to be calculated on the basis that the pension is 90% of its actual amount.
The pension income is treated as relevant foreign income for the purposes of section 838 of that Act (expenses attributable to collection or payment of relevant foreign income).

P1group.Title: Person liable for tax

P1para.Text: If section 629 applies, the person liable for any tax charged under this Part is the person receiving or entitled to the pension.

P1group.Title: Voluntary annual payments

P2para.Text: This section applies to an annual payment which—

P3para.Text: is paid voluntarily, or
is capable of being discontinued,

P2para.Text: if conditions A and B are met.
Condition A is that the payment is paid to—

P3para.Text: a former employee or a former office-holder,
the widow or widower or surviving civil partner of a former employee or former office-holder, or
any child, relative or dependant of a former employee or a former office-holder.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that the payment is paid by or on behalf of—

P3para.Text: the person—

P4para.Text: who employed the former employee, or
under whom the former office-holder held the office, or

P3para.Text: the successors of that person.

P2para.Text: But this section applies to a payment which is paid by or on a behalf of a person who is outside the United Kingdom only if it is paid to a person resident in the United Kingdom.
In this section “office” includes in particular any position which has an existence independent of the person who holds it and may be filled by successive holders.

P1group.Title: Taxable pension income: UK voluntary annual payments

P2para.Text: The taxable pension income for payments to which section 633 applies is determined in accordance with this section if the payments are made by or on behalf of a person who is in the United Kingdom.
The taxable pension income for a tax year is the full amount of the payments accruing in that year irrespective of when any amount is actually paid.

P1group.Title: Taxable pension income: foreign voluntary annual payments

P2para.Text: The taxable pension income for payments to which section 633 applies is determined in accordance with this section if the payments are made by or on behalf of a person who is outside the United Kingdom.
The taxable pension income for a tax year is the full amount of the pension income arising in the tax year, but subject to subsection (4) .

Substitution.Substitution: The full amount of the pension income arising in the tax year

Text.Substitution: is treated as relevant foreign income for the purposes of Chapters 2 and 3 of Part 8 of
(relevant foreign income: remittance basis and deductions and reliefs).
But if that pension income arises in the Republic of Ireland, section 839 of that Act (annual payments payable out of relevant foreign income) applies with the omission of

Substitution.Substitution: conditions B1 and B2 (and the reference to them in subsection (1))

Text.Substitution: and subsection (5)(a).
See also Chapter 4 of that Part (unremittable income).

P1group.Title: Person liable for tax

P1para.Text: If section 633 applies, the person liable for any tax charged under this Part is the person receiving or entitled to the payment.

Title.Substitution: Lump sums under registered pension schemes
for certain lump sums under registered pension schemes
Trivial commutation and winding-up lump sums
Trivial commutation and winding-up lump sum death benefits

Text.Substitution: This Chapter makes provision about the income tax treatment of authorised lump sums and authorised lump sum death benefits.
In this Chapter—
” means a lump sum permitted by the lump sum rule in section 166 of FA 2004 to be paid by a registered pension scheme to a member of the scheme;
” means a lump sum death benefit permitted by the lump sum death benefit rule in section 168 of that Act to be paid by a registered pension scheme in respect of a member of the scheme.
Expressions used in this Chapter and Part 4 of FA 2004 (pensions etc) have the same meaning in this Chapter as in that Part.

Title.Substitution: Tax treatment of authorised lump sums

Text.Substitution: No liability to income tax arises on a pension commencement lump sum paid under a registered pension scheme.

A person to whom a pension commencement excess lump sum is paid under a registered pension scheme is treated as having taxable pension income for the tax year in which the payment is made equal to the amount of the lump sum.
Subject to subsections (2) and (4), no liability to income tax arises on a serious ill-health lump sum paid under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a serious ill-health lump sum is paid under a registered pension scheme to a member who (at the time of the payment) is under 75, and
the lump sum exceeds the permitted maximum,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the excess as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
In subsection (2) “
”, in relation to a serious ill-health lump sum paid to a member, means so much of the member’s lump sum and death benefit allowance as is available
entitled to the lump sum (see section 637S).

If a serious ill-health lump sum is paid under a registered pension scheme to a member who (at the time of the payment) is 75 or over, section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
Subject to subsection (2), where an uncrystallised funds pension lump sum is paid under a registered pension scheme—
no liability to income tax arises on 25% of the lump sum, and
section 579A (pensions) applies in relation to the remainder of the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
an uncrystallised funds pension lump sum is paid under a registered pension scheme, and
25% of the lump sum is an amount that exceeds the permitted maximum,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the excess as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
In subsection (2) “
”, in relation to an uncrystallised funds pension lump sum paid to a member, means the lower of the following amounts—
so much of the member’s lump sum allowance as is available
entitled to the lump sum (see section 637Q);
so much of the member’s lump sum and death benefit allowance as is available
entitled to the lump sum (see section 637S).

A short service refund lump paid under a registered pension scheme is subject to income tax in accordance with section 205 of FA 2004 (charge to tax on scheme administrator in respect of such a lump sum) but not otherwise.

Title.Substitution: Refund of excess contributions lump sums

Text.Substitution: No liability to income tax arises on a refund of excess contributions lump sum paid under a registered pension scheme.

Title.Substitution: Trivial commutation lump sums and winding-up lump sums

Text.Substitution: Subject to subsection (2), a member of a registered pension scheme to whom—
a trivial commutation lump sum, or
a winding-up lump sum,
is paid under the scheme is treated as having taxable pension income for the tax year in which the payment is made equal to the amount of the lump sum.
If, immediately before the lump sum is paid, the member has uncrystallised rights under any one or more arrangements under the pension scheme, the amount of the taxable pension income

Substitution.Addition: if all the member’s rights under the pension scheme are uncrystallised rights, is 75% of the lump sum, and

Text.Substitution: is reduced by the tax-free element (if any).
In subsection (2) “
” means 25% of the value of any uncrystallised rights extinguished by the lump sum.
In this section “
” has the same meaning as in section 212 of FA 2004; and the value for the purposes of this section of any uncrystallised rights is to be calculated in accordance with that section.

Title.Substitution: Tax treatment of authorised lump sum death benefits
Defined benefits lump sum death benefits

Text.Substitution: Subject to subsections (2) to (6), no liability to income tax arises on a defined benefits lump sum death benefit paid under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a defined benefits lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum exceeds the permitted maximum,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the excess as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a defined benefits lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is not paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum is paid to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a defined benefits lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is not paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum is paid to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
If a defined benefits lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If a defined benefits lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
In this section—
” has the same meaning as in section 206 of FA 2004;
”, in relation to a defined benefits lump sum death benefit paid in respect of a member, means so much of the member’s lump sum and death benefit allowance as is available
paid (see section 637S);
” means a person who is not a non-qualifying person;

” means the period of two years beginning with the day on which the scheme administrator of the scheme first knew of the member’s death or (if earlier) the day on which the scheme administrator could first reasonably have been expected to have known of it.

Title.Substitution: Pension protection lump sum death benefits

Text.Substitution: Subject to subsections (2), (3) and (4) no liability to income tax arises on a pension protection lump sum death benefit paid under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a pension protection lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75, and
the lump sum exceeds the permitted maximum,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the excess as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If a pension protection lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If a pension protection lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
In this section—
” has the same meaning as in section 206 of FA 2004;
”, in relation to a pension protection lump sum death benefit paid in respect of a member, means so much of the member’s lump sum and death benefit allowance as is available
paid (see section 637S);
” means a person who is not a non-qualifying person.

Title.Substitution: Uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefits

Text.Substitution: Subject to subsections (2) to (6), no liability to income tax arises on an uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefit paid under a registered pension scheme.
If—
an uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum exceeds the permitted maximum,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the excess as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
an uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is not paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum is paid to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
an uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is not paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum is paid to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
If an uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If an uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
In this section—
” has the same meaning as in section 206 of FA 2004;
”, in relation to an uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefit paid in respect of a member, means so much of the member’s lump sum and death benefit allowance as is available
paid (see section 637S);
” means a person who is not a non-qualifying person;

” means the period of two years beginning with the day on which the scheme administrator of the scheme first knew of the member’s death or (if earlier) the day on which the scheme administrator could first reasonably have been expected to have known of it.

Title.Substitution: Annuity protection lump sum death benefits

Text.Substitution: Subject to subsections (2), (3) and (4), no liability to income tax arises on an annuity protection lump sum death benefit paid under a registered pension scheme.
If—
an annuity protection lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75, and
the lump sum exceeds the permitted maximum,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the excess as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If an annuity protection lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If an annuity protection lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
In this section—
” has the same meaning as in section 206 of FA 2004;
”, in relation to an annuity protection lump sum death benefit paid in respect of a member, means so much of the member’s lump sum and death benefit allowance as is available
paid (see section 637S);
” means a person who is not a non-qualifying person.

Title.Substitution: Drawdown pension fund lump sum death benefits

Text.Substitution: Subject to subsections (2) to (6), no liability to income tax arises on a drawdown pension
lump sum death benefit paid under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a drawdown pension
lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum exceeds the permitted maximum,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the excess as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a drawdown pension
lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is not paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum is paid to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a drawdown pension
lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is not paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum is paid to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
If a drawdown pension
lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If a drawdown pension
lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
A reference in this section to a “
”, in relation to a drawdown pension

lump sum death benefit under paragraph 17(2) of Schedule 29 to FA 2004 (lump sum payable on death of dependant of deceased member), is a reference to the dependant on whose death the lump sum is payable.
In this section—
” has the same meaning as in section 206 of FA 2004;
”, in relation to a drawdown pension
lump sum death benefit paid in respect of a member, means so much of the member’s lump sum and death benefit allowance as is available
paid (see section 637S);
” means a person who is not a non-qualifying person;

” means the period of two years beginning with the day on which the scheme administrator of the scheme first knew of the member’s death or (if earlier) the day on which the scheme administrator could first reasonably have been expected to have known of it.

Title.Substitution: Flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefits

Text.Substitution: Subject to subsections (2) to (6), no liability to income tax arises on a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit paid under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum exceeds the permitted maximum,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the excess as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is not paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum is paid to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If—
a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid in respect of a member who, on death, is under 75,
the lump sum is not paid before the end of the relevant two year period, and
the lump sum is paid to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
If a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a qualifying person,
section 579A (pensions) applies to the lump sum as it applies to any pension under a registered pension scheme.
If a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit under a registered pension scheme is paid—
in respect of a member who, on death, is 75 or over, and
to a non-qualifying person,
the lump sum is subject to income tax under section 206 of FA 2004 (special lump sum death benefits charge on scheme administrator) but not otherwise.
A reference in this section to a “member”—

in relation to a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit under paragraph 17A(2) of Schedule 29 to FA 2004 (lump sum payable on death of dependant of deceased member), is a reference to the dependant on whose death the lump sum is payable;

in relation to a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit under paragraph 17A(3) or (4) of Schedule 29 to FA 2004 (lump sum payable on death of nominee or successor of deceased member), is a reference to the nominee or successor on whose death the lump sum is payable.
In this section—
” has the same meaning as in section 206 of FA 2004;
”, in relation to a flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefit paid in respect of a member, means so much of the member’s lump sum and death benefit allowance as is available
paid (see section 637S);
” means a person who is not a non-qualifying person;

” means the period of two years beginning with the day on which the scheme administrator of the scheme first knew of the member’s death or (if earlier) the day on which the scheme administrator could first reasonably have been expected to have known of it.

Title.Substitution: Trivial commutation lump sum death benefits

Text.Substitution: A person to whom a trivial commutation lump sum death benefit is paid under a registered pension scheme is treated as having taxable pension income for the tax year in which the payment is made equal to the amount of the lump sum.
An individual’s “lump sum allowance” is £268,275.

Title.Substitution: Availability of individual’s lump sum allowance

Text.Substitution: This section is about the availability of an individual’s lump sum allowance on the occurrence of a relevant benefit crystallisation event (“the current event”).
In this section—
”, in relation to an individual, means the individual becoming entitled to a relevant lump sum;
” means—
a pension commencement lump sum, or
an uncrystallised funds pension lump sum.
If no relevant benefit crystallisation event has occurred in relation to the individual before the current event, the whole of the individual’s lump sum allowance is available.
Otherwise, the amount of the individual’s lump sum allowance that is available is—
so much of that allowance as is left after deducting the previously-used amount, or
if none is left after deducting that amount, nil.

For this purpose “the previously-used amount” is the aggregate of the non-taxable amounts in relation to each relevant benefit crystallisation event that has occurred in relation to the individual before the current event.
In subsection (5) “
”, in relation to a relevant benefit crystallisation event, means so much (if any) of the relevant lump sum to which the event relates as

Substitution.Substitution: is not, by virtue of any provision of this Chapter, taxable pension income

Substitution.Addition: Where more than one relevant benefit crystallisation event occurs in relation to an individual on the same day, it is for the individual to decide the order in which they are to be treated as occurring for the purposes of this section.

Text.Substitution: A reference in this section to a relevant benefit crystallisation event is to a relevant benefit crystallisation event occurring on or after 6 April 2024.

For transitional provision under which the amount of an individual’s lump sum allowance available on the occurrence of a relevant benefit crystallisation event may be reduced as a result of events occurring before 6 April 2024, see paragraph 125 of Schedule 9 to FA 2024.

Title.Substitution: Individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance

Text.Substitution: An individual’s “lump sum and death benefit allowance” is £1,073,100.

Title.Substitution: Availability of individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance

Text.Substitution: This section is about the availability of an individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance on the occurrence of a relevant benefit crystallisation event (“the current event”).
In this section—
”, in relation to an individual, means—
the individual becoming entitled to a relevant lump sum, or
a person being paid a relevant lump sum death benefit in respect of the individual;
” means—
a pension commencement lump sum,
a serious ill-health lump sum, or
an uncrystallised funds pension lump sum;
” means any authorised lump sum death benefit other than—
a charity lump sum death benefit, or
a trivial commutation lump sum death benefit.
If no relevant benefit crystallisation event has occurred in relation to the individual before the current event, the whole of the individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance is available.
Otherwise, the amount of the individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance that is available is—
so much of that allowance as is left after deducting the previously-used amount, or
if none is left after deducting that amount, nil.

For this purpose “the previously-used amount” is the aggregate of the non-taxable amounts in relation to each relevant benefit crystallisation event that has occurred in relation to the individual before the current event.
In subsection (5) “
”, in relation to a relevant benefit crystallisation event, means so much (if any) of the relevant lump sum, or relevant lump sum death benefit, to which the event relates as

Substitution.Substitution: is not, by virtue of any provision of this Chapter, taxable pension income

Text.Substitution: Where more than one relevant benefit crystallisation event within subsection (2)(a)(i) occurs in relation to an individual on the same day, it is for the individual to decide the order in which they are to be treated as occurring for the purposes of this section.

Substitution.Addition: The individual’s decision under subsection (7), so far as it relates to events that are relevant benefit crystallisation events for the purposes of section 637Q, must be consistent with the individual’s decision under subsection (6A) of that section.

Text.Substitution: A reference in this section to a relevant benefit crystallisation event is to a relevant benefit crystallisation event occurring on or after 6 April 2024.

For transitional provision under which the amount of an individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance available on the occurrence of a relevant benefit crystallisation event may be reduced as a result of events occurring before 6 April 2024, see paragraph 126 of Schedule 9 to FA 2024.
For further transitional provision that may affect the operation of this section, see paragraph 20 of Schedule 36 to FA 2004 (pensions in payment before commencement of Part 4 of FA 2004).

Addition.Substitution: Availability of individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance where

Title.Addition: multiple lump sum death benefits paid

Text.Addition: This section applies where two or more relevant benefit crystallisation events within section 637S(2)(a)(ii) occur in relation to an individual.
The relevant benefit crystallisation events are to be treated for the purposes of section 637S as occurring simultaneously—
immediately before the individual’s death, and
immediately after any pension commencement lump sum to which the individual becomes entitled immediately before death by virtue of section 166(2) of FA 2004 (lump sum rule).

Addition.Substitution: The amount of the individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance that is available on the occurrence of any of the relevant benefit crystallisation events mentioned in subsection (1) is the relevant proportion of the undivided available amount.

” means the amount of the individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance that would, apart from that subsection (but after taking into account subsection (2)), be available on the occurrence of the relevant benefit crystallisation event in question.

Text.Addition: In subsection (3), “
” means—
where—
A is the amount of the lump sum death benefit the payment of which constitutes the relevant benefit crystallisation event in question;
B is the aggregate of the amounts of each lump sum death benefit the payment of which constitutes a relevant benefit crystallisation event mentioned in subsection (1).

Addition.Addition: Where any inheritance tax is attributable to the value of the individual’s notional pension property, references in subsection (4) to the amount of a lump sum death benefit are to its IHT-adjusted amount.
The “IHT-adjusted amount” of a lump sum death benefit paid to a person under a registered pension scheme is (subject to subsection (7)) the amount determined as follows —
Take the amount of the lump sum death benefit paid to the person.
Add the amount (if any) by which the person’s entitlement to the lump sum death benefit was reduced in consequence of an adjustment under section 226B(5) of IHTA 1984.
Deduct the amount (if any) of inheritance tax—
that is attributable to the value of the individual’s notional pension property in relation to the scheme, and
is, or at any time was, liable under section 200(1)(c) of IHTA 1984, or
would at any time have been liable under that provision if the tax had not previously been paid by another person.
If the result is a negative amount, the IHT-adjusted amount of the lump sum death benefit is nil.

Where more than one lump sum death benefit is paid to the person under the scheme, the amount to be deducted under Step 3 is the following proportion of the amount of inheritance tax identified in that Step—
” is the amount resulting from Step 2;
” is the aggregate of the amounts resulting from Step 2 in respect of each lump sum death benefit paid to the person under the scheme.
” has the same meaning as in IHTA 1984.

Title.Addition: Availability of individual’s allowances where lump sums or lump sum death benefits already paid by non-UK schemes

Text.Addition: Subsection (2) applies where—

a payment within paragraph 1(1)(a) or (b) of Schedule 34 to FA 2004 (non-UK schemes: application of certain charges and protections etc) is made (or treated by Part 4 of that Act as made) to or in respect of an individual, and
the payment, or any part of it, is treated by virtue of that Schedule as—
a pension commencement lump sum, or
an uncrystallised funds pension lump sum,
for the purposes of the member payment charges.

In determining under section 637Q (availability of individual’s lump sum allowance) the availability of the individual’s lump sum allowance on the occurrence of any subsequent relevant benefit crystallisation event, the payment, or part of the payment, mentioned in subsection (1)(b) is to be treated as a relevant lump sum within the meaning of that section.
Subsection (4) applies where—

a payment within paragraph 1(1)(a) or (b) of Schedule 34 to FA 2004 (non-UK schemes: application of certain charges and protections etc) is made (or treated by Part 4 of that Act as made) to or in respect of an individual, and
the payment, or any part of it, is treated by virtue of that Schedule as—
a pension commencement lump sum,
a serious ill-health lump sum,
an uncrystallised funds pension lump sum, or
any authorised lump sum death benefit, other than a charity lump sum death benefit or a trivial commutation lump sum death benefit,
for the purposes of the member payment charges.

In determining under section 637S (availability of individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance) the availability of the individual’s lump sum and death benefit allowance on the occurrence of any subsequent relevant benefit crystallisation event, the payment, or part of the payment, mentioned in subsection (3)(b) is to be treated as—
in a case within subsection (3)(b)(i) to (iii), a relevant lump sum within the meaning of that section;
in a case within subsection (3)(b)(iv), a relevant lump sum death benefit within the meaning of that section.

P1group.Title: Awards for bravery

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension or annuity if it is paid to the holder of an award for bravery in respect of the award.
In this section “award for bravery” means—

Para.Text: the Victoria Cross,
the George Cross,
the Albert Medal,
the Edward Medal,
the Military Cross,
the Distinguished Flying Cross,
the Distinguished Conduct Medal,
the Conspicuous Gallantry Medal,
the Distinguished Service Medal,
the Military Medal,
the Distinguished Flying Medal.

P1group.Title: Pensions in respect of death due to military or war service

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on these pensions and allowances—

P3para.Text: a pension or allowance payable by or on behalf of the Ministry of Defence under so much of instrument specified in subsection (2), as relates to death due to—

P4para.Text: service in the armed forces of the Crown,
wartime service in the merchant navy, or
war injuries;

P3para.Text: a pension or allowance—

P4para.Text: payable by the Ministry of Defence in respect of death due to peacetime service in the armed forces of the Crown before 3rd September 1939, and
payable at rates, and subject to conditions, similar to those of a pension within paragraph (a);

P3para.Text: a pension or allowance—

P4para.Text: payable under the law of a country other than the United Kingdom, and
of a character substantially similar to a pension within paragraph (a) or (b).

Defence (Local Defence Volunteers) Regulations 1940 (S.R. & O. 1940/748),
