P1group.Title: Exemption under section 639 where income withheld

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: an individual is entitled to both of the following—

P4para.Text: a pension or allowance mentioned in section 639 (“pension A”), and
any other pension or allowance (“pension B”), and

P3para.Text: the whole or a part of pension A is withheld because of the individual’s entitlement to pension B.

P2para.Text: In such a case, an amount of pension B equal to the withheld amount of pension A is treated for the purposes of section 639 as part of pension A.

Title.Addition: Lump sums provided under armed forces early departure scheme

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises on a lump sum provided under a scheme established by the Armed Forces Early Departure Payments Scheme Order 2005 (
S.I.

Addition.Addition: or the Armed Forces Early Departure Payments Scheme Regulations 2014 (

P1group.Title: Wounds and disability pensions

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on—

P3para.Text: a wounds pension granted to a member of the armed forces of the Crown;
retired pay of a disabled officer granted on account of medical unfitness attributable to or aggravated by service in the armed forces of the Crown;

a disablement or disability pension granted to a member of the armed forces of the Crown, other than a commissioned officer, on account of medical unfitness attributable to or aggravated by service in the armed forces of the Crown;

a disablement pension granted to a person who has been employed in the nursing services of any of the armed forces of the Crown on account of medical unfitness attributable to or aggravated by service in the armed forces of the Crown;
an injury or disablement pension payable under any War Risks Compensation Scheme for the Mercantile marine;
a pension—

P4para.Text: granted to a person on account of disablement, and
payable under any scheme made under section 3, 4 or 5 of the Pensions (Navy, Army, Air Force and Mercantile Marine) Act 1939 (c. 83).

Text.Addition: a benefit under a scheme established by an order under section 1(2) of the Armed Forces (Pensions and Compensation) Act 2004 payable to a person by reason of his illness or injury—
by way of a lump sum, or
following the termination of the person's service in the armed forces or reserve forces.

P2para.Text: But if the Secretary of State certifies that a pension or retired pay of a kind listed in subsection (1) is only partly attributable to disablement or disability, that subsection applies only to the part attributable to disablement or disability.

P1group.Title: Compensation for National-Socialist persecution

P1para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension or annuity which is payable under any special provision for victims of National-Socialist persecution which is made by the law of—

P3para.Text: the Federal Republic of Germany or any part of it, or
Austria.

Title.Addition: Netherlands Benefit Act for Victims of Persecution 1940-1945

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises on a pension, annuity, allowance or other payment provided in accordance with the provisions of the scheme established under the law of the Netherlands and known as

P1group.Title: Malawi, Trinidad and Tobago and Zambia government pensions

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on—

P3para.Text: a Malawi government pension,
a Trinidad and Tobago government pension, or
a Zambia government pension,

P2para.Text: if conditions A, B and C are met.
Condition A is that the pension is paid to—

P3para.Text: the original pensioner, or
the widow or widower or surviving civil partner of the original pensioner.

P2para.Text: Condition B is that the pension is now paid under section 1 of OPA 1973 (whether or not it is paid out of a fund established under a scheme made under that section).

Condition C is that, at the time the pension is paid, provision is made by double taxation relief arrangements which would exempt the pension from income tax in the United Kingdom if the pension were still paid by the relevant government (rather than under section 1 of OPA 1973).
Subsection (1) does not apply to any part of a pension which is paid because the Pensions (Increase) Act 1971 (c. 56) applies to it.
In this section—

Para.Text: “double taxation relief arrangements” means arrangements which have effect under section 2(1) of TIOPA 2010;
“Malawi government pension” means a pension payable by the government of Malawi for services rendered—
to the government of Malawi, or
to the government of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland,
in the discharge of government functions;

“Trinidad and Tobago government pension” means a pension payable by the government of Trinidad and Tobago for services rendered to the government of Trinidad and Tobago in the discharge of governmental functions;
“Zambia government pension” means a pension payable by the government of Zambia for services rendered—
to the government of Zambia,
to the government of Northern Rhodesia, or
to the government of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland,
in the discharge of governmental functions.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section a person is the “original pensioner” in relation to a pension if—

P3para.Text: the pension is payable by virtue of the person’s service, and
the person retired from that service before 6th April 1973.

P1group.Title: Pensions payable where employment ceased due to disablement

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on the exempt amount of a disablement pension.
For the purposes of this section a pension is a “disablement pension” if—

P3para.Text: the pension is payable because a person has ceased to hold an employment or office because of disablement, and
that disablement is attributable to—

P4para.Text: performance of the duties of the employment or office, or
war injuries.
But “disablement pension” does not include any pension to which section 579A applies.

P2para.Text: The exempt amount of a disablement pension is determined in accordance with the following steps.
Determine what pension would have been payable if—

P3para.Text: the person had ceased to hold the employment or office because of the disablement mentioned in subsection (2)(a), but
the disablement had not been attributable to—
performance of the duties of the employment or office, or
war injuries.

P2para.Text: If no pension would have been payable, the exempt amount is the amount of the disablement pension.
If a pension of a smaller amount than the disablement pension would have been payable, the exempt amount is the amount by which the disablement pension exceeds the smaller amount.
In any other case, the exempt amount is nil.
For the purposes of this section “office” includes in particular any position which has an existence independent of the person who holds it and may be filled by successive holders.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of a pension or annuity payment if or to the extent that—
were the payment an annual payment falling within Chapter 7 of Part 5 of
ITTOIA
2005, it would be exempt from income tax under section 735 of that Act (health and employment insurance payments), and
it meets conditions A and B.
Condition A is that the payments are made—
to a person (“
”) who made payments or contributions in respect of premiums under an insurance policy which another person took out wholly or partly for the pensioner's benefit, or
to the pensioner's
Condition B is that the payments are attributable on a just and reasonable basis to the payments or contributions in respect of premiums.

P1group.Title: Social security pensions: increases in respect of children

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a part of a social security pension which is attributable to an increase in respect of a child.
In this section “social security pension” means—

P3para.Text: any pension, benefit or allowance to which section 577 applies, and
any pension, benefit or allowance which—

P4para.Text: is payable under the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom, and
is substantially similar in character to a pension, benefit or allowance to which section 577 applies.

P1group.Title: Former miners etc: coal and allowances in lieu of coal

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on—

P3para.Text: the provision of coal or smokeless fuel—

P4para.Text: to a former colliery worker, or
to the widow or widower or surviving civil partner of a former colliery worker, or

P3para.Text: any allowance paid to such a person in lieu of such provision,

P2para.Text: if the condition in subsection (2) is met.
That condition is that the amount of coal or fuel provided or in respect of which the allowance is paid does not substantially exceed the amount reasonably required for personal use.
That condition is assumed to be met unless the contrary is shown.
In this section “former colliery worker” means—

P3para.Text: any person who has ceased to be employed as a coal miner, or
any other person who has ceased to be employed at or about a colliery otherwise than in clerical, administrative or technical work.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of foreign pension income of a consular officer or employee in the United Kingdom for a foreign state if—
Her Majesty by Order in Council directs that this section applies to the foreign state for the purpose of giving effect to a reciprocal arrangement with that state, and
the officer or employee meets conditions A to C.
Condition A is that the officer or employee is not—
a British citizen,
a British overseas territories citizen,
a British National (Overseas), or
a British Overseas citizen.

Condition B is that the officer or employee is not engaged in any trade, profession, vocation or employment in the United Kingdom, otherwise than as a consular officer or employee of the state in question.
Condition C is that the officer or employee—
is a permanent employee of that state, or
was not ordinarily resident in the United Kingdom immediately before becoming a consular officer or employee in the United Kingdom of that state.
In this section—
” includes any person employed for the purposes of the official business of a consular officer at—
any consulate,
any consular establishment, or
any other premises used for those purposes,
” means—
income to which section 573 or 629 applies, and
income arising from a source outside the United Kingdom to which section 609, 610, 611 or 633 applies; and
” has the same meaning as in section 302.
Section 302(5) to (7) apply to an Order under subsection (1) and the operation of this section as they apply to an Order under section 302(1) and the operation of section 302.

Title.Addition: Registered schemes: beneficiaries' annuities from unused funds

Text.Addition: The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to a dependants' annuity, or nominees' annuity, payable to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased member of a registered pension scheme who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death,
the member died on or after 3 December 2014,
either—
the annuity was purchased using unused drawdown funds or unused uncrystallised funds, or

the annuity was purchased using sums or assets transferred to an insurance company by another insurance company in consequence of an annuity that was payable to the person by that other company, and was a dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity (as the case may be) purchased as mentioned in sub-paragraph (i) or this sub-paragraph, ceasing to be payable,

in a case where the annuity is purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(i) and using (whether or not exclusively) unused uncrystallised funds, the person became entitled to it before the end of the period of two years beginning with the earlier of—
the day on which the scheme administrator first knew of the member's death, and
the day on which the scheme administrator could first reasonably have been expected to know of the death,

in a case where the annuity is purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(ii) and the prior annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(i) was purchased using (whether or not exclusively) unused uncrystallised funds, the person became entitled to that prior annuity before the end of the period of two years specified in paragraph (d),
no payment of the annuity is made before 6 April 2015, and
in a case where the annuity is purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(ii), no payment is made before 6 April 2015 of—
the prior annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(i), and
any other annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(ii) that is in the chain of annuities beginning with that prior annuity and ending with the annuity.
The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to a successor's annuity payable to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased member of a registered pension scheme,
it is paid on the subsequent death of a dependant, nominee or successor of the member (“
the beneficiary had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the beneficiary's death,
the beneficiary died on or after 3 December 2014,
either—
the annuity was purchased using undrawn funds, or

the annuity was purchased using sums or assets transferred to an insurance company by another insurance company in consequence of an annuity that was payable to the person by that other company, and was a successors' annuity purchased as mentioned in sub-paragraph (i) or this sub-paragraph, ceasing to be payable,
no payment of the annuity is made before 6 April 2015, and
in a case where the annuity is purchased as mentioned in paragraph (e)(ii), no payment is made before 6 April 2015 of—
the prior annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (e)(i), and
any other annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (e)(ii) that is in the chain of annuities beginning with that prior annuity and ending with the annuity.
The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to a dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity payable to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased member of a registered pension scheme who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death,
the member died on or after 3 December 2014,
the annuity—
was purchased together with a lifetime annuity payable to the member, or

was purchased using sums or assets transferred to an insurance company by another insurance company in consequence of an annuity that was payable to the person by that other company, and was a dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity (as the case may be) purchased as mentioned in sub-paragraph (i) or this sub-paragraph, ceasing to be payable,
no payment of the annuity is made before 6 April 2015, and
in a case where the annuity is purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(ii), no payment is made before 6 April 2015 of—
the prior annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(i), and
any other annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (c)(ii) that is in the chain of annuities beginning with that prior annuity and ending with the annuity.
The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to payments to a person of a lifetime annuity if—
the payments are payable to the person under pension rule 2 (see section 165 of FA 2004),
either—
a member of a registered pension scheme was entitled to be paid the annuity immediately before the member's death, or

the annuity was purchased using sums or assets transferred to an insurance company by another insurance company in consequence of an annuity to which there was entitlement as mentioned in sub-paragraph (i), or which was purchased as mentioned in this sub-paragraph, ceasing to be payable,
the member had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death,
the member died on or after 3 December 2014,
any payment of the annuity made before 6 April 2015 is made to the member, and
in a case where the annuity is one purchased as mentioned in paragraph (b)(ii), any payment made before 6 April 2015—
of the prior annuity to which there is entitlement as mentioned in paragraph (b)(i), or
of any other annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (b)(ii) that is in the chain of annuities beginning with that prior annuity and ending with the annuity,
is made to the member.
Paragraph 27E(3) to (5) of Schedule 28 to FA 2004 (meaning of “
” and “
”) apply for the purposes of subsection (1).
Paragraph 27FA(2) of Schedule 28 to FA 2004 (meaning of “undrawn funds”) applies for the purposes of subsection (2)(e).

For the purposes of subsection (3)(c), a dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity is purchased together with a lifetime annuity if the dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity (as the case may be) is related to the lifetime annuity, and paragraph 3(4A) and (4B) of Schedule 29 to FA 2004 (meaning of “related”) apply for the purposes of this subsection.
For the purposes of this section, a person becomes entitled to an annuity when the person first acquires an actual (rather than a prospective right) to receive the annuity.

Title.Addition: Registered schemes: beneficiaries' annuities from drawdown funds

Text.Addition: The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to a dependants' short-term annuity, nominees' short-term annuity, dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity paid to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased member of a registered pension scheme who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death,
the member died on or after 3 December 2014, and
the annuity was purchased using sums or assets out of the person's—
dependant's drawdown pension fund,
dependant's flexi-access drawdown fund, or
nominee's flexi-access drawdown fund,
in respect of a money purchase arrangement under a registered pension scheme.
The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to a successors' short-term annuity, or successors' annuity, paid to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased beneficiary of a deceased member of a registered pension scheme where the beneficiary had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the beneficiary's death,
the beneficiary died on or after 3 December 2014, and
the annuity was purchased using sums or assets out of the person's successor's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of a money purchase arrangement under a registered pension scheme,
and here “
” means dependant, nominee or successor.
Subsection (1) is subject to subsections (4) to (6).

Subsection (1) does not exempt payments on or after 6 April 2015 to a person of a dependants' short-term annuity, or dependants' annuity, payable in respect of a deceased member of a registered pension scheme and purchased using sums or assets out of the person's dependant's drawdown pension fund in respect of a money purchase arrangement under a registered pension scheme (“
”) if before 6 April 2015—
any payment of the annuity was made,
any payment was made of any other dependants' short-term annuity, or dependants' annuity, purchased using sums or assets out of—
the drawdown fund, or
any fund represented (to any extent) by the drawdown fund, or
any payment of dependants' income withdrawal was made from—
the drawdown fund, or
any fund represented (to any extent) by the drawdown fund.

Subsection (1) does not exempt payments to a person of a dependants' short-term annuity, or dependants' annuity, payable in respect of a deceased member of a registered pension scheme and purchased using sums or assets out of the person's dependant's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of a money purchase arrangement under a registered pension scheme (“
”) if—
any of the sums or assets that make up the new fund—
became newly-designated dependant funds under paragraph 22A(2)(b) of Schedule 28 to FA 2004 or as a result of the operation of any of paragraphs 22B to 22D of that Schedule, or
arise, or (directly or indirectly) derive, from any such newly-designated funds or from sums or assets that to any extent so arise or derive,
before 6 April 2015—
any payment of dependants' income withdrawal in respect of the deceased member was made to the person from, or
any payment in respect of the deceased member was made to the person of a dependants' short-term annuity, or dependants' annuity, purchased using sums or assets out of,
the person's dependant's drawdown pension fund in respect of a money purchase arrangement under a registered pension scheme, and
any of the sums or assets that made up that fund at the time of the payment make up, or are represented by sums or assets that to any extent make up, the new fund.
Where relevant unused uncrystallised funds—
are designated on or after 6 April 2015 as available for the payment of dependants' drawdown pension or nominees' drawdown pension, and

as a result of the designation make up (to any extent) a person's dependant's flexi-access drawdown fund or nominee's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of a money purchase arrangement under a registered pension scheme, but
are not so designated before the end of the relevant two-year period,

subsection (1) does not exempt payments to the person of a dependants' short-term annuity, nominees' short-term annuity, dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity if any of the sums or assets used to purchase the annuity represent, at the time of the purchase, the whole or any part of those relevant unused uncrystallised funds.
In this section “

”, in relation to relevant unused uncrystallised funds held for the purposes of a money purchase arrangement relating to a deceased individual under a registered pension scheme, means the period of two years beginning with the earlier of—
the day on which the scheme administrator first knew of the individual's death, and
the day on which the scheme administrator could first reasonably have been expected to know of it.

For the purposes of this section, sums or assets held after the death of a member of a registered pension scheme for the purposes of a money purchase arrangement relating to the member under the scheme are “relevant unused uncrystallised funds” if—
they are unused uncrystallised funds, and
the member had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death.
Paragraph 27E(4) and (5) of Schedule 28 to FA 2004 (meaning of “unused uncrystallised funds”) apply for the purposes of subsection (8)(a).

Title.Addition: Non-registered schemes: beneficiaries' annuities from unused funds

Text.Addition: The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to an annuity payable to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased member of an overseas pension scheme, or relevant non-UK scheme, who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death,
it would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by subsection (8), be a dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity,
the member died on or after 3 December 2014,
either—
the annuity was purchased using sums or assets that would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme, be unused drawdown funds or unused uncrystallised funds, or
the annuity was purchased using sums or assets transferred to an insurance company by another insurance company in consequence of an annuity—
that was payable to the person by that other insurance company,
that was purchased as mentioned in sub-paragraph (i) or this sub-paragraph, and
that would have been a dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity (as the case may be) if the scheme had been a registered pension scheme,
ceasing to be payable,
no payment of the annuity is made before 6 April 2015, and
in a case where the annuity is purchased as mentioned in paragraph (d)(ii), no payment is made before 6 April 2015 of—
the prior annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (d)(i), and
any other annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (d)(ii) that is in the chain of annuities beginning with that prior annuity and ending with the annuity.
The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to an annuity payable to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased member of an overseas pension scheme or relevant non-UK scheme,
it is paid on the subsequent death of an individual who would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme, be a dependant, nominee or successor of the member (“
it would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by subsection (8), be a successors' annuity,
the beneficiary had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the beneficiary's death,
the beneficiary died on or after 3 December 2014,
either—
the annuity was purchased using sums or assets that would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme, be undrawn funds, or
the annuity was purchased using sums or assets transferred to an insurance company by another insurance company in consequence of an annuity—
that was payable to the person by that other insurance company,
that was purchased as mentioned in sub-paragraph (i) or this sub-paragraph, and
that would have been a successors' annuity if the scheme had been a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by subsection (8),
ceasing to be payable,
no payment of the annuity is made before 6 April 2015, and
in a case where the annuity is purchased as mentioned in paragraph (f)(ii), no payment is made before 6 April 2015 of—
the prior annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (f)(i), and
any other annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (f)(ii) that is in the chain of annuities beginning with that prior annuity and ending with the annuity.
The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to an annuity payable to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased member of an overseas pension scheme, or relevant non-UK scheme, who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death,

it would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by subsection (8), be a dependants' annuity payable to a dependant of the member or a nominees' annuity payable to a nominee of the member,
the member died on or after 3 December 2014,
the annuity—

was purchased together with an annuity payable to the member that would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by subsection (8), have been a lifetime annuity, or
was purchased using sums or assets transferred to an insurance company by another insurance company in consequence of an annuity—
that was payable to the person by that other insurance company, and

that would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by subsection (8), have been a dependants' annuity or nominees' annuity (as the case may be) purchased as mentioned in sub-paragraph (i) or this sub-paragraph,
ceasing to be payable,
no payment of the annuity is made before 6 April 2015, and
in a case where the annuity is purchased as mentioned in paragraph (d)(ii), no payment is made before 6 April 2015 of—
the prior annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (d)(i), and
any other annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (d)(ii) that is in the chain of annuities beginning with that prior annuity and ending with the annuity.
The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to payments to a person of an annuity if—
either—
a member of an overseas pension scheme, or relevant non-UK scheme, was entitled to be paid the annuity immediately before the member's death, or

the annuity was purchased using sums or assets transferred to an insurance company by another insurance company in consequence of an annuity to which there was entitlement as mentioned in sub-paragraph (i), or which was purchased as mentioned in this sub-paragraph, ceasing to be payable,
the payments would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by subsection (8), be—
payments of a lifetime annuity, and
payable to the person under pension rule 2 (see section 165 of FA 2004),
the member had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death,
the member died on or after 3 December 2014,
any payment of the annuity made before 6 April 2015 is made to the member, and
in a case where the annuity is one purchased as mentioned in paragraph (a)(ii), any payment made before 6 April 2015—
of the prior annuity to which there is entitlement as mentioned in paragraph (a)(i), or
of any other annuity purchased as mentioned in paragraph (a)(ii) that is in the chain of annuities beginning with that prior annuity and ending with the annuity,
is made to the member.
Paragraph 27E(3) to (5) of Schedule 28 to FA 2004 (meaning of “
” and “
”) apply for the purposes of subsection (1).
Paragraph 27FA(2) of Schedule 28 to FA 2004 (meaning of “undrawn funds”) applies for the purposes of subsection (2)(f).
For the purposes of subsection (3)(d), an annuity is purchased together with another if they are purchased—
in the form of a joint life annuity, or
separately in circumstances in which the day on which the one is purchased is no earlier than seven days before, and no later than seven days after, the day on which the other is purchased.
In this section “
” means—
an insurance company as defined by section 275 of FA 2004, or
a person—
whose normal business includes the activity of providing annuities,
who carries on that activity in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom, and
whose carrying on of that activity in any particular country or territory outside the United Kingdom—
is regulated in that country or territory, or
is lawful under the law of that country or territory because it is regulated in another country or territory,

and for this purpose an activity is regulated in a country or territory if it is regulated by the government of that country or territory or by a body established under the law of that country or territory for the purpose of regulating the carrying-on of the activity.

Title.Addition: Non-registered schemes: beneficiaries' annuities from drawdown funds

Text.Addition: The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to an annuity paid to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased member of an overseas pension scheme, or a relevant non-UK scheme, who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the member's death,
the person would, if that scheme were a registered pension scheme, be a dependant or nominee of the member,

the annuity was purchased using sums or assets held for the purposes of a money purchase arrangement under an overseas pension scheme or relevant non-UK scheme, and those sums or assets would if that scheme were a registered pension scheme form the whole or part of the person's—
dependant's drawdown pension fund,
dependant's flexi-access drawdown fund, or
nominee's flexi-access drawdown fund,
in respect of the arrangement,

the annuity would, if the scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by section 646D(8), be a dependants' short-term annuity or dependants' annuity or (as the case may be) a nominees' short-term annuity or nominees' annuity, and
the member died on or after 3 December 2014.
The charge to tax under this Part does not apply to an annuity payable to a person if—
it is paid in respect of a deceased individual (“
”) who had not reached the age of 75 at the date of the beneficiary's death,
the beneficiary would have been a dependant, nominee or successor of a deceased member of an overseas pension scheme, or relevant non-UK scheme, if that scheme had been a registered pension scheme,
the person would, if that scheme were a registered pension scheme, be a successor of the member,

the annuity was purchased using sums or assets out of a fund held for the purposes of a money purchase arrangement under an overseas pension scheme or relevant non-UK scheme and would, if that scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by section 646D(8), be a successors' short-term annuity, or successors' annuity, purchased using sums or assets out of the person's successor's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of the arrangement, and
the beneficiary died on or after 3 December 2014.
Subsection (1) is subject to subsections (4) and (5).
Subsection (1) does not exempt payments on or after 6 April 2015 to a person of an annuity payable in respect of a deceased member of an overseas pension scheme, or relevant non-UK scheme, if—
the annuity is purchased using sums or assets held for the purposes of a money purchase arrangement under an overseas pension scheme or relevant non-UK scheme,

the annuity would, if that scheme were a registered pension scheme and if “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by section 646D(8), be a dependants' short-term annuity or dependants' annuity,

the annuity was purchased using sums or assets out of a fund that would, if that scheme were a registered pension scheme, be the person's dependant's drawdown pension fund in respect of the arrangement (“
”), and
before 6 April 2015—
any payment of the annuity was made,
any payment was made to the person of any other annuity purchased using sums or assets out of the drawdown fund or out of any fund represented (to any extent) by the drawdown fund, or

any payment was made to the person out of the drawdown fund, or out of any fund represented (to any extent) by the drawdown fund, of any pension that would be dependants' income withdrawal if the fund concerned were held for the purposes of a registered pension scheme.
Subsection (1) does not exempt payments to a person of an annuity payable in respect of a deceased member of an overseas pension scheme, or relevant non-UK scheme, if—

the annuity was purchased using sums or assets held for the purposes of a money purchase arrangement under an overseas pension scheme or relevant non-UK scheme and would, if that scheme were a registered pension scheme and “insurance company” in Part 4 of FA 2004 had the meaning given by section 646D(8), be a dependants' short-term annuity or dependants' annuity,
the annuity was purchased using sums or assets out of a fund (“
”) that would, if that scheme were a registered pension scheme, be the person's dependant's flexi-access drawdown fund in respect of the arrangement,
before 6 April 2015—

any payment of pension in respect of the deceased member was made to the person from a fund held for the purposes of a money purchase arrangement under an overseas pension scheme, or relevant non-UK scheme, that would be a payment of dependants' income withdrawal from the person's dependant's drawdown pension fund in respect of the arrangement if the scheme were a registered pension scheme, or

any payment in respect of the deceased member was made to the person of an annuity purchased using sums or assets out of a fund held for the purposes of a money purchase arrangement under an overseas pension scheme, or relevant non-UK scheme, that would be a payment of a dependants' short-term annuity, or dependants' annuity, purchased using sums or assets out of the person's dependant's drawdown pension fund in respect of the arrangement if the scheme were a registered pension scheme, and
any of the sums or assets that made up the fund mentioned in paragraph (c)(i) or (ii) make up, or are represented by sums or assets that to any extent make up, the new fund.
In sections 646B to 646E, an expression listed in the first column of the table has the meaning given by the provision of FA 2004 listed against that expression in the second column of the table.

P1group.Title: Introduction and meaning of “foreign residence condition” etc.

P2para.Text: The provisions of this Part provide that no liability to income tax arises on certain kinds of pensions if the foreign residence condition is met.
The foreign residence condition is met in relation to a pension if the pension is payable to a person who is not resident in the United Kingdom.
For the purposes of the foreign residence condition, a person is taken to be not resident in the United Kingdom only if—

P3para.Text: a person makes a claim to the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs that the person is not resident, and
the Commissioners are satisfied that the person is not resident.

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “pension” includes—

P3para.Text: a gratuity or any sum payable on or in respect of death,
a return of contributions, and
any interest or other addition included in a return of contributions.

P1group.Title: The Central African Pension Fund

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension which is paid from the Central African Pension Fund if the foreign residence condition is met.

In this section “the Central African Pension Fund” means the fund established under that name by section 24 of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland (Dissolution) Order in Council 1963 (S.I. 1963/2085).

P1group.Title: Commonwealth government pensions

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension paid out of a fund which is established—

P3para.Text: in the United Kingdom,
by a Commonwealth government,
for the sole purpose of providing pensions payable in respect of service under that government,

P2para.Text: if the foreign residence condition is met.
In this section “Commonwealth government” means—

P3para.Text: the government of a territory or country mentioned in subsection (3),
the government of any part of a territory or country mentioned in subsection (3), or
a government constituted for two or more of the territories or countries mentioned in subsection (3).

P2para.Text: The territories and countries referred to in subsection (2) are—

P3para.Text: a country mentioned in Schedule 3 to the British Nationality Act 1981 (c. 61) apart from Australia, Canada, New Zealand, India, Sri Lanka and Cyprus,
an associated state,
a British overseas territory,
a protectorate,
a protected state, and
a United Kingdom trust territory.

P2para.Text: In subsection (2)(c) the reference to a government constituted for two or more of the territories or countries mentioned in subsection (3) includes a reference to any authority established for the purpose of providing or administering services which are common to, or relate to matters of common interest to, two or more of those territories or countries.
In subsection (3)(f) “United Kingdom trust territory” means a territory administered by the government of the United Kingdom under the trusteeship system of the United Nations.

P1group.Title: Oversea Superannuation Scheme

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension which is paid under the Oversea Superannuation Scheme (formerly known as the Colonial Superannuation Scheme) if the foreign residence condition is met.
For the purposes of subsection (1) a pension is paid under the Oversea Superannuation Scheme if—

P3para.Text: the pension is paid under the Scheme as it has effect (by reason of section 2(4A) of OPA 1973) as a scheme under section 2 of OPA 1973, or
the pension is paid under a scheme which—

P4para.Text: the Secretary of State has made under section 2(1) of OPA 1973, and
corresponds to the Oversea Superannuation Scheme.

P1group.Title: Overseas Pensions Act 1973

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension which is paid under section 1 of OPA 1973 if the foreign residence condition is met.
Subsection (1) applies whether or not the pension is paid out of a fund established under a scheme made under section 1 of OPA 1973.
But subsection (1) does not apply to any part of a pension paid because the Pensions (Increase) Acts apply to it.
In this section “the Pensions (Increase) Acts” means—

P3para.Text: the Pensions (Increase) Act 1971 (c. 56), and
any Act passed after that Act for purposes which correspond to the purposes of that Act.

P1group.Title: Overseas Service Act 1958

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension—

P3para.Text: which is paid under the authority of the Overseas Service Act 1958 (c. 14), and
which the Secretary of State certifies to be attributable to the employment of a person in the public services of an overseas territory,

P2para.Text: if the foreign residence condition is met.

If the Secretary of State certifies that only part of a pension paid under the authority of the 1958 Act is attributable to the employment of a person in the public services of an overseas territory, subsection (1) applies only to that part of the pension.
For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2) a pension is paid under the authority of the 1958 Act if condition A or B is met.
Condition A is that the pension is paid under either of the following—

P3para.Text: an order made under section 2 of the 1958 Act, or
section 4(2) of the 1958 Act,

P2para.Text: as it has effect (by reason of section 2(3) of OPA 1973) as a scheme under section 2 of OPA 1973.
Condition B is that the pension is paid under a scheme which the Secretary of State—

P3para.Text: has made under section 2(1) of OPA 1973, and
has certified to correspond to—

P4para.Text: an order made under section 2 of the 1958 Act, or
section 4(2) of the 1958 Act.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section, a person is taken to be employed in the public service of an overseas territory at any time when—

P3para.Text: the person is employed in any capacity under the government of that territory, or under any municipal or other local authority in it,

the person is employed in circumstances not falling within paragraph (a), by a body corporate established for any public purpose in that territory by an enactment of a legislature empowered to make laws for that territory, or
the person is the holder of a public office in that territory in circumstances not falling within paragraph (a) or (b).

P2para.Text: In subsection (6) references to the government of an overseas territory include references to—

P3para.Text: a government constituted for two or more overseas territories, and
any authority established for the purpose of providing or administering services which are common to, or relate to matters of common interest to, two or more such territories.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “the 1958 Act” means the Overseas Service Act 1958 (c. 14);
“certified” means certified for the purposes of ICTA 1970, ICTA or this Act.

P1group.Title: Overseas Service Pensions Fund

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension which is paid out of the Overseas Service Pensions Fund if the foreign residence condition is met.
In this section “the Overseas Service Pensions Fund” means the fund with that name established under section 7(1) of the Overseas Aid Act 1966 (c. 21).
In this section “pension” includes not only the things mentioned in section 647(4) but also any sum payable in respect of ill-health.

P1group.Title: The Pensions (India, Pakistan and Burma) Act 1955

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a pension paid under the authority of the Pensions (India, Pakistan and Burma) Act 1955 (c. 22) if the foreign residence condition is met.
A pension is paid under the authority of the 1955 Act if—

P3para.Text: the pension is paid under the 1955 Act as it has effect (by reason of section 2(3) of OPA 1973) as a scheme under section 2 of OPA 1973, or
the pension is paid under a scheme which the Secretary of State—

P4para.Text: has made under section 2(1) of OPA 1973, and
has certified to correspond to the provision made under the 1955 Act.

P2para.Text: This section does not apply to any part of a pension paid because the Pensions (Increase) Acts apply to it.
In this section—

Para.Text: “the 1955 Act” means the Pensions (India, Pakistan and Burma) Act 1955 (c. 22);
“certified” means certified for the purposes of ICTA 1970, ICTA or this Act;
“the Pensions (Increase) Acts” means—
the Pensions (Increase) Act 1971 (c. 56), and
any Act passed after that Act for purposes which correspond to the purposes of that Act.

P1group.Title: Structure of Part 10

P2para.Text: The structure of this Part is as follows—
Chapter 2—

P3para.Text: imposes the charge to tax on social security income, and
provides for deductions to be made from the amount of income chargeable;

P2para.Text: Chapter 3 sets out the UK social security benefits which are charged to tax under this Part and identifies—

P3para.Text: the amount of income chargeable to tax for a tax year, and

P2para.Text: Chapters 4 and 5 deal with exemptions from the charge to tax on UK social security benefits (whether under this Part or any other provision);
Chapters 6 and 7 make provision about foreign benefits.

Text.Addition: Chapter 8 makes provision for the high income child benefit charge.
Chapter 9 makes provision for the winter fuel payment charge.

P2para.Text: For other provisions about the taxation of social security benefits, see—

Para.Text: section 151 of FA 1996 (power for the Treasury to make orders about the taxation of benefits payable under Government pilot schemes);

Text.Substitution: section 781 of ITTOIA 2005 (exemption from income tax for payments under New Deal 50plus);
section 782 of ITTOIA 2005 (exemption from income tax for payments under employment zone programmes);

Text.Addition: section 44 of FA 2016 (tax treatment of supplementary welfare payments: Northern Ireland);
section 13 of FA 2020 (power to exempt social security benefits from income tax)
section 27 of F(No. 2)A 2023 (power to clarify tax treatment of devolved social security benefits).

P2para.Text: For the charge to tax on social security pensions, see Part 9 (pension income).

P1group.Title: Nature of charge to tax on social security income

P2para.Text: The charge to tax on social security income is a charge to tax on that income excluding any exempt income.
“Exempt income” is social security income on which no liability to income tax arises as a result of any provision of Chapter 4, 5 or 7 of this Part.
This definition applies for the purposes of this Part.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “social security income”, “taxable benefits” etc.

P2para.Text: This section defines—

Para.Text: “social security income” for the purposes of the Tax Acts, and
“taxable benefits”, “Table A” and “Table B” for the purposes of this Part.

P2para.Text: “Social security income” means—

P3para.Text: the United Kingdom social security benefits listed in Table A,
the United Kingdom social security benefits listed in Table B,
the foreign benefits to which section 678 applies, and
the foreign benefits to which section 681(2) applies.

P2para.Text: “Taxable benefits” means—

P3para.Text: the United Kingdom social security benefits listed in Table A, and
the foreign benefits to which section 678 applies.

P2para.Text: Subsections (2) and (3) are subject to section 660(2).
“Table A” means Table A in section 660.
“Table B” means Table B in section 677.

P1group.Title: Amount charged to tax

P2para.Text: The amount of social security income which is charged to tax under this Part for a particular tax year is as follows.
In relation to a taxable benefit, the amount charged to tax is the net taxable social security income for the tax year.
The net taxable social security income for a taxable benefit for a tax year is given by the formula—

Para.Text: where—
TSSI means the amount of taxable social security income for that benefit for that year (see subsections (4) to (7)), and
PGD means the amount of the deduction (if any) allowed from the benefit under Part 12 (payroll giving).

P2para.Text: In relation to bereavement allowance, carer’s allowance, carer's allowance supplement, carer support payment, contributory employment and support allowance, incapacity benefit, income support, Scottish Carer Supplement, welfare supplementary payments payable pursuant to the loss of contributory employment and support allowance and welfare supplementary payments payable pursuant to the loss of, or a reduction in the amount payable of, income support (which are listed in Table A), the amount of taxable social security income is determined in accordance with section 661.
In relation to any other benefit listed in Table A, the amount of taxable social security income is the amount of the benefit that falls to be charged to tax.
In relation to foreign benefits to which section 678 applies, the amount of taxable social security income is determined in accordance with section 679.
In determining for the purposes of this Act the amount of taxable social security income, any exempt income is to be excluded.

Chapter.Title: Taxable UK social security benefits: exemptions

P1group.Title: Long-term incapacity benefit: previous entitlement to invalidity benefit

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on long-term incapacity benefit if—

P3para.Text: a person is entitled to the benefit for a day of incapacity for work which falls in a period of incapacity for work which is treated for the purposes of that benefit as having begun before 13th April 1995, and
the part of that period which is treated as having fallen before that date includes a day for which that person was entitled to invalidity benefit.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “invalidity benefit” means invalidity benefit under—
Part 2 of SSCBA 1992, or
Part 2 of SSCB(NI)A 1992;
“long-term incapacity benefit” means incapacity benefit payable under—
section 30A(5), 40 or 41 of SSCBA 1992, or
section 30A(5), 40 or 41 of SSCB(NI)A 1992.

P1group.Title: Short-term incapacity benefit not payable at the higher rate

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on short-term incapacity benefit unless it is payable at the higher rate.
In this section—

P3para.Text: “short-term incapacity benefit” means incapacity benefit payable under—

P4para.Text: section 30A(1) of SSCBA 1992, or
section 30A(1) of SSCB(NI)A 1992;

P3para.Text: the reference to short-term incapacity benefit payable at the higher rate is to be construed in accordance with—

P4para.Text: section 30B of SSCBA 1992, or
section 30B of SSCB(NI)A 1992.

Title.Emphasis: Income support and relevant welfare supplementary payments

Title.Substitution: Exempt unless payable to a person involved in a trade dispute

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on income support unless—

P3para.Text: the income support is payable to one member of a ... couple (“the claimant”), and
section 126 of SSCBA 1992 or section 125 of SSCB(NI)A 1992 (trade disputes) applies to the claimant but not to the other member of the couple.

P2para.Text: In this section “couple” has the same meaning as in section 137(1) of SSCBA 1992 or section 133(1) of SSCB(NI)A 1992.

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises on a relevant welfare supplementary payment unless the whole or part of the payment relates to a period in which the claimant was prevented from being entitled to jobseeker’s allowance by–
section 14 of the Jobseekers Act 1995 (trade disputes), or
Article 16 of the Jobseekers (Northern Ireland) Order 1995 (trade disputes)
or would have been so prevented if otherwise entitled to that benefit.
Where part of a relevant welfare supplementary payment relates to such a period no liability to income tax arises on the part that does not relate to such a period.

P1group.Title: Child maintenance bonus

P1para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a part of income support which is attributable to a child maintenance bonus (within the meaning of section 10 of CSA 1995 or Article 4 of CS(NI)O 1995).

P1group.Title: Amounts in excess of taxable maximum

P2para.Text: If the amount of income support and relevant welfare supplementary payments paid to a person (“the claimant”) for a week or a part of a week exceeds the claimant’s taxable maximum for that period, no liability to income tax arises on the excess.

Text.Substitution: The claimant’s taxable maximum for a period is determined–
under section 668(1), (2) and (3) where the claimant is a member of a couple, and
under section 668(2A) and (3) where the claimant is not a member of a couple.

P1group.Title: Taxable maximum

P2para.Text: A claimant’s taxable maximum for a week is determined under this subsection if the applicable amount for the purpose of calculating the income support consists only of an amount in respect of the relevant couple.
The taxable maximum is equal to one half of the applicable amount.
A claimant’s taxable maximum for a week is determined under this subsection if the applicable amount includes amounts that are not in respect of the relevant couple.
The taxable maximum is equal to one half of the amount which is included in the applicable amount in respect of the relevant couple.

Text.Addition: A claimant’s taxable maximum for a week is determined under this subsection if the claimant is not a member of a couple.
The taxable maximum is equal to the applicable amount.

P2para.Text: A claimant’s taxable maximum for a part of a week is determined as follows—
Assume that the income support is paid to the claimant for the whole of, rather than part of, the week.
Determine under subsection (1) or (2) what the claimant’s taxable maximum for that week would be on that assumption.
Determine the claimant’s taxable maximum for the part of the week using this formula—

Para.Text: where—
N is the number of days in the part of the week for which the claimant is actually paid the income support, and
TMW is the taxable maximum for the whole week determined under step 2.

regulation 4 , 5 or 6 of WSP(LDRP)R(NI) 2016.

Title.Emphasis: Jobseeker’s allowance and relevant welfare supplementary payments

P1group.Title: Child maintenance bonus

P1para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a part of a jobseeker’s allowance which is attributable to a child maintenance bonus (within the meaning of section 10 of CSA 1995 or Article 4 of CS(NI)O 1995).

P1group.Title: Amounts in excess of taxable maximum

P2para.Text: If the amount of jobseeker’s allowance and relevant welfare supplementary payments paid to a person (“the claimant”) for a week or a part of a week exceeds the claimant’s taxable maximum for that period, no liability to income tax arises on the excess.
The claimant’s taxable maximum for a period is determined under sections 672 to 674.

P1group.Title: Taxable maximum: general

P2para.Text: A claimant’s taxable maximum for a week is determined—

P3para.Text: under section 673, if the claimant is paid an income-based jobseeker’s allowance for that week, or
under section 674, if the claimant is paid a contribution-based jobseeker’s allowance for that week.

P2para.Text: A claimant’s taxable maximum for a part of a week is determined as follows—
Assume that the jobseeker’s allowance is paid to the claimant for the whole of, rather than part of, the week.
Determine under section 673 or 674 what the claimant’s taxable maximum for that week would be on that assumption.
Determine the claimant’s taxable maximum for the part of the week using this formula—

Para.Text: where—
N is the number of days in the part of the week for which the claimant is actually paid the jobseeker’s allowance, and
TMW is the taxable maximum for the whole week determined under step 2.

P1group.Title: Taxable maximum: income-based jobseeker’s allowance

P2para.Text: A claimant’s taxable maximum for a week is determined under this section if—

P3para.Text: the claimant is paid an income-based jobseeker’s allowance for that week, or
the claimant is assumed under section 672(2) to be paid an income-based jobseeker’s allowance for that week.

P2para.Text: If the claimant is not a member of a ... couple, the claimant’s taxable maximum for the week is equal to the age-related amount which would be applicable to the claimant if a contribution-based jobseeker’s allowance were payable to the claimant for that week.

If the claimant is a member of a ... couple, the claimant’s taxable maximum for the week is equal to the portion of the applicable amount which is included in the jobseeker’s allowance in respect of the couple for that week.
But if—

P3para.Text: the claimant is a member of a ... couple, and
the other member of that couple is prevented by section 14 of JSA 1995 or Article 16 of JS(NI)O 1995 (trade disputes) from being entitled to a jobseeker’s allowance,

P2para.Text: the claimant’s taxable maximum for that week is equal to half the portion of the applicable amount which is included in the jobseeker’s allowance in respect of the couple for that week.

P1group.Title: Taxable maximum: contribution-based jobseeker’s allowance

P2para.Text: A claimant’s taxable maximum for a week is determined under this section if—

P3para.Text: the claimant is paid a contribution-based jobseeker’s allowance for that week, or
the claimant is assumed under section 672(2) to be paid a contribution-based jobseeker’s allowance for that week.

P2para.Text: If the claimant is not a member of a ... couple, the claimant’s taxable maximum for the week is equal to the age-related amount which is applicable to the claimant for that week.

If the claimant is a member of a ... couple, the claimant’s taxable maximum for the week is equal to the portion of the applicable amount which would be included in the jobseeker’s allowance in respect of the couple if an income-based jobseeker’s allowance were payable to the claimant for that week.

P1group.Title: Interpretation

Text.Addition: In section 671 “relevant welfare supplementary payments” means payments to which a person is entitled under–
regulation 8 (when the recipient is entitled to the payment by meeting the condition in regulation 8(2)(a)) of WSP(LCP)R(NI) 2016, or
regulation 11, 12, 13, 14 or 15 of WSP(LDRP)R(NI) 2016.

Para.Text: “age-related amount” and “applicable amount” mean the amounts determined as such in accordance with regulations made under section 4 of JSA 1995;

Text.Addition: “contribution-based jobseeker’s allowance” means a jobseeker’s allowance entitlement to which is based on the claimant satisfying conditions which include those set out in Article 4 of the JS(NI)O 1995;

“income-based jobseeker’s allowance” means a jobseeker’s allowance entitlement to which is based on the claimant satisfying conditions which include those set out in Article 5 of the JS(NI)O 1995 or a joint-claim jobseeker’s allowance (which means a jobseeker’s allowance entitlement to which arises by virtue of Article 3(2B) of the JS(NI)O 1995);

“contribution-based jobseeker’s allowance” and “income-based jobseeker’s allowance” have the same meaning as in Article 3(4) of JS(NI)O 1995;

P1group.Title: Taxable benefits: foreign benefits

P2para.Text: This section applies to any benefit which is payable under the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom if—

P3para.Text: it is substantially similar in character to a benefit listed in Table A, and
it is payable to a person resident in the United Kingdom.

P2para.Text: But this section does not apply to a benefit which is charged to tax under Part 9 (pension income).

See also Chapter 4 of that Part (unremittable income).

P1group.Title: Person liable for tax

P1para.Text: The person liable for any tax charged under this Part on a benefit to which section 678 applies is the person receiving or entitled to the benefit.

Chapter.Title: Taxable and other foreign benefits: exemptions

P1group.Title: Taxable and other foreign benefits: exemptions

P2para.Text: No liability to income tax arises on a taxable foreign benefit if, or to the extent that, the corresponding UK benefit is exempt income.

No liability to income tax arises on a benefit which is payable under the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom if it is substantially similar in character to a United Kingdom social security benefit listed in Table B.
In this section—

Para.Text: “taxable foreign benefit” means a benefit to which section 678 applies;
“corresponding UK benefit”, in relation to a taxable foreign benefit, means the taxable benefit listed in Table A to which the foreign benefit is substantially similar in character (see section 678).

Text.Addition: No liability to income tax arises in respect of any benefit to which section 678 applies of a consular officer or employee in the United Kingdom for a foreign state if—
Her Majesty by Order in Council directs that this section applies to the foreign state for the purpose of giving effect to a reciprocal arrangement with that state, and
the officer or employee meets conditions A to C.
Condition A is that the officer or employee is not—
a British citizen,
a British overseas territories citizen,
a British National (Overseas), or
a British Overseas citizen.

Condition B is that the officer or employee is not engaged in any trade, profession, vocation or employment in the United Kingdom, otherwise than as a consular officer or employee of the state in question.

Addition.Substitution: the officer or employee is a permanent employee of that state, or

the officer or employee was non-UK resident for each of the 2 tax years preceding the tax year in which the officer or employee became a consular officer or employee in the United Kingdom of that state.

Text.Addition: This section applies where—

a person (“R”) is entitled to an amount in respect of child benefit for a child for a week in a tax year by virtue of section 143(1)(b) of SSCBA 1992 or section 139(1)(b) of SSCB(NI)A 1992 (persons contributing to the cost of providing for a child),

A statutory instrument containing an order under this section which increases any person's liability to income tax may not be made unless a draft of it has been laid before and approved by a resolution of the House of Commons.

P1group.Title: Scope of this Part

P2para.Text: This Part provides for the assessment, collection and recovery of income tax in respect of PAYE income and includes provision in respect of the deduction of certain other amounts from, and the repayment of certain other amounts with, PAYE income.
The provisions of this Part are contained in—

Para.Text: this Chapter (which gives the meaning of “PAYE income”),
Chapter 2 (PAYE: general),
Chapter 3 (PAYE: special types of payer or payee),
Chapter 4 (PAYE: special types of income),
Chapter 5 (PAYE settlement agreements), and
Chapter 6 (miscellaneous and supplemental).

P2para.Text: Provision for PAYE regulations is made by Chapters 2 to 6.

P1group.Title: PAYE income

P2para.Text:
For the purposes of this Act and any other enactment (whenever passed)
“PAYE income” for a tax year consists of—

P3para.Text: any PAYE employment income for the year,
any PAYE pension income for the year, and
any PAYE social security income for the year.

P2para.Text: “PAYE employment income” for a tax year means income which consists of—

P3para.Text: any taxable earnings from an employment in the year (determined in accordance with section 10(2)), and
any taxable specific income from an employment for the year (determined in accordance with section 10(3)).

P2para.Text: “PAYE pension income” for a tax year means, subject to subsections (3A) to (3D), taxable pension income for the year determined in accordance with any of the following provisions—

Para.Text: section 571 (United Kingdom pensions),
section 578 (United Kingdom social security pensions),

Text.Substitution: section 579B (pension under registered pension scheme),

Text.Addition: section 612, so far as relating to annuities to which section 610 applies (annuities under non-registered occupational pension schemes),

Para.Text: section 616 (certain overseas government pensions paid in the United Kingdom),
section 621 (the House of Commons Members' Fund),
section 634 (voluntary annual payments).

Text.Substitution: section 637B (tax treatment of pension commencement excess lump sums),
section 637G (tax treatment of trivial commutation lump sums and winding-up lump sums),
section 637N (trivial commutation lump sum death benefits).

Text.Addition: PAYE employment income” for a tax year does not include any taxable specific income treated as paid or received in that tax year by section 394A or 554Z4A (temporary non-residents).

” for a tax year also includes any social security pension lump sum (within the meaning of section 7 of F(No.2)A 2005) in respect of which a charge to income tax arises under that section for that tax year.

Text.Substitution: PAYE pension income” for a tax year does not include any taxable pension income that is treated as accruing in that tax year by section 572A or 579CA (temporary non-residents)

Substitution.Addition: or section 579CB (inheritance tax overpaid by scheme administrator: refund treated as pension)

Text.Addition: PAYE pension income” for a tax year does not include any taxable pension income that is treated as accruing in that tax year by virtue of

Addition.Substitution: Chapter 15A of Part 9 (pension income: lump sums under registered pension schemes)

Text.Addition: so far as having effect as applied by
of Schedule 34 to FA 2004.
“PAYE pension income” for a tax year does not include any amount to which section 579A applies by virtue of any of the following provisions—
section 637H(2) (certain defined benefits lump sum death benefits),
section 637I(2) (certain pension protection lump sum death benefits),
section 637J(2) (certain uncrystallised funds lump sum death benefits),
section 637K(2) (certain annuity protection lump sum death benefits),
section 637L(2) (certain drawdown pension fund lump sum death benefits),
section 637M(2) (certain flexi-access drawdown lump sum death benefits).

P2para.Text:
“PAYE social security income” for a tax year means taxable social security income for the year determined in accordance with section 658(4) or (5)
(taxable United Kingdom social security benefits).

P1group.Title: Tax tables

P2para.Text: The Commissioners ... must construct tax tables with a view to securing that so far as possible—

P3para.Text: the total income tax payable in respect of PAYE income for any tax year and any relevant debts payable during that tax year are deducted from PAYE income paid during that year, and
the income tax and any relevant debts deductible or repayable on the occasion of any payment of, or on account of, PAYE income are such that the following proportions are the same—

P4para.Text: the proportion which the total net income tax and any relevant debts deducted since the beginning of the tax year bears to the total income tax and the total amount of any relevant debts payable for the year, and
the proportion which the part of the tax year which ends with the date of the payment bears to the whole year.

P2para.Text: References in subsection (1) to the total income tax payable for the year are to be read as references to the total income tax estimated to be payable for the year in respect of the income in question—

P3para.Text: subject to a provisional deduction for allowances and reliefs, and

Text.Substitution: subject to an adjustment in respect of amounts required to be deducted or repaid by
PAYE
regulations made under item 1A
in the list in section 684(2).

P2para.Text: For the purpose of estimating the total income tax payable as mentioned in subsection (1)(a), it may be assumed, in relation to any payment of, or on account of, PAYE income, that the following proportions will be the same—

P3para.Text: the proportion which the income paid in the part of the tax year which ends with the making of the payment bears to the income for the whole year, and
the proportion which that part of the tax year bears to the whole year.

Text.Addition: PAYE
regulations may make provision, where it appears to

Addition.Substitution: an officer of Revenue and Customs

Text.Addition: that it is impracticable for a payer to deduct tax by reference to tax tables—
for deductions to be made by the payer in accordance with other arrangements agreed as mentioned in section 684(7A)(a), or
for the payee to be required to keep records and make payments and returns as if he were the payer.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “payment”

P2para.Text: For the purposes of PAYE regulations, a payment of, or on account of, PAYE income of a person is treated as made at the earliest of the following times—
The time when the payment is made.
The time when the person becomes entitled to the payment.
If the person is a director of a company and the income is income from employment with the company (whether or not as director), whichever is the earliest of—

P3para.Text: the time when sums on account of the income are credited in the company’s accounts or records (whether or not there is any restriction on the right to draw the sums);
if the amount of the income for a period is determined before the period ends, the time when the period ends;
if the amount of the income for a period is not determined until after the period has ended, the time when the amount is determined.

Text.Addition:
But this is subject to subsection (5)

P2para.Text: Rule 3 applies if the person is a director of the company at any time in the tax year in which the time mentioned falls.
In this section “director” means—

P3para.Text: in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by a board of directors or similar body, a member of that board or body,
in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by a single director or other person, that director or person, and
in relation to a company whose affairs are managed by the members themselves, a member of the company,

P2para.Text: and includes any person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the company’s directors (as defined above) are accustomed to act.

For the purposes of subsection (3) a person is not regarded as a person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the company’s directors are accustomed to act merely because the directors act on advice given by that person in a professional capacity.

Chapter.Title: PAYE: special types of payer or payee

P1group.Title: Payments by intermediary

P2para.Text: If any payment of, or on account of, PAYE income of an employee is made by an intermediary of the employer, the employer is to be treated, for the purposes of PAYE regulations, as making a payment of the income of an amount equal to the amount given by subsection (3).

Subsection (1) does not apply if the intermediary (whether or not a person to whom PAYE regulations apply) deducts income tax and any relevant debts from the payment the intermediary makes, and accounts for it, in accordance with PAYE regulations.
The amount referred to is—

P3para.Text: if the amount of the payment made by the intermediary is an amount to which the recipient is entitled after deduction of income tax and any relevant debts , the aggregate of the amount of the payment and the amount of any income tax due and any relevant debts deductible , and
in any other case, the amount of the payment.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section a payment of, or on account of, PAYE income of an employee is made by an intermediary of the employer if it is made—

P3para.Text: by a person acting on behalf of the employer and at the expense of the employer or a person connected with the employer, or
by trustees holding property for any persons who include or class of persons which includes the employee.

Text.Addition: This section does not apply in relation to a payment so far as the sum paid is employment income under Chapter 2 of Part 7A.

Title.Addition: Payment of employment income under Part 7A

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
the value of a relevant step counts as employment income under Chapter 2 of Part 7A, and
the relevant step is the payment of a sum of money,
and references to A and B are to be read accordingly.
For the purposes of
PAYE
regulations B is treated as making a payment of
PAYE

The payment is treated as made on the latest of the following days—
the day on which the relevant step is taken,
the day on which A's employment with B starts, and
the day which is 30 days after the day on which FA 2011 is passed.
Subsection (2) does not apply if the person who takes the relevant step (whether or not a person to whom
PAYE
regulations apply) deducts income tax from the payment, and accounts for it, in accordance with
PAYE
regulations.

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: an employee during any period works for a person (“the relevant person”) who is not the employer of the employee,
any payment of, or on account of, PAYE income of the employee in respect of that period is made by a person who is the employer or an intermediary of the employer or of the relevant person,
