Subsection (1C) applies if—
the employee worked for the relevant person during the period under or in consequence of arrangements made between the relevant person and a third person,
the third person did not make the payment of, or on account of,
PAYE
income of the employee, and
PAYE
regulations would apply to the third person if the third person were to make a payment of, or on account of,
PAYE
income of the employee.
The third person is to be treated, for the purposes of
PAYE
regulations, as making a payment of
PAYE
income of the employee of an amount equal to the amount given by subsection (3).

P2para.Text: If subsection (1C) does not apply, the relevant person is to be treated, for the purposes of PAYE regulations, as making a payment of PAYE income of the employee of an amount equal to the amount given by subsection (3).
The amount referred to is—

P3para.Text: if the amount of the payment actually made is an amount to which the recipient is entitled after deduction of income tax and any relevant debts due under the PAYE regulations , the aggregate of the amount of the payment and the amount of any income tax and any relevant debts deductible due, and
in any other case, the amount of the payment.

P2para.Text: If, by virtue of any of sections 61Z1(5)(c)(i), 687A and 693 to 700, an employer would be treated for the purposes of PAYE regulations (if they applied to the employer) as making a payment of any amount to an employee, and if the case is not within subsection (4A), this section has effect as if—

P3para.Text: the employer were also to be treated for the purposes of this section as making an actual payment of that amount, and
paragraph (a) of subsection (3) were omitted.

Text.Addition: A case is within this subsection if—
the section concerned is section 687A or 695A (employment income under Part 7A), and
the relevant step concerned is within paragraph 1 of Schedule 11 to F(
No.
2)A 2017 (loans
etc
outstanding on 5 April 2019).
(And this section does not apply in a case within this subsection.)

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section a payment of, or on account of, PAYE income of an employee is made by an intermediary of the employer or of the relevant person if it is made—

P3para.Text: by a person acting on behalf of the employer or the relevant person and at the expense of the employer or the relevant person or a person connected with the employer or the relevant person, or
by trustees holding property for any persons who include or class of persons which includes the employee.

P2para.Text: In this section and sections 690 and 691 “work”, in relation to an employee, means the performance of any duties of the employment of the employee and any reference to the employee’s working is to be read accordingly.

Title.Addition: Oil and gas workers on the continental shelf

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
any payment of, or on account of,
PAYE
income of a continental shelf worker in respect of a period is made by a person who is the employer or an intermediary of the employer or of the relevant person,
PAYE
regulations do not apply to the person making the payment or, if that person makes the payment as an intermediary of the employer or of the relevant person, to the employer, and
income tax and any relevant debts are not deducted, or not accounted for, in accordance with
PAYE
regulations by the person making the payment or, if that person makes the payment as an intermediary of the employer or of the relevant person, by the employer.
Subject to subsection (5), subsection (1)(a) does not apply in relation to a payment so far as the sum paid is employment income under Chapter 2 of Part 7A.
The relevant person is to be treated, for the purposes of
PAYE
regulations, as making a payment of
PAYE
income of the continental shelf worker of an amount equal to the amount given by subsection (4).
The amount referred to is—
if the amount of the payment actually made is an amount to which the recipient is entitled after deduction of income tax and any relevant debts under
PAYE
regulations, the aggregate of the amount of the payment and the amount of any income tax due and any relevant debts deductible, and
in any other case, the amount of the payment.
If, by virtue of any of sections 687A and 693 to 700, an employer would be treated for the purposes of
PAYE
regulations (if they applied to the employer) as making a payment of any amount to a continental shelf worker, this section has effect as if—
the employer were also to be treated for the purposes of this section as making an actual payment of that amount, and
paragraph (a) of subsection (4) were omitted.
For the purposes of this section a payment of, or on account of,
PAYE
income of a continental shelf worker is made by an intermediary of the employer or of the relevant person if it is made—
by a person acting on behalf of the employer or the relevant person and at the expense of the employer or the relevant person or a person connected with the employer or the relevant person, or
by trustees holding property for any persons who include, or a class of persons which includes, the continental shelf worker.
PAYE
regulations may make provision for, or in connection with, the issue by Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs of a certificate to a relevant person in respect of one or more continental shelf workers—
confirming that, in respect of payments of, or on account of,
PAYE
income of the continental shelf workers specified or described in the certificate, income tax and any relevant debts are being deducted, or accounted for, as mentioned in subsection (1)(c), and
disapplying this section in relation to payments of, or on account of,
PAYE
income of those workers while the certificate is in force.
Regulations under subsection (7) may, in particular, make provision about—
applying for a certificate;
the circumstances in which a certificate may, or must, be issued or cancelled;
the form and content of a certificate;
the effect of a certificate (including provision modifying the effect mentioned in subsection (7)(b) or specifying further effects);
the effect of cancelling a certificate.
Subsection (10) applies if—
there is more than one relevant person in relation to a continental shelf worker, and
in consequence of the same payment within subsection (1)(a), each of them is treated under subsection (3) as making a payment of
PAYE
income of the worker.

If one of the relevant persons complies with section 710 (notional payments: accounting for tax) in respect of the payment that person is treated as making, the other relevant persons do not have to comply with that section in respect of the payments they are treated as making.
In this section—
” means a person in an employment some or all of the duties of which are performed—
in the
UK
sector of the continental shelf (as defined in section 41), and
in connection with exploration or exploitation activities (as so defined);
” means the employer of the continental shelf worker;
”, in relation to a continental shelf worker, means—
if the employer has an associated company (as defined in section 449 of CTA 2010) with a place of business or registered office in the United Kingdom, the associated company, or
in any other case, the person who holds the licence under Part 1 of the Petroleum Act 1998 in respect of the area of the
UK
sector of the continental shelf where some or all of the duties of the continental shelf worker's employment are performed.

Addition.Addition: The Treasury may by regulations modify the definitions of “continental shelf worker” and “relevant person”, as the Treasury thinks appropriate.

Text.Substitution: This section applies in relation to an employee if the employee is or has been internationally mobile at any time in tax year 2025-26 or a subsequent tax year.

An employee is “internationally mobile” at a time in a tax year if at that time the employee works or is likely to work both inside and outside the UK during the tax year (“the mobile tax year”) and at that time—
the employee is or is likely to be non-UK resident for the mobile tax year, or
the mobile tax year is or is likely to be a split year as respects the employee.
If the employer makes an uncertain payment to the employee in any tax year, the entire
payment is to be treated for the purposes of PAYE regulations as a payment of PAYE income of the employee.

the employer is unable to ascertain the extent to which the income

Subsection (3) is without prejudice to—
any assessment in respect of the income of the employee in question, and
any right to repayment of income tax and any relevant debts overpaid and any obligation to pay income tax underpaid and any relevant debts that remain wholly or partly unpaid.
For the purposes of this section and sections 690A to 690E—

any reference to a payment made by the employer includes a reference to a payment made by a person acting on behalf of the employer and at the expense of the employer or a person connected with the employer, and

in a case where section 689 or 689A applies, any reference to a payment made by the employer is to be read as a reference to a payment treated, for the purposes of PAYE regulations, as made by the relevant person.

Title.Substitution: Employer notification for internationally mobile employees

Text.Substitution: This section applies in relation to an employee if the employee is or has been internationally mobile within the meaning of section 690(2) at any time in tax year 2025-26 or a subsequent tax year (“the mobile tax year”).
The appropriate person may give a notice to an officer of Revenue and Customs at any time during the mobile tax year—
that the employer is proposing to treat

Substitution.Substitution: the non-PAYE proportion of any mobile payment

Text.Substitution: made by the employer to the employee as not being PAYE income of the employee for the purposes of PAYE regulations, and
specifying that proportion.

Substitution.Addition: For the purposes of this section and section 690B—
” means a payment of, or on account of, an amount of employment income of the employee in respect of which—
the extent to which the income is PAYE income depends or may depend on the extent to which the employee’s duties during the mobile tax year are performed in the United Kingdom, and
the reason it depends or may depend on that extent is connected to the employee being or having been internationally mobile in the mobile tax year;

” means the best estimate that can reasonably be made of the overall proportion of the amount of all mobile payments made by the employer to the employee that would not be PAYE income if the employee were non-UK resident for the mobile tax year or the mobile tax year were a split year as respects the employee (as appropriate).

Text.Substitution: If a notice given under this section has effect, the proportion of any

payment made by the employer to the employee in any tax year which is to be treated for the purposes of PAYE regulations as not being a payment of PAYE income is the proportion specified in the notice.

Substitution.Substitution: But subsection (3) does not apply to a mobile payment—
to the extent that section 690D(4) or 690E(4) (qualifying payments or treaty affected payments) also applies to the payment, or
if the payment is made after the end of the mobile tax year, other than to the extent the payment is also an uncertain payment.

Text.Substitution: A notice given under this section—

does not have effect if a direction has previously been given to the appropriate person under section 690B (direction by HMRC in relation to internationally mobile employees) in relation to the employee and the mobile tax year;
otherwise, has effect when it is acknowledged by an officer of Revenue and Customs.

Subsection (3) is without prejudice to—
any assessment in respect of the income of the employee in question, and
any right to repayment of income tax and any relevant debts overpaid and any obligation to pay income tax underpaid and any relevant debts that remain wholly or partly unpaid.
For the purposes of this section and sections 690B, 690D and 690E —

where an amount of employment income is treated as PAYE income paid by the employer for the purposes of PAYE regulations by virtue of section 693 (cash vouchers), section 694 (non-cash vouchers) or section 695 (credit-tokens), the employer is to be treated as making a payment of that amount of employment income, and

Title.Substitution: Employees who were internationally mobile etc. before 2025-26

Text.Substitution: This section applies in relation to an employee if the employee falls within subsection (2) or (3) in relation to a tax year that was before tax year 2025-26.
An employee falls within this subsection in relation to a tax year if the employee worked both inside and outside the UK in that tax year and—
the employee was non-UK resident for that tax year or it appears likely to the employer that the employee was non-UK resident, or
the tax year was a
year as respects the employee or it appears likely to the employer that the tax year was such a year.
An employee falls within this subsection in relation to a tax year if—
the employee worked outside the UK in the tax year,
the employee met the requirement of section 26A for that tax year or it appears likely to the employer that the employee met that requirement, and
the employee has made a claim under section 809B of ITA 2007 (claim for remittance basis) for that tax year or it appears likely to the employer that the employee has or will make such a claim.

If the employer makes a payment to the employee of, or on account of, general earnings for that tax year, the amount of the payment that is to be treated as PAYE income for the purposes of the PAYE regulations is the amount that, on the basis of the best estimate that can be reasonably made, is likely to be PAYE income.
For the purposes of subsection (4)—
where this section applies to an employee because it appears likely to the employer that a certain state of affairs exists, the employer may assume that state of affairs exists;
whether general earnings are “for” that tax year is determined in accordance with sections 29 and 30.

P1group.Title: Mobile UK workforce

P2para.Text: This section applies if it appears to the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs that—

P3para.Text: a person (“the relevant person”) has entered into or is likely to enter into an agreement that employees of another person (“the contractor”) are in any period to work for, but not as employees of, the relevant person,
payments of, or on account of, PAYE income of the employees in respect of work done in that period are likely to be made by or on behalf of the contractor, and

PAYE regulations would apply on the making of such payments but it is likely that income tax and any relevant debts will not be deducted, or will not be accounted for, in accordance with the regulations.

P2para.Text: The Commissioners may give a direction that, if—

P3para.Text: any of the employees of the contractor work in any period for, but not as employees of, the relevant person, and
any payment is made by the relevant person in respect of work done by the employees in that period,

P2para.Text: income tax and any relevant debts are to be deducted in accordance with the provisions of this section by the relevant person on making the payment.
A direction under subsection (2)—

P3para.Text: must specify the relevant person and the contractor to whom it relates;
must be given by notice to the relevant person; and
may at any time be withdrawn by notice to the relevant person.

P2para.Text: The Commissioners must take such steps as are reasonably practicable to ensure that a contractor is supplied with a copy of any notice under subsection (3) which relates to him.
If—

P3para.Text: a direction under subsection (2) has effect, and
any employees of the contractor specified in the direction work for, but not as employees of, the relevant person so specified,

P2para.Text: income tax and any relevant debts are, subject to and in accordance with PAYE regulations, to be deducted by the relevant person on making any payment in respect of that work as if so much of the payment as is attributable to work done by each employee were a payment of PAYE income of that employee.

P1group.Title: Organised arrangements for sharing tips

P2para.Text: PAYE regulations may make provision with respect to organised arrangements for tips to be shared among employees by a person (“P”) who is not the principal employer.
PAYE regulations may include provisions which, for the purposes of PAYE regulations—

P3para.Text: treat every payment made by P to an employee by way of the employee’s share of any tips (including the retention by P of P’s own share if P is an employee) as a payment of PAYE income by P, and
treat P as the employer in relation to every such payment.

P2para.Text: PAYE regulations may also include provisions which—

P3para.Text: apply if P has failed to comply with any of the requirements of PAYE regulations, and
treat the principal employer, for the purposes of PAYE regulations, as making payments to the employees of any tips paid over to P by the principal employer.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “the principal employer” means the person under whose general control and management the employees work;
“tips” means gratuities and service charges.

Title.Emphasis: Income provided by means of vouchers and tokens

P1group.Title: Cash vouchers

P2para.Text: If a cash voucher to which Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) applies is received by an employee at any time, the employer is to be treated, for the purposes of PAYE regulations, as making at that time a payment of PAYE income of the employee of an amount equal to the amount ascertained under subsection (2) of, or (as the case may be) referred to in subsection (1A)(b) of, section 81 (benefit of cash voucher treated as earnings).
This section does not apply to the provision of a cash voucher if—

P3para.Text: the voucher is used to meet expenses, and

if the amount for which the voucher is capable of being exchanged had been paid directly to the employee by his or her employer, the amount would not have been PAYE income except by virtue of section 70 (sums in respect of expenses).

P2para.Text: This section does not apply to the provision of a cash voucher if it is exchanged for an amount which—

P3para.Text: is used to meet expenses, and
if it had been paid directly to the employee by the employer, would not have been PAYE income except by virtue of section 70.

P2para.Text: PAYE regulations may exclude from the scope of this section the provision of cash vouchers in circumstances specified in the regulations.
A cash voucher provided for an employee and appropriated to the employee—

P3para.Text: by attaching it to a card held for the employee, or
in any other way,

P2para.Text: is to be treated for the purposes of this section as having been received by the employee at the time when it is appropriated.

P1group.Title: Non-cash vouchers

P2para.Text: If a non-cash voucher to which this section applies is received by an employee, the employer is to be treated, for the purposes of PAYE regulations, as making a payment of PAYE income of the employee of an amount equal to the amount ascertained under section 87(2) or 87A(4) (benefit of non-cash voucher treated as earnings).
This section applies to a non-cash voucher to which Chapter 4 of Part 3 (taxable benefits: vouchers and credit-tokens) applies if—

P3para.Text: either of the conditions set out below is met with respect to the voucher, and
the voucher is not of a description for the time being excluded from the scope of this section by PAYE regulations.

P2para.Text: The first condition is met with respect to a non-cash voucher if it is capable of being exchanged for anything which, if provided to the employee at the time when the voucher is received, would fall to be regarded as a readily convertible asset.
The second condition is met with respect to a non-cash voucher if (but for section 701(2)(b)) it would fall itself to be regarded as a readily convertible asset.
A payment under subsection (1) is made—

P3para.Text: in the case of a non-cash voucher other than a cheque voucher, at the time when the cost of provision is incurred or, if later, the time when the voucher is received by the employee;
in the case of a cheque voucher, at the time when the voucher is handed over in exchange for money, goods or services.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (5)—

Para.Text: “cheque voucher” has the same meaning as in Chapter 4 of Part 3;
“cost of provision”, in relation to a voucher provided by an employer, has the meaning given by section 87;
and a cheque voucher that is posted is to be treated as handed over at the time of posting.

P2para.Text: A non-cash voucher provided for an employee and appropriated to the employee—

P3para.Text: by attaching it to a card held for the employee, or
in any other way,

P2para.Text: is to be treated for the purposes of this section as having been received by the employee at the time when it is appropriated.

P1group.Title: Credit-tokens

P2para.Text: On each occasion on which an employee uses a credit-token provided to the employee because of the employee’s employment to obtain—

P3para.Text: money, or
anything which, if provided to the employee at the time when the credit-token is used, would fall to be regarded as a readily convertible asset,

P2para.Text: the employer is to be treated, for the purposes of PAYE regulations, as making a payment of PAYE income of the employee of an amount equal to the amount ascertained under section 94(2) (benefit of credit-token treated as earnings).

Text.Addition: If the credit-token is provided pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements, the reference in subsection (1) to the amount ascertained under section 94(2) is to be read as a reference to what that amount would be were the credit-token provided otherwise than pursuant to optional remuneration arrangements.
In this subsection “optional remuneration arrangements” is to be interpreted in accordance with section 69A.

P2para.Text: The use of a credit-token by an employee to obtain money is excluded from the scope of this section if the money—

P3para.Text: is used to meet expenses, and
if it had been paid directly to the employee by the employer, would not have been PAYE income except by virtue of section 70 (sums in respect of expenses).

P2para.Text: PAYE regulations may make provision for excluding from the scope of this section any other description of use of a credit-token.

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
the value of a relevant step counts as employment income under Chapter 2 of Part 7A, and
the relevant step is not the payment of a sum of money,
and references to A and B are to be read accordingly.
For the purposes of
PAYE
regulations B is treated as making a payment of
PAYE
income of A of an amount which, on the basis of the best estimate which can reasonably be made, is—
the amount of the employment income, less
so much of that amount (if any) to which section 554Z9(2) or 554Z10(2) applies.
The payment is treated as made on the latest of the following days—
the day on which the relevant step is taken,
the day on which A's employment with B starts, and
the day which is 30 days after the day on which FA 2011 is passed.
Subsection (2) does not apply if the person who takes the relevant step (whether or not a person to whom
PAYE
regulations apply) accounts for income tax on the relevant step in accordance with
PAYE
regulations.

P1group.Title: Readily convertible assets

P2para.Text: If any PAYE income of an employee is provided in the form of a readily convertible asset, the employer is to be treated, for the purposes of PAYE regulations, as making a payment of that income of an amount equal to the amount given by subsection (2).
The amount referred to is the amount which, on the basis of the best estimate that can reasonably be made, is the amount of income likely to be PAYE income in respect of the provision of the asset.

Text.Addition: This section does not apply to any
PAYE
income so far as it is employment income under Chapter 2 of Part 7A.

P1group.Title: Enhancing the value of an asset

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: any PAYE income of an employee is provided in the form of anything enhancing the value of an asset in which the employee or a member of the employee’s family or household already has an interest, and
that asset, with its value enhanced, would be treated as a readily convertible asset if PAYE income were provided to the employee in the form of the asset at the time of the enhancement.

P2para.Text: Section 696 has effect as if—

P3para.Text: the employee had been provided, at the time of the enhancement, with PAYE income in the form of the asset (with its value enhanced), instead of with what enhanced its value, and
the reference in subsection (2) to the provision of the asset were a reference to the enhancement of its value.

P2para.Text: Any reference in this section to enhancing the value of an asset is a reference to—

P3para.Text: the provision of any services by which the asset or any right or interest in it is improved or otherwise made more valuable,
the provision of any property the addition of which to the asset improves it or otherwise increases its value, or
the provision of any other enhancement by the application of money or property to the improvement of the asset or to securing an increase in its value or the value of any right or interest in it.

P2para.Text: There is excluded from the scope of what constitutes enhancing the value of an asset for the purposes of this section any enhancement of value arising on the acquisition by the employee (whether or not as a result of the exercise of a right to acquire shares) of—

P3para.Text: any shares acquired by the employee under a scheme approved under ... Schedule 9 to ICTA (approved profit sharing schemes),

Text.Addition: any shares acquired by the employee under a scheme which is a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme (see Schedule 3),
any shares acquired by the employee under a scheme which is a Schedule 4
CSOP
scheme (see Schedule 4),

P3para.Text: any right over or interest in shares obtained or acquired by the employee under a scheme mentioned in any of the preceding paragraphs, or
any shares acquired by the employee as a result of the exercise of a right over shares obtained before 27th November 1996,

P2para.Text: if the shares in question form part of the share capital of a company falling within section 701(3).

PAYE regulations may make provision excluding such other matters as may be described in the regulations from the scope of what constitutes enhancing the value of an asset for the purposes of this section.

Title.Substitution: PAYE: special charges on employment-related securities

Text.Substitution: This section applies where by reason of the operation of—
section 426 (chargeable events in relation to restricted securities and restricted interests in securities),
section 438 (chargeable events in relation to convertible securities and interests in convertible securities),
section 446B (charge on acquisition where market value of securities or interest artificially depressed),
section 446L (charge where market value of securities artificially enhanced),
section 446U (securities or interest acquired for less than market value: charge on discharge of notional loan),

Substitution.Addition: section 446UA (securities or interest acquired for less than market value: charge in avoidance cases),

Text.Substitution: section 446Y (charge where securities or interest disposed of for more than market value), or
section 447 (chargeable benefit from securities or interest),
in relation to employment-related securities, an amount counts as employment income of an employee.
Sections 684 to 691 and 696 have effect as if—
the employee were provided with PAYE income in the form of the employment-related securities by the employer on the relevant date, and
the reference in subsection (2) of section 696 to the amount of income likely to be PAYE income in respect of the provision of the asset were to the amount likely to count as employment income.

Substitution.Addition: For the purposes of this section the amount likely to count as employment income under section 426 or 438 means the amount after deducting the amount of any relief likely to be available under section 428A or 442A (relief for secondary Class 1 contributions met by employee).

Text.Substitution: In a case in which the employment-related securities are not readily convertible assets, if—
the amount counts as income by virtue of section 427(3)(c), 439(3)(b), (c) or (d), 446Y or 447, and
the whole or any part of the consideration or benefit concerned takes the form of a payment or consists in the provision of an asset,
subsection (4) applies.
Sections 684 to 691 and 696 have effect —
to the extent that the consideration or benefit takes the form of a payment, as if it were a payment of PAYE income of the employee by the employer, and

to the extent that the consideration or benefit consists in the provision of an asset, as if the provision of the asset were the provision of PAYE income in the form of the asset by the employer on the relevant date.

Section 696 as applied by subsection (4)(b) has effect as if the reference in subsection (2) of that section to the amount of income likely to be PAYE income were to the same proportion of the amount likely to count as employment income as so much of the consideration or benefit as consists in the provision of the asset bears to the whole of the consideration or benefit.
In this section “
” means—
in relation to an amount counting as employment income under section 426 or 438, the date on which the chargeable event in question occurs,
in relation to an amount counting as employment income under section 446B, the date of the acquisition of the securities or interest in securities in question,
in relation to an amount counting as employment income under section 446L, the valuation date in question,
in relation to an amount counting as employment income under section 446U, the date on which the notional loan in question is treated as discharged,

Substitution.Addition: in relation to an amount counting as employment income under section 446UA, the date of the acquisition of the securities or interest in securities in question,

Text.Substitution: in relation to an amount counting as employment income under section 446Y, the date of the disposal of the securities or interest in securities in question, and
in relation to an amount counting as employment income under section 447, the date on which the benefit in question is received.
In this section “
” has the same meaning as in Chapters 1 to 4 of Part 7.

Substitution.Addition: This section is subject to section 700A (employment-related securities etc:

P1group.Title: PAYE: conversion of shares

Text.Substitution: This section applies where by reason of the operation of section 476 (acquisition of securities pursuant to securities option etc) in relation to an employment-related securities option an amount counts as employment income of an employee.

In a case where the amount counts as employment income by virtue of section 477(3)(a)
(acquisition of securities), sections 684 to 691 and 696 have effect as if—
the employee were provided with PAYE income in the form of the securities by the employer on the relevant date, and
the reference in subsection (2) of section 696 to the amount of income likely to be PAYE income in respect of the provision of the asset were to the amount likely to count as employment income.

In a case where the amount counts as income by virtue of section 477(3)(b) or (c)
(assignment or release for consideration or receipt of benefit), sections 684 to 691 and 696 have effect —
to the extent that the consideration or benefit takes the form of a payment, as if it were a payment of PAYE income of the employee by the employer, and

to the extent that the consideration or benefit consists in the provision of an asset, as if the provision of the asset were the provision of PAYE income in the form of the asset by the employer on the relevant date.

Section 696 as applied by subsection (3)(b) has effect as if the reference in subsection (2) of that section to the amount of income likely to be PAYE income were to the same proportion of the amount likely to count as employment income as so much of the consideration or benefit as consists in the provision of the asset bears to the whole of the consideration or benefit.

Substitution.Addition: For the purposes of this section the amount likely to count as employment income under section 476 means the amount after deducting the amount of any relief likely to be available under section 481 or 482 (relief for secondary Class 1 contributions or special contribution met by employee).

Text.Substitution: In this section “
” means the date on which the chargeable event in question occurs.
In this section—
”, and
have the same meaning as in Chapter 5 of Part 7.

Substitution.Addition: This section is subject to section 700A (employment-related securities etc:

Text.Addition: This section applies if—
section 698 or 700 applies, and
part or all of the amount that counts as employment income is foreign securities income or is likely to be foreign securities income.
The amount of the payment treated under section 696 as made is limited to—
the amount that, on the basis of the best estimate that can reasonably be made, is likely to count as employment income, minus
the amount that, on the basis of such an estimate, is likely to be foreign securities income.
References in this section to “foreign securities income” are to income that is foreign securities income for the purposes of section

P1group.Title: Meaning of “asset”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “asset” includes any property and in particular any investment of a kind specified in Part 3 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Regulated Activities) Order 2001 (S.I. 2001/544).
This is subject to subsection (2).
In this Chapter “asset” does not include—

P3para.Text: any payment actually made of, or on account of, PAYE income;
... any cash voucher, non-cash voucher or credit-token;
the following—

P4para.Text: any shares acquired by the employee (whether or not as a result of the exercise of a right to acquire shares) under a scheme approved under ... ... Schedule 9 to ICTA (approved profit sharing schemes),

Text.Addition: any shares acquired by the employee under a scheme which is a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme (see Schedule 3),
any shares acquired by the employee

Addition.Substitution: in circumstances in which Condition A or B as set out in section 524(2) or (2A) is met;

P4para.Text: any shares acquired by the employee as the result of the exercise of a right over shares obtained before 27th November 1996 where the avoidance of tax or national insurance contributions is not the main purpose (or one of the main purposes) of any arrangements under which the right was obtained or is exercised,

P3para.Text: if the shares in question form part of the ordinary share capital of a company falling within subsection (3); or
any description of property for the time being excluded from the scope of this section by PAYE regulations.

P2para.Text: A company falls within this subsection if it—

P3para.Text: is the employer (“the employer company”);
has control of the employer company; or
either is, or has control of, a company which is a member of a consortium owning either the employer company or a company having control of the employer company.

Text.Addition: Paragraph (c) of subsection (2) does not apply to shares after their acquisition as mentioned in that paragraph.

P2para.Text: In this section “share” includes stock.

For the purposes of this section a company is a member of a consortium owning another company if it is one of a number of companies which between them beneficially own not less than 75% of the other company’s ordinary share capital and each of which beneficially owns not less than 5% of that capital.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “readily convertible asset”

P2para.Text: In this Chapter “readily convertible asset” means—

P3para.Text: an asset capable of being sold or otherwise realised on—

P4para.Text: a recognised investment exchange (within the meaning of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (c. 8)),
the London Bullion Market,
the New York Stock Exchange, or
a market for the time being specified in PAYE regulations;

P3para.Text: an asset consisting in—

P4para.Text: the rights of an assignee, or any other rights, in respect of a money debt that is or may become due to the employer or any other person,
property that is subject to a warehousing regime, or any right in respect of property so subject, or

anything that is likely (without anything being done by the employee) to give rise to, or to become, a right enabling a person to obtain an amount or total amount of money which is likely to be similar to the expense incurred in the provision of the asset; or

P3para.Text: an asset for which trading arrangements are in existence, or are likely to come into existence in accordance with—

P4para.Text: any arrangements of another description existing when the asset is provided, or
any understanding existing at that time.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section trading arrangements for any asset provided to any person exist whenever there exist any arrangements the effect of which in relation to that asset is to enable—

P3para.Text: that person, or
a member of that person’s family or household,

P2para.Text: to obtain an amount or total amount of money that is, or is likely to be, similar to the expense incurred in the provision of that asset.
PAYE regulations may exclude any description of arrangements from being trading arrangements for the purposes of this section.
References in this section to enabling a person to obtain an amount of money are to be read—

P3para.Text: as references to enabling an amount to be obtained by that person by any means at all, including in particular—

P4para.Text: by using any asset or other property as security for a loan or advance, or
by using any rights comprised in or attached to any asset or other property to obtain any asset for which trading arrangements exist; and

P3para.Text: as including references to cases where a person is enabled to obtain an amount as a member of a class or description of persons, as well as where the person is so enabled in the person’s own right.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section an amount is similar to the expense incurred in the provision of any asset if it is, or is an amount of money equivalent to—

P3para.Text: the amount of the expense so incurred, or
a greater amount, or
an amount that is less than that amount but not substantially so.

Text.Addition: An asset consisting in securities which is not a readily convertible asset apart from this subsection is to be treated as a readily convertible asset unless the securities are shares that are corporation tax deductible.
For the purposes of subsection (5A) shares are corporation tax deductible if they are acquired by a person—
by reason of that, or another person's, employment with a company, or
pursuant to an option granted by reason of that, or another person's, employment with a company,
and the company is entitled to corporation tax relief in respect of the shares under
(corporation tax relief for employee share acquisition).

If a person acquires additional shares by virtue of holding shares that are corporation tax deductible, the additional shares are to be treated for the purposes of subsection (5A) as if they were corporation tax deductible.
If—
on a person ceasing to be beneficially entitled to shares that are corporation tax deductible, that person acquires other shares, and
the circumstances are such that the shares to which the person ceases to be beneficially entitled constitute “
” and the other shares constitute a “
” for the purposes of sections 127 to 130 of
TCGA
the shares that constitute the new holding are to be treated for the purposes of subsection (5A) as if they were corporation tax deductible.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “money” includes money expressed in a currency other than sterling;
“money debt” means any obligation which falls to be, or may be, settled—
by the payment of money, or
by the transfer of a right to settlement under an obligation which is itself a money debt;

Text.Addition:
has the same meaning as in Chapters 1 to 5 of Part 7 (employment income from securities)
(see section 420),
” includes—
an interest in shares, and
stock or an interest in stock,

Para.Text: “warehousing regime” means—
a warehousing or fiscal warehousing regime (within the meaning of sections 18 to 18F of the Value Added Tax Act 1994 (c. 23)); or

any corresponding arrangements in a State other than the United Kingdom which is a Contracting Party to the Agreement on the European Economic Area signed at Oporto on 2nd May 1992 as adjusted by the Protocol signed at Brussels on 17th March 1993.

P1group.Title: Introduction

P1para.Text: This Chapter provides—

P3para.Text: for employers to make agreements with Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (“PAYE settlement agreements”) under which they agree to be accountable to the Commissioners for sums in respect of income tax on general earnings of their employees; and
for such earnings to be treated for certain purposes of the Income Tax Acts as excluded from the employees' income.

P1group.Title: Sums payable by employers under agreements

P2para.Text: PAYE regulations may provide—

P3para.Text: for a person to make a PAYE settlement agreement with Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs; and
to such extent as may be prescribed, for that person’s accountability, and the sums to be accounted for, in respect of income tax on general earnings of that person’s employees to be determined—

P4para.Text: in accordance with the agreement, and
not in accordance with PAYE regulations which would apply apart from this Chapter.

P2para.Text: Without prejudice to the generality of section 684(2), any power of the Commissioners to make PAYE regulations with respect to sums falling to be accounted for under such regulations includes power to make the corresponding provision with respect to sums falling to be accounted for in accordance with a PAYE settlement agreement.

P1group.Title: Approximations allowed in calculations

P1para.Text: PAYE regulations may provide for a PAYE settlement agreement to allow sums which an employer is to account for—

P3para.Text: to be computed, if two or more persons hold employments to which the agreement relates, by reference to a number of those persons all taken together;
to include sums representing income tax on an estimated amount taken to be the aggregate of the amounts of PAYE income consisting of—

P4para.Text: taxable benefits provided or made available by reason of the employments to which the agreement relates, and
expenses paid to the persons holding those employments; and

P3para.Text: to be computed in a manner under which they do not necessarily represent an amount of income tax which would be payable (apart from the agreement) by persons holding employments to which the agreement relates.

P1group.Title: Exclusion of general earnings from income etc.

P1para.Text: PAYE regulations may provide—

P3para.Text: that sums accountable for by an employer under a PAYE settlement agreement, or any other sums, are not to be treated for any prescribed purpose as tax deducted from general earnings;
that an employee is to have no right to be treated as having paid tax in respect of sums accountable for by the employer under such an agreement;
that an employee is to be treated, except—

P4para.Text: for the purposes of the obligations imposed on the employer by such an agreement, and
to such further extent as may be prescribed,

P3para.Text: as relieved from any prescribed obligations of the employee under the Income Tax Acts in respect of general earnings from an employment to which the agreement relates; and
that such earnings are to be treated as excluded from the employee’s income for such further purposes of the Income Tax Acts, and to such extent, as may be prescribed.

P1group.Title: Interpretation of this Chapter

P1para.Text: In this Chapter—

Para.Text: “employment” means any employment the general earnings from which are (or, apart from any regulations made by virtue of this Chapter, would be) PAYE income and related expressions are to be construed accordingly;
“prescribed” means prescribed by PAYE regulations;

“taxable benefit”, in relation to an employee, means any benefit provided or made available, otherwise than in the form of a payment of money, to the employee, or to a person who is a member of the employee’s family or household.

Title.Addition: Provision of additional information to His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs

Text.Addition: PAYE regulations may include provision requiring an employer to provide any information that is specified or described in regulations made by the Commissioners (whether or not that information is also relevant to the assessment, charge, collection and recovery of income tax in respect of PAYE income).

The Commissioners for His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs may only specify or describe information in regulations under subsection (1) if the Commissioners consider that the information is relevant for the purpose of the collection and management of any of the taxes listed in section 1 of TMA 1970.

P1group.Title: PAYE repayments

P2para.Text: PAYE regulations may provide that no repayment of income tax may be made under such regulations to a person—

P3para.Text: during a period for which the person has claimed jobseeker’s allowance, or

at a time when the person is prevented by the trade disputes provisions from being entitled to a jobseeker’s allowance, or would be so prevented if the person otherwise met the conditions for entitlement.

P2para.Text: Different provision may be made with respect to—

P3para.Text: persons within subsection (1)(a), and
persons within subsection (1)(b).

P2para.Text: “The trade disputes provisions” means—

P3para.Text: section 14 of JSA 1995, or
Article 16 of JS(NI)O 1995.

P1group.Title: Additional provision for certain assessments

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: an assessment to income tax is made as respects relevant income (with or without other income), and
the assessment is made after the end of the period of 12 months following the tax year for which it is made.

P2para.Text: In so far as it relates to relevant income, the assessment is to be made in accordance with the practice generally prevailing at the end of that period.
“Relevant income” means income which—

P3para.Text: has been taken into account in the making of deductions or repayments of tax under PAYE regulations, and
was received not less than 12 months before the beginning of the tax year in which the assessment is made.

P1group.Title: Notional payments: accounting for tax

P2para.Text: If an employer makes a notional payment of PAYE income of an employee, the employer must, subject to and in accordance with PAYE regulations, deduct income tax at the relevant time from any payment or payments the employer actually makes of, or on account of, PAYE income of the employee.
For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: a notional payment is a payment treated as made by virtue of any of sections 687, 687A, 689, 689A and 693 to 700, other than a payment whose amount is given by section 687(3)(a), 689(3)(a) or 689A(4)(a), and
any reference to an employer includes a reference to a person who is treated as making a payment by virtue of section 689(2) or 689A(3).

P2para.Text: Subsection (4) applies if, because the payments actually made are insufficient for the purpose, the employer is unable to deduct the full amount of the income tax as required by subsection (1).

The employer must, subject to and in accordance with PAYE regulations, account to the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs at the relevant time for an amount of income tax equal to the amount of income tax the employer is required, but is unable, to deduct.
PAYE regulations may make provision—

P3para.Text: with respect to the time when any notional payment (or description of notional payment) is made;

applying (with or without modifications) any specified provisions of the regulations for the time being in force in relation to deductions from actual payments to amounts deducted or accounted for (or required to be deducted or accounted for) in respect of any notional payments;
with respect to the collection and recovery of amounts deducted or accounted for (or required to be deducted or accounted for) in respect of notional payments.

P2para.Text: Any amount—

P3para.Text: which an employer deducts as mentioned in subsection (1), or
for which an employer accounts as mentioned in subsection (4),

P2para.Text: is to be treated as an amount of tax which, at the time when the notional payment is made, is deducted in respect of the employee’s liability to income tax.
“The relevant time” means (subject to subsection (7A))—

P3para.Text: in subsection (1), any occasion—

P4para.Text: on or after the time when the notional payment is made, and
falling within the same income tax period,

P3para.Text: on which the employer actually makes a payment of, or on account of, PAYE income of the employee;
in subsection (4), any time within 14 days of the end of the income tax period in which the notional payment was made.

Text.Addition: In a case where the notional payment is treated by virtue of any Act as made before the date on which the Act is passed—
the reference in sub-paragraph (i) of paragraph (a) of subsection (7) to the time when the notional payment is made is to the date on which the Act is passed,

the reference in sub-paragraph (ii) of that paragraph to any occasion falling within the same income tax period is to any occasion falling before the end of the income tax period next after that in which that date falls, and
the reference in paragraph (b) of that subsection to the income tax period in which the notional payment was made is to the income tax period next after that in which that date falls.

P2para.Text: In subsection (7) “income tax period” has the same meaning as in the Income Tax (Employments) Regulations 1993 (S.I. 1993/744), or any subsequent regulations making corresponding provision.

P1group.Title: Right to make a return

P2para.Text: A person who has PAYE income for a tax year in respect of which deductions or repayments are made under PAYE regulations may by notice require an officer of Revenue and Customs to give that person a notice under section 8 of TMA 1970 (personal return) for the tax year.
A notice to an officer of Revenue and Customs under subsection (1) must be given no later than 3 years after the 31st October next following the tax year.

P1group.Title: Interpretation of this Part

P2para.Text: In this Part—

Para.Text: “employee” means a person who holds or has held employment with another person;
“employer” means—
in relation to an employee, a person with whom the employee holds or has held an employment, and

in relation to any PAYE income of an employee, the person who is the employer of the employee in relation to the employment in respect of which the income is or was provided or, as the case may be, by reference to which it falls to be regarded as PAYE income. The above definitions are subject to sections 688 and 710(2)(b).

Text.Addition: ” has the meaning given by section 684(7AA).

P2para.Text: Sections 4 and 5 apply for the purposes of this Part as they apply for the purposes of the employment income Parts.

P1group.Title: Donations to charity: payroll deduction scheme

P2para.Text: This section applies if—

P3para.Text: an individual is entitled to receive payments of, or on account of, PAYE income in respect of which PAYE regulations require deductions or repayments of income tax in accordance with those regulations, and
at the request of the individual, the person making the payments (the “payer”) withholds sums from them as donations.

P2para.Text: In determining whether there is such a requirement under PAYE regulations for the purposes of subsection (1)(a), any requirement under the regulations which requires the deduction of an amount in calculating the payments of, or on account of, PAYE income is to be disregarded.
The amount of the donations is allowed as a deduction in calculating the amount of the individual’s income which is charged to tax in accordance with subsection (4).
In the case of a payment of, or on account of—

P3para.Text: taxable earnings from an employment, the deduction is allowed from the taxable earnings from the employment in calculating the net taxable earnings from the employment for the relevant tax year for the purposes of Part 2 (see section 11(1));

taxable specific income from an employment, the deduction is allowed from that taxable specific income in calculating the net taxable specific income from the employment for the relevant tax year for the purposes of Part 2 (see section 12(1));

taxable pension income for a pension, annuity or other item of pension income, the deduction is allowed from that taxable pension income in calculating the net taxable pension income for that income for the relevant tax year for the purposes of Part 9 (see section 567(3));

taxable social security income for a taxable benefit, the deduction is allowed from that taxable social security income in calculating the net taxable social security income for that benefit for the relevant tax year for the purposes of Part 10 (see section 658(3)).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (4) “relevant tax year” means—

P3para.Text: in the case of paragraphs (a) and (b), the tax year in which the donation is withheld, and
in the case of paragraphs (c) and (d), the tax year for which the income referred to in subsection (1)(a) is taxable pension income or taxable social security income, as the case may be.

Text.Addition: This section is subject to
of ITA 2007 (removal of income tax relief in respect of tainted charity donations
etc

P1group.Title: Meaning of “donations”

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Part “donations” means sums which—

P3para.Text: are withheld by the payer under a scheme which is an approved scheme at the time of the withholding,
constitute gifts by the individual to one or more specified charities under the scheme, and
satisfy the conditions (if any) set out in the scheme.

P2para.Text: In this section—

Para.Text: “approved scheme” means a scheme which is approved (or is of a kind approved) by an officer of Revenue and Customs and under which—
the payer is required to pay sums withheld to a body which is an approved agent at the time of the withholding, and
the approved agent is required—
to pay sums withheld to the specified charity or charities, or
in a case where the agent is itself a specified charity, to retain any sum due to itself;
“charity” ... includes each of the bodies mentioned in section 468 of CTA 2010;
“specified charity” means a charity specified by the individual.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section a body is an “approved agent” if it is approved by an officer of Revenue and Customs for the purpose of paying donations to one or more charities.

P1group.Title: Approval of schemes: regulation by Treasury

P2para.Text: The Treasury may by regulations prescribe the circumstances in which an officer of Revenue and Customs may grant or withdraw approval of any—

P3para.Text: scheme,
kind of scheme, or
agent.

P2para.Text: The circumstances, whether relating to the terms of schemes or the qualifications of agents or otherwise, are to be such as the Treasury think fit.
The Treasury may by regulations make provision—

P3para.Text: requiring a payer or agent who participates (or has at any time participated) in an approved scheme under this Part—

P4para.Text: in prescribed circumstances, to furnish to an officer of Revenue and Customs prescribed information;

P3para.Text: for, and in relation to, appeals ... against a refusal by an officer of Revenue and Customs to approve, or the officer's withdrawal of approval from, any—

P4para.Text: scheme,
kind of scheme, or
agent;

P3para.Text: generally for giving effect to sections 713 and 714.
In this subsection “prescribed” means prescribed by the regulations.

P1group.Title: Alteration of amounts by Treasury order

P2para.Text: The Treasury may by order increase or further increase the sums of money specified in any of the following provisions.
They are—

P3para.Text:
section 179(2)(a)
(limit on exception for advances for necessary expenses),

section 241(3)(a) and (b)
(incidental overnight expenses: overall exemption limit),

section 264(2) and (3)
(annual parties and functions),

section 287(1)
(limit on exemption under Chapter 7 of Part 4: removal benefits and expenses),

section 322(1) and (4)
(suggestion awards: “the permitted maximum”),

section 323(2)
(long service awards),

Text.Addition: section 323A(4) (trivial benefits provided by employers: cost of providing benefit),
section 323B(2) (trivial benefits provided by employers: annual exempt amount),

P3para.Text:
section 324(6)
(small gifts from third parties), and

section 358(3)(b)
(business entertainment and gifts: other exceptions).

P2para.Text: An order relating to section 241(3)(a) or (b) may make provision for determining what earnings are treated as received on or after the date when the order comes into force.
An order relating to section 287(1) applies to a change of an employee’s residence where the employment change occurs on or after the day specified in the order for the purpose.

Para.Text: “The employment change” here has the same meaning as in Chapter 7 of Part 4 (see section 275).

Text.Addition: Any income, so far as it falls within—
Part 2, 9 or 10 of this Act, and
Chapter 3 of Part 4 of
ITTOIA
2005 (dividends
etc.
from
UK
resident companies
etc.
is dealt with under Chapter 3 of Part 4 of ITTOIA 2005.

Title.Addition: Employment intermediaries to keep, preserve and provide information etc

Text.Addition: For purposes connected with Chapter 7
(treatment of workers supplied by agencies)
or Part 11 (PAYE), the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs may by regulations make provision for, or in connection with, requiring a specified employment intermediary—
to keep and preserve specified information, records or documents for a specified period;
to provide Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs with specified information, records or documents within a specified period or at specified times.
An “employment intermediary” is a person

Addition.Addition: (other than an individual mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b))

Text.Addition: who makes
arrangements under or in consequence of which—
an individual works, or is to work, for a third person, or
an individual is, or is to be, remunerated for work done for a third person.
For the purposes of subsection (2), an individual works for a person if—
the individual performs any duties of an employment for that person (whether or not the individual is employed by that person), or
the individual provides, or is involved in the provision of, a service to that person.
In subsection (1) “
” means specified or described in regulations made under this section.
Regulations under this section may—
make different provision for different cases or different purposes, and
make incidental, consequential, supplementary or transitional provision or savings.

P1group.Title: Orders and regulations made by Treasury or Commissioners

P2para.Text: Any power of the Treasury or the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs to make any order or regulations under this Act is exercisable by statutory instrument.
This is subject to subsection (2).

Subsection (1) does not apply to the power conferred by section 28(5) (overseas Crown employment: order excepting certain earnings) or section 421L(7)
(persons to whom section 421J applies: order in relation to excluded securities).

Any statutory instrument containing any order or regulations made by the Treasury or the Commissioners for Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs under this Act is subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of the House of Commons.
This is subject to subsection (4).

Subsection (3) does not apply to any statutory instrument made under section 24A(11) (assumptions about related employments), section 270AA(3) (exemption from income tax for qualifying childcare vouchers: meaning of “eligible employee”), section 318AZA(3) (exemption from income tax for other care: meaning of “eligible employee”), section 323C(1) (trivial benefits provided by employers), section 343(3) (deduction for professional membership fees: order adding certain fees) or section 688A(7)
(PAYE regulations: managed service companies) or to which section 312A(10) (reduction of tax-exempt amount in respect of certain bonus payments) , section 402D(10) (meaning of basic pay for purpose of calculating charge on termination award), section 404B(4) (reduction of tax-free threshold for employment-termination etc payments) or section 681F(3) or 681J(3) (variation of income limit etc for high income child benefit or winter fuel payment charge: orders increasing liability to tax) applies .

P1group.Title: Connected persons

P1para.Text: Section 993 of ITA 2007 (how to tell whether persons are connected) applies for the purposes of this Act.
Section 995 of ITA 2007 (meaning of “control”) applies for the purposes of this Act, unless otherwise indicated.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “ an officer of Revenue and Customs ” etc.
Other definitions

P2para.Text: In this Act—

Para.Text: “cash voucher” has the same meaning as in Chapter 4 of Part 3 (see section 75),

SSCBA
1992 or SSCB(
NI

Para.Text: “credit-token” has the same meaning as in Chapter 4 of Part 3 (see section 92),

Text.Substitution: ” means an individual, partnership or body of persons resident outside, and not resident in, the United Kingdom,

Para.Text: “non-cash voucher” has the same meaning as in Chapter 4 of Part 3 (see section 84),

P2para.Text: Any reference in this Act to being domiciled in the United Kingdom is to be read as a reference to being domiciled in any part of the United Kingdom.
For the purposes of this Act the following are members of a person’s family—

P3para.Text: the person’s spouse or civil partner,
the person’s children and their spouses or civil partners,
the person’s parents, and
the person’s dependants.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Act the following are members of a person’s family or household—

P3para.Text: members of the person’s family,
the person’s domestic staff, and
the person’s guests.

P2para.Text:
The following provisions (which relate to the legal equality of illegitimate children) are to be disregarded in interpreting references in this Act to a child or
children—

P3para.Text: section 1 of the Family Law Reform Act 1987 (c. 42);

the paragraph inserted in Schedule 1 to the Interpretation Act 1978
(c. 30) by paragraph 73 of Schedule 2 to the 1987 Act;

section 1(2) of the Law Reform (Parent and Child)
(Scotland) Act 1986 (c. 9);
Article 155 of the Children (Northern Ireland) Order 1995 (S.I. 1995/755 (N.I. 2)).

P2para.Text: In the employment income Parts any reference to earnings which is not limited by the context—

P3para.Text: to earnings within Chapter 1 of Part 3, or
to any other particular description of earnings,

P2para.Text:
includes a reference to any amount treated as earnings by any of the provisions mentioned in section 7(5)
(meaning of “employment income” etc.).

P1group.Title: Consequential amendments

P1para.Text: Schedule 6 contains consequential amendments.

P1group.Title: Commencement and transitional provisions and savings

P2para.Text: This Act comes into force on 6th April 2003 and has effect—

P3para.Text: for the purposes of income tax, for the tax year 2003-04 and subsequent tax years, and
for the purposes of corporation tax, for accounting periods ending after 5th April 2003.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) is subject to Schedule 7, which contains transitional provisions and savings.

P1group.Title: Repeals and revocations

P2para.Text: The enactments specified in Part 1 of Schedule 8 (which include certain spent provisions) are repealed to the extent specified.
The instruments specified in Part 2 of that Schedule are revoked to the extent specified.

P1group.Title: Citation

P1para.Text: This Act may be cited as the Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003.
