with effect from—
such relevant time as is specified in the default notice, or
if no relevant time is specified, the time of the giving of the default notice, and
the company is liable for a further penalty of an amount decided by HMRC.
Sub-paragraph (7)(a) does not affect the operation of the
SIP
code in relation to shares appropriated to, or acquired on behalf of, an individual under the
SIP
before the time mentioned in sub-paragraph (7)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be).
In particular, if the
SIP
was a Schedule 2
SIP
when the shares were appropriated to, or acquired on behalf of, the individual, the
SIP
is to continue to be a Schedule 2
SIP
in relation to those shares.
The penalty under sub-paragraph (7)(b) must not exceed an amount equal to twice
HMRC
's reasonable estimate of—
the total income tax for which participants in the
SIP
have not been liable, or will not be liable in the future, and
the total contributions under Part 1 of
SSCBA
1992 or SSCB(
NI
)A 1992 for which any persons have not been liable, or will not be liable in the future,
in consequence of the
SIP
having been a Schedule 2
SIP
at any relevant time before the time mentioned in sub-paragraph (7)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be).
The liabilities covered by sub-paragraph (10) include liabilities for income tax or contributions which a person has not had, or will not have, in consequence of sub-paragraphs (8) and (9).
In this paragraph “
” means any time before the giving of the default notice when requirements of Parts 2 to 9 of this Schedule were not met in relation to the SIP.
This paragraph applies if the company is liable for a penalty under this Part.
HMRC
must assess the penalty and notify the company of the assessment.
Subject to sub-paragraphs (4) and (5), the assessment must be made no later than 12 months after the date on which the company becomes liable for the penalty.
In the case of a penalty under paragraph 81E(1)(b), the assessment must be made no later than—
12 months after the date on which
HMRC
become aware of the inaccuracy, and
6 years after the date on which the company becomes liable for the penalty.

In the case of a penalty under paragraph 81H(2)(b) or 81I(2)(a) or (7)(b) where notice of appeal is given under paragraph 81K(2) or (3), the assessment must be made no later than 12 months after the date on which the appeal is determined or withdrawn.
A penalty payable under this Part must be paid—
no later than 30 days after the date on which the notice under sub-paragraph (2) is given to the company, or
if notice of appeal is given against the penalty under paragraph 81K(1) or (4), no later than 30 days after the date on which the appeal is determined or withdrawn.
The penalty may be enforced as if it were corporation tax or, if the company is not within the charge to corporation tax, income tax charged in an assessment and due and payable.
Sections 100 to 103 of
TMA
1970 do not apply to a penalty under this Part.

Substitution.Addition: The company may appeal against a decision of
under paragraph 81A(5A) that there was no reasonable excuse for its failure to give notice on or before the initial notification deadline.

Text.Substitution: The company may appeal against a decision of
HMRC
that the company is liable for a penalty under paragraph 81C or 81E.
The company may appeal against—
a decision of
HMRC
mentioned in paragraph 81H(1) or a decision of
HMRC
to specify, or not to specify, a relevant time in the closure notice;
a decision of
HMRC
mentioned in paragraph 81I(1).
The company may appeal against a decision of
HMRC
to give the company a default notice under paragraph 81I;
to specify, or not to specify, a relevant time in the default notice.
The company may appeal against a decision of
HMRC
as to the amount of a penalty payable by the company under this Part.
The company may appeal against a decision of an officer of Revenue and Customs to give a direction under section 998 of CTA 2009 (withdrawal of corporation tax deductions in relation to a Schedule 2
SIP
Notice of appeal must be given to
HMRC
no later than 30 days after the date on which—

Substitution.Addition: in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (A1), notice of
's decision is given to the company;

Text.Substitution: in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (1) or (4), the notice under paragraph 81J(2) is given to the company;
in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (2), the closure notice is given;
in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (3), the default notice is given;
in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (5), notice of the officer's decision is given to the company.
On an appeal under sub-paragraph
(1), (3)(a) or (5) which is notified to the tribunal, the tribunal may affirm or cancel the decision.
On an appeal under sub-paragraph (2) or (3)(b) which is notified to the tribunal, the tribunal may—
affirm or cancel the decision, or
substitute for the decision another decision which
HMRC
had power to make.
On an appeal under sub-paragraph (4) which is notified to the tribunal, the tribunal may—
affirm the amount of the penalty decided, or
substitute another amount for that amount.
Subject to this paragraph and paragraph 81J, the provisions of Part 5 of
TMA

1970 relating to appeals have effect in relation to an appeal under this paragraph as they have effect in relation to an appeal against an assessment to corporation tax or, if the company is not within the charge to corporation tax, income tax.

Text.Addition: A
SIP
ceases to be a Schedule 2
SIP
if (and with effect from the time when) a disqualifying event occurs.
The following are disqualifying events—
an alteration being made in—
the share capital of a company any of whose shares are subject to the plan trust, or
the rights attaching to any shares of such a company,
that materially affects the value of the shares that are subject to the plan trust;
shares of a class of shares that is subject to the plan trust receiving different treatment in any respect from the other shares of that class.
Sub-paragraph (2)(b) applies in particular to different treatment in respect of—
the dividend payable,
repayment, or
any offer of substituted or additional shares, securities or rights of any description in respect of the shares.
Sub-paragraph (2)(b) does not however apply where the difference in treatment arises from—
a key feature of the plan, or
any of the participants' shares being subject to any restriction.

Nor does sub-paragraph (2)(b) apply as a result only of the fact that shares which have been newly issued receive, in respect of dividends payable with respect to a period beginning before the date on which they were issued, treatment less favourable than that accorded to shares issued before that date.
For the purposes of this paragraph a “key feature” of a plan is a provision of it that is necessary to meet the requirements of this Schedule.
This paragraph does not affect the operation of the
SIP
code in relation to shares awarded to participants in the plan before the disqualifying event occurred.

P2para.Text: In this Part of this Schedule a “company reconstruction” means a transaction to which this paragraph applies.
This paragraph applies to a transaction which occurs in relation to any of a participant’s plan shares (“the original holding”) and—

P3para.Text: results in a new holding being equated with the original holding for the purposes of capital gains tax, or
would have that result but for the fact that what would be the new holding consists of or includes a qualifying corporate bond.

P2para.Text: But where an excluded issue of shares is made—

P3para.Text: that issue of shares does not by itself count as a transaction within sub-paragraph (2); and
if made as part of a transaction within that sub-paragraph (that is, as part of a company reconstruction), the shares issued are to be regarded as not forming part of the new holding.

P2para.Text: An “excluded issue of shares” means an issue of shares of any of the following descriptions (in respect of which a charge to income tax arises)—

P3para.Text: redeemable shares or securities issued as mentioned in paragraph C or D in section 1000(1) of CTA 2010 (distributions);
share capital issued in circumstances such that section 1022(3) of CTA 2010 (bonus issues) applies;
share capital to which section 410 of ITTOIA 2005 (stock dividends) applies that is issued in a case where subsection (2) or (3) of that section applies.

P2para.Text: In the SIP code references to a participant’s plan shares in relation to a SIP are to be read, after the time of a company reconstruction—

P3para.Text: as referring to the new shares, or
as including those shares,

P2para.Text: as the case may be.
This is subject to the following provisions of this paragraph.
For the purposes of the SIP code—

P3para.Text: a company reconstruction is to be treated as not involving a disposal of the shares comprised in the original holding;
new shares are to be treated as having been awarded to the participant on the date on which the corresponding old shares were awarded;

the conditions in Part 4 of this Schedule (types of share that may be awarded) are to be treated as fulfilled with respect to any new shares if they were (or were treated as) fulfilled with respect to the corresponding old shares; and
the provisions of—

P4para.Text: sections 489 to 514 (SIPs: income tax advantages and charges under this Act),

Text.Substitution: sections 392 to 395 and 405 to 408 of
ITTOIA
2005 (SIPs: special rules for charges under Chapters 3 and 4 of Part 4 of that Act (dividends
etc.
from
UK
or non-UK resident companies
etc.
)) and section 770 of that Act (exemption for amounts applied by
SIP
trustees acquiring dividend shares or retained for reinvestment),

P4para.Text: sections 686B and 686C of ICTA (SIPs: income tax advantages for trustees), and
Part 1 of Schedule 7D to TCGA 1992 (SIPs: capital gains tax),

P3para.Text: apply in relation to the new shares as they would have applied in relation to the corresponding old shares.

P2para.Text: If the corresponding old shares were dividend shares, the reference in sub-paragraph (2)(b) to the corresponding old shares being awarded is a reference to those shares being acquired on behalf of the participant.
Sub-paragraphs (1) to (3) are subject to paragraph 88 (treatment of shares acquired under rights issue).

For the purposes of the SIP code if, as part of a company reconstruction, trustees become entitled to a capital receipt, their entitlement to the capital receipt is to be taken to arise before the new holding comes into being.

In the SIP code, in the context of a new holding, “shares” includes securities and rights of any description which form part of the new holding for the purposes of Chapter 2 of Part 4 of TCGA 1992 (reorganisation of share capital etc.).
In this paragraph—

P3para.Text: “new shares” means shares comprised in the new holding which were issued in respect of, or otherwise represent, shares comprised in the original holding;
“the new holding” and “the original holding” mean respectively the new and original holdings mentioned in paragraph 86(2);
“corresponding old shares”, in relation to any new shares, means the shares in respect of which the new shares are issued or which the new shares otherwise represent.

Title.Emphasis: Treatment of shares acquired under rights issue

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies for the purposes of the SIP code where the trustees exercise rights arising under a rights issue and conferred in respect of a participant’s plan shares.
In such a case, any shares or securities or rights allotted are to be treated as if they were plan shares—

P3para.Text: identical to the shares in respect of which the rights were conferred, and
appropriated to, or acquired on behalf of, the participant under the plan in the same way and at the same time as those shares.

P2para.Text: If, however, either of the conditions set out in sub-paragraph (4) is met, sub-paragraph (5) applies instead.
The conditions are—

P3para.Text: that the funds used by the trustees to exercise the rights are not provided by the exercise of the trustees' powers under paragraph 77 (trustees' powers to raise funds to subscribe for rights issue);
that similar rights are not conferred in respect of all ordinary shares in the company.

P2para.Text: If either of those conditions is met—

P3para.Text: any shares, securities or rights allotted are not plan shares, and
sections 127 to 130 of TCGA 1992 (reorganisation of share capital etc.) do not apply in relation to them.

P2para.Text: The plan may provide for the company to issue a plan termination notice in respect of the plan in circumstances specified in the plan.
The plan must provide that, where a plan termination notice is issued, a copy of the notice must be given, without delay, to—

P3para.Text: the trustees,
each individual who has plan shares, and
each individual who has entered into a partnership share agreement which was in force immediately before the notice was issued.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies if the company has issued a plan termination notice under paragraph 89.
No further shares may be appropriated to, or acquired on behalf of, individuals under the plan.
The trustees must remove the plan shares from the plan as soon as practicable after whichever is the later of—

P3para.Text: the end of the notice period, or

the first date on which the shares may be removed from the plan without giving rise to a charge to income tax under sections 501 to 507 (SIPs: tax charges) on the participant on whose behalf they are held.

P2para.Text: In sub-paragraph (3) “the notice period” means the period of 3 months beginning with the date on which the requirements imposed by the plan in accordance with paragraph 89(2) are met in respect of the plan termination notice.
The trustees may remove a participant’s shares from the plan at an earlier date with the participant’s consent.
Any consent given by the participant before receiving a copy of the plan termination notice is to be disregarded for the purposes of sub-paragraph (5).
As soon as practicable after the plan termination notice is issued, the trustees must pay any money held on an individual’s behalf to the individual.
In this paragraph references to the trustees removing the plan shares from the plan are to their doing the following in the case of each participant—

P3para.Text: transferring the shares to the participant on behalf of whom they are held, or to another person, at the participant’s direction, or
disposing of the shares and accounting (or holding themselves ready to account) for the proceeds to the participant or to another person at the participant’s direction.

P2para.Text: Where a participant has died, the references in this paragraph to a participant are to the participant’s personal representatives.
This paragraph applies for the purposes of the provisions of the SIP code relating to group plans.
Each joint owner of a jointly owned company is to be treated as controlling every company within sub-paragraph (3).
The companies within this sub-paragraph are—

P3para.Text: the jointly owned company, and
any company controlled by that company.

P2para.Text: However, no company within sub-paragraph (3) may be—

P3para.Text: a constituent company in more than one group plan, or
a constituent company in a particular group plan if another company within that sub-paragraph is a constituent company in a different group plan.

P2para.Text: In this paragraph a “jointly owned company” means a company—

P3para.Text: of which 50% of the issued share capital is owned by one person and 50% by another, and
which is not controlled by any one person.

P2para.Text: This paragraph does not apply for the purposes of paragraph 27(1)(b) (requirement that plan shares are in a company not under another company’s control).
For the purposes of the SIP code the “market value” of shares has the same meaning as it has for the purposes of TCGA 1992 by virtue of Part 8 of that Act.

Text.Substitution: For the purposes of this Schedule the market value of shares subject to a restriction is to be determined as if they were not subject to the restriction.

P2para.Text: Where the market value of shares on any date has to be determined for the purposes of the SIP code, an officer of Revenue and Customs and the trustees may agree that it is to be determined by reference—

P3para.Text: to a date or dates, or
to an average of the values on a number of dates,

P2para.Text: stated in the agreement.

Text.Substitution: An officer of Revenue and Customs may by notice require a person to provide the officer with any information—
which the officer reasonably requires for the performance of any functions of Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs or an officer of Revenue and Customs under the
SIP
code, and
which the person to whom the notice is addressed has or can reasonably obtain.

P2para.Text: The power conferred by this paragraph extends, in particular, to—

P3para.Text: information to enable an officer of Revenue and Customs —

Text.Substitution: to check anything contained in a notice under paragraph 81A or a return under paragraph 81B or to check any information accompanying such a notice or return, or”, and

P4para.Text: to determine the liability to tax, including capital gains tax, of any person who has participated in a plan or any other person whose liability to tax the operation of a plan is relevant to, and

P3para.Text: information about the administration of a plan and any proposed alteration of the terms of a plan.

P2para.Text: The notice must require the information to be provided within a specified period, which must not end earlier than 3 months after the date when the notice is given.
For the purposes of the SIP code one company is an “associated company” of another company at a given time if—

P3para.Text: one has control of the other, or
both are under the control of the same person or persons.

P2para.Text: Sub-paragraph (1) does not, however, apply for the purposes of paragraph 29 (prohibited shares).
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (1) the question whether a person controls a company is to be determined in accordance with sections 450 and 451 of CTA 2010.

Title.Emphasis: Meaning of participant ceasing to be in relevant employment

P2para.Text: This paragraph explains what is meant, for the purposes of the SIP code, by a participant ceasing to be in relevant employment.
For the purposes of the SIP code “relevant employment” means employment by the company or any associated company.
A participant who remains in the employment of the company or any associated company does not cease to be in relevant employment.

Title.Emphasis: Meaning of shares being withdrawn from plan

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the SIP code plan shares are withdrawn from a SIP when—

P3para.Text: they are transferred by the trustees to the participant, or another person, on the direction of the participant,
the participant assigns, charges or otherwise disposes of the beneficial interest in the shares, or

they are disposed of by the trustees, on the direction of the participant, in circumstances where the trustees account (or hold themselves ready to account) for the proceeds to the participant or to another person.

P2para.Text: Where the participant has died, the references in sub-paragraph (1) to the participant are to the participant’s personal representatives.

Title.Emphasis: Meaning of shares ceasing to be subject to plan

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the SIP code plan shares cease to be subject to a SIP when—

P3para.Text: they are withdrawn from the plan,
the participant to whom the shares were awarded ceases to be in relevant employment at a time when the shares are subject to the plan, or
the trustees dispose of the shares under provision made in accordance with paragraph 79 (meeting by trustees of PAYE obligations).

P2para.Text: If an individual—

P3para.Text: participates in an award of partnership shares, and
ceases to be in relevant employment at any time during the acquisition period relating to that award,

P2para.Text: the individual is to be treated for the purposes of this paragraph as ceasing to be in relevant employment immediately after the shares are awarded.
In sub-paragraph (2) “the acquisition period” in relation to an award means—

P3para.Text: where there was no accumulation period, the period beginning with the deduction of the partnership share money and ending with the acquisition date (as defined by paragraph 50(4)), and
where there was an accumulation period, the period beginning with the end of that period and ending immediately before the acquisition date (as defined by paragraph 52(5)).

P2para.Text: If a participant ceases to be in relevant employment, the participant’s plan shares are to be treated as ceasing to be subject to the plan on the date of leaving.
In the SIP code—

Para.Text: “articles of association”, in relation to a company, includes any other written agreement between the shareholders of the company;
“company” means a body corporate;
“group of companies” means a company and any other companies of which it has control, and “group company” has a corresponding meaning;
“participant’s plan shares”, in relation to a SIP, means plan shares that have been awarded to an individual participant;
“PAYE obligations” means (subject to paragraphs 79(2) and 80(2)) obligations of any person under—
Part 11 of this Act, or
PAYE regulations;
“plan shares”, in relation to a SIP, means—
free, partnership or matching shares which have been awarded to participants under the plan,
dividend shares which have been acquired on behalf of participants under the plan, and
shares in relation to which paragraph 87(1) applies (company reconstructions: new shares),
and which (in each case) remain subject to the plan;

“provision for forfeiture” means a provision to the effect that a participant ceases to be beneficially entitled to shares on the occurrence of certain events, and “forfeiture” is to be read accordingly;
“qualifying corporate bond” has the meaning given by section 117 of TCGA 1992;
“redundancy” has the same meaning as in ERA 1996 or ER(NI)O 1996;

“rights arising under a rights issue” means rights conferred in respect of a participant’s plan shares to be allotted, on payment, other shares or securities or rights of any description in the same company.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the SIP code references to “shares” include fractions of shares forming part of the share capital of a company registered in a foreign country the law of which recognises such fractions.
For the purposes of the SIP code a company is a member of a consortium owning another company if it is one of a number of companies—

P3para.Text: which between them beneficially own not less than 75% of the other company’s ordinary share capital, and
each of which beneficially owns not less than 5% of that capital.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of the
SIP
code—

shares are subject to a “restriction” if there is any contract, agreement, arrangement or condition which makes provision to which any of subsections (2) to (4) of section 423 (restricted securities) would apply if the references in those subsections to the employment-related securities were to the shares, and
the “restriction” is that provision.

P1para.Text: In the SIP code the following expressions are defined or otherwise explained by the provisions indicated below:

xhtml:tr.xhtml:td: ceasing to be in relevant employment (in relation to a participant)
ceasing to be subject to plan (in relation to shares)
the company (in relation to a SIP)
company reconstruction (in Part 11 of this Schedule)
eligible shares (in Part 4 of this Schedule)
participation in an award of shares
plan requirements (in relation to a SIP)
plan shares (in relation to a SIP)
rights arising under a rights issue

xhtml:td.Addition: paragraph 1 and Part 10 of this Schedule

xhtml:tr.xhtml:td: paragraph 99(2) (and in the context of a new holding, paragraph 87(6))

xhtml:td.Substitution: section 4(2) of ITA 2007 (as applied by section 989 of that Act)

Title.Emphasis: Introduction to Schedule 3 SAYE option schemes

Text.Substitution: For the purposes of the
SAYE
code an
SAYE
option scheme is a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme if the requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule are met in relation to the scheme.

P2para.Text: The requirements consist of general requirements (see Part 2) and requirements as to—

Para.Text: the eligibility of individuals to participate in a scheme (see Part 3),
the shares to which schemes can apply (see Part 4),
the existence of a linked savings arrangement (see Part 5),
the share options that may be granted under the scheme (see Part 6), and
the exchange of share options (see Part 7).

Text.Substitution: Sub-paragraph (A1) is subject to Part 8 of this Schedule which—
requires notice of a scheme to be given to Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (“
HMRC
”) in order for the scheme to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme (see paragraph 40A(1)),
provides for a scheme in relation to which such notice is given to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme (see paragraph 40A(4)), and
gives power to
HMRC
to enquire into a scheme and to decide that the scheme should not be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme (see paragraphs 40F to 40I).

P2para.Text: In the SAYE code an “SAYE option scheme” means (in accordance with section 516(4)) a scheme established by a company which provides—

P3para.Text: for share options to be granted to employees and directors, and
for the shares acquired by the exercise of the share options to be paid for in the way mentioned in paragraph 24 (payments for shares to be linked to approved savings arrangements).

P2para.Text: In the SAYE code, in relation to an SAYE option scheme—

Para.Text: “participant” means an individual who has been granted (but has not yet exercised) share options under the scheme (“the options”);
“participate” means obtain and exercise share options under the scheme;
“the scheme organiser” means the company which has established the scheme.

P2para.Text: An SAYE option scheme established by a company that controls one or more other companies (a “parent scheme company”) may extend to all or any of those other companies.
In the SAYE code an SAYE option scheme established by a parent scheme company which so extends is called a “group scheme”.
In relation to a group scheme a “constituent company” means—

P3para.Text: the parent scheme company, or
any other company to which for the time being the scheme is expressed to extend.

P2para.Text: Paragraph 46 deals with jointly owned companies and companies controlled by them.

P1para.Text: An SAYE option scheme must meet the requirements of—

Para.Text: paragraph 5 (general restriction on contents of scheme),
paragraph 6 (all-employee nature of scheme),
paragraph 7 (participation on similar terms), and
paragraph 8 (no preferential treatment for directors and senior employees).

Title.Emphasis: General restriction on contents of scheme

Text.Substitution: The purpose of the scheme must be to provide, in accordance with this Schedule, benefits for employees and directors in the form of share options.
The scheme must not provide benefits to employees or directors otherwise than in accordance with this Schedule.
For example, the scheme must not provide cash as an alternative to share options or shares which might otherwise be acquired by the exercise of share options.

P2para.Text: The scheme must provide that every person who meets the conditions in sub-paragraph (2) is eligible to participate in the scheme.
A person (“E”) meets the conditions in this sub-paragraph if—

P3para.Text: E is an employee or a full-time director of the scheme organiser or (in the case of a group scheme) of a constituent company,
E has been such an employee or director at all times during a qualifying period of not more than 5 years,

Text.Substitution: E's earnings from the office or employment within paragraph (a) are (or would be if there were any) general earnings to which section 15 applies (earnings for year when employee
UK
resident),

P3para.Text: E is not ineligible under paragraph 11 (the “no material interest” requirement).

P2para.Text: The scheme must not contain any feature which has or is likely to have the effect of discouraging any description of persons who—

P3para.Text: meet the conditions in sub-paragraph (2), or
met those conditions before ceasing to be persons within sub-paragraph (2)(a),

P2para.Text: from actually participating in the scheme.
Sub-paragraph (3) does not apply to any provision required or authorised by a provision of this Schedule.
The requirements of this paragraph are—

P3para.Text: that every person who meets the conditions in paragraph 6(2) (all-employee nature of scheme) must be eligible to participate in the scheme on similar terms, and
that every person who participates in the scheme must actually do so on similar terms.

P2para.Text: The requirements of this paragraph are not infringed by the fact that the rights of those participating in the scheme to obtain and exercise share options vary according to—

P3para.Text: the levels of their remuneration,
the length of their service, or
any similar factors.

Title.Emphasis: No preferential treatment for directors and senior employees

P2para.Text: The requirement of this paragraph is that, if the scheme organiser is a member of a group of companies, the scheme does not and is not likely to have the effect of conferring benefits wholly or mainly—

P3para.Text: on directors of companies in the group, or
on employees of companies in the group who receive the higher or highest levels of remuneration.

P2para.Text: “A group of companies” means a company and any other companies of which it has control.

Part.Title: Eligibility of individuals to participate in scheme

Title.Emphasis: Requirements relating to the eligibility of individuals: introduction

P1para.Text: An SAYE option scheme must meet the requirements of—

Para.Text: paragraph 10 (the employment requirement),

P2para.Text: The scheme must ensure that an individual is not eligible to participate in the scheme at a particular time unless the individual is then a director or employee of—

P3para.Text: the scheme organiser, or
in the case of a group scheme, a constituent company.

P2para.Text: The requirement of this paragraph is not infringed by a provision of the scheme required or authorised by a provision of this Schedule.

Title.Emphasis: Material interest: options and interests in SIPs
Meaning of “associate”: trustees of employee benefit trust
Meaning of “associate”: trustees of discretionary trust

Part.Title: Shares to which schemes can apply

Title.Emphasis: Requirements relating to shares that may be subject to share options: introduction

P2para.Text: An SAYE option scheme must meet the requirements of—

Para.Text: paragraph 18 (shares must be ordinary shares of certain companies),
paragraph 19 (requirements as to listing),
paragraph 20 (shares must be fully paid up and not redeemable), and
paragraph 22 (requirements as to other shareholdings).

Text.Addition: Sub-paragraph (1) and the other paragraphs of this Part are subject to paragraph 37(6B).

P2para.Text: In this Part “eligible shares” means shares which may be acquired by the exercise of share options under the scheme.

Title.Emphasis: Shares must be ordinary shares of certain companies

P1para.Text: Eligible shares must form part of the ordinary share capital of—

P3para.Text: the scheme organiser,
a company which has control of the scheme organiser, or
a company which either is, or has control of, a company which is a member of a consortium owning either the scheme organiser or a company having control of the scheme organiser.

P2para.Text: Eligible shares must be—

P3para.Text: shares of a class listed on a recognised stock exchange,
shares in a company which is not under the control of another company, ...

Text.Addition: shares in a company which is subject to an employee-ownership trust (within the meaning of paragraph 27(4) to (6) of Schedule 2), or

P3para.Text: shares in a company which is under the control of a listed company.

P2para.Text: A “listed company” is a company whose shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange, other than—

P3para.Text: a close company, or
a company that would be a close company if resident in the United Kingdom.

Text.Addition: But a company is not a close company for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2) if it is subject to an employee-ownership trust (within the meaning of paragraph 27(4) to (6) of Schedule 2).

Title.Emphasis: Shares must be fully paid up and not redeemable

P1para.Text: Eligible shares must be—

P3para.Text: fully paid up, and
not redeemable.

Title.Emphasis: Only certain kinds of restriction allowed

P2para.Text: The majority of the issued shares of the same class as the eligible shares must be—

P3para.Text: employee-control shares, or
open market shares,

P2para.Text: unless the eligible shares are shares in a company whose ordinary share capital consists of shares of one class only.
Shares in a company are “employee-control shares” if—

P3para.Text: the persons holding the shares are, by virtue of their holding, together able to control the company, and
those persons are or have been employees or directors of the company or of another company which is under the control of the company.

P2para.Text: Shares in a company are “open market shares” if the persons holding the shares are not—

P3para.Text: persons who acquired their shares as a result of a right conferred on them or an opportunity afforded to them as a director or employee of the scheme organiser or any other company, and not as a result of an offer to the public, or
trustees holding shares on behalf of persons who acquired their beneficial interests in the shares as mentioned in paragraph (a), or
in the case of shares which—

P4para.Text: are not of a class listed on a recognised stock exchange, and
are in a company which is under the control of a listed company (as defined by paragraph 19(2)),

P3para.Text: companies which have control of the company whose shares are in question or of which that company is an associated company.

Title.Emphasis: Requirements as to linked savings arrangement : introduction

P1para.Text: An SAYE option scheme must meet the requirements of—

Para.Text: paragraph 24 (payments for shares to be linked to approved savings arrangements), and
paragraph 25 (requirements as to contributions to savings arrangements).

Title.Emphasis: Payments for shares to be linked to approved savings arrangements

P2para.Text: The scheme must provide for shares acquired by the exercise of share options granted under the scheme to be paid for with money not exceeding the amount of repayments made and any interest paid under a certified SAYE savings arrangement which has been approved by an officer of Revenue and Customs for the purposes of this Schedule (“the approved savings arrangement”).

Title.Emphasis: Requirements as to contributions to savings arrangements

P2para.Text: The scheme must provide for a person’s contributions under the the approved savings arrangement to be of an amount that will secure, as nearly as possible, repayment of an amount equal to the option price.
The “option price” means the amount payable, on exercising share options granted under the scheme, in order to acquire the maximum number of shares that may be acquired under them (see paragraph 28).
The scheme must neither—

P3para.Text: permit the aggregate amount of a person’s contributions under certified SAYE savings arrangements linked to Schedule 3 SAYE option schemes to exceed £500 per month, nor
impose a minimum on the amount of a person’s contributions which exceeds £10 per month.

P2para.Text: The Treasury may by order amend sub-paragraph (3) by substituting for any amount for the time being specified there an amount specified in the order.

Title.Emphasis: Repayments under a savings arrangement : whether bonuses included

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this Schedule repayments under a certified SAYE savings arrangement may be taken as including, or as not including, a bonus.
The bonus may either be the maximum bonus under that arrangement or a lesser bonus.
An SAYE option scheme must require the question whether repayments are to be taken as including bonuses to be determined at the time when share options are granted.

Part.Title: Requirements etc. relating to share options

Title.Emphasis: Requirements etc. relating to share options: introduction

P2para.Text: An SAYE option scheme must meet the requirements of—

Para.Text: paragraph 28 (requirements as to price for acquisition of shares),
paragraph 29 (share options must not be transferable),
paragraph 30 (time for exercising options: general),
paragraph 32 (exercise of options: death), and
paragraph 34 (exercise of options: scheme-related employment ends).

P2para.Text: An SAYE option scheme may make any provision authorised by—

Para.Text: paragraph 36 (exercise of options: employment in associated company at bonus date), and
paragraph 37 (exercise of options: company events).

Title.Emphasis: Requirements as to price for acquisition of shares

P2para.Text: The price at which shares may be acquired by the exercise of a share option granted under the scheme—

P3para.Text: must be stated at the time when the option is granted, and
must not be manifestly less than 80% of the market value of shares of the same class—

Text.Substitution: at that time, or
at such earlier time as may be determined in accordance with guidance issued by the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs.

P3para.Text: This is subject to sub-paragraph (3).

P2para.Text: The scheme may provide for one or more of the following—

P3para.Text: the price at which shares may be acquired by the exercise of a share option granted under the scheme,
the number of shares which may be so acquired, or
the description of shares which may be so acquired,

P2para.Text: to be varied so far as necessary to take account of a variation in the share capital of which the shares form part.

Text.Addition: If the scheme makes provision under sub-paragraph (3), the variation or variations made under that provision to take account of a variation in any share capital must (in particular) secure—

that the total market value of the shares which may be acquired by the exercise of the share option is immediately after the variation or variations substantially the same as what it was immediately before the variation or variations, and
that the total price at which those shares may be acquired is immediately after the variation or variations substantially the same as what it was immediately before the variation or variations.
Sub-paragraph (3) does not authorise any variation which would result in the requirements of the other paragraphs of this Schedule not being met in relation to the share option.
At the time a share option is granted—
it must be stated whether or not the shares which may be acquired by the exercise of the option may be subject to any restriction, and
if so, the details of the restriction must also be stated.
For the purposes of this paragraph the market value of shares subject to a restriction is to be determined as if they were not subject to the restriction.

Title.Emphasis: Share options must not be transferable

P2para.Text: The scheme must ensure that share options granted to a participant are not capable of being transferred by the participant.
Paragraph 32 provides for the exercise of the options where the participant has died.
The scheme must ensure that share options granted under it must not be capable of being exercised—

P3para.Text: before the bonus date, or
later than 6 months after that date.

P2para.Text: However, in sub-paragraph (1)—

P3para.Text: paragraph (a) is subject to paragraphs 32, 34 and 37 (exercise of options in the event of death, ... scheme-related employment ending or certain events occurring in relation to the company), and
paragraph (b) is subject to paragraph 32.

P2para.Text: In the SAYE code “the bonus date” means the date on which repayments under the approved savings arrangement are due.
For this purpose repayments are to be regarded as due as follows—

P3para.Text: if the repayments are to be taken as including the maximum bonus (see paragraph 26(2)), on the earliest date on which that bonus is payable, and
in any other case, on the earliest date on which a bonus is payable.

P1para.Text: The scheme must provide that, if a participant dies before exercising the options, they may be exercised at any time on or after the date of death but not later than—

P3para.Text: 12 months after the date of death, in a case where the participant dies before the bonus date, or
12 months after the bonus date, in a case where the participant dies on or within 6 months after that date.

Title.Emphasis: Exercise of options: reaching specified age without retiring
Exercise of options: scheme-related employment ends

P2para.Text: The scheme must provide that, if a participant (“P”) no longer holds scheme-related employment (see paragraph 35), the options are exercisable as set out in sub-paragraphs (2) to (4).
In a case where P ceases to hold the scheme-related employment because of—

P3para.Text: injury or disability or redundancy within the meaning of ERA 1996 or ER(NI)O 1996 , ...
retirement ...,

Text.Addition: a relevant transfer within the meaning of the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006, or

if P holds office or is employed in a company which is an associated company (as defined in paragraph 35(4)) of the scheme organiser, that company ceasing to be an associated company of the scheme organiser by reason of a change of control (as determined in accordance with sections 450 and 451 of CTA 2010),

P2para.Text: the options may only be exercised within 6 months after the termination date.
In a case where P ceases to hold the scheme-related employment for any other reason, share options granted more than 3 years before the termination date either—

P3para.Text: may not be exercised, or
may only be exercised within 6 months after the termination date,

P2para.Text: according to which of these alternatives is specified in the scheme.

Subject to any provision made under sub-paragraph (5), in a case where P ceases to hold the scheme-related employment for any reason other than one within sub-paragraph (2)(a) to (d), share options granted 3 years or less before the termination date may not be exercised at all.
The scheme may make provision about the time when the options may be exercised in a case where P ceases to hold the scheme-related employment only because—

P3para.Text: it relates to a business or part of a business which is transferred to a person who is not an associated company of the scheme organiser where the transfer is not a relevant transfer within the meaning of the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006.

Text.Addition: If the scheme makes provision by virtue of sub-paragraph (5), the provision must be either—
that the options may be exercised within 6 months after the termination date, or

that the options may be exercised within 6 months after the date (if any) when P ceases to hold the employment which (before the termination date) was the scheme-related employment for a reason within sub-paragraph (2)(a)

P2para.Text: This paragraph has effect subject to paragraph 30(1)(b) (options must not be capable of being exercised later than 6 months after bonus date).
In this paragraph—

Para.Text: “scheme-related employment” means the office or employment by reference to which the person satisfies the condition in paragraph 10(1) (“the employment requirement”);
“the termination date” means the date when P ceases to hold the scheme-related employment (see paragraph 35).

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies for the purposes of paragraph 34 (exercise of options: scheme-related employment ends).
Unless sub-paragraph (3) applies, a participant (“P”) is to be regarded as ceasing to hold scheme-related employment on the date when the office or employment in question terminates.
If—

P3para.Text: P’s scheme-related employment terminates, but
P continues to hold an office or employment in the scheme organiser or any associated company,

P2para.Text: P is to be regarded as ceasing to hold the scheme-related employment on the date when P no longer holds any office or employment within paragraph (b), and not at any earlier time.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (3) one company is an “associated company” of another company if—

P3para.Text: one has control of the other, or
both are under the control of the same person or persons;

P2para.Text: and for this purpose the question of whether a person controls a company is to be determined in accordance with sections 450 and 451 of CTA 2010 (“control” in the context of close companies).
Nothing in paragraph 34 or this paragraph applies where a person’s scheme-related employment terminates on that person’s death (see instead paragraph 32).
In this paragraph “scheme-related employment” has the same meaning as in paragraph 34.

Title.Emphasis: Exercise of options: employment in associated company at bonus date

P1para.Text: The scheme may provide that if at the bonus date a participant holds an office or employment in a company which is—

P3para.Text: an associated company of the scheme organiser, but
not a constituent company,

P1para.Text: the options may be exercised within 6 months after that date.

P2para.Text: The scheme may provide that share options relating to shares in a company may be exercised within 6 months after the relevant date for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2), (4) , (4ZA) , (4A) or (5).
The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date when—

P3para.Text: a person has obtained control of the company as a result of making an offer falling within sub-paragraph (3), and
any condition subject to which the offer is made has been satisfied.

P2para.Text: An offer falls within this sub-paragraph if it is—

P3para.Text: a general offer to acquire the whole of the issued ordinary share capital of the company, which is made on a condition such that, if it is met, the person making the offer will have control of the company, or
a general offer to acquire all the shares in the company which are of the same class as the shares in question obtained under the scheme.

Text.Addition: In sub-paragraph (3)(a) the reference to the issued ordinary share capital of the company does not include any capital already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person and in sub-paragraph (3)(b) the reference to the shares in the company does not include any shares already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (3)(a) and (b) it does not matter if the general offer is made to different shareholders by different means.

P2para.Text: The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date when the court sanctions under section 899 of the Companies Act 2006 (court sanction for compromise or arrangement) a compromise or arrangement applicable to or affecting—

Text.Substitution: all the ordinary share capital of the company or all the shares of the same class as the shares to which the option relates, or
all the shares, or all the shares of that same class, which are held by a class of shareholders identified otherwise than by reference to their employment or directorships or their participation in
SAYE
option scheme.

Text.Addition: The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date when the court sanctions under section 901F of the Companies Act 2006 (court sanction for compromise or arrangement) a compromise or arrangement applicable to or affecting—
all the ordinary share capital of the company or all the shares of the same class as the shares to which the option relates, or

all the shares, or all the shares of that same class, which are held by a class of shareholders identified otherwise than by reference to their employment or directorships or their participation in a Schedule 3 SAYE option scheme.
The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date on which a non-UK company reorganisation arrangement applicable to or affecting—
all the ordinary share capital of the company or all the shares of the same class as the shares to which the option relates, or

all the shares, or all the shares of that same class, which are held by a class of shareholders identified otherwise than by reference to their employments or directorships or their participation in a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme,
becomes binding on the shareholders covered by it.

P2para.Text: The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date when the company passes a resolution for voluntary winding up.

The scheme may provide that share options relating to shares in a company may be exercised at any time when any person is bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company under sections 979 to 982 or 983 to 985 of the Companies Act 2006 (takeover offers: right of offeror to buy out minority shareholder etc).

Text.Addition: Sub-paragraphs (6B) to (6F) apply if the scheme makes provision under sub-paragraph (1) or (6).

The scheme may provide that if, in consequence of a relevant event, shares in the company to which a share option relates no longer meet the requirements of Part 4 of this Schedule, the share option may be exercised under the provision made under sub-paragraph (1) or (6) (as the case may be) no later than 20 days after the day on which the relevant event occurs, notwithstanding that the shares no longer meet the requirements of Part 4 of this Schedule.
In sub-paragraph (6B) “
” means—
a person obtaining control of the company as mentioned in sub-paragraph (2)(a);
a person obtaining control of the company as a result of a compromise or arrangement sanctioned by the court as mentioned in sub-paragraph (4)
a person obtaining control of the company as a result of a non-UK company reorganisation arrangement which has become binding on the shareholders covered by it as mentioned in sub-paragraph (4A);
a person who is bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company as mentioned in sub-paragraph (6) obtaining control of the company.
Provision made under sub-paragraph (6B) may not authorise the exercise of a share option, as the case may be—
at a time outside the 6 month period mentioned in sub-paragraph (1), or
at a time not covered by sub-paragraph (6).
The scheme may provide that a share option relating to shares in a company which is exercised during the period of 20 days ending with—
the relevant date for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2), (4)
or (4A), or
the date on which any person becomes bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company as mentioned in sub-paragraph (6),
is to be treated as if it had been exercised in accordance with the provision made under sub-paragraph (1) or (6) (as the case may be).
If the scheme makes provision under sub-paragraph (6E) it must also provide that if—
a share option is exercised in reliance on that provision in anticipation of—
an event mentioned in sub-paragraph (2), (4)
or (4A) occurring, or
a person becoming bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company as mentioned in sub-paragraph (6), but
as the case may be—
the relevant date for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2), (4)
or (4A) does not fall during the period of 20 days beginning with the date on which the share option is exercised, or
the person does not become bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company by the end of the period of 20 days beginning with the date on which the share option is exercised,
the exercise of the share option is to be treated as having had no effect.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this paragraph—

P3para.Text: “share options” means share options granted under the scheme; and
a person is to be treated as obtaining control of a company if that person and others acting in concert together obtain control of it.

P2para.Text: This paragraph has effect subject to paragraph 30(1)(b) (options must not be capable of being exercised later than 6 months after bonus date).

Title.Emphasis: Exchange of options on company reorganisation

P2para.Text: An SAYE option scheme may provide that if—

P3para.Text: there is a company reorganisation affecting a scheme company (that is, a company whose shares may be acquired by the exercise of share options obtained under the scheme: see paragraph 18), and
a participant has obtained share options under the scheme which are to acquire shares of the scheme company (“the old options”),

P2para.Text: the participant may agree with the acquiring company to release the old options in consideration of the participant being granted new share options.
For the purposes of this paragraph there is a company reorganisation affecting a scheme company if another company (“the acquiring company”)—

P3para.Text: obtains control of the scheme company—

P4para.Text: as a result of making a general offer to acquire the whole of the issued ordinary share capital of the scheme company which is made on a condition such that, if it is met, the person making the offer will have control of that company, or
as a result of making a general offer to acquire all the shares in the scheme company which are of the same class as those subject to the old options;

Text.Substitution: obtains control of the scheme company as a result of a compromise or arrangement sanctioned by the court under section 899
of the Companies Act 2006 (court sanction for compromise or arrangement);

Substitution.Addition: obtains control of the scheme company as a result of a non-UK company reorganisation arrangement which has become binding on the shareholders covered by it; or

Text.Substitution: becomes bound or entitled to acquire shares in the scheme company under sections 979 to 982
of that Act (takeover offers: right of offeror to buy out minority shareholder

Text.Addition: In sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) the reference to the issued ordinary share capital of the scheme company does not include any capital already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person and in sub-paragraph (2)(a)(ii) the reference to the shares in the scheme company does not include any shares already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) and (ii) it does not matter if the general offer is made to different shareholders by different means.

P2para.Text: A scheme that makes provision under sub-paragraph (1) must require the agreement referred to in that sub-paragraph to be made—

P3para.Text: where control is obtained in the way set out in sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) or (ii), within the period of 6 months beginning with the time when the acquiring company obtains control and any condition subject to which the offer is made is met,
where control is obtained in the way set out in sub-paragraph (2)(b), within the period of 6 months beginning with the time when the court sanctions the compromise or arrangement, ...

Text.Addition: where control is obtained in the way set out in sub-paragraph (2)(ba), within the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which the non-UK company reorganisation arrangement becomes binding on the shareholders covered by it, and

P3para.Text: where sub-paragraph (2)(c) applies, within the period during which the acquiring company remains bound or entitled as mentioned in that provision.

Title.Emphasis: Requirements about share options granted in exchange

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies to a scheme that makes provision under paragraph 38 (exchange of options on company reorganisation).
The scheme must require the new share options to relate to shares in a company which—

P3para.Text: is different from the company whose shares are subject to the old options, and
is either the acquiring company itself or some other company within sub-paragraph (b) or (c) of paragraph 18 (shares must be ordinary shares of certain companies), namely—

P4para.Text: a company which has control of the scheme organiser, or
a company which is, or has control of a company which is, a member of a consortium owning either the scheme organiser or a company having control of the scheme organiser.
For this purpose the control in question may be through the medium of the acquiring company.

P2para.Text: The scheme must also require the new share options to be equivalent to the old options.
For the new options to be regarded as equivalent to the old options—

P3para.Text: the shares to which they relate must meet the conditions in paragraphs 18 to 22 (types of share that may be used),
they must be exercisable in the same manner as the old options and subject to the provisions of the scheme as it had effect immediately before the release of the old options,

the total market value of the shares subject to the old options immediately before the release of those options by the participant must be substantially the same as the total market value, immediately after the grant of the new options to the participant, of the shares subject to those options, and

the total amount payable by the participant for the acquisition of shares under the new options must be substantially the same as the total amount that would have been so payable under the old options.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the SAYE code, new share options granted under the terms of a provision included in a scheme under paragraph 38 are to be treated as having been granted at the time when the corresponding old options were granted.
This also applies for the purposes of the provisions of the scheme in their operation, after the grant of the new options, by virtue of a condition complying with sub-paragraph (4)(b).

Text.Addition: For the purposes of this paragraph the market value of shares subject to a restriction is to be determined as if they were not subject to the restriction.
For the purposes of this paragraph the market value of any shares is to be determined using a methodology agreed by Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs.

Title.Substitution: Notification of schemes, annual returns and enquiries
Notice of scheme to be given to

Text.Substitution: For an
SAYE
option scheme to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme, notice of the scheme must be given to Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (“
HMRC
The notice must—
be given by the scheme organiser,
contain, or be accompanied by, such information as
HMRC
may require, and
contain a declaration within sub-paragraph (3) made by such persons as
HMRC
may require.
A declaration within this sub-paragraph is a declaration—
that the requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule are met in relation to the scheme, and
if the declaration is made after the first date on which share options are granted under the scheme (“the first grant date”), that those requirements—
were met in relation to those grants of share options, and
have otherwise been met in relation to the scheme at all times on or after the first grant date when share options granted under the scheme are outstanding.
If notice is given under this paragraph in relation to an
SAYE
option scheme, for the purposes of the
SAYE
code the scheme is to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme at all times on and after the relevant date (but not before that date).
But if the notice is given after the initial notification deadline, the scheme is to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme only from the beginning of the relevant tax year.

Substitution.Addition: Sub-paragraph (5) does not apply if the scheme organiser satisfies
(or, on an appeal under paragraph 40K, the tribunal) that there is a reasonable excuse for the failure to give notice on or before the initial notification deadline.
Paragraph 40C(9) (what constitutes a reasonable excuse) applies for the purposes of sub-paragraph (5A).
are required under sub-paragraph (5A) to consider whether there was a reasonable excuse,
must notify the scheme organiser of their decision within the period of 45 days beginning with the day on which
received the scheme organiser's request to consider the excuse.
are required to notify the scheme organiser as specified in sub-paragraph (5C) but do not do so—
are to be treated as having decided that there was no reasonable excuse, and
must notify the scheme organiser of the decision which they are treated as having made.

Text.Substitution: For the purposes of this Part—
“the initial notification deadline” is 6 July in the tax year following that in which the first grant date falls,
”, in relation to a share option, means that the option—
has not been exercised, but
is capable of being exercised in accordance with the scheme (whether on the meeting of any condition or otherwise),
“the relevant date” is—
the date on which the declaration within sub-paragraph (3) is made, or
if that declaration is made after the first grant date, the first grant date, and
“the relevant tax year” is—
the tax year in which the notice under this paragraph is given, or
if that notice is given on or before 6 July in that tax year, the preceding tax year.
Sub-paragraph (4) is subject to the following paragraphs of this Part.
This paragraph applies if notice is given in relation to an
SAYE
option scheme under paragraph 40A.
The scheme organiser must give to
HMRC
a return for the tax year in which the relevant date falls and for each subsequent tax year (subject to sub-paragraph (9)).
If paragraph 40A(5) applies in relation to the scheme, in sub-paragraph (2) the reference to the tax year in which the relevant date falls is to be read as a reference to the relevant tax year.
A return for a tax year must—
contain, or be accompanied by, such information as
HMRC
may require, and
be given on or before 6 July in the following tax year.
The information which may be required under sub-paragraph (4)(a) includes (in particular) information to enable
HMRC
to determine the liability to tax, including capital gains tax, of—
any person who has participated in the scheme, or
any other person whose liability to tax the operation of the scheme is relevant to.
If during a tax year—
an alteration is made in a key feature of the scheme, or
variations are made under a provision made under paragraph 28(3) to take account of a variation in any share capital,
the return for the tax year must contain a declaration within sub-paragraph (7) made by such persons as
HMRC
may require.
A declaration within this sub-paragraph is a declaration, as the case may be—
that the alteration has, or
that the variations have,
not caused the requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule not to be met in relation to the scheme.

For the purposes of sub-paragraph (6)(a) a “key feature” of a scheme is a provision of the scheme which is necessary in order for the requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule to be met in relation to the scheme.
A return is not required for any tax year following that in which the termination condition is met in relation to the scheme.
For the purposes of this Part “the termination condition” is met in relation to a scheme when—
all share options granted under the scheme—
have been exercised, or
are no longer capable of being exercised in accordance with the scheme (because, for example, they have lapsed or been cancelled), and
no more share options will be granted under the scheme.
If the scheme organiser becomes aware that—
anything which should have been included in, or should have accompanied, a return for a tax year was not included in, or did not accompany, the return,
anything which should not have been included in, or should not have accompanied, a return for a tax year was included in, or accompanied, the return, or
any other error or inaccuracy has occurred in relation to a return for a tax year,
the scheme organiser must give an amended return correcting the position to
HMRC
without delay.

This paragraph applies if the scheme organiser fails to give a return for a tax year (containing, or accompanied by, all required information and declarations) on or before the date mentioned in paragraph 40B(4)(b) (“the date for delivery”).
The scheme organiser is liable for a penalty of £100.
If the scheme organiser's failure continues after the end of the period of 3 months beginning with the date for delivery, the scheme organiser is liable for a further penalty of £300.
If the scheme organiser's failure continues after the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the date for delivery, the scheme organiser is liable for a further penalty of £300.
The scheme organiser is liable for a further penalty under this sub-paragraph if—
the scheme organiser's failure continues after the end of the period of 9 months beginning with the date for delivery,
HMRC
decide that such a penalty should be payable, and
HMRC
give notice to the scheme organiser specifying the period in respect of which the penalty is payable.
(The scheme organiser may be liable for more than one penalty under this sub-paragraph.)
The penalty under sub-paragraph (5) is £10 for each day that the failure continues during the period specified in the notice under sub-paragraph (5)(c).
The period specified in the notice under sub-paragraph (5)(c)—
may begin earlier than the date on which the notice is given, but

may not begin until after the end of the period mentioned in sub-paragraph (5)(a) or, if relevant, the end of any period specified in any previous notice under sub-paragraph (5)(c) given in relation to the failure.
Liability for a penalty under this paragraph does not arise if the scheme organiser satisfies
HMRC
(or, on an appeal under paragraph 40K, the tribunal) that there is a reasonable excuse for its failure.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (8)—
an insufficiency of funds is not a reasonable excuse, unless attributable to events outside the scheme organiser's control,
where the scheme organiser relies on any other person to do anything, that is not a reasonable excuse unless the scheme organiser took reasonable care to avoid the failure, and

where the scheme organiser had a reasonable excuse for the failure but the excuse ceased, the scheme organiser is to be treated as having continued to have the excuse if the failure is remedied without unreasonable delay after the excuse ceased.

Title.Substitution: Notices and returns to be given electronically

Text.Substitution: A notice under paragraph 40A, and any information accompanying the notice, must be given electronically.
A return under paragraph 40B, and any information accompanying the return, must be given electronically.
But, if
HMRC
consider it appropriate to do so,
HMRC
may allow the scheme organiser to give a notice or return or any accompanying information in another way; and, if
HMRC
do so, the notice, return or information must be given in that other way.
The Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs—
must prescribe how notices, returns and accompanying information are to be given electronically;
may make different provision for different cases or circumstances.
This paragraph applies if a return under paragraph 40B, or any information accompanying such a return—
is given otherwise than in accordance with paragraph 40D, or
contains a material inaccuracy—
which is careless or deliberate, or
which is not corrected as required by paragraph 40B(11).
The scheme organiser is liable for a penalty of an amount decided by HMRC.
The penalty must not exceed £5,000.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (1)(b)(i) an inaccuracy is careless if it is due to a failure by the scheme organiser to take reasonable care.
This paragraph applies if notice is given in relation to an
SAYE
option scheme under paragraph 40A.
HMRC
may enquire into the scheme if
HMRC
give notice to the scheme organiser of
HMRC
's intention to do so no later than—
6 July in the tax year following the tax year in which the initial notification deadline falls, or
if the notice under paragraph 40A is given after the initial notification deadline, 6 July in the second tax year following the relevant tax year.
HMRC
may enquire into the scheme if
HMRC
give notice to the scheme organiser of
HMRC
's intention to do so no later than 12 months after the date on which a declaration within paragraph 40B(7) is given to HMRC.
Sub-paragraph (5) applies if (at any time)
HMRC
have reasonable grounds for believing that requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule—
are not met in relation to the scheme, or
have not been met in relation to the scheme.
HMRC
may enquire into the scheme if
HMRC
give notice to the scheme organiser of
HMRC
's intention to do so.
Notice may be given, and an enquiry may be conducted, under sub-paragraph (2), (3) or (5) even though the termination condition is met in relation to the scheme.
An enquiry under paragraph 40F(2), (3) or (5) is completed when
HMRC
give the scheme organiser a notice (a “closure notice”) stating—
that
HMRC
have completed the enquiry, and
that—
paragraph 40H is to apply,
paragraph 40I is to apply, or
neither paragraph 40H nor paragraph 40I is to apply.

If the scheme organiser receives notice under paragraph 40F(2), (3) or (5), the scheme organiser may make an application to the tribunal for a direction requiring a closure notice for the enquiry to be given within a specified period.
The application is to be subject to the relevant provisions of Part 5 of
TMA
1970 (see, in particular, section 48(2)(b) of that Act).
The tribunal must give a direction unless satisfied that
HMRC
have reasonable grounds for not giving the closure notice within the specified period.
This paragraph applies if
HMRC
decide—
that requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule—
are not met in relation to the scheme, or
have not been met in relation to the scheme, and
that the situation is, or was, so serious that this paragraph should apply.
If this paragraph applies—
the scheme is not to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme with effect from—
such relevant time as is specified in the closure notice, or
if no relevant time is specified, the time of the giving of the closure notice, and
the scheme organiser is liable for a penalty of an amount decided by HMRC.
Sub-paragraph (4) applies in relation to a share option granted under the scheme if the option—
is granted at a time before that mentioned in sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be) when the scheme is a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme, but
is exercised at or after the time mentioned in sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be).
For the purposes of section 519 (exemption in respect of exercise of share option) in its application to the option, the scheme is to be taken still to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme at the time of the exercise of the option.
The penalty under sub-paragraph (2)(b) must not exceed an amount equal to twice
HMRC
's reasonable estimate of—
the total income tax for which persons who have been granted share options under the scheme have not been liable, or will not be liable in the future, and
the total contributions under Part 1 of
SSCBA
1992 or SSCB(
NI
)A 1992 for which any persons have not been liable, or will not be liable in the future,
in consequence of the scheme having been a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme at any relevant time before the time mentioned in sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be).
The liabilities covered by sub-paragraph (5) include liabilities for income tax or contributions which a person has not had, or will not have, in consequence of sub-paragraph (4).
In this paragraph “
” means any time before the giving of the closure notice when requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule were not met in relation to the scheme.
This paragraph applies if
HMRC
decide—
that requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule—
are not met in relation to the scheme, or
have not been met in relation to the scheme, but
that the situation is not, or was not, so serious that paragraph 40H should apply.
If this paragraph applies, the scheme organiser—
is liable for a penalty of an amount decided by
HMRC
, and
must, no later than 90 days after the relevant day, secure that the requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule are met in relation to the scheme.
The penalty under sub-paragraph (2)(a) must not exceed £5,000.
In sub-paragraph (2)(b) “
” means—
the last day of the period in which notice of an appeal under paragraph 40K(2)(b) may be given, or
if notice of such an appeal is given, the day on which the appeal is determined or withdrawn.

Sub-paragraph (2)(b) does not apply if the termination condition was met in relation to the scheme before the closure notice was given or is met before the end of the 90 day period mentioned in sub-paragraph (2)(b).
If the scheme organiser fails to comply with sub-paragraph (2)(b),
HMRC
may give the scheme organiser a notice stating that that is the case (a “default notice”).
If the scheme organiser is given a default notice—
the scheme is not to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme with effect from—
such relevant time as is specified in the default notice, or
if no relevant time is specified, the time of the giving of the default notice, and
the scheme organiser is liable for a further penalty of an amount decided by HMRC.
Sub-paragraph (9) applies in relation to a share option granted under the scheme if the option—
is granted at a time before that mentioned in sub-paragraph (7)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be) when the scheme is a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme, but
is exercised at or after the time mentioned in sub-paragraph (7)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be).
For the purposes of section 519 (exemption in respect of exercise of share option) in its application to the option, the scheme is to be taken still to be a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme at the time of the exercise of the option.
The penalty under sub-paragraph (7)(b) must not exceed an amount equal to twice
HMRC
's reasonable estimate of—
the total income tax for which persons who have been granted share options under the scheme have not been liable, or will not be liable in the future, and
the total contributions under Part 1 of
SSCBA
1992 or SSCB(
NI
)A 1992 for which any persons have not been liable, or will not be liable in the future,
in consequence of the scheme having been a Schedule 3
SAYE
option scheme at any relevant time before the time mentioned in sub-paragraph (7)(a)(i) or (ii) (as the case may be).
The liabilities covered by sub-paragraph (10) include liabilities for income tax or contributions which a person has not had, or will not have, in consequence of sub-paragraph (9).
In this paragraph “
” means any time before the giving of the default notice when requirements of Parts 2 to 7 of this Schedule were not met in relation to the scheme.
This paragraph applies if the scheme organiser is liable for a penalty under this Part.
HMRC
must assess the penalty and notify the scheme organiser of the assessment.
Subject to sub-paragraphs (4) and (5), the assessment must be made no later than 12 months after the date on which the scheme organiser becomes liable for the penalty.
In the case of a penalty under paragraph 40E(1)(b), the assessment must be made no later than—
12 months after the date on which
HMRC
become aware of the inaccuracy, and
6 years after the date on which the scheme organiser becomes liable for the penalty.

In the case of a penalty under paragraph 40H(2)(b) or 40I(2)(a) or (7)(b) where notice of appeal is given under paragraph 40K(2) or (3), the assessment must be made no later than 12 months after the date on which the appeal is determined or withdrawn.
A penalty payable under this Part must be paid—
no later than 30 days after the date on which the notice under sub-paragraph (2) is given to the scheme organiser, or
if notice of appeal is given against the penalty under paragraph 40K(1) or (4), no later than 30 days after the date on which the appeal is determined or withdrawn.
The penalty may be enforced as if it were corporation tax or, if the scheme organiser is not within the charge to corporation tax, income tax charged in an assessment and due and payable.
Sections 100 to 103 of
TMA
1970 do not apply to a penalty under this Part.

Substitution.Addition: The scheme organiser may appeal against a decision of
under paragraph 40A(5A) that there was no reasonable excuse for the failure to give notice on or before the initial notification deadline.

Text.Substitution: The scheme organiser may appeal against a decision of
HMRC
that the scheme organiser is liable for a penalty under paragraph 40C or 40E.
The scheme organiser may appeal against—
a decision of
HMRC
mentioned in paragraph 40H(1) or a decision of
HMRC
to specify, or not to specify, a relevant time in the closure notice;
a decision of
HMRC
mentioned in paragraph 40I(1).
The scheme organiser may appeal against a decision of
HMRC
to give the scheme organiser a default notice under paragraph 40I;
to specify, or not to specify, a relevant time in the default notice.
The scheme organiser may appeal against a decision of
HMRC
as to the amount of a penalty payable by the scheme organiser under this Part.
Notice of appeal must be given to
HMRC
no later than 30 days after the date on which—

Substitution.Addition: in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (A1), notice of
's decision is given to the scheme organiser;

Text.Substitution: in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (1) or (4), the notice under paragraph 40J(2) is given to the scheme organiser;
in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (2), the closure notice is given;
in the case of an appeal under sub-paragraph (3), the default notice is given.
On an appeal under sub-paragraph
(1) or (3)(a) which is notified to the tribunal, the tribunal may affirm or cancel the decision.
On an appeal under sub-paragraph (2) or (3)(b) which is notified to the tribunal, the tribunal may—
affirm or cancel the decision, or

HMRC
had power to make.
On an appeal under sub-paragraph (4) which is notified to the tribunal, the tribunal may—
