Subject to this paragraph and paragraph 40J, the provisions of Part 5 of
TMA

1970 relating to appeals have effect in relation to an appeal under this paragraph as they have effect in relation to an appeal against an assessment to corporation tax or, if the scheme organiser is not within the charge to corporation tax, income tax.

Text.Addition: An officer of Revenue and Customs may by notice require a person to provide the officer with any information—
which the officer reasonably requires for the performance of any functions of Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs or an officer of Revenue and Customs under the
SAYE
code, and
which the person to whom the notice is addressed has or can reasonably obtain.
The power conferred by this paragraph extends, in particular, to—
information to enable

Addition.Substitution: an officer of Revenue and Customs
to check anything contained in a notice under paragraph 40A or a return under paragraph 40B or to check any information accompanying such a notice or return, or”, and

Text.Addition: to determine the liability to tax, including capital gains tax, of any person who has participated in a scheme

Addition.Addition: or any other person whose liability to tax the operation of a scheme is relevant to

Text.Addition: , and
information about the administration of a scheme and any alteration of the terms of a scheme.
The notice must require the information to be provided within a specified time, which must not end earlier than 3 months after the date when the notice is given.

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies for the purposes of the provisions of the SAYE code relating to group schemes.
Each joint owner of a jointly owned company is to be treated as controlling every company within sub-paragraph (3).
The companies within this sub-paragraph are—

P3para.Text: the jointly owned company, and
any company controlled by that company.

P2para.Text: However, no company within sub-paragraph (3) may be—

P3para.Text: a constituent company in more than one group scheme, or
a constituent company in a particular group scheme if another company within that sub-paragraph is a constituent company in a different group scheme.

P2para.Text: In this paragraph a “jointly owned company” means a company which (apart from sub-paragraph (2)) is not controlled by any one person and—

P3para.Text: of which 50% of the issued share capital is owned by one person and 50% by another, or
which is otherwise controlled by two persons taken together.

P2para.Text: In this paragraph “joint owner” means one of the persons mentioned in sub-paragraph (5)(a) or (b).

For the purposes of the SAYE code, except in paragraph 35(3) (time when “scheme-related employment” ends), one company is an “associated company” of another company at a given time if, at that time or at any other time within one year previously—

P3para.Text: one has control of the other, or
both are under the control of the same person or persons.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of sub-paragraph (1) the question whether a person controls a company is to be determined in accordance with sections 450 and 451 of CTA 2010.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of the
SAYE
code a “non-UK company reorganisation arrangement” is an arrangement made in relation to a company under the law of a territory outside the United Kingdom—

which gives effect to a reorganisation of the company's share capital by the consolidation of shares of different classes, or by the division of shares into shares of different classes, or by both of those methods, and
which is approved by a resolution of members of the company.

A resolution does not count for the purposes of sub-paragraph (1)(b) unless the members who vote in favour of approving the arrangement represent more than 50% of the total voting rights of all the members having the right to vote on the issue.

P2para.Text: In the SAYE code—

Para.Text: “ certified SAYE savings arrangement ” has the meaning given in section 703(1) of ITTOIA 2005;
“company” means a body corporate;
“market value” has the same meaning as it has for the purposes of TCGA 1992 by virtue of Part 8 of that Act.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the SAYE code a company is a member of a consortium owning another company if it is one of a number of companies—

P3para.Text: which between them beneficially own not less than 75% of the other company’s ordinary share capital, and
each of which beneficially owns not less than 5% of that capital.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of the
SAYE
code—

shares are subject to a “restriction” if there is any contract, agreement, arrangement or condition which makes provision to which any of subsections (2) to (4) of section 423 (restricted securities) would apply if the references in those subsections to the employment-related securities were to the shares, and
the “restriction” is that provision.

P1para.Text: In the SAYE code the following expressions are defined or otherwise explained by the provisions indicated below:

xhtml:tr.xhtml:td: eligible shares (in Part 4 of this Schedule)
the options (in relation to a participant)

xhtml:td.Addition: paragraph 1 and Part 8 of this Schedule

Text.Substitution: For the purposes of the
CSOP
code a
CSOP
scheme is a Schedule 4
CSOP
scheme if the requirements of Parts 2 to 6 of this Schedule are met in relation to the scheme.

P2para.Text: The requirements consist of general requirements (see Part 2) and requirements as to—

Para.Text: the eligibility of individuals to participate in a scheme (see Part 3),
the shares to which a scheme can apply (see Part 4),
the share options which may be granted under a scheme (see Part 5), and
the exchange of share options (see Part 6).

Text.Substitution: Sub-paragraph (A1) is subject to Part 7 of this Schedule which—
requires notice of a scheme to be given to Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (“
HMRC
”) in order for the scheme to be a Schedule 4
CSOP
scheme (see paragraph 28A(1)),
provides for a scheme in relation to which such notice is given to be a Schedule 4
CSOP
scheme (see paragraph 28A(4)), and
gives power to
HMRC
to enquire into a scheme and to decide that the scheme should not be a Schedule 4
CSOP
scheme (see paragraphs 28F to 28I).

P2para.Text: In the CSOP code a “CSOP scheme” means (in accordance with section 521(4)) a scheme which—

P3para.Text: is established by a company,
provides for share options to be granted to employees and directors, and
is not an SAYE option scheme (within the meaning of the SAYE code: see section 516(4)).

P2para.Text: In the CSOP code, in relation to a CSOP scheme—

Para.Text: “participant” means an individual who has been granted (but has not yet exercised) share options under the scheme (“the options”);
“participate” means obtain and exercise share options under the scheme;
“the scheme organiser” means the company which has established the scheme.

P2para.Text: A CSOP scheme established by a company that controls one or more other companies (a “parent scheme company”) may extend to all or any of those other companies.
In the CSOP code a CSOP scheme established by a parent scheme company which so extends is called a “group scheme”.
In relation to a group scheme a “constituent company” means—

P3para.Text: the parent scheme company, or
any other company to which for the time being the scheme is expressed to extend.

P2para.Text: Paragraph 34 deals with jointly owned companies and companies controlled by them.

P1para.Text: A CSOP scheme must meet the requirements of—

Para.Text: paragraph 5 (general restriction on contents of scheme), and
paragraph 6 (limit on value of shares subject to options).

Title.Emphasis: General restriction on contents of scheme

Text.Substitution: The purpose of the scheme must be to provide, in accordance with this Schedule, benefits for employees and directors in the form of share options.
The scheme must not provide benefits to employees or directors otherwise than in accordance with this Schedule.
For example, the scheme must not provide cash as an alternative to share options or shares which might otherwise be acquired by the exercise of share options.

Title.Emphasis: Limit on value of shares subject to options

P2para.Text: The scheme must provide that an individual may not be granted share options under it which would at the time when they are granted cause the aggregate market value of the shares which the individual may acquire by exercising share options granted under—

P3para.Text: the scheme, or
any other Schedule 4 CSOP scheme established by the scheme organiser or an associated company of the scheme organiser,

P2para.Text: to exceed or further exceed £60,000.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (1) share options that have already been exercised are to be left out of account.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (1) the market value of shares is to be calculated as at—

P3para.Text: the time when the options relating to them were granted, or
if an agreement relating to them has been made under paragraph 22 (requirements as to price for acquisition of shares) the earlier time or times stated in the agreement.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of this paragraph the market value of shares subject to a restriction is to be determined as if they were not subject to the restriction.
The Treasury may by regulations amend sub-paragraph (1) by substituting a different sum of money for the sum for the time being specified there.

Part.Title: Eligibility of individuals to participate in scheme

Title.Emphasis: Requirements relating to the eligibility of individuals: introduction

P1para.Text: A CSOP scheme must meet the requirements of—

Para.Text: paragraph 8 (the employment requirement), and
paragraph 9 (the “no material interest” requirement).

P2para.Text: The scheme must ensure that an individual is not eligible to be granted share options under the scheme at a particular time unless the individual is then a full-time director or a qualifying employee of—

P3para.Text: the scheme organiser, or
in the case of a group scheme, a constituent company.

P2para.Text: A “qualifying employee”, in relation to a company, means an employee of the company other than one who is a director of—

P3para.Text: the company, or
in the case of a group scheme, a constituent company.

P2para.Text: The scheme must ensure that an individual is not eligible to participate in the scheme on any date if the individual has on that date, or has had within the 12 months preceding that date, a material interest in a close company—

P3para.Text: whose shares may be acquired as a result of exercising share options granted under the scheme, or
which has control of a company whose shares may be acquired as a result of exercising share options granted under the scheme, or
which is a member of a consortium which owns a company within paragraph (b).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this paragraph an individual is to be regarded as having a material interest in a company if—

P3para.Text: the individual, or
the individual together with one or more of the individual’s associates, or
any such associate, with or without any other such associates,

P2para.Text: has a material interest in the company.
This paragraph is supplemented—

P3para.Text: as regards the meaning of “material interest”, by paragraphs 10 and 11, and
as regards the meaning of “associate”, by paragraph 12 (read with paragraphs 13 and 14).

P2para.Text: In this paragraph and paragraph 10 “close company” includes a company that would be a close company but for—

P3para.Text: section 442(a) of CTA 2010 (exclusion of companies not resident in the United Kingdom), or
sections 446 and 447 of CTA 2010 (exclusion of certain quoted companies).

P2para.Text: In paragraph 9 (the “no material interest” requirement) references to a “material interes” in a company are to—

P3para.Text: a material interest in the share capital of the company, or
a material interest in its assets.

P2para.Text: A material interest in the share capital of a company means—

P3para.Text: beneficial ownership of, or
the ability to control (directly or through the medium of other companies or by any other indirect means),

P2para.Text: more than 30% of the ordinary share capital of the company.
A material interest in the assets of a company means—

P3para.Text: possession of, or
an entitlement to acquire,

P2para.Text: such rights as would, in the event of the winding up of the company or in any other circumstances, give an entitlement to receive more than 30% of the assets that would then be available for distribution among the participators.
In this paragraph “participator” has the meaning given by section 454 of CTA 2010.
This paragraph is supplemented by paragraph 11 (material interest: options etc.).

Title.Emphasis: Material interest: options and interests in SIPs

P2para.Text: For the purposes of paragraph 10 (meaning of “material interest”) a right to acquire shares (however arising) is to be treated as a right to control them.
Sub-paragraph (3) also applies for the purposes of paragraph 10 in a case where—

P3para.Text: the shares to be attributed to an individual consist of or include shares which the individual or another person has a right to acquire, and

the circumstances are such that, if that right were to be exercised, the shares acquired would be shares which were previously unissued and which the company would be contractually bound to issue in the event of the exercise of the right.

P2para.Text: In determining at any time prior to the exercise of the right whether the number of shares to be attributed to the individual exceeds 30% of the ordinary share capital of the company, that ordinary share capital is to be treated as increased by the number of unissued shares referred to in sub-paragraph (2)(b).
The references in sub-paragraphs (2) and (3) to the shares to be attributed to an individual are to the shares which—

P3para.Text: for the purposes of paragraph 10(2) (material interest in share capital), and
in accordance with paragraph 9(2) (material interest can consist of or include that of individual’s associates),

P2para.Text: fall to be brought into account in the individual’s case so that it can be determined whether their number exceeds 30% of the company’s ordinary share capital.
In applying paragraph 10 the following are to be disregarded—

P3para.Text: the interest of the trustees of any Schedule 2 SIP (within the meaning of the SIP code: see section 488(4)) in any shares which are held by them in accordance with the plan but which have not been appropriated to, or acquired on behalf of, an individual, and
any rights exercisable by the trustees as a result of that interest.

P2para.Text: In paragraph 9(2) (the “no material interest” requirement) “associate”, in relation to an individual, means—

P3para.Text: any relative or partner of that individual,
the trustee or trustees of any settlement in relation to which that individual, or any of the individual’s relatives (living or dead), is or was a settlor, or
where that individual is interested in any shares or obligations of the company mentioned in paragraph 9(2) which are subject to any trust or are part of the estate of a deceased person—

P4para.Text: the trustee or trustees of the settlement concerned, or
the personal representatives of the deceased,

P3para.Text: as the case may be.

P2para.Text: Sub-paragraph (1)(c) needs to be read with paragraphs 13 and 14 (which relate to employee benefit trusts and discretionary trusts).
In this paragraph—

Para.Text: “relative” means—
spouse or civil partner,
parent, child or remoter relation in the direct line, or
brother or sister;
“settlor” and “settlement” have the same meaning as in Chapter 5 of Part 5 of ITTOIA 2005 (see section 620 of that Act).

Title.Emphasis: Meaning of “associate”: trustees of employee benefit trust

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies for the purposes of paragraph 12(1)(c) (meaning of “associate”: trustees of settlement) where the individual is interested as a beneficiary of an employee benefit trust in shares or obligations of the company mentioned in paragraph 9(2).
The trustees of the employee benefit trust are not to be regarded as associates of the individual as a result only of the individual’s being so interested if neither—

P3para.Text: the individual, nor
the individual together with one or more of the individual’s associates, nor
any such associate, with or without any other such associates,

P2para.Text: has at any time after 13th March 1989 been the beneficial owner of, or been able (directly or through the medium of other companies or by any other indirect means) to control, more than 30% of the ordinary share capital of the company.

In sub-paragraph (2)(b) and (c) “associate” has the meaning given by paragraph 12(1), but does not include the trustees of an employee benefit trust as a result only of the individual’s having an interest in shares or obligations of the trust.
Chapter 11 of Part 7 of this Act (which deals with the attribution of interests in companies to beneficiaries of employee benefit trusts) applies for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2).
In this paragraph “employee benefit trust” has the same meaning as in that Chapter (see sections 550 and 551).

Title.Emphasis: Meaning of “associate”: trustees of discretionary trust

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies for the purposes of paragraph 12(1)(c) (meaning of “associate”: trustees of settlement) where—

P3para.Text: the individual (“the beneficiary”) is one of the objects of a discretionary trust,
the property subject to the trust has at any time consisted of, or included, shares or obligations of the company mentioned in paragraph 9(2),
the beneficiary has ceased to be eligible to benefit under the trust as a result of—

P4para.Text: an irrevocable disclaimer or release executed by the beneficiary, or
the irrevocable exercise by the trustees of a power to exclude the beneficiary from the objects of the trust,

P3para.Text: immediately after the beneficiary ceased to be so eligible, no associate of the beneficiary was interested in the shares or obligations of the company that were subject to the trust, and

during the period of 12 months ending with the date on which the beneficiary ceased to be so eligible, neither the beneficiary nor any associate of the beneficiary received any benefit under the trust.

P2para.Text: The beneficiary is not, as a result only of the matters referred to in sub-paragraph (1)(a) and (b), to be regarded as having been interested in the shares or obligations of the company at any time during that period of 12 months.
In sub-paragraph (1) “associate” has the meaning given by paragraph 12(1) but with the omission of paragraph (c).

Part.Title: Shares to which schemes can apply

Title.Emphasis: Requirements relating to shares that may be subject to share options: introduction

P2para.Text: A CSOP scheme must meet the requirements of—

Para.Text: paragraph 16 (shares must be ordinary shares of certain companies),
paragraph 17 (requirements as to listing) , and
paragraph 18 (shares must be fully paid up and not redeemable) ...

Text.Addition: Sub-paragraph (1) and the other paragraphs of this Part are subject to paragraph 25A(7B).

P2para.Text: In this Part “eligible shares” means shares which may be acquired by the exercise of share options under the scheme.

Title.Emphasis: Shares must be ordinary shares of certain companies

P1para.Text: Eligible shares must form part of the ordinary share capital of—

P3para.Text: the scheme organiser,
a company which has control of the scheme organiser, or
a company which either is, or has control of, a company which is a member of a consortium owning either the scheme organiser or a company having control of the scheme organiser.

P2para.Text: Eligible shares must be —

P3para.Text: shares of a class listed on a recognised stock exchange, ...
shares in a company which is not under the control of another company, ..., or

Text.Addition: shares in a company which is subject to an employee-ownership trust (within the meaning of paragraph 27(4) to (6) of Schedule 2).

Title.Emphasis: Shares must be fully paid up and not redeemable

P1para.Text: Eligible shares must be—

P3para.Text: fully paid up, and
not redeemable.

Title.Emphasis: Only certain kinds of restriction allowed

Part.Title: Requirements etc. relating to share options

Title.Emphasis: Requirements etc. relating to share options: introduction

P2para.Text: A CSOP scheme must meet the requirements of—

Text.Addition: paragraph 21A (general requirements as to terms of option),

Para.Text: paragraph 22 (requirements as to price for acquisition of shares), and
paragraph 23 (share options may not be transferred).

P2para.Text: A CSOP scheme may make any provision authorised by—

Para.Text: paragraph 24 (exercise of options: ceasing to be director or employee), ...
paragraph 25 (exercise of options: death) , or

Text.Addition: paragraph 25A (exercise of options: company events)

Emphasis.Addition: General requirements as to terms of option

Text.Addition: The following terms of a share option which is granted under the scheme must be stated at the time the option is granted—
the price at which shares may be acquired by the exercise of the option,
the number and description of the shares which may be acquired by the exercise of the option,
the restrictions to which those shares may be subject,
the times at which the option may be exercised (in whole or in part), and
the circumstances under which the option will lapse or be cancelled (in whole or in part), including any conditions to which the exercise of the option is subject (in whole or in part).
Terms stated as required by sub-paragraph (1) may be varied after the grant of the option, but—
in the case of the price, only as provided for in paragraph 22,
in the case of the number or description of shares, only as provided for in paragraph 22 or by way of a mechanism which is stated at the time the option is granted, and
in any other case, only by way of a mechanism which is stated at the time the option is granted.
Any mechanism stated for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2)(b) or (c) must be applied in a way that is fair and reasonable.

Terms stated as required by sub-paragraph (1), and any mechanism stated for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2)(b) or (c), must be notified to the participant as soon as practicable after the grant of the option.

Title.Emphasis: Requirements as to price for acquisition of shares

P2para.Text: The price at which shares may be acquired by the exercise of a share option granted under the scheme—

P3para.Text: must not be manifestly less than the market value of shares of the same class —

Text.Substitution: at the time when the option is granted, or
at such earlier time as may be determined in accordance with guidance issued by the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs.

P3para.Text: This is subject to sub-paragraph (3).

P2para.Text: The scheme may provide for one or more of the following—

P3para.Text: the price at which shares may be acquired by the exercise of a share option granted under the scheme,
the number of shares which may be so acquired, or
the description of shares which may be so acquired,

P2para.Text: to be varied so far as necessary to take account of a variation in the share capital of which the shares form part.

Text.Addition: If the scheme makes provision under sub-paragraph (3), the variation or variations made under that provision to take account of a variation in any share capital must (in particular) secure—

that the total market value of the shares which may be acquired by the exercise of the share option is immediately after the variation or variations substantially the same as what it was immediately before the variation or variations, and
that the total price at which those shares may be acquired is immediately after the variation or variations substantially the same as what it was immediately before the variation or variations.
Sub-paragraph (3) does not authorise any variation which would result in the requirements of the other paragraphs of this Schedule not being met in relation to the share option.
For the purposes of this paragraph the market value of shares subject to a restriction is to be determined as if they were not subject to the restriction.

Title.Emphasis: Share options must not be transferable

P2para.Text: The scheme must ensure that share options granted to a participant are not capable of being transferred by the participant.
Paragraph 25 provides for the exercise of the options where the participant has died.

Title.Emphasis: Exercise of options: ceasing to be director or employee

P2para.Text: The scheme may provide that an individual may exercise share options under it after ceasing to be a full-time director or qualifying employee.
“Qualifying employee” has the same meaning as in paragraph 8 (the employment requirement).
The scheme may provide that, if a participant dies before exercising the options, they may be exercised on or after the date of death ....

Text.Addition: Provision made under sub-paragraph (1) must permit the exercise of the options at any time on or after the date of death but not later than 12 months after that date.
The scheme may provide that share options relating to shares in a company may be exercised within 6 months after the relevant date for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2)
The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date when—
a person has obtained control of the company as a result of making an offer falling within sub-paragraph (3), and
any condition subject to which the offer is made has been satisfied.
An offer falls within this sub-paragraph if it is—

a general offer to acquire the whole of the issued ordinary share capital of the company which is made on a condition such that, if it is met, the person making the offer will have control of the company, or
a general offer to acquire all the shares in the company which are of the same class as the shares to which the option relates.

In sub-paragraph (3)(a) the reference to the issued ordinary share capital of the company does not include any capital already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person and in sub-paragraph (3)(b) the reference to the shares in the company does not include any shares already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (3)(a) and (b) it does not matter if the general offer is made to different shareholders by different means.

The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date when the court sanctions under section 899 of the Companies Act 2006 (court sanction for compromise or arrangement) a compromise or arrangement applicable to or affecting—
all the ordinary share capital of the company or all the shares of the same class as the shares to which the option relates, or
all the shares, or all the shares of that same class, which are held by a class of shareholders identified otherwise than by reference to their employment or directorships or their participation in
CSOP
scheme.

Addition.Addition: The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date when the court sanctions under section 901F of the Companies Act 2006 (court sanction for compromise or arrangement) a compromise or arrangement applicable to or affecting—
all the ordinary share capital of the company or all the shares of the same class as the shares to which the option relates, or

all the shares, or all the shares of that same class, which are held by a class of shareholders identified otherwise than by reference to their employment or directorships or their participation in a Schedule 4 CSOP scheme.
The relevant date for the purposes of this sub-paragraph is the date on which a non-UK company reorganisation arrangement applicable to or affecting—

etc

Addition.Addition: Sub-paragraphs (7B) to (7F) apply if the scheme makes provision under sub-paragraph (1) or (7).

a person obtaining control of the company as mentioned in sub-paragraph (2)(a);

a person who is bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company as mentioned in sub-paragraph (7) obtaining control of the company.
Provision made under sub-paragraph (7B) may not authorise the exercise of a share option, as the case may be—
at a time outside the 6 month period mentioned in sub-paragraph (1), or
at a time not covered by sub-paragraph (7).
The scheme may provide that a share option relating to shares in a company which is exercised during the period of 20 days ending with—
the relevant date for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2), (6)
the date on which any person becomes bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company as mentioned in sub-paragraph (7),
is to be treated as if it had been exercised in accordance with the provision made under sub-paragraph (1) or (7) (as the case may be).
If the scheme makes provision under sub-paragraph (7E) it must also provide that if—
a share option is exercised in reliance on that provision in anticipation of—
a person becoming bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company as mentioned in sub-paragraph (7), but
the relevant date for the purposes of sub-paragraph (2), (6)
or (6A) does not fall during the period of 20 days beginning with the date on which the share option is exercised, or
the person does not become bound or entitled to acquire shares in the company by the end of the period of 20 days beginning with the date on which the share option is exercised,
the exercise of the share option is to be treated as having had no effect.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of this paragraph a person is to be treated as obtaining control of a company if that person and others acting in concert together obtain control of it.

Title.Emphasis: Exchange of options on company reorganisation

P2para.Text: A CSOP scheme may provide that if—

P3para.Text: there is a company reorganisation affecting a scheme company (that is, a company whose shares may be acquired by the exercise of share options obtained under the scheme: see paragraph 16), and
a participant has obtained share options under the scheme which are to acquire shares of the scheme company (“the old options”),

P2para.Text: the participant may agree with the acquiring company to release the old options in consideration of the participant being granted new share options.
For the purposes of this paragraph there is a company reorganisation affecting a scheme company if another company (“the acquiring company”)—

P3para.Text: obtains control of the scheme company—

P4para.Text: as a result of making a general offer to acquire the whole of the issued ordinary share capital of the scheme company which is made on a condition such that, if it is met, the person making the offer will have control of that company, or
as a result of making a general offer to acquire all the shares in the scheme company which are of the same class as those subject to the old options;

Text.Substitution: obtains control of the scheme company as a result of a compromise or arrangement sanctioned by the court under section 899
of the Companies Act 2006 (court sanction for compromise or arrangement);

Text.Addition: obtains control of the scheme company as a result of a non-UK company reorganisation arrangement which has become binding on the shareholders covered by it; or

Text.Substitution: becomes bound or entitled to acquire shares in the scheme company under sections 979 to 982
of the Companies Act 2006 (takeover offers: right of offeror to buy out minority shareholder

Text.Addition: In sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) the reference to the issued ordinary share capital of the scheme company does not include any capital already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person and in sub-paragraph (2)(a)(ii) the reference to the shares in the scheme company does not include any shares already held by the person making the offer or a person connected with that person.
For the purposes of sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) and (ii) it does not matter if the general offer is made to different shareholders by different means.

P2para.Text: A scheme that makes provision under sub-paragraph (1) must require the agreement referred to in that sub-paragraph to be made—

P3para.Text: where control is obtained in the way set out in sub-paragraph (2)(a)(i) or (ii), within the period of 6 months beginning with the time when the acquiring company obtains control and any condition subject to which the offer is made is met,
where control is obtained in the way set out in sub-paragraph (2)(b), within the period of 6 months beginning with the time when the court sanctions the compromise or arrangement, ...

Text.Addition: where control is obtained in the way set out in sub-paragraph (2)(ba), within the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which the non-UK company reorganisation arrangement becomes binding on the shareholders covered by it, and

P3para.Text: where sub-paragraph (2)(c) applies, within the period during which the acquiring company remains bound or entitled as mentioned in that provision.

Title.Emphasis: Requirements about share options granted in exchange

P2para.Text: This paragraph applies to a scheme that makes provision under paragraph 26 (exchange of options on company reorganisation).
The scheme must require the new share options to relate to shares in a company which—

P3para.Text: is different from the company whose shares are subject to the old options, and
is either the acquiring company itself or some other company within sub-paragraph (b) or (c) of paragraph 16 (shares must be ordinary shares of certain companies), namely—

P4para.Text: a company which has control of the scheme organiser, or
a company which is, or has control of a company which is, a member of a consortium owning either the scheme organiser or a company having control of the scheme organiser.
For this purpose the control in question may be through the medium of the acquiring company.

P2para.Text: The scheme must also require the new share options to be equivalent to the old options.
For the new options to be regarded as equivalent to the old options—

P3para.Text: the shares to which they relate must meet the conditions in paragraphs 16 to 18 (types of share that may be used),
they must be exercisable in the same manner as the old options and subject to the provisions of the scheme as it had effect immediately before the release of the old options,

the total market value of the shares subject to the old options immediately before the release of those options by the participant must be substantially the same as the total market value, immediately after the grant of the new options to the participant, of the shares subject to those options, and

the total amount payable by the participant for the acquisition of shares under the new options must be substantially the same as the total amount that would have been so payable under the old options.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of the CSOP code, new share options granted under the terms of a provision included in a scheme under paragraph 26 are to be treated as having been granted at the time when the corresponding old options were granted.
This also applies for the purposes of the provisions of the scheme in their operation, after the grant of the new options, by virtue of a condition complying with sub-paragraph (4)(b).

Text.Addition: For the purposes of this paragraph the market value of shares subject to a restriction is to be determined as if they were not subject to the restriction.
For the purposes of this paragraph the market value of any shares is to be determined using a methodology agreed by Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs.
